tl;dr: This Airbnb policy is an absolute disaster. They only grant a full service fee refund if you cancel within the free cancellation period; otherwise, you're left with zilch. When the host chooses a percentage refund, one would assume that the service fee would align with that percentage refund. But in the realm of Airbnb, the service fee is non-refundable entirely, conveniently allowing Airbnb to pocket every bit. Yet, throughout this entire process, neither the host nor I have benefited from this supposed "service". It seems like a despotic maneuver by Airbnb, padding their pockets with pointless service fees that provide zero value in return. ----- full story ----- I had an incredibly disappointing experience with Airbnb's customer service, and it's disheartening to see how little they value their customers. Recently, I encountered a situation that perfectly embodies their lack of care for customer experiences. Despite safety concerns due to a stormy weather forecast at my destination lasting the entirety of my stay, when I attempted to reschedule my booking 72 hours before the check-in time, I was met with an infuriating roadblock. The option to "change booking" seemed straightforward enough, so I requested to shift the dates to the following week, which showed availability on the host's calendar. However, the host insisted I contact customer service, expressing a preference for cancellation. Here's where the trouble began: by canceling, the host would only refund a portion of my payment, as Airbnb requires a five-day cancellation notice for a full refund. The frustrating part? I could cancel another stay elsewhere on some reputable hotel booking website, just 48 hours before check-in, without facing any refund or exchange fees. I understand the reduced rebooking opportunity for the host due to the short notice, and I was willing to accept the consequences and compensate accordingly. What doesn't make sense, though, is Airbnb's stance on their non-refundable service fee. The stay hadn't even started, yet I was slapped with an irremovable service fee. What service did I receive apart from being forced to cancel when a clear rescheduling option exists on their website? During my interaction with customer service, I attempted to find a middle ground by offering to rebook the exact same listing for different dates to ensure that both the host and the platform didn't lose revenue. However, my request for a service fee refund was met with false promises. They assured me of a full refund but later reneged, stating that the host declined the rescheduling due to potential event blockings—claims that I later discovered were outright lies, as the dates remain available on the host's calendar. It's apparent that Airbnb attempts to shift blame onto hosts for their own shortcomings. My grievance is not with the host, who has nothing to do with Airbnb's service fee. The customer service further misled me by claiming these fees go to the host's account, or maybe not, which I found utterly laughable. At this point, my frustration has surpassed the issue of refunds. Adding to this disappointing encounter, my previous experiences with Airbnb haven't been positive: malfunctioning AC (host wouldn't fix it or offer an alternative), unreasonable host requests (take out their dirty personal clothes, put them into washer and dry them out before I leave), and cleanliness issues (unknown liquid on towels/pillows/sheets). Despite these, I never complained or left one negative review, understanding that small businesses might have occasional imperfections. But my patience with Airbnb has run out, and I've permanently deleted my account. I'll be opting for reputable hotel websites for future bookings.

This review is about Airbnb as a company snd not about individual hosts. However, it is a warning to those who may be considering booking. I have mostly had good experiences with past Airbnb bookings, but they have now introduced a pricing system called ‘Smart Pricing’, which essentially allows the host to advertise their property on the site with a nightly price that is the lowest price they would charge at any point during the year. You only find out the actual price when you put the dates in. However, I put my dates in and the price I was shown looked fine - then when I went to confirm and pay, the price went up exorbitantly. Having now looked up Smart Pricing on the internet, I found a Reddit post referring to this practise that said the host in question eventually admitted that they never actually offered their property on any night at the price shown. It’s clearly there to draw the customer in. I know very well the expected price for the type of property and location I chose, as I have been there recently and several times previously. This ‘Smart Pricing’ is nothing but bait and switch. It is shameful that a company as profitable and well-known as this should resort to a ploy that is deceiving its customers. Had it not been for my bank stopping the payment, I would have paid well over the odds for my accommodation. To anyone booking on Airbnb, I recommend that you check very carefully the amount you will be charged before clicking to confirm payment. Not all hosts have opted for smart (aka bait and switch) payment, so I have now booked with an honest host whose prices are transparent. I will NEVER book with a host who uses smart pricing. This has left a very unpleasant taste in my mouth about Airbnb.

Awful experience with rude staff. They charged me over 200 in error and blamed the whole thing on me. Refused to cover any related unplanned overdraft charges and were just plain rude.

AirBnB is not mediating between tenant and landlord, i.e. any problem is with high probability on the tenant side. It is hard to find honest reviews in advance as they are deleted if too honest. I have been hosting on Airbnb for years. I have had a good experience with both guests and airbnb itself. I have had 2 guests damage a chair and a figurine. Both not major, I did not claim because I allow for minor things. Most guests are respectful. A few dirty and then I just do a deep clean. Overall as a single parent airbnb kept me out of debt and I appreciate them helping Ukrainian by letting people book places they don’t intent to stay in. For guests who book and cancel last min, who left bad reviews here, am disappointed because when you book, you block the host’s calendar, stopping others from booking. I had a guest who did this recently and worse thing is she would not respond to my messages, 1 min she is coming next she just goes mute, eventually she said she wants a refund. On Airbnb’s side, if it is true that guests need only click once to pay, I think they should bring up a notification box with the cancellation policy and make the guest confirm reading it before taking payment and blocking off the host’s calendar. Safes both parties a lot of trouble.

On the 22nd January 2020 (pre-pandemic) I booked a stay using AirBNB. The stay was for 3 nights from the 16th - 19th April 2020. Anyone reading this would know that the U.K went into full lockdown on the 23rd March 2020. It would have been illegal for me to stay in my AirBNB during that time, but despite me stating that weeks before, AirBNB refused to issue me a refund. Eventually after pestering customer service I was offered a 50% refund or a travel credit for the full amount - I reluctantly took the travel credit & had to refund my own friends out of my pocket who were going to be staying in the AirBNB with me. Despite having a travel credit on my account, I couldn’t actually see it or even use it on all AirBNB bookings (it just didn’t give me the option sometimes) & fast forward to present day (2023) & I still have £51 left of my travel credit. This wouldn’t be an issue, however AirBNB have now emailed to state that all unused travel credits will now expire on 31st December 2023. Absolutely no reason for it whatsoever! It’s like my bank suddenly deciding that my money in my account is expiring unless I spend it! No justification for this at all from AirBNB, just an excuse for a simple cash grab from its users! Absolutely disgusting company. DO NOT SUPPORT AIRBNB!

Booked a 1 night stay in Manchester for my first ever booking as an airbnb customer. I was asked to pay my host a £200 'security' deposit which was refundable within 48 hours post check out. I messaged the host with my bank details for the refund on the day of check out and was ignored. Another 9 days went by of messaging and again I was ignored. Eventually I got a response from the host and they told me come back to Manchester and do something about it if I want my money back. I opened a dispute case with airbnb who appear to have the WORST customer service I have ever experienced. The only response I get from them is that they are looking into my case and will respond shortly. Then thats the end of it, I no longer get a response from them. I then have to open another case, for the next agent to tell me someone else is already looking into my case so they close the new one down... So after 17 cases opened with no response from anybody I tried contacting management. I am currently on Manager number 5 and still experiencing the same thing. DISGRACE!

Horrible. Airbnb is not what it once was.Only about money. I’ve just canceled my account and will never use them again. We had a trip booked months in advance to Alicante which was a gift for my wife’s birthday. In the morning we were due to fly my wife woke up feeling terrible, went to the emergency dr and was diagnosed with an infection and prescribed antibiotics. She was in no state to fly. I called Airbnb to explain and ask if there was anything we could do (the terms on the website stated it was too late for a refund) as it was an exceptional situation. The advisor said it was no problem and if I could provide evidence of the illness we would get a full refund(almost 400€) As requested I immediately uploaded the dr’s note to the chat in Airbnb and asked if that was ok. Then it went downhill. I got no response until 3 days later someone called me from their outsourced call Center in Egypt to say there would be no refund unless the host agreed to it. I explained that wasn’t the deal I was promised but he chose to ignore the fact that his colleague had already promised me a full refund and there was evidence of this in both the chat and the initial call which had been recorded. A back and forth of messages and calls ensued which lasted about 2 weeks. Mostly with Airbnb support people who could barely communicate in English and just made matters worse. Eventually, I managed to get in contact again with a local support agent who agreed I had been promised a full refund and assured me she would sort it out. Then she disappeared too. The last I heard from them was another message in broken English saying the host would not agree to a refund and that was it. I called again and ended up talking to Egypt and asked for a local supervisor to call me. I was assured this would happen in 1 hour. Never materialized. I finally gave up. Lied to, messed around and a lot of my time wasted to no avail. We were only refunded the €40 cleaning fee. If they had simply said you are not eligible for a refund at the start that would have been fine, but the point here is I was promised a full refund then they lied and snaked out of it passing me from pillar to post. I’ve used Airbnb as host and guest for over a decade. It’s really hit rock bottom. More revenue at all costs and screw the customer seems to be the motto here. Ridiculously high service and cleaning fees sneaky dynamic pricing and using cheap substandard outsourced customer service means the experience has gone drastically downhill and it’s mostly cheaper to book a hotel or through booking.com. Thanks for nothing Airbnb.
Booked paid then booking cancelled with no explanation , apartment listed at higher price!! Now got flights but no accomodation! What is the point of these sites if they can just cancel bookings

Do not book anything with Airbnb! They'll take your money immediately. If the host refuses the booking, it'll take 15 working days....3 weeks! to get it back. I've been arguing with them by text, email, chat and phone calls for days. Copy and paste answers is all you get.

We stop using AirBnb services as from now, we will only use Booking.com as they work with professional people who do not set the security of people in danger.

I sent an email to Airbnb within a few days of booking our trip wanting to cancel a booking. Worst customer service, always think about their commission. Couldnt check in with old age mother as access road to the host property is not safe and need to walk around 200mts, when i cancelled my trip, they didnt refunded and showed cancellation policy, if the access road is not safe how can i occupy

UPDATE Just found exactly same villa advertised on Vrbo with FULL refund up until 13th April 2024. So who is lying, Airbnb, the ‘Hosts’ or some other entity? Waiting for an explanation before I contact the Financial Ombudsman as I think this is fraud. Just wanted to add that the Villa was booked with Our Maderia, super host ‘Linda’. Whilst I respect the right to have these cancellation policies in place, a 50% deduction of your booking is high, and it would seem it doesn’t matter what the circumstances are. This is determined by the hosts. Sadly I failed to notice this when booking. I have asked and asked for them to reconsider, as I feel sure the villa will be relet, therefore the hosts will not lose out financially. I have asked Airbnb to help with the situation, however it is clear they are not interested, despite having a resolution Centre. Please be careful when booking through Airbnb, their customer service leaves a lot to be desired. Very disappointed. I reserved a place and emailed the host about whether it was a shared place. He didn't answer me but took over $1100 from my account through PayPal that I did not authorize. When I tried to be refunded I was informed the 'host had declined' my request. Feels as if I have been 'scammed.'

This is completely out of order to demand money before even confirming the booking! Upon further investigation we tracked down the owner direct, and it transpired that there was no changeover day on a Saturday which was not mentioned on the website. It has caused huge frustration and complete lack of faith in Airbnb to ever use them again. Airbnb get your act together.

Usual customer of Airbnb but have reviewed my options for the future. Booked a place up in Maroochydore, Sunshine Coast for 4 nights. I was overcharged for adding an additional night to my reservation and sent in a request to Arbnb to review what was going on with the charges. They have ignored it. There customer service has tanked and apparently how they overall treat guests using their services. I am switching to VRBO.

Booked a couple of places in Brittany and Normandy for next year for an adventure with the grandchildren. I now have to wait 15 plus days for my deposits back... in effect money was taken from my account for a service that was never there to be offered in the first place... mmmm what do they call this in legal terms?
My case was closed without being resolved. Terrible customer service

Horrendous service, allow hosts to falsely advertise properties and fail to provide basics such as hot water! Absolute rip off with their fees, for the lack of service you get when needed.

They said they are waiting for the host to reply, to hear their side of the story. A few days later, they came back saying the host never replied. How convenient! It took "support" one week to finally let me know they can't do anything about it, as parking wasn't specified in the listing. I am traumatized from staying in Airbnb. And a big part of the issue is that community at large is so heavily composed of deranged unprofessional idiots. Terrible experience yet again as a host - guest decided to leave because they wanted the whole apartment to themselves despite booking only the private room. Air BNB ignored my cancellation policy and used air cover by fining me £200 to pay the customer. A disgusting organization

Completely unethical practice, when cancelling a booking and opting for credit to account instead of refund to card. NEVER NEVER NEVER opt to have credit to your account when cancelling a booking, even if you plan to make a new booking. AirBnB don't make this clear at all but when they calculate your payment for the new booking, if splitting the payment, you end up having to pay 75% upfront instead of the usual 50% upfront. This is clearly a scam to get you to commit further. Also, they do not ever allow you to have the credit returned back to your card, once it is applied to your account. Again, completely unethical from a company that I thought prided itself on ethics and fair practice. Beware, you credit will never be refundable once applied as credit, so ALWAYS when cancelling a booking, opt for a refund to your card, even though it might take a few days. Overall, their customer service we found to be very unhelpful and in future, we will avoid where possible.

Poor after care service! Still waiting on a response from my host and it’s been nearly a fortnight. Apparently, this what you get with a super host, I dread to think how bad things are with a host. Thankfully there’s alternatives and people will go else where if the experience isn’t good.

Another negative host review removed by Airbnb. Do not believe its claims of transparency and impartiality: Airbnb will fall over itself to remove bad reviews when requested by the host. Complain about a negative review of you as a guest, however, and you are simply told to suck it up. I stayed at an Airbnb in Lisbon in October 2023. The accommodation wasn’t nice, rather dank and damp smelling. There was a large dehumidifier the owner had installed obviously in an attempt to reduce the damp smell. We didn’t like it much, moved somewhere nicer a day early, and flew back to London. Imagine our shock to then receive a message from the host a day later demanding to know the whereabouts of his dehumidifier, plus a cheap kettle and hairdryer which he claimed had gone missing. We told him the idea of us stealing a 3-foot high dehumidifier and somehow smuggling it back as cabin baggage on the plane or disposing of it on the streets of Lisbon was absurd and expected that to be the end of it. He then proceeded to demand £515 from us to cover the cost of the ‘missing’ items. He also left a review on my profile detailing the missing items and essentially insinuating I was a thief. Despite zero evidence and the obvious absurdity of the whole situation. Ludicrous right? Not according to Airbnb. They refused to remove his review citing their desire for ‘transparency’. Despite this, they removed my review of this host - which was simple and honest and detailed the situation without accusing anyone of anything - within hours for ‘violating its rules’. I can only presume because this host had a dozen properties with Airbnb and was worth quite a lot of money to them. Despite being cleared of any involvement (obviously) Airbnb have repeatedly refused to remove the review implying I am a thief. Transparency? Integrity? I doubt I’m the only one whose experience suggests the precise opposite

I’ve had such a bad customer service experience that I’m left totally shocked. My initial complaint was frustrating, but I expected that by raising a complaint through their clearly defined process, I would get a resolution. What I got was appalling avoidance tactics, stonewalling and no way to escalate. How do I escalate this so I can complain about the Airbnb support team? Transaction ID 1SN49723B3422933K
Terrible, Refunded me £40 instead of £550 and then it took me two weeks to get through to support. where they would put me on hold for 30 minutes and end the call. This happened 4 times.

Customer Service and the hosts are partners in crime. Never again in my life!!! Didn’t refund me £600 saying it’s the host who will refund you. The host said it’s Airbnb… Spent almost 2 months in phone calls and e-mails. They only lie!

I booked this place based on the description, which promised a luxurious, clean, and new apartment. However, my experience was far from that. After a long flight, when we arrived at the apartment, we were greeted by a girl who requested my passports. I was willing to provide my passport, but I requested to be taken to the office so that someone from there could take a picture of it. Unfortunately, the girl informed me that she had to take a picture of our passport using her cell phone, which I refused to allow. Upon entering the apartment, I immediately noticed that it was extremely dirty. There was an abundance of dust and hairballs all over the place. The kitchen table and chairs were covered in dried food and coffee stains, which was quite disgusting. The bathroom and shower area had mold, and there was water damage on the ceiling. It was unbelievable that I had paid a significant amount of money for such a filthy place. I felt like I had fallen victim to a scam. I contacted Airbnb to report the situation, but unfortunately, I was transferred from one person to another, with no resolution. I kept receiving notifications on the Airbnb app, stating that they were unable to assist me at that time, and I had to wait. Frustrated, I ended up booking a hotel and immediately moved my family there. Finally, On the second day, I finally managed to speak with someone from the Airbnb management team. They assured me that my money would be refunded immediately. However, I also requested compensation for the additional expenses I incurred due to having to book a last-minute hotel, which ended up costing me an extra thousand dollars. Unfortunately, I have not received any communication from Airbnb regarding this matter. This was my first experience with Airbnb, and it has left me extremely disappointed. I no longer have any trust in their service, as you never know what you will end up with in the end. I strongly advise travelers to book directly with hotels instead of going through Airbnb. Overall, my experience with this apartment was incredibly disappointing. The false promises of luxury and cleanliness, coupled with the lack of assistance from Airbnb, made it a nightmare start to our trip. I highly advise others to avoid this place and exercise caution when booking through Airbnb.

We have booked several spaces through AirBnB and found them good in the past. Probably because things didn't go wrong. We will never book through them again because they know that our host misrepresented the listing we booked and we didn't get what we paid for. Shocking service. They claim to offer support 24/7, however this is not the case. We had a complaint about a booking that was deceiving and misleading on the listing. Airbnb Frustration - I've reached my breaking point with Airbnb after enduring more unpleasant experiences than positive ones during my five years of using their services. Throughout my travels as an Airbnb guest, I've encountered numerous unfortunate incidents worldwide. Hosts have been dishonest, falsely claiming damages to furniture that were already old or broken, merely to secure free replacements. I've even faced threats from hosts, with Airbnb inexplicably honoring their payment despite clear evidence that my stay would likely lead to confrontations or worse. Airbnb's response was disappointingly unhelpful, leaving me with no recourse. On multiple occasions, hosts have invoked the "No refund" policy after making booking mistakes, and despite promptly bringing these issues to their attention, they've shown no empathy and kept the entire booking fee. Now when I think "Airbnb" I think of "Stress" At this point, I've lost trust in Airbnb and have grown tired of their questionable policies and deceitful hosts.

I had a complicated issue involving Payoneer as payout method on my host account. Customer specialist called Anna helped resolve the issue through and through. A crap Poor support Time wasting Has not evolved in 20 years

When we didn't need Airbnb to assist with anything, everything was great. However, we needed to report our last Airbnb stay - the hosts were spying on us and openly admitted it on a review! We reported it to Airbnb, they took 15 minutes to "investigate" and allowed the host to take further bookings by saying they did not breach any safety rules. If you stay in any Airbnbs, check for Hidden cameras! Scan the room slowly with the torch on your phone (in complete darkness), the light from your phone will reflect the lense of any hidden cameras. This matter has been reported to the local police (Christchurch, Zealand). Will never book with Airbnb again, profit is all that matters to them. Thankfully there are plenty of other platforms to use to book accommodation, they can have our business instead.

I recently booked a property in London, and unfortunately, the experience was far from satisfactory. Despite these challenges, I made numerous attempts to address the issues with the host and sought Airbnb's support, hoping for a resolution. Over the course of my stay, I sent a total of seven emails to Airbnb detailing the problems faced. Regrettably, I received no acknowledgment or response to any of these emails. This lack of support has been deeply disappointing, especially considering the premium price paid for the accommodation. Airbnb's customer support used to be something I could rely on. However, this experience has significantly eroded my trust and confidence in the platform. I hope others don't have to face such an unresponsive service in their times of need.

I’m using Airbnb for 5 years now and never had an issue until last time. We’ve booked accommodation for 3 nights but had to leave after 1 night due to dump and mould in the house, cold, extra charges for electricity, dirty house etc. reported issue to Airbnb who run an investigation first and refunded me for 2 nights we never stood there.

My friend booked an Air BnB in Cape Town, S. Africa, months ago (for mid-December, 2023). A few weeks ago, she learned her elderly dad is going to need surgery. She cancelled the reservation online with the Host, who said they had a no refund policy. She gave 3 MONTHS NOTICE. The Host then found another guest for that same time period. So the Host is now getting paid twice for the same time period when my friend gave that much notice. She is an only child and has to care for her elderly father. It was NOT her fault!

To be perfectly clear, I'm well aware that there are Airbnb Hosts that take their hosting very seriously and treat it as a business with the idea of learning from their mistakes. However, they are few and far in between. For the most part, folks get into the hosting business because they think it's a quick way to make a buck. They know nothing of the hospitality industry nor do they care to learn. They just want a "plug and play" business and don't really care about improving. The result is that guests end up in a place that is far inferior to what the photos indicate and since the Airbnb company does not allow guests to post their own photos (unlike booking.com), future guests don't get an accurate portrayal of the premises and end up booking blindly. Some of the guest reviews are accurate and many are simply overly tolerant in what is acceptable quality. I don't wish to put all hosts in the same basket because I know there are some that truly take pride in their establishment but it's very difficult to find those in a forest of pure crappy stays. Increasingly, the number 1 comment that I've read online from aggravated hosts after reading bad reviews is, "We're not a hotel". From the perspective of business modelling, it's clear that Airbnb Hosts are not hotels. However, they ARE in the business of hospitality and should act like it. Just for the record, I've been in 18 different Airbnbs in the last 12 months covering Mexico, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, and Montenegro.

Awful customer service. Had a very bad experience booking through Airbnb as a guest. The Bubble Hotel in Bali was not as described - was in poor state of repair and the transparent bubble to sleep under the stars was cloudy m, so you couldn’t see anything out of this. It was dirty and the door didn’t open / close properly. The handle was broken and the day bed was also dirty. The support from AirBnB trying to get a refund for this was a long, drawn out experience - resulting in only a 30% refund. They could do no more - even though they agreed from the video footage this was not an accurate listing and the owner was not corresponding appropriately. Because it was such a long winded process, we were then unable to leave a review on this accommodation to warn future guests!! No support or help around this - even though they acknowledged this had been caught up in a dispute which took a long time to still be unresolved satisfactory. They are not 24/7 support ad they lead you to believe on their website. If you’re in the UK they tend to call after 9pm and through the night - one time was 2am in the morning!! They have done nothing about the deceptive listing, so this hotel business is getting away with lies and not being held to account. Shocking!! I will not be booking any more “luxury” accommodation again with Airbnb

DO NOT BECOME A HOST. Air Bnb has gone significantly downhill. It is super shady. I have been hosting for YEARS. I am a "superhost". They now do not allow you to vet potential guests. Their pictures are hidden and you are pressured to immediately accept or decline, without the ability to chat back and forth to get a sense of the person. And in the past three months, out of six guests, THREE have ripped me off, stolen, or damaged my place. Air Bnb does not care about hosts, period. In all three cases, I have had to chase Air Bnb for more than a month for any response. In the third case I am still waiting. When something goes wrong they automatically blame the host, charge you money, take the guests side. You need to fight for it and I won't give up but I QUIT being a host. Protect your time, stress, and your home. Don't do it.
S.H.I.T. A host filed a complaint against me because I canceled the reservation and is now asking for money through Airbnb support center.

Booked a long stay. But I have been disturbed by other guests chatting overnight. Airbnb say I must "evidence" this disturbance by giving them "documentation" or "video" of the noise. Airbnb require me to go in the middle of the night to record people covertly outside their rooms to prove they are making a noise! I will not do this! I just want to leave. I am exhausted. Airbnb utterly useless. I have been a customer for years. I've received many compliments and positive reviews. I have given many positive reviews. But this does not help me now so what is the point with all those internal airbnb reviews? This counts for nothing. Warning to you all - always go for one night before booking your long stay. Airbnb utterly useless at customer service for me the customer. Airbnb has me helpless and hopeless and sleepless.

We arrived at our property and expected a washer and dryer, utensils and flatware. The washer did not work, there was no dryer and there were not enough utensils and flatware. We contacted the management who kept saying, when they did answer, that they were looking into the situation. Nothing was ever done. We had no internet and no cable for the rest of our stay with no communication from management. We also had the fire alarm go off twice, with no communication from management again. They offered for us to move but we needed to be in the area we were and they could only offer places miles away. This company should be avoided at all costs. Their host cancelled my stay at the last minute but a refund has not been forthcoming. Airbnb have failed to enter into discussion about it despite repeat messaging. Their lack of interest in the issue is very telling.

We were cancelled because we didn't answer a question quickly. We did answer it many times on the site and by the host email...but we were still cancelled. Airbnb is a waste of our time. We will never attempt to rent again with this company.

I'm a long-standing user of Airbnb as a guest. Up until recently, I had no complaints. I've always loved the diversity of properties available on the app. I've had twenty-nine stays through Airbnb. For my first twenty-eight stays, the price I paid at the point of booking was the final price. However, on my latest one, electric and gas was a separate charge. I could forgive this, except Airbnb is actively telling hosts to put this information hidden away in 'house rules'. Such information about additional mandatory charges belong on the payment screen, not hidden away. This is a clear attempt at a lack of transparency. I have spoken with hosts on r/Airbnb on Reddit, and hosts are being told that house rules are where to put this information. Bear in mind, you have to click TWICE away from the main listing screen to see this. This is a clear decision to not be transparent with guests. It's sleazy, and deceptive. This 1 star rating will remain here until ALL listings are required to put ALL mandatory fees and charges at the payment screen at the point of booking. Booking and Agoda manage to get this right, why not Airbnb?

Our host cancelled our reservation at the very last minute (I.e. we had arrived). This was not her fault. Airbnb offered us £21 extra to find somewhere else. Problem: we had booked the cheapest option in a city. The extra £21 didn't even come close to booking a replacement room. (We had paid £35) rooms were starting at £70. We spent the whole day in communication with Airbnb who assured us they would call back and resolve the issue. By 4pm they hadn't. We then decided to book somewhere ourselves. We added £20 to our small budget and booked 20 miles from the city. We changed a filter during our search (the one which says you do not have to wait 24 hours for the host to respond) obviously, only to realise too late that the Airbnb platform had changed our dates (I believe the heading is 'similar dates'), but I failed to notice this. The host of this accommodation was willing to refund us, but the Airbnb platform would not allow a refund. So the next 3 hours was spent trying to explain this to Airbnb, unsuccessfully it turns out. They could only see we had rebooked and their conscious was clean. So at 9pm, with no accommodation, no money, no wonderful weekend, we returned home.

I have stayed in dozens of Airbnb’s with generally great experiences. However, I just had a super disheartening experience with the company’s customer service around the integrity of reviews that has caused me to completely lose faith as a guest. I left a 2 star review after a stay where the “superhost” asked for excessive personal information before the stay, which I refused to provide. When I got to the apartment my friends and I were shocked to find it had one working exterior door, and no windows to the outside, so no emergency egress. The former back patio had been converted into a crawl space under a deck with buildings on all sides, so no escape route, and all former windows had the exterior walls of other buildings immediately outside. This also meant no natural light in the entire space. Photos of the space were very deceiving and showed bright windows. This plus some cleanliness issues led us to give a negative review. Fast forward a few weeks and I get a message from airbnb accusing me of blackmailing the host, and informing me my review was being taken down and I could lose my account if I ever did it again. I pushed back and eventually airbnb replied to a tweet. They investigated and stood their ground, informing me the host had provided evidence of off-platform messaging where I asked for monetary compensation in return for a positive review. I pointed out my airbnb messaging with the host where they asked for my personal information and I refused to provide it, saying I would only message them on airbnb. I lost the appeal! This host made fraudulent evidence and won, so my honest review has been taken down! And now this host is likely continuing to rent out this death box of an apartment! I’m so disturbed.

Calling a host at 3am to deal with an issue then blocking the account because I did not respond to your 3am text meassage threat of getting back to you in 20 minutes. The bed was very low to the ground, more like a futon with a Tempur mattress. There were stains on the bedroom carpet and the bathroom was in need of an upgrade. The gate keypad was temperamental. The house smelt overpoweringly of air freshener, carpet freshener and plug ins. The kitchen equipment was sparse and 'well used'. Not good value for money. Short review: One of the worst experiences I had with customer services. Basically, the customer service of Airbnb gave us (what it turned out to be) wrong information about their policy (which were shared through their chat and saved by us into a PDF). Once we booked our reservation based on the wrong information received, Airbnb decided that we had to stick to a different understanding of their policy. We tried everything (calls, emails, new tickets, escalate to managers) to no avail. Eventually, we had to stick with the reservation and we are now considering what to do with the remaining days. Moreover, bear in mind that if you need to cancel your reservation, the calculation of how much you have to pay will not be what you would have paid for the subsequent 30 days. Overall, it's like dealing with scammers and expect they will respect what they say. Save yourself time, money, and headaches...if you can, go for another broker or hotels. Longer review: We went to Santiago (Chile) and we booked an entire place through Airbnb for 15 days. As we needed to stay in Santiago for several months, we decided to find another place throuhg Airbnb, this time long-term. In fact, several friends told us that Airbnb is 'the platform' used in Santiago for renting places to tourists. Nevertheless, we wanted some warranties before booking a place for the entire period. We started contacting people to ask for information about their apartments and, in parallel, we contacted Airbnb to double check our understanding of their policy for long-term rentals before going ahead with the reservation. Here is where problems started. Airbnb told us that, as we were renting a place for such a long period, we were entitled to change the dates of our reservation at our liking. We were a bit surprised about that but, unfortunately, we could not find any additional information on the website. We called Airbnb customer service again and we confirmed again that what they said was true. At that point, we had a transcript of the chat (which we saved in a PDF...just in case) and two calls to the customer service. We needed a place as time was running out and so we reserved a place. As soon as we entered the apartment, we realised that the apartment wasn't right for us. Plus, it was very dirty and pictures were taken many years before, showing a place that was in much better shape than in reality. Fortunately, we were very careful and we triple checked the policy and our rights before reserving the place. We called Airbnb within 24 hours we entered the new place and we told them that we wanted to change our reservation. The Airbnb ambassador who responded to our case told us that this was not possible and that we needed to find an agreement with the host before going ahead. We shared with them that that was NOT what they told us a couple of days earlier. The ambassador checked the other chat and agreed that the information we had been given was not right. We then shared with Airbnb that the place was very dirty, many things were broken and pictures didn't reflect the current state of the apartment. But at this point, Airbnb just stopped caring for us (once they have your money, their services are over). Every time we called, a new ambassador needed to review the case from scratch (which took hours every time). They never proceeded to offering a solution and simply passed the case to someone else each time. Then, contrasting information were shared by different ambassadors. We ended up escalating the case to a manager (we had to asked explicitly and insist). Even the manager confirmed that the initial ambassador made a mistake but Airbnb cannot do anything when their customer service shares wrong information. They didn't offer any partial refund or tried to put things right. They didn't even offer to refund cleaning fees (which, anyway, were minimal). They kept referring to their policy so we asked multiple times to see a document outlining their policies. However, all we constantly got was a copy and paste message from their website, which is very unclear, leaving them space to interpret it as they wish (even though, when telling us what we could or could not do, they kept referring to their policy and the contract we had signed by reserving the place). Basically, they can sell you thin air and then it's your problem to make it work. That's what we did, we ended up cleaning the apartment and fixing the broken things. We're now considering to cancel the reservation, and probably lose some money, as Airbnb is not of any help. I wish we would have looked at their reviews before even considering using their services. I hope this, and all the other negative reviews, help others make an informed choice when booking with Airbnb.

Terrible Experience with Airbnb - Avoid at All Costs! I had an absolutely nightmarish experience with Airbnb, and I strongly advise anyone considering booking accommodations to steer clear of this platform and opt for alternatives like Expedia or booking directly with hotels. If the 12.000 thousands of one-star reviews on Trustpilot haven't convinced you, let my own experience serve as a cautionary tale. Firstly, Airbnb's lack of privacy is alarming. The moment you innocently click on a property to "check dates and prices," Airbnb immediately sends a message to the host stating that there is a request for a stay. This invasion of privacy and blatant disregard for user intentions should raise red flags for anyone. My personal experience involved a host named "Avi" from Brooklyn New York who had the audacity to treat his neighbors as "queens of the planet." Apparently, any minor grievance from these neighbors could result in you being evicted with no refund. As a paying guest, I had legitimate concerns about my rights and comfort. I reached out to Avi to seek clarification on his house rules, but instead of addressing my concerns, he responded with utter disrespect. In response, I blocked Avi, thinking I had severed all communication ties. To my horror, the next day, I received a message from Avi on the Airbnb platform. This was a clear violation of my privacy and a breach of Airbnb's supposed "blocking" feature. It gets worse - Airbnb sent me an email stating that Avi had rejected my "stay request." The problem? I had never made such a request in the first place. These incidents raised serious concerns about the platform's security and integrity. Frustrated and bewildered, I decided to contact Airbnb's customer support, hoping for some clarity and resolution. Unfortunately, my interactions with Airbnb's support team were nothing short of infuriating. The agents I encountered, Nadejda, Roxana, Jeshu, and Moumita, seemed completely robotic, senseless, and ignorant. None of them were able to comprehend or address my two primary concerns: first, how a blocked host could message me on the Airbnb platform, and second, how Airbnb could claim that Avi rejected a stay request that I never made. Instead of addressing these legitimate concerns, these agents simply provided me with rudimentary instructions on how to block someone on Airbnb. It was a glaring display of incompetence and lack of customer empathy. In conclusion, my experience with Airbnb was nothing short of a nightmare. From the invasion of privacy to the unprofessional behavior of hosts and the abysmal customer support, Airbnb has proven itself to be a platform that simply cannot be trusted. Save yourself the trouble and choose more reputable alternatives for your accommodation needs. Do not use Airbnb.

In March 2023, we booked an apartment in Paris for 8 adults for a week late December - early January. We booked with a "super host", and immediately paid the required deposit. We then received a conformation email that our reservation was confirmed. On the weekend, we received an automated email advising that the booking was cancelled and our deposit was being refunded. It took multiple calls to AirBnB to try and find out what happened AirBnB said the host cancelled We had messaged the host at the time of booking to confirm our arrival time. We messaged her, and she said that AirBnB cancelled. We contacted AirBnB again, and they offered to find alternative accommodation. They provided several options - all of which were inferior to our original booking. One place was described by multiple reviewers as being "very dirty" and "in need of repairs and a deep clean." One place had bunk beds One place was not even in Paris, but 20km to the south. AirBnB's position is that they are sorry, but there is nothing more they will do. It is our problem to sort out if we are not happy with the alternatives they found. My advice would be 1. Don't use AirBnB as they are not helpful when something goes wrong 2. If you use AirBnB, make 2-3 different bookings so you have something secured if someone (host or AirBnB) cancels. Hold these until the cancellation date (usually only 1-2 weeks before), and then cancel the spare bookings. Booking many months out leaves you at a significant disadvantage.

I've used Airbnb around 24 times in 8 years, but the first time I needed them, they revealed themselves to be an atrociously poor company. One star is the minimum one can give here, but it should be zero. I rented a flat in Brussels, found out in my first night (of the 7 that I booked) that the place had a silverfish infestation, and left - leaving the place in good nick and communicating with Airbnb in a clear and courteous manner at all times. What does the owner do? She ignores me and says she won't give me a refund - despite her written assurance on Airbnb that I should get 50% back of every night I don't spend there. What does Airbnb do? After insisting for two days, they say they will refund me £8 (!!!), out of the £800 that I paid, by way of compensation. Useless. Airbnb has a long list of assurances on its website and it produces neat, feel-good commercials - but I've found out that this is a service that sells sweaty bedrooms to strangers with no quality control, no service and no regard for its terms and conditions. Avoid. There are sites like booking.com that have much better service.

If there was a minus star rating mine would be -100. We have been with Airbnb since 2013 as Guests and as Hosts with 5 star ratings. We moved to Greece 3 years ago and built a fabulous Dome in an Olive Grove next to the beach to use as holiday accommodation for guests. (Everyone calls it amazing). July 2023 changed our life after a guest from Airbnb booked. We suspected trouble at the booking stage but because it was our first season we accepted the 4 night booking. What could go wrong! I'll shorten the version but please be aware while reading this that as experienced hosts we didn't realise we were being scammed by the guest. His motivation is about discounts and free holidays. The main problem started when the BBQ had to be temporarily removed due to the government rules during the serious wild fires around us. He complained to Airbnb and insisted on using it but we had to send the Government guide to Airbnb who supported us. He then complained through Airbnb about the outside lighting and wanted the timings changed by 15 mins. When my husband went to the dome (outside area) to do the change the guest ran out of the dome and shouted at him. Apparently this breached Airbnb's privacy rules. I call it entrapment but luckily it was in writing that the lights were to be changed. Airbnb were in communication with him regarding other problems he had found ie WIFI was slow. The end result was Air bnb cancelled the reservation and found him other accommodation. Airbnb wrote to apologise and said the booking was cancelled at No cost or penalty to us. The guest was still in the accommodation at 7,30pm that day and refused to leave therefore we called the police and advised Airbnb. The guest and his unauthorised guest were screaming at each other and the door was being banged . We were expecting trouble and called the police again. Thankfully the guests left at 8pm. We immediately checked the place. The bed was broken and there was other damage but all in all we were just glad they left. We advised Airbnb who were very supportive with our claim and said we'd received it at the next pay out. We never received any money but instead were removed from their site due to a Breach of Privacy Rule! Our other bookings were removed and our summer was ruined. We cannot even book as Guests anywhere in the world. 7 months later the police arrived with a summons to appear at the station with our side of the story. Its an absolute nightmare with no support from Airbnb. They have closed our listing and there is no access to the platform showing the correspondence between us and the guest and this is vital but they wont allow us on to the platform to retrieve it. Luckily we had saved the written request to change the lights or we wouldn't have a leg to stand on. The unauthorised guest video'd the episode which I hope we can view in court because there was absolutely no violation of privacy on our part. Its our only hope Something to keep in mind is that at the time of this video it was10 hours after check out! The guest and his unauthorised guest had already been told by Airbnb to leave. I hope this ramble makes sense to you but it definitely doesn't make sense to us that Airbnb have sided with a guest who has been in the wrong all the way through. They just don't care for the hosts and now we have a court case hanging over us. We are gutted and now not so keen to carry on with this years holiday season.

A month later I told Sarah a fuse was gone a second time as power outlets in a certain section of the unit stopped working again. She assumed it was my electric car (it’s a hybrid) which I explained wouldn’t make sense given the smaller size of the battery and faster charging time versus something like a Tesla. Over a week later, I see outside the window a gentleman in a security vest with what looked like a volt tester in his hand (device for checking electricity). Days later I try to charge my car and the outlet is not working. So I test my charging cable inside the house and it works! I found this to be so shady of Sarah and Chris. Keep in mind that the first time this happened with power outlets not working I hadn’t even charged my car. It was the night I moved in and so I wasn’t even parked in the right spot, which I have messages between Sarah to corroborate this which makes it even more questionable why they would deactivate the power outlet. At this point I realized there was a clear fracture in communication. Not to mention that as helpful as Airbnb support was in vouching for me to stay when the hosts didn’t want me to, I was also under the condition that any future problems I would have to foot the bill even if I was told to leave. From August all the way to my move out date in October, there was no heat. The heater didn’t work, no hot water, and so laundry was only cold as well. With regards to the place, it was nicely set up, wi-fi was overall solid although once or twice a week it would get slow and I’d have to use my phone as a hotspot. The parking is also very tight and not what I expected when I saw the photos. It’s between the house wall and neighbour fence and tucked right behind the garbage collection area and a basketball net. The overall area is nice, quiet and safe. This experience could have been way better had Sarah and Chris actually tried to resolve issues with me like adults instead of going behind my back knowing they probably looked foolish the first time Airbnb support took my side when they wanted me to leave. Flagstaff AZ known for its picturesque landscapes and outdoor adventures, became the site of our unforgettable Airbnb nightmare, What was supposed to be a relaxing vacation turned into a series of shocking and distressing events, as we encountered rodents, a filthy grill, and grave safety concerns that left us feeling stranded and unsafe. Upon arriving at the property, our excitement turned into disappointment as we noticed the unkempt exterior. The once charming cabin appeared neglected, with overgrown bushes, and debris scattered around the yard. We hesitated but decided to give it a chance, hoping the inside would be better. Little did we know, the exterior was just a glimpse of what was awaiting us. As we entered the cabin, a musty odor permeated the air, and we immediately spotted evidence of rodent infestation. Dropping littered cabinets, and the unmistakable sounds of scurrying feet echoed in the walls. Alarmed and disgusted, we reached out to the host to address the issue. However, the communication wasn't met with any concern for our safety, and our hopes for a swift resolution faded away. Our kitchen plans quickly crumbled when we ventured to the backyard to find the grill in an appalling state. Layers of grime covered the grates, rendering it unusable, and the prospect of an outdoor barbecue vanished. The most alarming aspect of our stay was the blatant disregard for safety. The missing fire detector was distressing as our minds raced with thoughts of potential disasters. The elevated deck had a broken slat which made it a risk hazard especially at night. With mounting frustrations, we turned to Airbnb for assistance, hoping they would intervene and ensure our safety and comfort. The lack of response from both the host and Airbnb left us feeling helpless and abandoned, trapped in subpar and hazardous environment. Desperate for a resolution, we decided to document the appalling conditions, capturing photographic evidence of the rodent dropping and broken step, missing laundry closet door, as well as missing fire alarm. Armed with these images, we persisted in contacting Airbnb, demanding a full refund and no one should be subjected to these unsafe accommodations. Finally, after several days of persistence, Airbnb responded to our case. Though they expressed regret over our unpleasant experience, their resolution was far from satisfactory. They offered a mere token refund and insisted the responsibility for addresing the safety hazards fell upon the host. Their lack of accountability left us disillusioned and distrustful of the platform, as they failed to uphold their promise of provinding a sae and enjoyable travel experience. In the end, our Airbnb stay in Kachina Village, Flagstaff AZ was nothing short of a nightmare. Rodents, a dirty grill, safety hazards, and unreasonable hosts and platform left us scarred and anxious. Our hope is that by sharing our ordeal, other travelers can be forewarned and encouraged to prioritize safety and thorough research when selecting an Airbnb accommodation. Let this serve as a cautionary tale of he potential pitfalls of vacation rentals, and a reminder to companies like Airbnb to take their guests' safety and well being seriously.

I used to hold Airbnb in high esteem and my husband and I have used them frequently. So when, due to a blatant error on Airbnb’s part, we were left completely stranded in the middle of nowhere Washington on a holiday weekend and having to scramble to find different lodging, we expected this company we held in high esteem to make things right. This was unfortunately far from our experience. Instead of Airbnb covering the cost of our replacement lodging that was booked through Airbnb (an INCREDIBLY fair ask when all the financial costs of the situation are added up), Airbnb blamed the situation on the “host cancellation” (which is NOT what happened, but even if it did, Airbnb should be able to show a shred of care for its loyal customers and step in to make right the situation) and issued a FUTURE coupon for $120 (not even a third of the financial cost we incurred, and we now have to use it on a future booking and can’t even use it to pay for our current damages). Does a future coupon help my situation at all? I had to last minute find new lodging that was 2.5 hours away from my original Airbnb (which I drove 3 hours to get to in the first place). The cost of gas, time, and further gas for the rest of the weekend (which we are now staying 3 hours from our desired location where we had planned all our hikes as all reasonable lodging was sold out). I feel as though I have explained my situation several times only for the “customer service” representative to look back and see where the first representative cancelled the booking, but the host, who no longer has an active account (all of their listings have all the dates blocked out) had no clue we were even coming and had no way to cancel. I spoke directly with the host (in person) who was kind and felt awful for us, and they informed us that Airbnb told them that a cancellation message would be sent to all their bookings when they closed their account several months ago. I know that we must seem to be a small glitch in your software somewhere, but that glitch cost us a lot of money and time—which even though large for us, seems like an easy fix for such a large and successful company. I find it absurd that this company that we have faithfully booked through for years cannot simply make this awful situation right by covering the cost of the lodging we were forced to book last minute on your site. We will be widely sharing this story to our friends and family, warning them of the lack of care Airbnb will offer should ANYTHING happen during their stay. We are sad that this situation has come to this, and we attempted to handle the situation kindly and with respect. Unfortunately, Airbnb has not shown the same back to us.

On the morning of June 13th Aliesha sent us a message informing us our tour would be hosted by Andreas, because she is 7 months pregnant. We booked this tour based on the reviews of her excellent storytelling and that she was a native to Edinburgh. After the rave reviews of Aliesha, we decided on a private tour. Due to our limited time in the city and the short notice provided by Aliesha informing us she was not the one leading our tour until the morning of the tour, we proceed with the guide she provided. Andreas did a good job of following the script of everything on the site but there was no great storytelling experience as the reviews state with Aliesha. The final insult after these comments was receiving her automatically generated letter via Airbnb that begins with “Well I hope that was as much fun for you as it was for me” signed off by Aliesha, Murdoch Tours

Home away from home… Perfect place for someone looking for a simple and peaceful stay, yet with all amenities. Only 10 kms away from Manali, Seema’s place, as I knew from my sister, gave me an experience to carry forever. We spent 6 nights in this fairy tale like wooden loft house hidden inside an apple orchard. From cooking our own food to sharing local recipes, sipping hot cup of tea while completing our daughter’s homework during the day, to chitchatting in the garden, hearing the sound of river Beas go up with sun down….all together was such a blend of our life and nature. What makes this place special are the the warmth and care that Seema, and her husband Subhash ji brings in to their guests. With almost no additional house help, Seema is always on the go to keep her home clean and guests comfortable. Her passion to make her home beautiful and cozy is felt in every corner. The stories of trekking and biking we heard from Seema’s elder son Abhinav (who is currently staying with them) took us to a different world of adventure. Two of the days we mostly spent on the roads - chasing rivers, nature, reaching isolated valleys - and what came in as the biggest surprise was great food being freshly prepared and served by a world experienced Chef! These will all remain with us as a lifetime experience. I have to mention about Chandrataal. The endless off-road and cliff hanging drive, passing through narrow snow cladded lanes, rescuing cars out of swamps, dealing with mountain sickness…everything was worth seeing this hidden paradise. While my sister was the key motivation behind this trek, we realised how deeply committed our hosts were to give us the experience we couldn’t even think of. Chandrataal was a tough, long journey to and fro the same day. Seema’s smile even in the most tensed situation, and Subhash Ji’s level of patience all throughout made our journey more lively, and fun/filled amidst the challenges. I will never forget how Subhash ji carried my daughter on his back for almost the entire trek. The day of check out, as I cleaned the kitchen, wrapped up our clothes last min, and finally started stepping down the uneven stairs that takes a curve below the huge Walnut tree, it felt as if this home was calling me back once again…as if I was leaving a home behind, only to come back soon. It is good people who make good places…and I have seen Seema and her family being a perfect example of it. The emotional connect we made in a week’s time is to remain forever.

I’ve been a host with Airbnb since 2014. I’m a property manager so I run 10-20 properties on their platform at any given time. Secondly, they have blocked a few bookings every year with their ‘algorithm’ which deemed the bookings unsafe. I have been able to verify in person that they were safe, yet Airbnb support was unable to override their algorithm = lost bookings. Thirdly, their new airbnbcover policy, means that guests can submit any false claim about your property and get a refund from their booking. Guests submit evidence to Airbnb about why they want a refund, but Airbnb does not share this evidence with Hosts, nor ask for counter proof from Hosts, they simply refund the guest from the Hosts earnings. I found this a particularly absurd policy when I was told of an insect outbreak in my apartment. I could find none there myself, and Airbnbs policy was not to share any of the evidence the guest provided, so I have yet to know where they were seen and what kind of bug they were. They consider the pictures of bugs in my apartment confidential information belonging to the guest. Seems like important information to share with a Host. So be warned, as a host with Airbnb, you will have no ability to protect yourself from false claims from guests. These are just a few of the things which make me wish I wasn’t attached to the platform. Be warned future Hosts!

Parking The parking lot is not located within the apartment building. You will have to walk about 200 meters to get to it. When we arrived, the designated parking space was already occupied. In the morning, the stairs, elevator, and hallway smelled bad. I suspect that the building has some sewage problems. This did not make for a pleasant stay. Cleaning Even though the hosts charged a cleaning fee, it was the guests' responsibility to sort and dispose of recyclable items and garbage on their own. We had to cross a busy street to reach the recycling bins. Overall, I would not recommend this apartment to anyone who is looking for accessibility or host support. After being on the platform since 2015 and having used them all over the world for bookings; I have now left the platform. They have become just another listing agent and don’t check the quality of the properties and have no user protection. In the early days the platform and accommodation was genuinely nice people that had extra room or places to rent. Now the professional landlords are squeezing every penny out of it with substandard properties with poor customer experience to boot in many cases. The decent landlords will suffer as customers like us will leave in droves! After a particularly bad experience recently we left fact based feedback on the platform. It was the first review we had ever left with negative feedback but we were fair and had written it off as a bad booking with no intention of asking for a refund. The host then clearly complained and the review was taken down with no recourse as a user. The feedback was fact based and balanced; there was some ‘minor wording’ they didn’t seem happy with at Airbnb. It didn’t go against their user policy; although they said it did; I went back to them and said that people are entitled to an opinion as that’s the whole point of a review mechanism, but it really was just a justification to keep the host happy as they were afraid that us reporting on poor soundproofing in the property (where we heard the upstairs flat bathroom visits through the ceiling all night!) and the fact that the smoke alarm had a flat battery keeping me up all night weren’t justified as part of the feedback! I think they are now trying to keep hosts happy and are not thinking that users and people that book need to be happy also. There’s zero help and support and no customer service and no recourse. As an early adopter of the platform am I saddened and disappointed at their approach but good luck in a congested market where VRBO and many others are now in this space. Shame on you Airbnb; I was a hugely happy customer but this one really super small thing and a couple of recent bad experiences mean I have walked away. On another note we booked a property on there recently and then had a landlord cancel as she said she was testing the platform and the property wasn’t even ready. Where’s your regulation Airbnb?

Do you remember how Airbnb helped mediate donations for Ukraine at the beginning of the war? They removed commissions and helped hosts receive donations through their platform. It was a nice gesture, but unfortunately, their actions since then have been a huge disappointment. Instead of supporting hosts with their dwindling income, Airbnb has blocked new listings in Ukraine and delisted apartments in non-occupied parts of the country that are claimed by Russia. It seems like Putin has a say even on territories that are not occupied, such as Zaporizhia. As a host, I have been experiencing the negative impacts of these decisions by Airbnb. Here are some examples: 1. Inability to list new properties: I bought and renovated two apartments in Kyiv downtown and Kharkiv before the war. However, I cannot list either of them as Airbnb always responds with “New listings in Ukraine are blocked.” When I contacted Airbnb support, they cited “sanctions” as the reason. I was confused since Ukraine is not sanctioned, but the support person clarified that it was due to “platform rules”. What rules are these that punish hosts for merely being located in Ukraine? 2. Delisted old properties: My apartment in Zaporizhia, which had good demand during the war from journalists and military personnel, was suddenly delisted by Airbnb after Putin claimed the entire region. Although his army never managed to take the city of Zaporizhia, Airbnb still punished their hosts for having property in the area. How is that helping anyone or keeping Airbnb safe? Aircover doesn’t insure against bombs, only compensating for problems caused by guests or hosts. Therefore, it is irrelevant in this case. These decisions have had a significant impact on hosts like myself. The income that I could have used to support my country's fight against the enemy by donating to volunteers and the military is no longer available. Furthermore, being a “superhost” requires maintaining high ratings, which involves a lot of cleaning, check-ins, and ensuring that guests are satisfied. Although I am grateful to Airbnb for ceasing operations in Russia, I implore them to take action so that Ukrainian hosts can have their income and support their country. Airbnb should re-enable new listings in Ukraine and re-list the delisted properties, just like they did at the beginning of the war when they were helping with donations. PS: If anyone knows anyone who works at Airbnb and can relay this message to the leadership, please spread the word.

Airbnb steals money, hides fees and generally tries to get away with being a decent business. I made a booking and paid the first payment for a full 30 days at a rental property. The amount was €915 per month to the host (I agreed that rate with the host), then airbnb charges a cleaning fee, a service fee and taxes - that they show you, that is all you know about. For each month the cost was €1059.62. I paid that for the first month and reserved the property for several months. Unfortunately, I had to cancel before arriving. Their cancellation policy states that the first 30 nights are non refundable -so I knew that I would lose that first amount I paid. I went to cancel and the screen showed me that I would receive €0 refund, per the cancellation policy. No other information was shown. The screen asked me to continue, so I did. The next screen suddenly showed that the reservation was cancelled and that I was charged to my credit card an additional €539.86. The charge was pushed through on my credit card and sent me over my limit. I was not informed what the charge was for, when I had already paid first 30 days in full. I've been waiting to get a resolution on this and nobody at Airbnb support can tell me when they will be able to give an answer. Also, I talked to the host and she said she will only get paid €915 minus the fees that Airbnb charges her. So the rate she agreed with me, also already included fees that she knew Airbnb would charge her. I was charged a total of €1599.48 when initially airbnb told me I owed €1059.62. The host agreed €915, so that I know of, Airbnb is trying to make out €684.48 on a cancellation without informing of what those charges are. Also that is without taking into consideration the fees Airbnb is charging the host. Also the cancellation was done 24 hours ago and the host is already able to republish the property and get it booked again. I on the other hand, have no resolution from Airbnb as to how they can get away with charging me the additional €539.86 with no explanation, authorization or information. So all in all, they make money by charging fees that are not fully visible to the parties involved, the host and the guest, and with no explanation as to how or why there are those fees. I would NEVER use them again and encourage EVERYONE to think about why not use another service.

They refused to do anything about it, saying I needed to provide a picture of the bug that bit me. WHAT? How is that possible when they bite in the middle of the night and hide all day. Impossible! Then they tried to tell me the bites were from fleas. Not even close to a flea bite. I didn't ask for a refund, only some action taken. I’ve been having Airbnb guests for around four years. On the whole, it’s been a positive experience. I’ve met some lovely people and have never had a bad experience. I am honest in my listing. I won’t let people book without ID or a posted photo. When I have had to contact airbnb, they have on the most part been friendly and helpful. I know there are bad hosts, and reading through the reviews confirms that. However, some guests are a pain in the ass too. A few tips. Read the property description and house rules right through - if you are not sure ask the host to clarify. Don’t arrive with food if a host says there is no kitchen use, and expect an exception to be made. Don’t bring other people or children, if a host says the accommodation is for single people. Leave time for your travel. I know stuff happens, but if you are running late, contact the host. Last of all, hosts provide accommodation not travel insurance - I am glad Airbnb are at last being fair to hosts about this. If you’ve had a bereavement, I’ll offer my condolences but no refund. Same if you are ill, or your train or plane gets cancelled. I’ll tell you to speak to your travel insurance provider. Get travel insurance when you go on holiday, it’s a false economy not to.

Now (14 days later), Airbnb is saying that our situation does not qualify under their cancellation policies for extenuating circumstances. The death of an immediate family member doesn't qualify?! After multiple customer service members over the phone and through messaging told me we would receive a refund. They were all very sympathetic. Now our reservation doesn't qualify for a refund. Someone in the company is not communicating effectively. Don't sit there and tell me I'm sorry for your loss, please provide these documents and we will work with you. Then say nevermind, your circumstance does not qualify under our policy. Suddenly we are referring to your policy. Originally, it was, "let us work with you" . I read and re-read the policy. You know what IS covered? Everything that is convenient and supports the host. A resort at that. Do not say "I'm sorry for the inconvenience", you're not. Do not say, "how can we help?" and " I am here to better support/assist you" when you have no intention of supporting the customer. The death of an immediate family member needs to be covered. How were we supposed to travel when we were trying to process and figure everything out for immediate family? How were we supposed to have a good time on a trip when we were in a state of shock and grief? Explain that Airbnb!!!

When you say that you are a big company, at least on my tiny piece of mind, you need to ACT LIKE IT! My daughter and I were set to stay at a property in Lubbock, TX on New Year’s Eve. When we arrived, the host refused to allow us to stay because I had followed the Airbnb instructions that stated not to include my service animal (small dog, trained to get basic help in case I fall. She has registration docs, and although I’m not legally obligated to provide them, I ALWAYS offer!) in the section asking if I had any pets that would stay with us. I hesitated when filling that out, and ultimately did what the app suggested and left her information out. After the host noticed my dog and rejected our stay, we called Airbnb support, as it was getting late on New Year’s Eve! We were desperate and I wouldn’t allow my daughter to end up sleeping in the car with me. The first support agent was Hazel, one of the Senior Support Ambassadors from the Resolutions team, and she was so incredibly apologetic, understood the situation, and was very upset we’d been turned away, when it’s basically illegal to do so because of a service animal who assists a person with a disability. The agent also understood that we were struggling with funding another property, until the previous funds were reimbursed, which would take some time. She immediately was able to get us a coupon to use for both nights of the 2 night stay, so we could find other accommodations. And, she assisted in that process entirely, and wouldn’t allow us to head out on our own without making 100% sure we had other accommodations. However, nobody was taking reservations so late on New Year’s Eve, so after waiting and waiting and not receiving any confirmations, we were again without shelter. I had to call back, and an agent named John made sure he connected me an actual Host and found a place that would allow us to check in at that late hour. This new property was nearly twice the amount we had paid. He quickly had the coupon amount raised and booked the property. I was crying by then, because I didn’t know there were people left in the world like these agents at Airbnb. They were angels that night—HEROES, SAVIORS! And, not to mention, the hosts of the property, Jaiven and Heidi, a beautiful couple who are so kind-hearted, have messaged me a couple of times checking on us, making sure we settled in and saying they’re sending blessings to us! They sure did! I’ll never forget the way everyone worked together and so hard to make sure my little family had shelter that night AND the next. Not just shelter—a beautiful townhome that was so colorfully, happy, and gorgeously decorated—my daughter and I just smiled at each other when we opened the door to this amazing home. It felt so much LIKE home, too. It became our perfect home away from home. We’ve been staying in hotel after hotel, trying to get relocated from the extremely expensive area of Round Rock, TX. Actually, Hutto, the next town over, east of Round Rock, had been our home for nearly 14 years. During and after the Pandemic, tons of Americans moved into the area, understandably—it’s a great area to raise kids and live in general. But, we could no longer afford the rise in rent and the higher cost of living in OUR OWN hometown. So, we headed north, after doing some research. We are so fortunate to now call Lubbock our home….it truly IS the “friendliest city in America”, and we’ve already felt that first hand here in this little city of OURS. And this Airbnb experience has made it truly a happier relocation for us, when it’s been very stressful and exhausting—everyone has made up for that stress and exhaustion so very much! Thank you to each of our angels that night—a New Year’s Eve we’ll remember forever because of the love we were given by not just one, but at least 5 strangers. That is extremely rare, and we truly felt kindness from them all!

Hosts are allowed to make very strict policies, write misleading posts about their locations, and completely ignore you before, during, and after your stay.
