I am writing this review in full for Atika Villa 11 in Patong- Hosted by John as Airbnb limit characters this a full review couldn't be written. We stayed in this Villa 1 night of a 7-night stay, leaving the next morning and requesting a refund for the remaining nights. The problems with the property were too numerous for us to have confidence that a Host that would put us into such a property could or would make it right. Reasons; 1) the advert for the Villa said we would be met by a Western Host, this was confirmed by text 1-hour before arrival -“we were not”. 2) on arrival the Villa was not clean, 2 of 3 TVs did not work, the interior door handle to bedroom-2 came off in your hand and the exterior door would not lock. 3) The kitchen sink had 5% water pressure and no hot water; this was a major issue for our family that planned to cook and eat-in. 4) The pool had no furniture to use for seating. 5) The upper deck had furniture and no cushions on the premises which made it un-useable. 6) The quality of the Villa was severely over-represented by the advert photos. The Host response was, Quote- “Airbnb know photos can be staged” – There must be a practical line here though, what is staging and what is false representation? These were far more than staging differences. We rented Villa 11 and were put into a property labeled-29/10. The host said this is the postal code, but they rent it as Villa-11. No explanation of why this would not be called Villa 10. Ultimately the Host admitted. Quote- “ We understand the Villa is not the property you wanted and you don’t want stairs and many floors but you will not receive a refund for cancellation for such petty reasons”. For my family, for my 76-year-old mother-in-law, these reasons were not PETTY. Whether we were put in Villa 10 or 11, the property was far from what is represented in the advert. Additionally in Airbnb’s (“What is Expected of Host – Accurate Details” “Be honest about unexpected factors that will impact your guests’ stay. Your guests deserve to know if your neighbors just started a noisy construction project or if they’ll have to climb 8 flights of stairs to get to your place.”) – This Villa was spread across 4-full levels, traveling with our 76-year old mother-in-law, we would have made a different choice had the Host been honest and shared this in “Things to Know” as directed by Airbnb. At some point, the omission of “Key Information” in the property advert is the same as providing “false information”. Obviously, we were very disappointed in this Airbnb rental. We have used Airbnb many times since joining in 2013 and consider ourselves educated consumers, knowing properties are not new or perfect. We will continue to use Airbnb but research Host and ask many more questions. Ultimately Airbnb made this right for which we are thankful though it created a lot of stress that was unnecessary if the Host were more transparent with information and facts.

I've used Airbnb since I was 17. Me and my boyfriend have stayed in approximately 5-6 places. We have had some lovely experiences, but unfortunately we've also had a disproportionately terrible time with 2 of those hosts. I think because we are young, the hosts think they can get away with ridiculous claims against us. October 2018 - we stayed with an extremely anal OCD cleaner. While I appreciate the high standards, they sent a very unexpected message after our stay, which accused us of ridiculous things. For example, we apparently left coffee stains in her fridge, when we never made coffee or even opened the fridge. We apparently made her oven and pans unusable. She was clearly a vegetarian, so I think she didn't like that we cooked meat in her house. At the time, I was only 18. This upset me a lot, as we had made a great effort to leave the place clean. This experience has led me to second guess my judgement; I've become as neurotic as this obsessive cleaner host. October 2022 - This experience made me realise how terrible some Airbnb hosts are, and that my earlier experience was in fact not an anomaly, and not my fault. We booked what we thought was a lovely flat with a sea view. We arrived to a cold, clinical apartment block. I wish it was as clean as a clinical setting, but there was rotting food in the freezer (the freezer wasn't turned on, hence the food could rot), and on the kitchen counter. The place was generally unclean; it needed a sweep everywhere. There seemed to be soil or crumbs on most floors. They had also left their personal items in the flat: damp wet suits in the bedroom, baby wipes and other sanitary products in the tiny bathroom, alcohol in the cupboards. Oh, and they had lied about the sea view. We had a view of a wall. We took photos of the state of the flat and then disposed of the food. It was tolerable. I would have been happy at that point if we had a refund. I looked at the reviews (I wish I had before I went there!) and it seemed as though others had had the same issues. The owner was apparently on a honeymoon, hence they couldn't arrange a cleaner. That is okay - things happen. I understand. But it was what happened next that made me extremely annoyed... ... Due to the ridiculous requirements for a photo on AirBnB, the owner knew we are young. They left a false review on my profile, claiming that I left THEIR place in a mess. The owner seemed generally illiterate, as they sent me messages like "hi are u ok", etc. I bet they thought I wouldn't have had the sense to photograph the state of their apartment. They also seemed too dim to recognise that their reviews showed people had experienced the same issues as we did both BEFORE and AFTER our stay. But hey, we are the cause of their flat being a mess BEFORE we stayed there? I'm really disappointed in the lack of professionalism from Airbnb hosts. They need to do a better job of screening these places. There are some people who are unfit to run a business, such as Karen the cleaner who hates meat eaters, and our illiterate 3-month honeymooner. I'm tired of Airbnb. I'm sick of people who are supposedly adults, twice our age, thinking that they can disrespect us. Airbnb has genuinely had an effect on my mental health, because of these people who want to cover their tracks after receiving a spate of bad reviews. As Airbnb has become as expensive as, or even more so, than hotels in the local area, I will be taking my custom to a -real business- with professionalism. Goodbye Airbnb! Also, we stayed in another place that smelled of mould. Other people said this as well. I didn't complain about it, because the host was so nice. I am a nice and understanding person, unlike your rancid hosts!

She then specifically told me that she can get more than double the price that I paid for the dates that I had booked-- however it was advertised for a specific price and I had already booked, paid and received confirmation of my vacation. The workers will call customers not because anything is wrong but just because they feel like it. I can't imagine having a job where harassment of customers is o.k. Really fed up with airbnb and after using the forum for the last 4 years I've decided I'd rather put my money towards hotels. This a review on our latest booking experience with AirBnb and their appalling behaviour. It’s important to mention that we have booked accommodation using AirBnb before and we had never encountered a situation like this. We booked this place last minute to stay in London for one night before going to the airport the following day. We had communication with the host before arrival asking for an earlier check in as we could not ask for this at the moment of booking (as it was done quite late in the night). The host did contact me later on the day of arrival to say it was possible to check in earlier for an extra fee, but by then we had already decided to wait and to arrive at the scheduled time of check in. On arrival, we entered the place and the first thing we noticed was how dirty it was. Yes, the beds were made with what appeared to be clean bed linen; but unfortunately, that was it. Different areas of the floor throughout the house were dirty, with black soil on them. The skirting boards were all covered in dirt and dust, the kitchen mat was mucky from previous food preparation and the toilet seat was dirty as it had not been properly cleaned, which is shocking. When reading the previous reviews, we saw that cleanliness had been an issue before, but that previous person contacted the host and they cleaned the place for them. Therefore, we were expecting that cleanliness would not be an issue anymore as someone else had already drawn attention to it. After all, the host is offering a service and one of the reasons guests have to check in after a certain time on the day is to provide the host with enough time to make sure everything is ready for the new guests to arrive. We felt it was not fair on us having to ask the host to clean the place properly within the time of our stay as this should have been done before we arrived, so we left the property within less than 20 minutes of arrival. We took pictures of this issue and sent them to AirBnb, claiming a full refund on the paid tariff as we left the house because it was dirty. However, and for our surprise, AirBnb response was quite bad as they washed their hands off and left the issue to be solved by the host, which we find very unfair as we did not book this place with the host directly but using the AirBnb platform instead. In their app (and also in the booking confirmation we received), it can be seen that AirBnB has something they call AirCover, some kind of guarantee in case things go wrong. However, given our experience, this AirBnb cover policy does not seem to protect the guests’ rights but quite the opposite, it seems to protect the host and, probably, AirBnb’s commission. What we cannot understand is the fact this host is classified as a Superhost by AirBnb. We thought AirBnb Superhosts were given this title when they had gone beyond of what it is considered basic, going the extra mile to improve the stay of their guests whilst using their accommodation. Certainly, having a clean space would be part of the minimum requirements to host someone and if this is not met then they should not be described with such a title as it is misleading. I mean, we are clear this is not a five star hotel but at least it should be clean. I have messaged AirBnb several times now and instead of giving a proper response, they just sent this form for us to review the accommodation. Quite appalling, one must admit, as we are still waiting for the refund for this rather bitter experience. I do not think we will be using AirBnb in the future anymore, which is a real shame as I have used them in different countries over the past seven years and it’s always a nice way to meet new people and other cultures, but if they are not going to protect the travellers when things go wrong, we prefer to steer away from such a company.

Hosts can DOUBLE your price on a confirmed and pre-paid booking! We learned about this the hard way, and the best you can hope for is a full refund from AirBnB if you know how to "play the game". The way it works is that the host will "REQUEST" that you accept a new price change. If you accept it and pay it, then everything continues as expected. However if you DECLINE the offer, they may create a 2nd lower offer, which again you can decline. By the time you get to the end of this game the Host will probably ask YOU to cancel the booking. DO NOT DO THAT. If you cancel it, you can't post a bad review, and you probably won't get a full refund. If THEY cancel it, you will get 100% refund. Plus they will have to pay a fine to AirBnB for 10% to 50% of the booking value, plus they get an automatic negative posting for cancellation after their next quarterly review, plus their calendar will be frozen for bookings during your time slot for a while. Needless to say, they will try various tactics to get YOU to cancel, but don't do that. If the disagreement continues you can get AirBnB to force the host to cancel, by simply saying "you are very uncomfortable with the new relationship" with the host.

I also had good experiences with AirBnB as a tenant, until now. The incompetent role of the resolution centre in a dispute made me cancel my registration. As a tenant, I was held liable for defects I had not caused and AirBnB decided in favour of the plaintiff: this is how you are outlawed as a tenant. Below is the case. At my last stay, there was a dispute with the landlord about who was ultimately responsible for the final cleaning. She then comes up with a declaration of maintenance costs for defects of which I was unaware. I refuse to pay and the landlord calls in the help of AirBnB resolution centre for mediation. The latter "vindicates" the landlord on the basis of photos, the invoice and that she had submitted the claim in time. However, the landlord could not prove that there was a direct causal relationship between the defects and our stay; it was overdue maintenance that was claimed from us and to my amazement AirBnB went along with her claim. The adage "he who claims must prove" was not applied. For me, renting via AirBnB is becoming too big a risk, because if a landlord gets his right by sending only photos and an invoice of repair costs; as a tenant you can hardly defend yourself against that.

When I booked a rental home with Air Bnb it states "entire home" in the listing title. Come to find out that we only get half of the home and have to share the pool and hot tub with renters who rent the other half. I would be okay with this if I wasn't tricked by the misleading "entire home" in the listing. I requested a refund because I felt tricked but they will not because they state that it says "ADDT’L ACCOMMODATIONS: An additional 1-bedroom property for 6 guests is available on-site with a separate nightly rate. I will never rent with them again.

Airbnb customer service seems to have 2 modes: do nothing at all or take on a parental role and start doing all sorts of things you never asked for / wanted without checking in with you first. Airbnb is great when is great but the absolute worst when you need any assistance at all. Not to mention they allow some hosts to have no contact info listed so that you have to contact them through Airbnb and wait hours upon hours for any response, no matter how urgent the problem is. There are 2 memorable times when we needed assistance this year - the first, some guy was screaming his head off in the hotel room next to ours between 1 am and 3 am and Airbnb did absolutely nothing. We contacted the host through the app seeing that there was no other way to do so (they had no front desk attendant, the security guard seemed to have left, no number listed on Airbnb or online anywhere) but only got a response 1 hour before we were due to checkout anyway. Did Airbnb give us as much as a discount voucher for the sleepless night? Nope! The most recent time was when I contacted them to ask for advice on how to handle a rather awkward situation in a shared accommodation and instead of actually talking to me about it, they asked me for photographic proof (which I did not have since I don’t go around documenting every disgusting mess other Airbnb guests leave around) and kept passing my case along to different representatives while seemly doing nothing, only for me to get a message from the host that they had been contacted to issue a refund, citing the issues I had at the place - which I had never asked Airbnb to do - and Airbnb only notified me they started mediation after they had already contacted the host. Absolutely no concern for how it would affect me. All I wanted was to know the protocol in the event of unresolved problems and maybe get some advice, but they went and started a whole thing without my consent making a bad situation worse. Again, great when everything is going well but should you have a problem, I wish you luck. They either don’t care or, when they “seem to care”, they don’t involve you in decisions and are as discreet as a car with a broken muffler because their customer service reps are not interested in actually helping customers (neither hosts nor guests) - they just want to close every single ticket as fast as possible, regardless of the situation being resolved. I literally lost track of how many times the person assigned to me brought up closing the ticket but he was way more worried with that than with the issue at hand
My car got vandalized at Airbnb host garage but the Airbnb owner refused to give me host insurance information showing Airbnb are scammers!

Customer Service that agrees with the issue but can't do anything to help! I had a guest living at my place for 3 months. He was very rude and verbally aggressive towards me. He finally said he wanted to move out if he could get the money back and I wanted him to leave as well since I didn't feel safe in my own home anymore. I am considering closing down my account because of this.

Booked a beautiful modern apartment in Bedford UK for a visit from Australia, Through Claire Walton, I continually asked for the lockbox access code, only to be advised less than 24 hours of our arrival that the boiler had been condemned and we couldn’t use the accomodation, we were offered another apartment which we assumed would be to the same standard, how wrong we were, it was really dirty, extremely low standard dirty furnishings, above a cafe that played loud music everyday, many very large fly filled rubbish bins that we needed to walk past each time we left or arrived back, cigarette buts by the front door & piles of rubbish. The bins were emptied around 5.30am which woke us, 2 public houses across the road which had deliveries around 6am which were also noisy. All in all a very unpleasant stay. I have not named the letting agent as don’t wish to embarrass them, maybe I should? I have photographic evidence of my complaint. I contacted Airbnb & the agent who asked how they could help rectify the issue, I asked for a refund. Airbnb have now decided that we are not entitled to anything. Whilst we understand that things happen. If you book and pay for 5 star accomodation you don’t expect to receive 1 star accomodation. Shame on you Airbnb for this horrible experience.

AirBnb was very helpful, accountable and trustworthy. I’m so used to companies not caring about excellent customer service these days, but they went over and behind for me. I appreciate this company excellence.

We booked a house in Long Island called the Good Vibez house. The pictures looked fantastic. That's where the good bits end. Interestingly, the hosts requested to see pictures of people that would be staying in the house....hmmm. 2 days before we were due to check-in AirBnB sent me an email cancelling the booking & informed me that we would be refunded in full within 14 days. When I tried to contact them thro' my account, I found that I was locked out of the account "for security reasons". I got no satisfaction when I tried ringing them to try & re-arrange accommodation. I then discovered that they had billed me twice for bookings that had nothing to do with me. I now was due monies back of over €4500 & I was struggling to arrange accommodation on the 4th July weekend. Our holiday was a disaster for that week as we were trying to manage our credit card limit. We ended up staying in a hotel & had to eat out which can be very expensive for a family of 5. All together it cost us over €2000 more than we had bargained for. It took a month to get all the monies back. When I contacted Customer Service to get compensation, it went around & around. When I asked for explanation as to why the booking was cancelled I was told it was for "security reasons". I have no doubt that I was gazumped as either AirBnB or the Hosts had the property listed on another website & had got a significantly better price. They were trying to wear me down. Eventually I was offered $688 dollars against any future house booked on AirBnB. Given that I had already spend the money this was a cheap shot. When I contacted them again, explaining that I'm already at a financial loss, I was then offered $200...!! At the moment I'm considering my options. I will however never ever use these shower of morons again.

We had an argument with the host 1 month before the stay. He went to personalities right from the start. After that, I wanted all my money back since I would never want to meet him nor sleep in his apartment. I contacted Airbnb. Airbnb said that they could do nothing except that to ask from the host that would he be willing to give all the money back. The host of course didn't accept. After waiting for 2 weeks, I decided to accept the loss and get at least half of the money (600€ of 1200€) back by canceling the reservation myself. After that, the host sent me a message where he thanks me for giving him money for doing nothing, and told me to go see a psychiatrist. I am shocked of how bad the customer service is at airbnb, and I will never use it again.

Awful experience. My guest stolen from me 2 days ago. I am still awaing a call from the super specialised team that deals with this situations!! I would have been better not reporting anything

Airbnb’s review policy is just for show. I recently learned that although there is a public review policy posted on their website, the actual policy is internal and governed by undisclosed internal matrixes and policies. A guest recent spent 40% of their review slagging my property about an unexpected hydro outage that lasted a whopping hour and a 1/2. The policy states review must be relevant and not based on circumstances outside of another’s control. I have tried reasoning with them a dozen times. When you contact Airbnb you get a series of canned responses, when you finally get through to a person their position is to do nothing citing the secret internal policies. It’s a breach of contract and I will have to take legal action to rectify. They also have a host referral bonus, a friend suggested I sign up, I did, informed them and they never paid her. I’ve been using the service for 10 months now so I think a reasonable amount of time has passed so that payment should have been made. We also use VRBO, by comparison, the guests that come from VRBO are clean, quiet, mature, and respectful. They stay for longer periods and tend to be a little older. Most of the guests that book with us through this platform are property owners, so understand how to look after you place. Airbnb renters are demographically very young, most have been good but any time there has been a problem: property damage, noise, filth, rule breaking, overstaying, or poor behaviour it has been their guests. Unfortunately, you’re in a position where you can’t say anything unless you want to be punished via the review process - this is true of both platforms.

We've been on a road trip for a year and a half, staying in Airbnb's the entire time. It had been a wonderful experience until we got to Louisville, KY. There, our house: had an ant infestation all over the kitchen, had rats, had a neighboring tenant who let their dogs poop all over the yard without cleaning it up, and worst of all, the host GAVE OUR LOCK CODE to a COMPLETE STRANGER. We woke up one day to a man in our living room saying "hello?" Per Airbnb's policy, we tried to work with the host to resolve these issues. She promised us a refund, promised and promised and said she had our back. Then, we checked out, still hadn't heard. Posted our truthful, negative review that was 100% within posting guidelines, and in response got a message from the host explicitly saying she'd not give us any refund as retaliation. Then we involved Airbnb. They penalized us for following their policy and working with the host—said we should have moved out immediately, though we had nowhere to go. Said we should have involved them sooner, though there was no option to do so until the host refused us. Offered $28 refund for a month-long stay, and then closed the case saying there was no further appeals process. Worst of all, they removed my review, won't tell me why, so now the host has no negative consequences whatsoever and future guests will likely have the same issues. Airbnb does not care about the health or safety of their guests who trust the Airbnb brand to help them in bad situations against a complete stranger of a host. I'd been a loyal customer for years, and I'll never use them again. I realize Airbnb does not care, but at least they won't ever get another one of the pennies I actually work hard for.
We as neighbours complained about the noise from an Airbnb flat on our street (Marjorie Grove, SW11) and the Airbnb representatives could not care less.

I rented a house for a week with my two special needs sons, husband, dog, and my mom. We checked out and received a damage claim of almost $500. The hosts said my dog scratched their sliding glass shower door and knocked it off track. We took my dog everywhere we went and certainly didn't lock him in the bathroom. The kids left a small stain on sheets (had an accident) and there was a small stain the rug. I didn't think much of it as we were getting everything to leave by the 10am check out because it could easily be washed out with carpet cleaner and bleach. I was charged $300 for sheets, $110 for a new rug, and $50 for the shower door. Airbnb accepted all of these charges just because a "receipt" was provided. In their terms and conditions, hosts are reimbursed for the cheaper option between repairing and replacing. No way there was $300 sheets in a kids room and no way it cost that amount to launder. They likely charged us the entire laundering bill for their rentals. The "receipt" was a screenshot of their budget tracker. We asked for an itemized receipt and airbnb said no. For the rug, it was a poop stain. Anyone who has a dog has cleaned poop stains out of carpet no problem but we were charged for a brand new rug. For the shower door, we didn't do anything to that door but were told to somehow prove we didn't do anything. Insane. It's one thing to charge us for the laundering fee to remove the stain (not to wash, which is normal maintenance for a host but the extra effort/fee for removing stains), but for airbnb to just accept damage claims without any due diligence and then refuse to consider anything else because they've already paid out the host under their "aircover guarantee" is terrifying. I will NEVER use this company again.

Worst experience I have ever had! First time using airbnb. I booked two houses for our family vacation from Germany to California. Paid the first half up front. I can only advise you to stay away from this company and the poor service that they give!!!

Outrageous review policy Left an honest 2 star review about my inadequate accommodation, only to have it removed for "violating Airbnb's terms". Can totally recommend staying at Airbnb

Still disputing this and place partial blame on Airbnb for letting hosts use their platform to rip people off.

We booked a house in Chester through Airbnb not realising it wasn’t an individuals house but a letting company called Noki. After booking Noki said we needed to sign a long contract. Airbnb have only just messaged me 5 months after complaint to say they won’t be posting my review on Noki !

Booked apartment 29th of March 2022. Was canceled 30 minutes before our arrival in Reading Friday 19th of august 2022, after traveling from Norway. At least not for a long time. Absolutely horrific customer treatment.

My experience was at Serafin Amestates in the Las Congrejas in Cabo San Lucas. Sergio is the guys name. He promised me my $850 security deposit back, Never saw it. He claimed I signed a contract. I suffered for one month with a drunk grifter I shared a kitchen and terrace with. I provided both my host AND AirB&B with video of her falling down drunk and peeing on the terrace. After multiple pleadings, nothing was done to stop this disgusting behavior. I wanted to leave but was refused. And the stray dogs…..unbelievable. I had to carry pepper spray and a large stick to protect my dog and me. Dog poo everywhere, stepping in new piles almost daily but was told I had to pick my small dogs poo up and place it in the container. Sent photos of unbelievable amounts of stray dog poo to AirB&B. Nobody cared. And the constant barking at night was unbelievable. I arrived in July to 100 degree weather and no functional air conditioner. No help from AirB&B. Don’t use 3rd parties for vacation rentals. Please don’t. There are plenty of home owners that will work with you individually. Do that. Please.

BED BUG ALERT I found bed bugs at the property I rented through AirBnB and had to arrange last minute accommodations to stay somewhere else. Neither the host nor AirBnB was willing to offer a refund. I guess they consider bed bugs a reasonable amenity for listings on their website. Disgusting! I will be using Vacasa from now on.

Four separate calls to four separate agents regarding the same issue resolved nothing. Another company ought to start up. They could easily offer improved service and compete with airbnb. It's been a misreable experience and unnecessary financial loss.

After years of using airbnb successfully and staying in lovely places with great people, I didn't believe all the bad press you hear and was reassured by their blurb about protecting everyone's safety. Then I was attacked by a dog on an airbnb stay and received zero help from airbnb, in fact they made the whole situation worse. I phoned and asked them for help with rebooking, no response for 3h, phoned and texted and raised requests through the app. They got back to me after midnight by which time I'd booked myself into a hotel. The only contact was with a woman via the chat which was unclear and misleading. They made requesting the payment for medical expenses back impossible, even though the owner had immediately agreed to pay. She insisted on paying outwith the app, and I eventually gave her my PayPal address as airbnb were being so obstructive. I phone again and again and am always told the call handler can't deal with that and someone will call me back in 24h. It's been 2 weeks, I've called 6 times, no one has ever called me back. They did send me an email addressed to the host to claim back from the insurance, I replied to say I was the guest and have heard nothing again. I will never use them again and would urge everyone to avoid them. Their rating system is biased towards higher reviews - I rated the host 1 star, she had 6 reviews and went from 4.8 to 4.2. There are absolutely no safety checks or action taken if they endanger a guest.

Used to be a rental from owners, it became a booking system for hotels, where you book a "type" sort of accomodation, and you get sonething totally different that don't match neither the description nor the advertised pics.

Customer service is absolutely horrible. I stayed in one broad and had a bar located right below the apartment. The noise level was unbelievable: the floors, the walls and furniture were shaking in the apartment until 5AM daily. The apartment filled up with smoke during those times. I stayed with a minor and had to move out 4 days earlier. The host ghosted me and Airbnb customer service was no where to be found. Airbnb finally got back to me 3 days later and kept bouncing my case from person to person. They ended up declining my offer for a refund of unused funds because they claimed that the host disclosed it in the posting (but only partially). The host's post said there was a bar below that operated on weekends until 3AM. No mentioning weekdays or that this place has such enormous noise levels that you can't do anything there other than party every day until 5AM. Also, no mentioning of the smoke. Airbnb made me sound like I was crazy in asking for a refund for unused nights. Customer service was very preferential towards the host. Seems like a very transactional business model. I will never stay at an Airbnb again. I mean it.
Shocking. Paid £10,000 for a villa with no smoke alarm, no aircon and 8km further away from the town than advertised. Contacted Airbnb who ignored me. Save your money and book on a random website!

Honestly, I'd give less stars if I could. Have used Airbnb for a long time, but it has gone downhill in the last few years. Most recently, I stayed in a house in Copenhagen with my family and the host kept piling on unexpected fees. The final straw was when they accused us of stealing a bread knife (how would we have even got it home on our hand luggage only flight?!) and Airbnb took her side. the house had so much cutlery that we probably didn't put it all back in the right place, so the knife is there, she just hasn't looked properly. They gave us 72 hours to respond, which is ridiculous, and completely impractical when you have young children. They have now decided to ban my account, despite having no evidence that I've done anything wrong. Just don't bother. It's ruining local areas - go with a hotel instead.

The flat we were going to stay at didn't exist. It was a fake listing. So after a long flight, we were stuck on the pavement and in coffee shops frantically looking for new places. Despite us doing everything we needed to and them failing to verify the house actually existed. It's the 21st Century, make the hosts do a video call and show you their id documents before you let hustlers register fake houses on your site. Come on.

I had a horrible experience, I was placed in the main street for a sex business in Izmir in Alsancak 1463., I have all the evidence from photos to video recordings and everything that was written to me regarding the refund which is over 1200 Euro. The host immediately rented out her apartment, she reimbursed the money quickly Airbnb does not protect guests at all, what kind of frivolity is this??? I will take legal action because they keep escalating it to the next team: Scarlett, William Rachel, Apple... and it's been like this for almost two months

AIRBNB does not deserve any stars. They are the most unprofessional Rip off company I have ever dealt with. My family of 8 booked villa in Antigua . We also contacted AirBNB Within the policy they should have refunded our money . We were left stranded...trying to survive that night as the villa was so disgusting. You cannot speak to anyone. We fought to get our refund from both host and AirBNB for many months without any luck. It has been so stressful! These people do not care about their clients. I will never ever book with them again.

I had issues with my rental. Turns out that the property is managed by another company and not directly by the host. I complained and I got a minor refund; however, I won’t ever use Airbnb again. They only care about the host and not the person who is paying. Shameful.
Easy to book, sometimes cheaper than Hotels. Some issues arise every now and then but are usually host relates and fixed quickly.

I got in touch with Airbnb, asking for assistance with the issue i faced. Issue being, i contacted a host regarding the distance between their property and the airport. On arrival we were shown around the apartment at lightning speed which was fine. We were given a range of instructions - including what we could and could not put down the toilet, don't get the bed sheets dirty and you don't really need the AC - opening a window will do. Not what you want to hear in Rome in July in the midst of a heatwave. It was only after the host had left us to it, did the extent of the problems come to light. However, we stopped cleansing when we saw the state of the other utensils and pans. Most had congealed food residue stuck to them and there was evidence of the previous occupants food in the oven. The cooker hood was caked in grease, with rather a lot of dust clinging to it. The splash back also had a coating of grease. The cupboard containing the pans had what can only be described as a 'unique' odour. It certainly wasn't pleasant. The other notable feature of the kitchen was the window that couldn't be closed. This opened onto a stairwell and courtyard, allowing hot air to stream into the kitchen. There was a lattice grill 'window' between the kitchen and the lounge which allowed the hot air front the courtyard to enter the lounge via the kitchen. Lounge This was a decent space with very nice cotto tiles. However, the AC unit - as pointed out by the host, was partly broken and was clearly well past its best. Aside from the fact that it could not cope, it was also incredibly noisy. Bedroom. The bed was fine and the linen was clean. However, the second AC unit was almost as bad as the first, so a decent nights sleep was pretty much impossible. So, we stayed one night as we had little option. We contacted Airbnb support the following day. We did speak to someone who said 'someone would call back urgently'. In the meantime, I sent a set of photographs detailing the problems. The promised phone call never materialised and any other contact I initiated was left unanswered. Given that the apartment failed to meet Airbnb's own 'Reliability Standards' it was a reasonable expectation that it would act swiftly and at the very least provide us with alternative accommodation. I did check and there was plenty available on Airbnb..... Due to their total lack of action, we were compelled to stay a second night. The following day, we'd had enough and we moved into a hotel. After a few days (and quite a few messages sent) we still had heard nothing from Airbnb. So, I posted a few photo's on their Facebook page and on my own page tagging Airbnb. Incredibly, BOTH posts were deleted. Following this, someone did make contact and I did get a refund barring the two nights we had stayed. After some arguing, they did also give me a 20% reduction for each night we stayed. What I find most shocking, is the complete lack of support or care from Airbnb. So, never again.

I’ve been using Airbnb for 8 years now. I swear there is a trend (USA only) of raising the cleaning rates while at the same time increasing the amount of “chores” the guest must do. On top of that, in spite of cleaning fees up to $100, I’ve arrived at places to find hair in bedsheets, garbage in trash cans, dried food on kitchen appliances, etc. I used to be a motel maid and I am very respectful of the profession, so I try to reduce their load when I can. However, being charged 30, 50, 80, even 100 dollars as a cleaning fee and then being told I am required to strip beds, tote trash out to a dumpster, and “leave the place exactly as I found it” seems insulting. (I’ve also been asked at several different places to gather all towels and sheets and put them in the washing machine and start a load.) At first I was delighted to find Airbnb as a wonderful alternative to hotels and motels. It became even more attractive during the pandemic. However, as a senior citizen, I’m starting to miss my hotel/motel days when I was treated as a true guest- no chores to do on my vacation. Airbnb is no longer always a cheaper alternative. These days, with rising extra fees (again, USA only) hotels are often now cheaper, with free breakfast and 24-hour cancellation policies to boot. These increasing cleaning fees and their accompanying chore requirements are tipping me back towards traditional lodging, and I have many friends who feel the same way. I know guests can always complain to Airbnb with concerns about cleanliness or unfairness, but then we risk getting bad reviews – another thing you don’t have to worry about when staying at a hotel. One place I recently stayed in San Francisco was dirty, had a $100 cleaning fee, and required that I go through the house upon check-in and make a list of any and all damage because if I did not report the damage, my credit card would be charged. I stressfully went through the house for an hour documenting cracks in windows, stains on walls, dings in appliances, and scrapes on doors, fearing they would try to charge my credit card for pre-existing damage. For each of those items, the host replied “Oh, those were already there.” Why put a guest to that much work and stress worrying that they missed some piece of damage? Shouldn’t be up to the host in that case to provide a list of pre-existing damage so the guest doesn’t have to do all that documenting? Ridiculous. I hope Airbnb will take this to heart as something that I know concerns more guests than I and will start advocating for reasonable (or even zero) cleaning fees, and get rid of laundry and trash collection chores for guests. Or at LEAST make it either/or. All of that being said, I typically have good experiences with most properties ( other than the fees and chores) and I have had prompt refunds in a couple instances where things went wrong.

Had an account breached and hacked, and the perpetrator has changed everything in it - phone number, name, added two factor authentication, and even added a fake property for who knows what. I have tried to contact them regarding this matter, but in order to write an email or open a support ticket, you have to be logged in... Well, in order to be logged in, I had to change the password.... But for that, I needed to get through two factor authentication, which was impossible. Thus, there is absolutely definitely no way to contact them via email or support tickets when the breach happens, and only via Facebook. Now, this enough is a proof that Airbnb does not have a sufficient fail-saves when the account is breached, and it completely locks you out to contact via an email. BUT THERE IS MORE. Airbnb has sent a recovery form-submission, and I have managed to regain access to account and check all of the information there, update it, change two factor authentication, remove all of the perpetrators data, and I thought that was it. BUT NO, IT WAS BREACHED AGAIN, AFTER TWO HOURS OF RECOVERING. My questions is HOW? I have checked every corner of viruses and emails redirecting somewhere from my accounts - nothing to be found on my end. I have scanned even the whole network, but nothing was found. But the perpetrator HAS REGAINED ACCESS to my account somehow, even if I have changed all the perpetrator's data! Finally, the account was deleted... Not because of my messages that the account was breached or my contacting, but because the perpetrator listed another fake property. Not because of my concerns, but FOR FALSE PROPERTY. WHICH THEY FAILED AT THE FIRST TIME TO REGISTER. To sum up, Airbnb is nothing more than a cybersecurity black-hole of issues. No fail-saves, no ways to urgently contact from European Union, no email addresses to write to, only a Facebook page. And if your account is breached, good luck to recover it, 'cause IT IS ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE. And being an IT technician, I have NEVER EVER experienced such security issues. TL;DR: No proper cybersecurity, huge chance of getting account stolen after recovery. The worst security practices and issues I've ever saw as IT technician.

After getting nowhere with Customer Support I finally had to find and book new accommodations and pay for a second booking while hoping AirBnb would refund the money for my canceled stay "within 10 business days". Unfortunately, by the time all this was settled, it was almost 9:00pm and too late to check into the NEW listing I just booked. I didn't know that Hosts have 24 hours to confirm and accept even for a reservation paid for on the first day!!?? (Beware of this if you need quick accommodations through the AirBnB). Also keep in mind that even though their website WILL LET YOU PAY for a booking right up until midnight, it's a gamble as to whether the Host will contact you to provide check- in instructions (I'm still waiting for my refund for the first night). I ended up in a hotel through another service for the first night (additional costs I'll never get back). Also be aware that the so-called AirCover "protection" listed on the site really does nothing. While the "Booking Protection Guarantee" states that "we'll find you a similar or better home...", what really happens is that the support team just tells you to look in the area and offers you a discount. My discount ended up being 20% off of the ORIGINAL booking price and even that took two hours to "confirm with a supervisor". I had booked the original stay over 6 months prior and now needed immediate weekend accommodations, so I was looking at twice the cost of my original booking in places half as nice - so you can imagine how useless that "20% of original booking" discount was. In addition to providing no actual help, the Support Team will try to get you off the phone as quickly as possible by promising to call you back. This "call back promise” is a complete lie. I never received a single call back throughout the entire five-hour rebooking nightmare. I had to call back four times and a NEW "specialist" every time. When I complained about no call backs, the support team told me I had to be patient since it was a holiday weekend and they were short staffed: the irony that I was STUCK on a holiday weekend, in a foreign country, and was about pay premium, last-minute prices for new booking was apparently lost on them. Keep in mind that ALL of this could have been avoided had an AirBnB Specialist simply reached out to me at any time between June 30 (the day they were notified that my booking was cancelled) and morning of July 5 (the check-in day and time that I was still in the States with cell and Internet service and could have found something else). AirBnB may work for some, but the complete lack of any real Corporate policies to assist customers and the company’s willingness to leave people stranded and potentially in danger is not worth the risk in my opinion.

Don’t be a Host on Airbnb Airbnb would be nothing without Hosts. Yes, guests are just as important, but even if there were no Guests, they still need Hosts to provide the product. Yet, Airbnb treat Hosts as disposable. They make it challenging to deal with their customer service. And they always side with Guests in a dispute. I’ve been a Host for 9 months with two listings and made a considerable amount of money in that time. It started out very smooth and the bookings were pouring in as well as the five star reviews. But I soon started to notice a lack of support they give to Hosts. We’ve had situations where guests have written false reviews, which we’ve proven with evidence, yet they refuse bluntly to take them down. There have been times when they’ve double charged guests, yet we’ve only (and correctly) received one payment - but when the Guests complained to Airbnb, they deducted money from our future payout, assuming it’s our fault, and it’s almost impossible to fix via their convoluted ‘support’ services. Their COVID policy is a joke. As a Guest, if you book a non-refundable room, you can easily get a refund by sending them an image of a lateral flow test from Google - this happened to us, and Airbnb deducted the money from our payout. When we proved it by showing them the search results they simply sent a link to their COVID policy with no attempt to assist. They sided with a Guest who complained directly to Airbnb at 3am there was a small spider on the wall. Seriously! And Airbnb agreed this was cause for them to receive a full refund. These guests still stayed until the final moment before check-out, used all our facilities, and also enjoyed the hot drinks, milk and breakfast we provided. Again, when we challenged this, Airbnb simply sent a link to their policy. Another time Airbnb messed up by allowing a Guest to book outside of our schedule. The Guest sadly turned up and couldn’t be accommodated. Although Airbnb agreed the error was theirs and sorted the refund, it was such hard work trying to contact them, explain and sort this out. This are just a FEW of the issues I’ve experienced over the past 9 months. So, although the money has been great, I have now removed both my listings as I don’t think it justifies the hassle, especially when I have a job and family to look after. What Airbnb claim is simple and easy, with support, it’s actually been anything but. And it certainly leaves me feeling Airbnb are very arrogant and would rather protect the paying Guests and themselves over the Host, and at all costs. I’m sure there are other Hosts who will be singing Airbnb’s praises. And perhaps I’ve had bad luck. But this is my personal experience and it seems to be a trend after seeing so many similar experiences on this platform.

I planned a week long trip with my 19 yr old in Tennessee. We drove from Wisconsin to Tennessee on May 21, 2022. Checked in late in the evening just before sundown. Cabin appeared clean and as described, we were thrilled! Due to my medical condition, we stayed in the cabin the next day, all day, watching movies and resting. I stepped outside a few times to sit on the deck but otherwise, we had an inside day which we planned for. That night, it began to storm and rained hard into, and throughout the next day. So we made the best of it, happy to just be relaxing. About noon on that day, my daughter showed me big bites emerging on her arms and legs. Some were in clusters, some were in lines. They were intensely itchy, and definitely not mosquito bites. We searched around the cabin, and upstairs in the loft where her bed was and found nothing. The day wore on and we turned in around midnight. About 10 minutes after going to bed, I heard my daughter say, hey, something is moving on me! I went upstairs, we threw the covers back, and we saw little tiny bugs moving around. The lighting was poor in all the cabin except for the bathroom, but we took photos and I contacted the host, including photos. I moved my daughter downstairs to the couch. In the morning, the host contacted me and seemed very concerned, offered to do whatever I wanted. She had another cabin next door however, at this point, my daughter was so uncomfortable and upset and just wanted to go home. Since it was a 12 hr drive, and she wasn't budging, I finally made the call to end the trip. We packed up and left. Out of paying $1382 for the week, I originally asked for $900 refund. They provided $700. And a $400 coupon for another stay. I did not want the coupon because my experience was awful and I would not use them again. After leaving, the host began making up conversations that never occurred (all communications were via text), asserting we had stayed in other locations prior to arriving (I have gas receipts indicating my travel from home to her cabin in one day) and getting incredibly nasty. So much for all the crosses and Christian related decor... I submitted for full reimbursement for the entire debacle, including my ruined vacation and cleanup afterwards. My luggage is still sitting in bags in the garage because I'm nervous to bring anything into the house. Airbnb states they fulfilled their contract by the refund provided. I've since noticed they do not put negative reviews for hosts up (I left one), nor can you review them in many places. This is a buyer beware business!!

Airbnb took our savings, from our years-long dreamed family trip to take my grandmother to see Paris for the first time on her 80-year-old birthday. We chose an apartment we could afford in Paris, a small but cozy one, and reserved it, for around 1000EUR. This is a lot of money, around six months of minimum wage where we come from in Latin America. My mom, my sister and I contributed: it was, after all, my grandmother's lifelong dream and, on a budget, with Airbnbs and a flight sale, we would be able to achieve it. Then COVID-19 hit hard. Airbnb denied the full refund for the booking, which we wanted, but would give us a coupon instead. Without options, we took it. Then the coupon was about to expire amidst the crisis...Nothing to do, the prices had skyrocketed by then. We booked a new apartment and told the owner the dates should be flexible, as the world remained uncertain. He agreed. Another 1000EUR for the new apartment. 2000 EUR is a year of salary now, amidst the crisis. It was so much money, but we did not have options other than losing the already paid 1000EUR (exactly 966EUR). The dates of the booking kept changing, as COVID-19 continued to create havoc. At some point, the host decided to change the reservation dates, as agreed, but instead of what we agreed by message, that is, to keep the dates as so to keep the same value of the booking, he changed it in a way that he would make even more money (around 50EUR extra). At this point, any foreseeable trip was unthinkable, COVID-19 seemed determined to stay. I then wrote to Airbnb explaining I wanted to keep the reservation, but not pay MORE money for a trip that looked more and more improbable. I was willing to reserve it for one less day, for not to have to pay any extra but keep the booking, even if that would mean losing some money on my end. They dismissed the text completely and answer "pay or you lose the reservation". Then I got an email, saying that the COVID-19 related coupons would be extended throughout 2022. Okay, if this was so, we could get a refund of the money we had paid in the second time (1000EUR) and still use our 1000EUR, as per their policy, throughout 2022. So today, in May 2022, as my family is fully vaccinated, I went to get the coupon. For my total surprise, it is not there. I wrote to Airbnb. Again, dismissive, again, without any attention to the individual case, they said "the coupon expired", even though the policy of extension is clear and automatic. They took 966EUR from us, a Latin family trying to make good to our grandmother. And they just took it. They sent emails with lying policies, tried to take more and more money from the reservation and finally scammed us. A company that took money in this shameless way, that knows no accountability and no customer support is truly tragic. I have no words to describe the hassle, the pain, the despair this company has put us through as they took so much of our money and as we need to tell my grandmother she still, with the pandemic over, doesn't get to see Paris in this lifetime, as Airbnb took our accommodation money after sending us policies and promises that they would not. Before that experience, I was a regular Airbnb customer, having traveled with them without issues for another nine times. They made me loyal, and then took all they could from my family. I truly and utterly regret having ever used this platform and once recommended it to friends. Please be cautious.

I left a negative but calm, entirely factually, and completely judicious review of a bad experience with a Lisbon Airbnb this past Monday, then woke this morning to an email from Airbnb telling me that they had removed my review for violating "community standards,” but offering no explanation. Several hours and phone calls with supervisors (Harish) and their “special team” (led by Chirag) later, Chirag informed me that Airbnb’s verdict stood: that I had violated their community standards. When I asked for specifics, Chirag named the following three baffling “examples,” then told me, when I offered to submit a review that took out all three mentions, that I could not submit a revised review. So, there is no record of my bad experience at the listing. 1) The team construed my mentioning that the host tried to keep me from turning the fan she loaned me on anything other than low as “circumstances beyond her control” because there was a heat wave. (Don’t ask: it makes no sense.) 2) The team said I had violated community standards by mentioning that “I have shared space with over three dozen Airbnb hosts in cities ranging from London, Rome, Florence, and Naples to Barcelona, Madrid, Seville, Córdoba, and Mexico City in the past few years.” (Don’t ask: it makes no sense.) 3) The team construed my mentioning that the host’s boyfriend stayed over twice in my first 4 days in the small apartment, that I hadn’t expected him to be there at all, and that I first ran into him in the wee hours of the morning when I got up to use the bathroom as a violation because it referred to host’s “personal life or political views.” (Don’t ask: it makes no sense.) Here’s why I think Airbnb is so keen to remove my bad review, despite my having stayed in 45+ of their properties over the past four years and received positive reviews from all my hosts (including this last one): Airbnb just wants to make money, and they already have mine. But they might not continue to make money from the bad host if other customers are warned away by my honest review. So, they make it easy to "disappear" bad reviews but hard to post them. That’s disgusting and dishonest, as well as bad business. It’s also a disservice to other Airbnb customers and to the many very good hosts I've had. Buyers beware!

I made a reservation on May 1 on Airbnb inadvertently for a stay starting on May 2 instead of June 2, 2022. The reservation process on Airbnb is based on a simple principle of minimizing the number of clicks to maximize sales, I barely had time to check the dates! (#GoodGameAirbnb) After an instant confirmation from the owner, I immediately contacted the property owner to ask if it was possible to move the dates or cancel the booking. Unsurprisingly, I got no response from him. Tantalizing dilemma for the owner: - "Either the customer does not take any action within 24 hours and I win the full amount", - "Either the customer cancels in the next few hours and I gain ~50% of the amount of the reservation and I can even hope to re-let the property on the dates of the stay" Having had no response from the owner, I decided to cancel the reservation so as not to be charged the full amount and minimize my losses. I contacted Customer Service within minutes of making the reservation, who then told me there was nothing they could do. Bad luck, each owner sets their cancellation and refund policy so I was offered a solution worthy of a Customer Service that helps its customers: “Contact the owner and see with him directly”. Airbnb customers who make a mistake are therefore not in the same boat and the rule of error at Airbnb is therefore discriminatory. So we have a Customer Service that seeks to clear customs and absolve itself of responsibility with a beautiful refrain: “we are only intermediaries”. I regret that this platform leaves no room for error and does not help its customers in any way in solving problems, moreover, knowing that I contacted the owner within 5 minutes which followed, and therefore that no prejudice has been caused to the owner of the property linked to the blocking of the property and the non-possibility of re-renting it! Airbnb is a company whose legal contours have been studied to the nearest millimeter to relieve itself of responsibility as much as possible, with no customer approach and common sense to judge the context of a case. Airbnb didn't even attempt to contact the host to try to fix the situation, as it was not their responsibility. Apparently they still don't know what CUSTOMER SERVICE is in 2022. In addition, the consumer's right of withdrawal of 14 days, for services and products is in force in France, it is inadmissible that in 2022, some companies such as Airbnb are freed from it. A child or a malicious person can make a reservation in the space of an instant and make you lose thousands of euros in a few seconds, beware! In addition, Airbnb has already been pinned down and sentenced by the courts (in France) on the right of withdrawal, I remind you which is a right that has been put in place to protect consumers against an error, an impulsive or poorly thought out purchase, conditions of disadvantageous purchase… In short, a platform that is there only to make numbers, to free itself from any responsibility to the detriment of customers. It was the second time that I made a reservation on Airbnb, the first time, the owner had tried to play the insurance to repair her boiler in very bad condition, forcing me to take cold showers… In short, it is the last time me, my friends and relatives book on this website!

If that doesn't tell you everything you need to know about this company, I'm not sure what would. *** I'll start my one-star review (the last review I gave on TrustPilot, very recently, was a five-star review, by the way) by saying that I work in tech, and so have a pretty intimate knowledge of User Design & Experience. Airbnb's design has deteriorated SIGNIFICANTLY since its beginnings. On a related note, I've been a long-time user of Airbnb. I'm a frequent traveler and, one of the things I liked about the (original) "ethos" of the company is that it emphasized what it means to be a traveler rather than a tourist. Staying locally and being able to search, via a handy filter (that, for no obvious reasons[s], no longer exists) in specific neighbourhoods, and often being able to rent someone's personal dwelling, is what made Airbnb unique and separated it from other offerings. The customer service used to be good, as well. If you had an issue, you felt it was being addressed caringly and sufficiently by their support team. Well, those days are LONG GONE. Rather than making the search experience more user-friendly, it's now an endless maze of navigation that can only be described as a massive time waster. Customer service, to put it nicely, SUCKS. As others have mentioned, responses are canned, no one seems to know their left foot from their right, and they'll close a case prematurely (just so they don't have to address a problem), rather than truly listening to their users and ensuring a resolution. Solutions-oriented, they are not. Airbnb loves to take your money, and that's where their business model, in 2022, starts and finishes. It's a crappy company with crappy service, and I wish they didn't have such a corner on the market.

We were not looking for a refund but wanted assurances that we would not be charged any further fees. I had even worked with the resolution center who instructed me on how to accomplish our departure with no further charges. With these assurances in mind, we departed as soon as we could find alternative accommodations at the end of the first month. At one point I received a phone call from "Ambassador Brittany" of Airbnb who assured me my dispute was successful and I would not be charged further, but this phone conversation was not honored by Airbnb and they have closed the message thread allowing no further communication. I have disputed the charge with my credit card company multiple times but Airbnb continues to re-charge the amount. I have called, emailed, and attempted communication through Airbnb’s website, yet they continue to stall and re-charge my account. At this point, I have filed a complaint with the BBB and will continue to fight this battle. I have read other Airbnb horror stories, such as guests being charged for damages to a new sofa where the damage occurred 2 days prior to the guests check-in. Do yourself a favor, save potential hours of stress, distress and financial difficulties and find another means of booking your next vacation.

We found ourselves in airports for two days and a night with our kids, and when learning all hotels were full in the middle of it, decided to try airbnb. After paying for a rental car by phone from our gate, we booked the only home we could find available on airbnb, and made our way across the airport and outside to the car rentals. The host communication was above and beyond the entire time we were updating her on our circumstances and making our decision to stay, and bent several policies for us in order to allow us to book in the middle of the night. Upon getting to the car rental counter, however, we were told that because of all the canceled flights and weather, every company had NO cars available - including ours - no buses were running that time of night, and uber was going to charge $400. However - somehow now that they had the $700 that we paid to use the house for 10 hours, no policy bending happened! I would have hoped that by getting airbnb involved, airbnb would act as a middle man to help us work with the homeowner and advise each side in order to come to an agreeable compromise. Each time as an airbnb guest we always go above and beyond with our communication and our care of the properties we rent. My friend and I booked a very highly rated Airbnb (a 'superhost') by the sea. The host texted us fairly early in the evening and seemed anxious about our check-in time. We agreed to arrive by 9.30pm and the host apologised for being a bit overzealous in their first message (it had had a certain tone!) and wished us a good evening. We arrived on time at the host's house by taxi - the taxi driver actually knew the place and the lady hosting, when we confirmed her name, so we knew it was the right place. We rang the bell. No-one answered. We knocked the door. No-one answered. We texted the host. She told us she was with her mother. who was end of life, and that her husband was there to let us in. We rang again, we knocked again - and again and again. We saw lights that were on go off upstairs. We wondered if this lady's husband might not be up for hosting this evening. We waited over half an hour, repeatedly ringing the bell and knocking. We were concerned the neighbours might come out about the noise. We texted the host again but we didn't get any reply. It was raining the whole time. When it was gone 10pm, we thought - grief, let's go back to the seafront and get a hotel. We tried to call a cab. None were available. This was one of the early weekends out of Covid when everyone had rushed to the coast. We were literally stranded in the rain. We started to walk back to the seafront, which was a 40 minute walk. About 15 minutes' down the road, we saw the golden arches - a 24 hour McDonalds. We thought it would be wiser to stop here and call up hotels rather than walk in the rain. We called all the hotels along the sea front. We explained the situation over and over again. No vacancies, anywhere. We tried neighbouring towns all around - nothing. We finally thought to contact Airbnb, after all, we had paid in full for our booking and hadn't been let in. We were only able to submit something via an online form. Now, we had a pretty crappy night under the strip lighting and with the constant dance music playing. We saw the clubbers come and go around 4am. The second day of our trip, we decided, was a write-off. What would we do about our train tickets? We'd bought the cheaper fixed-time return. Airbnb called us in the morning. The guy offered to refund out £11 taxi we'd taken to the host's house. They refunded our booking. Did we get compensation? Nope. Did we get to leave a review? No, because we hadn't stayed with the host. And then hours at the train station waiting a friendly train driver to let us go home on an earlier train....!

Airbnb says they, “…take cancellations seriously as this may really disrupt our guests plans”. They state that they will post an auto review to let potential guests know that a host canceled a reservation (You are not allowed to leave a review if the host cancels before your stay!). However, in my case they did not post an auto review after a host canceled my seasonal ski rental just before the 2021/22 season was about to start. I did not see an auto review after a few days so I asked Airbnb support why? They answered “We’ve given your case and its details careful consideration and we determined that this case will be closed….We understand that this might not be what you’d hoped for, but we came to this outcome because there's nothing that we can further do anymore about the automatic review of the host.” Mad as Hell, I fired back “Unacceptable! I do not think the auto review ever went up. Even if it did, it's only been a week since my reservation was canceled, why would you take it down at all? It should stay up at least as long as any other reviews so people can read not only what other guests have to say about their stays and interactions with the host, but also so they can see that he canceled a reservation, possibly multiple times. If you're taking auto reviews down, or not putting them up at all, then it's possible that this host, and others, have canceled multiple times and potential guests have no idea! You say that protecting the community is very important to you. This certainly doesn't look like it is! It looks like revenues from hosts are more important” Here’s why you should be concerned about renting on Airbnb If Airbnb doesn’t post these auto reviews then potential guests may be unaware that a host has canceled reservations before, possibly multiple times! Further, if Airbnb often doesn’t apply the penalties they say could be applied if a host cancels, then hosts may be aware that there is very little, if any, penalty for cancelations, and have no real incentive to think twice before ruining your plans. Why might a host cancel a reservation? I believe in my case the host likely learned that other people will pay them far more than what they listed on Airbnb because of a shortage of available rentals this season.

My husband and I lost roughly $3,000 to AirBNB and a host in Fairview, NC, near Asheville, due to a mistaken cancellation that was the fault of AirBNB. Not only did we lose this money, which was our deposit paid six months ago, we learned of the cancellation the day we were meant to arrive at the house for the Christmas holiday. We were leaving from our rental in Macon, GA, halfway on route from Southwest Florida, with four others traveling in to Asheville that same day from New York, Mexico and Raleigh. I went to the website to double check the address to type into Maps and saw that the reservation had been cancelled! We had to scramble to find a new place because the property was rebooked to someone else and the host had no other vacancies. The host initially assured us he would absolutely refund the deposit but he said there was nothing else he could do and we had to work the rest out with AirBNB. AirBNB seemed reasonable at first, even suggesting they may reimburse us if we book another AirBNB reservation. So, I booked another AirBNB nearby (not nearly as nice but there were few options for 6 people and a dog at Christmas). After I booked the alternative place, AirBNB changed their tune and not only didn't mention reimbursing us again, but also said they couldn't release the deposit without the host's permission. I'm not sure what AirBNB said to the host when they called to get his permission, but whatever they said changed the host's mind and he decided NOT to refund the $3,000 deposit. So of course you're wondering what the error was. Well, AirBNB sent ALL of our booking correspondence to my husbands active email account - the one he used to book the reservation - naturally, right? They sent a final billing reminder for the balance due to an old email address my husband never uses! We had no idea there was a deadline to pay prior to arrival, much less that the deadline had arrived! We paid the deposit at the time of booking in July. We fully understood and were ready to pay when asked, but since the billing correspondence went to the wrong email we had no idea. AirBNB assumed we were cancelling. This happened on Dec. 14. Oddly, my husband received a reservation confirmation - with NO mention of a balance due - to his active email account the VERY SAME day!!! To make things even more confusing, the Host's received a notification that my husband had cancelled the reservation that day too, with no explanation, no indication that AirBNB made the cancellation without our knowledge. Coincidentally, I had called the host on Dec. 14 too. Probably when my husband saw the reservation confirmation, he asked me to request a late check-out. I called the host. He said he needed to call the cleaning crew and get back to me. He never did. The day that we were driving to the place and found out about the mistake, the host said he thought it was odd that we had cancelled the reservation but he figured we changed our minds. He really should have called us. Someone should have called us. This is really AirBNB's fault. They made no effort to contact us by any other means to let us know there was any sort of payment deadline. The hosts didn't know there was such a deadline either or they would have known why the reservation was cancelled. We had every intention in the world and the means to pay the balance but with absolutely no communication about payment and plenty of communication about our reservation, including a confirmation the same day, how would we know our reservation was in jeopardy? AirBNB has refused to work this out with us. Everyday we call and get a different person who says we need to talk to someone else. They say they will escalate it and someone will call us back the next day. No one ever has called us back, not even late. It has been over a week now and we still have yet to talk to anyone with authority to remedy the situation. Making matters worse, this whole ordeal hung over us the whole time we were trying to celebrate Christmas together as a family. We hadn't travelled in ages and it ended up being a nightmare. The place we booked was a luxury cabin with each bedroom containing a king size bed. We ended up in a campy little place on a busy highway, near a hairpin turn and my mother in law had to sleep in a bunk bed. Our bedroom had no windows! And there were no king sized beds. It was the only option available that met our basic needs. Since our calls are going unanswered, we are beginning to feel like this is a scam tactic AirBNB uses to make more money. Why would they send billing and confirmation correspondence to two separate emails instead of sending all correspondence to both emails if they're not sure one is correct, especially when it comes to billing and reservations!

UPDATE: With persistence and patience, I was able to get a full refund. I filed a claim with my credit card company. It took over 2 months but finally the refund was granted. Here's the story: A friend and I planned a 4-day, 3-night trip to Montreal for the first days of Thanksgiving week, including Thanksgiving Day. Canada does not celebrate Thanksgiving and, since neither of us had any other plans for Thanksgiving, this was going to be a good time to go up there, see some art, enjoy the city, eat some good food. The trip was put together several weeks earlier, when Covid cases in VT were remarkably low and had been for quite a while. Canada requires a negative Covid test taken within three days of your border crossing and we were both scheduled for tests on Friday the 19th for a Monday the 22nd departure. Then, there was a sudden and alarming spike in Covid cases in the Burlington area of Vermont during the week before our trip. On Friday the 19th, my friend, who works nights as a nurse practitioner with highest credentials in emergency medicine, was directly exposed to a hospitalized Covid patient who needed to be intubated, Her PPE mask, a halo mask (battery-operated) failed. There were also a number of other Covid patients that she was admitting to the medical center that same night. She was running around dealing with many of these patients, as the hospital was overrun with Covid patients and understaffed. My friend, a highly responsible and experienced medical professional, was the head person on duty the night she was exposed. She wrote to me that it would be irresponsible for her to expose me and to travel, as the Covid-19 incubation period went beyond the time we would be leaving. She said she could potentially pass it to me and would need to stay home and wait for her Friday test results and then retest on Monday and also quarantine and wait for those results. We had booked our stay at a nice 2-bdrm Airbnb apartment in Old Montreal. Since I was the one who booked the reservation through my account, I explained the situation in detail and provided proof of the two tests my friend took—on Friday and on Monday. We were refused a refund of $434—get this—because my friend's tests were not positive for Covid. But it would have been entirely against commonly accepted guidelines for us to drive up there together and cross the border when there was that clear an exposure on Friday. This is what I was told by a manager at Airbnb: If we are able to secure one of the documents needed, we may be able to reconsider. The document must also be dated prior to the reservation. 1. Positive COVID-19 test (preferred) 2. Doctor's note that confirms a COVID-19 diagnosis 3. Notice from a local government stating the user has been exposed 4. She also mentioned that one or more other adults “might” be joining them for a birthday celebration. I asked for additional information and she ignored me. After waiting 12 hours I declined her request. No parties, maximum occupancy 4, no children and no unregistered visitors. 8 minutes later my account disappeared. So, if you want to list your property with Airbnb, just keep in mind that you are giving up your rights to protect yourself. They plan to use it any way they want, and if you refuse to accept ANYONE for ANY reason, you can be accused of discrimination and banned. If you really want to be in the STR business I suggest that you try VRBO.
Booked a host with a lot of problems and made a complaint to AirBnB to rectify it. Eventually I received a refund but it was a very lengthy process to do so (took me around 1month).

got scammed by the host asking me to cancel the booking knowing that the terms and conditions say no refund. asked the host to cancel since they said it was already booked by error (scam). the host the instantly cancelled, then got a message from airbnb saying the host has cancelled and you'll be refunded and compensated. my account was then reported as fraudulent and airbnb deleted it and i was then recharged the full amount for an apartment that i never saw where the host (scammer) cancelled. big loophole scam......airbnb allowing their customers to be scammed and then calling us fraudulent.

Wasn’t able to book even with the hosts own approval and link she sent me due to being the age of 24 and not 25 with the other guest becoming 25 1 month after the stay. Very disappointed.

This was not a safe place to be. I dont know how you can avoid this situation it is I suppose the risk you take when using a service like Airbnb. To add insult to injury Airbnb were down when I cancelled meaning that I could not cancel until after the 2pm on the second day. As a result I received a refund of €106 out of €530 spent. Needless to say we moved to a more appropriate accommodation the next day. Airbnb were unhelpful, I opened a support case before the deadline to let them know I was trying to cancel but the app wasn't working. This made no difference they left it up to the host to decide and of course he declined. My fault I did not write a review on Airbnb which then gave the host an opportunity to slate me. Bottom line I am cancelling my Airbnb account and will inform my contact sphere about the dangers of booking on this site. Just a quick update! Now more than a year since my poor experience with AiRBnB. Having deleted my account back then I have to say I do not miss it. I continue to use booking.com and enjoy a customer focused experience. Good riddance to AirBnB
