If I could give them 0 stars I would. I have been trying for 3 weeks to get a full refund for a stay in Sep 20. We were planning a month trip around Scotland and planned on staying 3 night in Skye. It was a long trip and with several ladies in their 70's. One of our group was stranded in New Zealand for weeks so we decided to cancel until next Spring. I contacted the host and she agreed to a full refund and told me to cancel with Airbnb and she will look for the cancellation and ok the refund. Well 3 weeks later and dozens of emails including all that was required of me using extenuating circumstances, and Airbnb is refusing stating different reasons at different times. The latest reason was they contacted the host, Susie, at No 15, Harrapool, Broadford, Scotland said she wasn't going to ok the refund but would offer to let me reschedule up to a year. I feel I have been scammed. She told me to cancel and she okayed a full refund and then lied after the fact. Now I am out $400 and hours and days of wasted time and stress. The company in dishonest and deceiving and only cares about the bottom line and not the guests well being. This is fraudulent behavior and should not be allowed to get away with it. I will never use them again.

AirBnB are not following their own Covid19 policy. They are doing all possible to avoid giving a full refund, even though the policy offers this as an unconditional choice. For trips booked before 14 March, with Check-in between 14 March and 31 May the policy clearly says a full refund or credit is offered at the customers choice. But in reality they are offering either credit with no conditions, but refund only if Government documentation can be supplied showing that at the time of the trip the travel is not permitted. As all countries are reviewing policies every few weeks, it means AirBnB are not offering refunds for more than two or three weeks into the future. This time window is impossible for most people to work with, as AirBnB know full well. The policy is deliberately misleading. They have sought positive publicity by announcing this policy, and then deliberately diverged from it to the detriment of customers. It is disgusting when thousands are dying. As a host I have told customers I will offer a full refund, without question. But AirBnB will not allow me to do this. They also will not allow me to retrospectively change cancellation policy to provide a refund option to long-booked guests. AirBnB are doing everything possible to hang on to their pennies when people are sick and dying, when rural areas are pleading with people to stay away. An utterly immoral company.

Brenda from air bnb customer service has refused to give us a full refund, clearly contradicting the COVID-19 extenuating circumstances policy. Because we cancelled before the policy was extended to May 31st, this now aparently means that only 50% of our booking can be refunded. It doesn’t say that on the website and clearly the factors that will get you a refund are: 1. If you booked before 14th March and 2. If your booking is before 31st May. We are within both these factors and yet they are arguing to not give us a full refund! It’s so disgusting to see a company revel in this pandemic and put their own financial gain ahead of customer service. To not refund people who, you don’t know how this may have affected them financially, is so outrageous! And once this blows over, it will be back to business as usual. So why on Earth you wouldn’t be understanding in this current situation is disgraceful and will put people off from ever using this company again. It’s like the saying goes: you don’t know who your true friends are, until you are at your lowest. I will rephrase to: you don’t know what companies are genuinely good, until we experience a pandemic!!!

I'm very disappointing that they won't do anything about our accommodation cancellation due to COVID-19, Airbnb is not following their own Covid19 policy. They are doing all possible to avoid giving a full refund, even we escalate our claim they reply it depends on landlord and close it in 4 hours. Which we do not get any refund. Please do not trust them anymore!

Pls read. It's long but hopefully my experience may be of help... As a guest who was to travel during the March 14-May 31 time period, I had to cancel due to covid 19. I cancelled well in advance of 30 days and only received 1/12th of my deposit back. The host was keeping 11/12ths of my deposit. It was a strict cancellation and the policy noted I had to cancel 15 days in advance to receive a FULL REFUND. I canceled over 30 days in advance and only got the 1/12th of the deposit. It took me weeks to finally get a hold of Airbnb. There were times I spent over 2 hours holding. When I finally got thru and told the rep I only got back 1/12th of my deposit, I was told it was the host's right to keep my money... and I pointed out to her that I fall within the outline on Airbnb's website for extenuating circumstances. And legally I cancelled within the protocol of the strict cancellation policy. I suddenly realized this person was reading from a script. When the rep finally figured out my situation and probably found the correct script, I was told I had to go to the resolution area on Airbnb to start a request for a refund. I did this and two days later I received an email from Airbnb in another country noting they were trying to contact the host to see if the host would agree to give me a refund or a portion of it. This did not settle well with me. I called Airbnb back late at night. I was connected to another country. I again stated my case to the rep and started to hear about all the woes Airbnb was going thru. I replied that EVERYONE IN THE WHOLE WIDE WORLD was going thru the same thing... i noted that i had done everything by the book, and that the result was it was the host's decision if i would get any money back..and that the host was stealing 11/12ths of my deposit and Airbnb was an accomplice by letting the host get away with stealing my refund. I also ranted and raved how disappointed I was in Airbnb to allow this disloyalty to happen..I was asked to be placed on hold... I held for a long time but finally was told I was getting my full refund back.. I was told the money was not released to the host yet, and it was in an account and would be released to me immediately I see articles how hosts are losing money. I can't speak for any other host but it sounded like my host was in control of the decision of refunding my deposit. I respect Airbnb for making the right moral decision to refund the deposit to me.

Anyone who is trying to get a refund through Airbnb just needs to send a link showing your local/state stay at home orders. This is what I did. I had to jump through many hoops and talk to a variety of people at Airbnb before anyone acted on it. The superhost was completely uncooperative (Ray Ramsey of Seaside, CA "Sunny Seaside Bungalow"at 2090 Cross Street). In addition, keep in mind that the host DOES HAVE A SAY! I am a superhost with a strict cancellation policy. When the guest cancelled due to the COVID crisis, I thought that was it. Several days later I HAD TO APPROVE HIS REQUEST for a refund. Why should I have had to approve it? Shouldn't Airbnb automatically do it? I don't even get paid until the host is scheduled to check in. Airbnb is holding that money, and probably making money on it. Of course I approved his request, as in my eyes it would have been unethical to do anything else. We are in the middle of a global crisis and NOBODY SHOULD BE TRAVELING, let alone haggling with unethical hosts and Airbnb. So, keep in mind that when a host tells you they don't have anything to do with the cancellation policy, it is a lie. Hosts set their own cancellation policy, based on choices Airbnb provides. All hosts were contacted and ENCOURAGED to alter their cancellation policies due to the pandemic. As some of you have experienced, many have not done it. I encourage you to write reviews naming your hosts and as much details about their rentals, as possible. This way, for those who dare to continue using Airbnb, potential guests can at least find out who was unethical during the pandemic - and avoid booking with them at any cost!
I was a host for four years with a 5 star review rating and superhost status. Airbnb was terrible to work with after the virus.

As with other recent reviews, it took an inordinate amount of time to finally get a refund for a planned trip to Vancouver April 14-16, 2020. It only happened through the kindness of the host, after Airbnb denied the claim, stating I had cancelled before their COVID 19 rule was in place. I, like many others, have used Airbnb for 6 years, have been a super host, and will find another way in the future. Great model, poor customer service straight from the top of the company.

I'm VERY upset with Airbnb during this time. We planned a trip back in February before this whole Corona virus scare really took over. We were going to go to San Diego for my sister's high school graduation and make a whole vacation out of it. We are going to go to SeaWorld and the beach and other fun activities. However, once this Corona virus scare started, we realized that was not going to be a possibility anymore. My sister's graduation got postponed and everything has been closed down. We contacted the host of the Airbnb and they said they had no say in the cancellation process so to contact Airbnb. I contact Airbnb and all they would offer was a $53 refund of a $330 payment we had already made or we could get a $330 credit on our account to use within the next year and a half. This, to me, is complete BS and manipulation during this tough time. People are being laid off and need their money back more than ever, and Airbnb is not being understanding at all!!! And it's not even the host, it's AirBNB being cheap and cruel during a very tough time. I'm blown away by their inconsideration and would never want to work with a company with such low morals ever again!!!

I recently used Airbnb to make reservations for a spring break trip...will NEVER use them again! I canceled like they said to do on their website.. this is all when COVID-19 was just emerging and they were telling people not to travel. Airbnb has given me the runaround and so has the host. Needless to say I am out $585.50 because Airbnb and the host were not gracious enough by refund me ... even though I followed their guidelines in canceling a reservation!

I was using AirBnB for 4 years during which time I had always been a Superhost. I work with a strict cancellation policy to protect my business as I have mortgages and bills to pay. During Covid-19 AirBnB overrode this strict cancellation policy without consulting me as a long-term business partner first and offered 100% refunds to all guests against my will. Anytime I tried to reason with them I would only receive an automated message. This meant I was unable to pay bills, had to take a high interest loan to cover these bills and I'm currently running three empty flats with no hope of finding a tenant during lockdown. My cancellation policy would have protected me against this. I won't be using this platform every again for booking trips, nor to rent out my properties.

AirBnB deleted our review of a host claiming it was biased. What we wrote in the review: 1. The host gave the wrong adress so we spend a long time finding our apartment. 2. The kitchenware was dirty and not clean when we arrived. 3. Some laundry was left out to dry taking up most of the floor space in a 1 room studio. 4. An electrician showed up and wanted to check the eletricity meter. We were not notified and had to spend time and effort to figure out if it was legit and help him. 5. Due to the Covid outbreak we had to return since both Denmark and France closed down. We asked for a minor reimbursement which both Airbnb and the host declined. All of the above happened. I am not sure how this is biased reporting. I cannot see how one can trust AirBnB's review section if they just delete any negative comments about hosts. This reflects very poorly on AirBnB as a business. Note: We did try to contact and talk with AirBnB support to no avail. We do not recommend AirBnB. Or at least know that you are on your own if you book through them.

They won’t refund me after having to cancel because of COVID. So bad. Imagine being forced to use your reservation in Montreal even when that is the Canadian epicenter of COVID in Canada. $1100 cost and no way to use that without risking death.

I was signed up for a big race coming up in NY (a major epicenter for infection and exposure). Due to COVID, the race will imminently be cancelled. I am also a first responder and now devote 60-80 hours per week managing our crisis locally, without a clear end in sight. Training is out the window at this point. The host of the home I rented was incredibly gracious when I reached out to her directly. She quickly approved a full refund in the amount of $565 (this was 50% down). She told me to call Airbnb for this refund since I made the reservation through them. After getting the run around, I was only refunded $39. It was quite a fight to get any more because my reservation was AFTER May 31, the date they deemed as “safe” for travel after COVID. Considering my health care clinic (a major world renown hospital system) isn’t seeing anyone in clinic until July, this date is by no means “safe”. They eventually agreed to reach out to the host to confirm what she had told me. After that, I got an email that they could only refund $380...the rest are non-refundable Airbnb “fees”. What fees...?? Fees for what?? Essentially, the host gets nothing but Airbnb keeps a portion for themselves. Great business model. I’m still fighting for the rest of my money... This company has been terrible and I will not be going through them again. I may use them as a search engine but will work directly with a host/hostess If needed. Very disappointed.

Because of COVID19, my cruise was cancelled, so I had to cancel my Airbnb reservation. Airbnb wouldn't refund me my deposit so I lost $390. Do not deal with this company! They are not flexible nor Fair!!! Run like the plague that caused my vacation to be canceled!!!

We rented a house in Florida for the Spring break on Mar 15 2020. We cancelled 2 days before the trip because the seriousness of the situation in the US due to Covid-19 was getting really big. Our intentions to leave the state were completely blocked. First, our employer told us we have to get ourselves on self quarantine after returning from a personal trip. Second, the beaches, restaurants, businesses for boat, bike, kayak rentals, in Florida were ordered to close. Third, the state of ILLINOIS ordered shelter in place. Forth, we were worried for our kids safety and not being able to get back home and get stuck in Florida for uncertain period of time. After all that even if we wanted we could not leave, unless you are telling me that we should go against the Government restrictions anyway???? We contacted the host and asked for a refund, he refused. Then we involved Airbnb customer service. They said that our trip is not covered under their policy because our reservation was made on March 15 and the policy covers reservations made on or before Mar 14, 2020. We lost $750. We were refunded only cleaning and booking fees. We asked Airbnb to revise the cancellation policy for Illinois and other states that are currently sheltered. They replied that their decision is final, no refund will be issued. Nothing about policy revision. This situation is out of our control, when you are advertising a house for rent you are advertising also the area, that's why the prices are so high and if everything in the area closed, then the prices should go down or close all dates for rental. If you are renting a house somewhere but there's nothing else to do, then why do you need to go to sit in somebody's house? Airbnb is not willing to help customers in this unprecedented, extraordinary situation. I will not rent through Airbnb again. I'll give negative review for Airbnb and the host, and involve the media. Airbnb should downgrade the status of the host. Your super host is not that super after all. He cares only about your money. To me getting money from the people is just inhumane, lack of compassion, not carrying for the people but care for the money, the hard cold cash that somebody would like to make for doing nothing using the unfortunate situation that the people are in, with other words this is steeling.

One star is too many. Worse company ever. I have been trying to get a refund due to COVID 19 for weeks. I have sent over 50 messages, been left on hold for literally hours, been hung up on numerous times, been told someone would get back to me or call me back numerous times, and to no resolve. I have ended up losing £500. Worse customer service I have ever experienced. I will take it to Citizens Advice, but I'm sure Air BnB will manage to hold on to my money. You have been warned.

This company should not be allowed to trade. They have publically made a song and dance about full cash refunds when really they will only give you a time limited travel credit. Their customer service is horrific they have no qualms about publically saying they will give full cash refunds and then not honoring them. The CEO of this company should hang his head in shame. At a time when everyone is struggling they are indefinately holding into people's money in the form of a travel credit. What happens if they go bust? This credit is worthless. They should not be allowed to publish that they will give full refunds and then make it so complex requiring proof that you cannot travel, well news flash no one can travel. Your company's morals disgust me and as soon as everyone is out of this living nightmare I hope Airbnb is realised for what it is, a lying evil morally corrupt company. AIRBNB SHOULD BE ASHAMED OF THEMSELVES, absolutely disgusting behaviour.

In November I had booked a house in California near the end of May for our daughter’s graduation. Obviously with covid-19 we had to cancel our plans. Our deposit was $400. Per the policy I should have gotten 50% back minus a fee. I got $4.98 instead because apparently their covid-19 cancellation policy trumps my hosts policy. Then, after days of crappy customer service they tell me I can get a full refund if I prove that I cannot travel (I am immunocompromised with a primary immune deficiency along with 4 autoimmune diseases and we can’t make that trip until the pandemic is under control). BUT I also need to show proof that there is a travel ban or closure of the airports. So I’m screwed either way. We have used VRBO in the past and that’s where I will be booking once we can make travel plans again.

I booked accommodation in Nice for 17th April which had to be cancelled due to the corona virus. Our flights were obviously cancelled and travel banned. They have a policy that covers cancellations for this period but state that it only covers cancellations actually requested after 30th March. I cancelled a week before but it is clearly for the same reason. I think that the host for "Le Comfy" is also completely unreasonable and pretty stupid really because I would have re booked when it is all over but they seemed to prefer to keep the deposit now rather than have a full booking later. I would never use this service again.

Unbelieveable and unacceptable service in these extreme COVID-19 circumstances. Airbnb is not willing to provide a refund or any kind of compensation while we would've had to cross the border via public transport for our stay in Belgium - that was in complete lockdown as of our travel date.

Trip to Paris on 24th April obviously I cancelled a few weeks ago as France went into lockdown, lots of airlines grounded their fleet and UK start of lockdown procedures. Paid in 2 parts and luckily cancelled before the 2nd payment was taken as no chance of me getting my 1st instalment back or even a credit note for future use!!! Surely the host should be made to offer rearranged travel dates or credit note for future use. Terrible service, will never ever use again not even for business travel. Absolute joke of a company. Constantly changing their policies too so if you’re looking to file a claim I’d screenshot the policies when you read them as they will probably change them!! Disgusting from a large company especially when people are just trying to protect others and themselves. Do you think I’d cancel a trip to my favourite place in the world for the fun of it?!??!??? Embarrassment and I truly hope this affects your business in the future. Shocking shocking customer service.

I had to book a hotel because of the bad room condition which I booked on Airbnb. They refunded me the amount which I spent on hotel booking. They are great company but they must have a good check on their listings. As most of the listed place are different then as shown in pictures.

Refused to refund me for a trip starting on 27th May as I cancelled before 14th March. Very lacking compassion and being absolutely uncompromising. Was only expecting to get a credit for a future booking ... that's being fair.
Very fast refunds, good support. Even in this difficult time, they refunded everything within 2 days. We'll continue using them after this pandemic for sure.

I only had to press one button to get a full refund for my reservation, including the service fee. The best part is that the refund was processed immediately and I was able to receive it the very same day!!

Once Airbnb finally extended their COVID-19 extenuating circumstances to cover my stay in mid-April, I cancelled by booking. When cancelling my booking there is no option to process the full refund on the site. Calling customer service doesn't help either because they have a special department that handles the refund (they wouldn't forward me to the department on the phone). I had to wait for them to contact me via their Airbnb messaging for a refund. To get my refund I had to show documentation. My documents included canceled flights, travel restrictions in destination country, and US travel advisory. With current circumstances, it seems really silly that I have to show documentation and go through so many steps to get my refund. Airbnb should have refunded automatically.

The problem with Airbnb is that if you need to resolve an issue, you will be met with total incompetence. I have used Airbnb for years and have had pretty great experiences with hosts for the most part, but Airbnb itself as a company is terrible and I do not trust them. I really hope they get some competition soon. I attempted to cancel a trip to Canada whose borders are closed and they had an inaccurate cancelation policy for the host and declined my refund. Her listing clearly states that you can cancel up to 48 hours, even without COVID. The host wanted to refund my $, but was helpless to do so since it had not been transferred to her and Airbnb was unresponsive to either of our many attempts to contact them. I was only able to get a response when I filed a dispute with PayPal and the communications consist of semi-robo responses from a mandarin speaker in China who says he does not speak English very well, so he just keeps sending pre-formatted responses that don't address the issue and inaccurately state facts. FINALLY after much effort on the part of myself and the host, Airbnb is agreeing to a refund minus the service fees, which are over $200 even though the border to Canada is closed. I have also read horror stories about undisclosed cameras in rentals that Airbnb was terrible about responding to. I feel lucky that my issue is just about $. Think about it, what if there was a more frightening issue that came up? Look at their initial incompetence in responding to COVID-19. Do you trust Airbnb to help you and keep you safe when things go awry?

I booked a condo Scottsdale AZ 4/19-4/25.As Covid crisis escalated, I knew I would need to reschedule in the fall.My sister is a breast cancer survivor/severe COPD & cast of cormobidities.My brother who we were visiting is a heart transplant recipient.In addition hotel at the Grand Canyon emailed to say they were closing till mid May and now Canyon itself is closed.I filled out required request for refund and have been given $517 credit much of which will be a "voucher" for further bookings.I work on the front line as RN.Common sense and need to distance myself from them is a no brainer.I have contacted condo owner for remainder which remains to be seen but don't have much faith in them either. It is my first and last booking with them.I read that VBRO is also affiliated with Airbnb so be forewarned.I have used others and no problems with them.The arrogance of their service members and the complete indifference to people's problems is outrageous

We booked a trip to Virginia Beach for Memorial Day weekend! cancelled today due to coronavirus based on the site saying that we could cancel and get a full refund including service fees based on COVID 19 being the cancellation reason. Our hosts were great and even stated that they would not dispute our full refund in light of the pandemic! When I actually went to cancel after putting COVID 19 as the reason, it only gave me 2 options: (1) get $60 cash refund of our $515 deposit OR (2) get full travel credit to be used at another time. So I selected option 1 with the hopes that it would just give me the full refund since I selected COVID 19 as the cancellation reason. I then immediately called customer service and was told that there was an option to get a full refund and provide documentation (which there WAS NOT). She then proceed to ask me to send 1 of 3 documents: (1) official government documentation with Travel restrictions, (2) letter from my employer stating medical or “disease control” duties related to COVID 19, OR (3) letter from airline or ground transportation company cancelling my travel which had to be initiated by them and not the customer (which was a ridiculous request). The fact that they asked for any documentation and the specific type of documentation I thought was ridiculous! Especially when everything on TV at this point in time is about the dangers of coronavirus and travel restrictions/limitations! However, I provided screenshots of the CDC stating pregnant women are high risk due to being immunocompromised, a letter from my OBGYN to my employer suggesting a job with little patient Interaction (just to prove that I’m actually pregnant), and also a screen shot of “The president’s guidelines for coronavirus in America” which recommends that high risk people should stay home & avoid people in addition to avoiding discretionary travel for everyone. Even with all of the documents I provided, I was then asked if I had an actual letter from my OBGYN telling me not to travel (which I do not have). This was a totally Outrageous request since the first 3 documents I provided met 1 of the required guidelines they asked of me initially! Aside from that, who would actually need a letter from a doctor telling them not to travel when again, THIS IS ALL OVER THE NEWS EVERYDAY! After that, I provided screenshots of the governor of Virginia’s executive stay at home order which is In effect until June 10 which is a couple of weeks after our initial reservation. They finally agreed to give me a full refund after all this which they said will take 5-15 days to get back! I just think it’s totally unacceptable that the company still tries to keep your money even after posting on their site that they will give full refunds if cancelling due to COVID 19 by making you jump through hoops! My recommendation for people who did not get their full refunds is to dispute the charges if you paid on a credit card! That was my plan B had they not agreed to give my money back! I will never book with Airbnb again due to how they are doing business during this unprecedented time when many people are being laid off or furloughed and wondering how they are going to pay their rent/mortgages and feed their families! I’m sure the CEO of Airbnb has NEVER had to worry about such things! ABSOLUTELY NO COMPASSION AT ALL! I’ll NEVER give them another dime and I hope you don’t either!

We had to cancel a trip to California because our event was canceled due to the coronavirus. The website promised a full refund in 5 to 15 days. We have heard nothing except that we don't get a refund from the host Marcie. Transversing the site is a viscous circle where you can never contact anyone. This was my first experience with Airbnb and I will NEVER use airbnb. Even the host stopped answering any emails and this was BEFORE the cancellation. All I wanted was info about how many cars the driveway would hold.

I Travis Crawford had booked a trip to Paris with my wife (Laura). Our stay was from Mar 14-29, 2020 which falls within the timeframe that AirBnB permits a full refund for COVID-19 extenuating circumstances policy. They are now saying that because I cancelled it on the same day that there policy came out, that they won’t honor the refund. This shows an absolute lack of accountability as a company. Horrible customer service. It is obvious that they are looking only for their self interests and are a completely dishonorable company.

I am a physical therapy student and was in Seattle/Tacoma are for a clinical rotation. Unfortunately my clinical began at about the same time as the virus (2 weeks before their policy). I understand they, like us, couldn’t have known this would happen. I have since been dropped from my rotation by the company to limit exposure and need to return home to continue coursework to graduate. There is now a government shelter mandate in place, so I would like to get home to be with family instead of being stuck in rough neighborhood alone. They refuse to refund anything, even their service fees. So now $6000+ of my student loans go to them and I have to figure out how to pay for housing at my next rotation. They do not care about heath care professional students and I will never be utilizing them again. I am so disappointed since I have been living in air bnbs the last four months on clinical rotations and am going into traveling physical therapy after graduation in May, which will have me on three month rotations at a time over the next two years. I can tell you I will be putting my thousands of dollars into hotels, VRBO, furnished finder, OR LITERALLY ANYWHERE BUT AIRBNB. Thanks for showing the community you do not care.

Lies About COVID-19 Policies. My trip to Japan was cancelled through the airline and when I reached out to customer service regarding this clear, extenuating situation, they let me know that I don't qualify. This took over 8 attempts to contact them and multiple service representatives, who let me know that despite Japan having an outbreak of the COVID-19 virus, that it wasn't covered. I contacted them back in February 28th regarding this when my work didn't want me to travel (understandably) and that my flight was cancelled directly through the airlines. I had to issue a chargeback since neither the host or customer service would give me a full refund (only partial). Done with using this dishonest service that clearly does not stand by their very own policies. I've deactivated my account because out of principle, I refuse to deal with a company that can't even support people dealing with a worldwide, human life crisis.

I waited until the Airbnb cancellation policy due to Covid 19 included the dates I were travelling at the end of May. I went through the process of cancellation and were offered no refund or a credit. My host, an excellent chap, had no issue with a refund. Airbnb will not refund as I cannot prove, by a suggested screen shot, that a third option of a refund was not available to me. Airbnb cannot prove it was available so I am stuck with a credit. So anyone reading this and thinking of cancelling take a photo of the screen at the point of cancelling so you have proof. Just another case of a company holding onto someone else's money....just because they can.

PLEASE READ IF YOU WANT A CHANCE TO GET YOUR MONEY!!! (This worked for me and will work as well if you live in the United States) As many of you I was very upset and frustrated as I’ve tried calling them and dealing with them for over 2 weeks. They finally extended the dates of their “Extenuating circumstances” policy and I thought I would finally get my money back right? Nope. I had to fight and be firm and continue to call until I finally figured it out. They will not give you your money back unless you fight till the end. They will ask for “proof” or “documentation” that shows you cannot travel. All you have to do is find an article stating what the president has said and also send them the travel.state.gov link with a screenshot of the first paragraph It states we are Level 4 “Do Not Travel” And they are forced to give you your money because it is a government order. Follow this advice along with being FIRM and you will most likely get your money back! Good luck!!! If you live somewhere else just send them any government link and screenshot that states citizens cannot travel!
Thank you for what you did in these hard times. I appreciate a lot that you offer refund and also offer to help the hosts. That's great!

I had booked a stay at an AirBNB in Boston for the end of April. With Covid-19 restrictions we are unable to go. We could not get our whole deposit back which is sad and difficult. What is deceitful is that we did not even get half our deposit back. It states if we cancel before April 23rd we would get a 50% refund minus the service fee. I had a $945.82 deposit and got a $102.32 refund. The non refundable service fee was $193.50. I contacted the owner and he said the refund only applied if the full amount had been paid. My spouse and I have used Air BnB a lot over the years for business travel etc., BUT - I have a few major gripes with them. Firstly, the fact that you can only leave a review for the host BEFORE you can view the review that they left for you, creates an unequal power balance in my opinion (which kind of doesn't make sense to me from a 'customer' perspective when you are paying for a service). Secondly, the rates and availability seem to change a lot - even within a single browsing session, which makes the information on the site seem unreliable. Inconsistency in hosting/communication is sometimes an issue - some hosts are amazing; friendly, yet not intrusive, flexible with check in time, easy-going about things (ie. a coffee mug or two left by the sink etc. - after all, this is what you tend to pay a cleaning fee for - which sometimes gets quite costly), and yet there are some hosts that are terrible (or run their property like a military school - ie. everything must be SPOTLESS, even when you pay a hefty cleaning fee), which happened on our anniversary get-away when we left a couple of dishes drying in the rack on the counter (after WASHING them thoroughly, which the host complained about - um seriously). I am told from a host that Air BnB also takes a pretty substantial service fee from hosts (I can only speculate on this to be fair), which is too bad since the host is the one who does the work primarily. I also have an ideological issue with too many short-term rentals that can price locals who need housing out of the market, and I know that some cities/municipalities have set limits on them, which I think is appropriate - even if it affects our travel plans. Finally, when an issue arises, customer service is not always particularly helpful or timely, and we have had to 'eat' a few dollars due to issues such as delayed flights or other periodic travel woes. We have tried a couple of other short-term rental sites with good results so far, so it might be time to branch out to other methods or go directly through the accommodation provider.

I am always a clean freak OCD personal regardless of being a host, I am also a very well rated host with a great history on Airbnb. This guest ironically has zero history Airbnb and no reviews. About 45 minutes goes by and I hear a notification from the Airbnb app saying that the guest has sent a message. I open the message only to read that that guest is feeling uncomfortable and would like to leave the unit. It was at this point that I start wondering what is actually going on and why is the guest now leaving? Why is the guest clearly lying? What was the motive or purpose of this entire situation? I then decided to call Airbnb support and speak with someone from the team, after 30 minutes of speaking with a staff member (Robert) I feel good and confident at this point that the guest refund will not be issued back the guests due to the situation being 100% false, and more importantly my great history my profile has with the company and the guest not having any history or reviews at all.I then get a call from another Airbnb agent who asked me what my side of the situation was but then went on to say the guests provided documents which warranted a refund. One would think with all things considered (along with my phone call to Airbnb and my communication with the guest throughout this entire situation) that this situation would be handled with a detailed report and photos along with an investigation being conducted into the unit. I would of hoped that all of these factors (including my strict refund setting policy) would of been taken into consideration before Airbnb made the shocking decision to fully issue the guests a 100% refund on the booking which resulted in myself getting zero payment as originally expected and planned for from myself. Airbnb promotes the idea that a guest can lie and get away with it on level because no matter how false the accusation is and no matter how much a host has a stellar history the guest is unfortunately always right even when they are clearly lying. I do empathise, you play a risky game when paying for a trip to someone's house/flat that you don't know much about. However, my personal experiences have been mostly great. I've had a few minor issues, but considering how much could have gone wrong, I've had a lot of good times travelling and part of that is down to airbnb. I know you'll think I'm biased, but I actually met my fiance on an airbnb trip. I'm not just talking about a random meeting, we actually met in the airbnb because he was the guy responsible for looking after the place. For that reason, airbnb has a soft spot in my heart. Airbnb in general is a good platform, it's not perfect and if I'd had some of the bad experiences that others have had then I'd probably feel less positive. We can only talk about our own experiences and considering I've booked and stayed in quite a few places: Austria, Texas, NY, New Zealand, Paris and even a romantic stay in London, I tend to think airbnb is pretty reliable and most of my friends who've also used it for travel, have enjoyed their trips. I hope my experiences with them continue to be good, because there aren't any alternatives that I'm aware of (apart from Hotels).

Last year's New Years was the first and last time I ever used Airbnb. Everytime someone says they use it, I pray to the almighty Airbnb gods that they make it out alive and in one piece. Here's why: So last year, I researched a place to stay in Chicago for New Years for a good couple hours. My budget was low, and I wanted somewhere close to the venue I was going to be seeing a show at that night. Airbnb was the cheapest and most convenient option I could find. I found a cute little place in Ukranian Village pretty close to the venue, and Chad (the host) had pretty good reviews. The only bad reviews complained about how the place was kinda dirty and run down. If that was the only thing people complained about, it had to be safe, right? (WRONG!!) I can handle a little dirt so I booked a night for ~30$. When I got there to check in, Chad seemed like a decent guy. He made me food and showed me around. The place was beat up and he hadn't shown some of the more rough areas of the place to me, but it was livable for a night. What I should have done was run away screaming and never look back when I got to my room and found a broken window by the alleyway and STAB MARKS ON THE WALLS. I wish I was exaggerating. I also wish I had had the frame of mind to take pictures. Some of the marks were small enough and at the right height that they could have been from nailing something into the wall and having the nail dragged down from the weight of a frame or something, but not all of them. My stomach dropped but I wasnt able to afford a hotel room that was any better than this. Since he seemed like a nice guy, I asked him about the stab marks on the walls. He told me he had had a crazy guest threaten him like that in a fit of rage. We left it at that and talked for a couple more hours before I left to get ready and go to my show. The show was amazing and I had a great time. When I got back to the house, Chad was still awake and let me back in. I offered him a cigarette and we went outside to go smoke in the backyard. We were talking and smoking out there for a while before we heard a sort of muted bang and his fire alarm going off inside. He said that his fire alarm went off randomly sometimes and told me not to worry about it. It kept going off for a while, and a look of concern started to spread over his face. He kept his cool at this point in time, though, and went in to go see what had transpired. Not more than five seconds later, a look of panic spread over his face and he jumped back, saying "We need to get out of here." He grabbed a couple things off the table and frantically ran out of the backyard around to the front of the house. Not knowing what was going on, I ran after him. He opened the front door and I saw nothing but bright orange flames filling the house. He had been charging his LITHIUM BATTERY MOTORBIKE in the LIVING ROOM OF THE HOUSE and it had EXPLODED. Let me say that again. He had been charging his LITHIUM BATTERY MOTORBIKE in the LIVING ROOM of the bnb and it had F***ING EXPLODED. Look up "Ukranian Village fire Chicago January 1" if you dont believe me. Out of sheer panic he started to abandon me and the apartment completely, running off down the ALLEYWAY to leave me there to deal with the entire thing. I was the one who had to call 911. I was the one who had to talk to the fire department and police and landlord and everyone else who contacted me as if I had been the one who had put everyone's lives at risk. But nope. This spineless idiotic f*** had just destroyed all of my and his belongings and the entire first floor of the complex, causing the people on the top floors to have to be RESCUED by the fire department, and he took off like a little b***h. Told me to LIE to the fire department and anyone else I made contact with, aka put myself at risk to save his pathetic a** from the consequences of his own actions. Happy New Years. I ran after him because I'm a small female without protection and I was in fishnets, out on the streets of Chicago, at 3 in the morning. I protested this to him as I wouldn't have booked should I have known this to be the case. My host proceded to get angry, starting swearing at me and telling me it is not a matter of discussion and that i need to leave immediately. After not giving the keys to him immediately as I needed them to leave and did not feel safe having to need him to let me leave, he followed me upstairs and in to my room where he became threatening. At one point he was stood over me (he is 6ft, I am 5ft 7) and said 'give me the keys little boy'. There are even more details I am sparing here but I moved to pass him and he shoved me in to the window. I then called the police and left as soon as I could. After calling Airbnb, their response was to give me a case manager. I didn't hear from this case manager until the next day when he heard me tell my story. After a few days wait I received an email saying that I have been banned from using Airbnb indefinitely as I had broken safety rules. I looked at these rules and could not begin to work out how I had broken any of them. I replied asking for an explanation and received nothing. I called up and they said they would assign a new case manager who would call me the next day. Instead I received an email which said almost word to word the same thing the previous person had said, still with no explanation as to HOW I broke any rules. Airbnb have no complaints or appeals process so I am left powerless. It baffles me that I got threatened and assaulted by a host and get banned for life without any explanation as to how I broke any rules. It seems they have a blanket response to ban all parties involved in such circumstances and don't actually care about the victim of the assault. I am a touring musician and used the site a lot, without any problems before I might add. Now, because a power crazy psychopath decided to pick on me, and Airbnb only care about themselves, I could be left in the lurch in many destinations I go. I don't feel treated like a person, let alone a person who went through something genuinely frightening. I would implore people to use other options when possible - somewhere where you can feel like the people running it will back you if something nasty happens to you.

AirBnB Bad Experience at the Beautiful Garden Unit Close to the Water – Host Jacinta 2022 Beach Street, San Francisco, California, 94123 We rented this unit for a month and regretted it. There was no welcome card, no information about the area, or even basic information like which day the garbage would be picked up. It turns out that the regular entry to the apartment is down a dark, dank, dusty hall that looks like no one has been there for years. Spooky! The bedding looked very used, On top of that, the mattress squeaks with every turn. When we took their bedding off we found stains and rips in the mattress protector. If you are allergic to dust mites, good luck. No amount of Zyertec will help. So the next morning we went to Ikea and bought our own bedding. My husband was starting a new a job the next day. When he left for work I bought my own cleaning supplies. There was no mop or broom or anything else to keep the apartment clean. No paper towels. Nothing. Yet the minimum rental is a month. I guess you're just supposed to let it get dirty. So I started cleaning. It took days. When I mopped the floor the water was black. Whatever I wiped showed layers of dirt - the tables, chairs, headboard, cushions, the shelves, everything. I took videos to show my family and friends. They couldn't believe that such an expensive place was in that condition. We decided it would better if we covered the couch. It smelled bad. There was an old carpet that looked very dusty. And it was. When I lifted it to clean there was a cloud of dust. We set it aside, not wanting to it to foul the air through our visit. The kitchen utensils look like a mixed bag of whatever other visitors may have left behind. The sprayer on the sink is rusty and there's rust on the refrigerator too. We didn't want to touch the dishes so we ate off of paper plates and plastic utensils. When we sat down to our first meal at the table, we could see sticky spots from previous visitors. When you see the picture of the outdoor patio it looks inviting. In fact, all the furniture is covered in dirt and mold. I tried to clean it but it was way too beat up and old. The chaise has a couple of old, moldy cushions. You can't sit in the furniture anyway because it's falling apart. It would be nice to open the sliding door to the patio for the pleasant air. Unfortunately, there is no screen and the bushes are filled with mosquitos. When we did leave the door open, bugs and flies would come in. On the walls you will find squashed mosquitos – left behind by other visitors. My husband was bitten many times – I took pictures of the red blotches on his face. The door to the unit is next to the Host's garage. Several times we opened the door to find that their car had blocked our exit. Either we had to climb over the bumper or push through the bushes to get out. Unsafe! I hope you're not looking for a quiet evening. On random evenings you'll hear pounding on the ceiling. It's the kids jumping and running around above you. Now about safety; the address is "2022 A." The main house is "2022." The only indication that there is an entrance to "A" is a tiny 1/2" letter. So if you have any mail or packages, you're in for trouble. Twice the owner took my packages and opened them. A bigger problem is theft. Two very large packages were delivered at the owner's door. They were new clothes that I had specially ordered. After a couple of days, I noticed that they hadn't been delivered to 2022 A. They were stolen. So we had to file a police report. I have my copy. Here's something else creepy. I was in the kitchen and I heard a noise in the bedroom. I went to see and found that someone was trying to get in from the main house through the door from the owner's garage. It was a woman who called herself Nanny. If I hadn't remembered to lock the door while I was cleaning, the owner and other people in their house can just come and go unannounced. Don't leave anything valuable! Good luck. We left 10 days early. And we were glad to go. I know what the owner will say. "Why didn't you tell me?" But shouldn't an owner who constantly rents their property do more to make it livable, clean, sanity, and safe? Is it our job to point all this out to the Host? Who lives upstairs? And then the second bad experience… trying to post a review on AirBnB. We posted our review at the end of our rental which means it was available for AirBnB to review at any time. They wait 14 days to see if the owner is going to write a review too. After 13 days and 18 hours (late in the evening) AirBnB sent an email saying… "This is Zakee with Airbnb Experience Team. I wanted to reach out to you about the review that you left about the host (Jacinta). We wanted to let you know that we investigated the review and in the review you give out the address of the listing which is a violation of the Airbnb Policy, so because of that we will have to remove the review." We hadn’t listed the address, only the street numbers because of the problems we encountered. But, okay. No problem. We could make the tiny edits. But by the next day they said the "time limit" to edit the review was up. So the review did not appear. I called AirBnB four times and also emailed them. The operators were pleasant but in the end, no one would listen. I simply explained that they had not given us any time to make the tiny correction and that we wanted to post the review So we let the Host know about our review. She immediately threatened us writing, "Do not spread a bad review and rumors. I would consider it libelous to do so. The AirBnB lawyers will handle this." AirBnB prohibits "extortion" saying, "Reviews are a way for Airbnb guests and hosts to share their experiences with the community. Any attempt to use reviews or review responses to force a user to do something they aren't obligated to do is a misuse of reviews, and we don't allow it." And that includes, "Hosts asking a guest to take specific actions related to a review in exchange for a resolution to a dispute between the parties." Beyond that they say the Hosts and Guests agree to follow all Airbnb guidelines and policies, including the Extortion Policy and that failure to do so may result in the restriction, suspension or termination of your Airbnb account. "If you think you've experienced extortion, please contact us" which we did. No response. I know this is a lengthy review but if your experience was like ours, you will regret not paying attention to this story.

I've been an AirBnb user (and an outspoken supporter) for 8 years now. I will try to refrain from giving too many details, so please just keep the following things in mind if you plan to use Airbnb in China. 1. Remember your password. Logging in with Facebook and Google does not work, since Facebook and Google do not work in PRC. You might think a VPN could take you around, but it won't. VPNs were another disappointment during my trip. 2. Be aware that Google Maps does not work in China either. So the "directions" that the AirBnb app is giving you to find the place are unusable. 3. Be aware that the "translation" function in the AirBnb app does not cover all the text in the listings. There are fields that you can't even copy to paste into a translating app. So you might miss crucial info. Sometimes, the automatic translations are unusable because they make no sense. 4. Be aware that most Chinese people, old or young, urban or rural, don't speak a word of English. Most of your communication with the hosts will be conducted via translating apps. Also, some of the hosts will send you photos with written text do help you find the building, elevator, door. Most of the descriptions are in Chinese and cannot be translated from the photos. 5. Be advised that "self check-in" seems to be a rule with Airbnb in China. Consider yourself lucky to ever meet another human being. Prepare to navigate through a maze of directions to get to the address, to pick your room key (or code), to find the room and to check-in. Also, if you are given an access code to the room, write it down and keep it with you all the time, as some of them are 12 digits long and very hard to memorize. You'd leave your apartment to empty the garbage bin and won't be able to come back in. 6. Be aware that AirBnb is a big business for some Chinese hosts who manage tens of different units. For them, you'll be just a confirmation number and nothing more. Probably, Chinese tourists are easy going and don't mind if something is wrong with communication, access or amenities. Besides, it's easier for them to find a way around, because they understand and speak Chinese. But for a foreigner, trying to solve a problem with this "room warehouse" businesses improperly called "hosts" might impossible. Oh, and they are very good in saying "sorry". 7. If you think you'll have a better chance if you use the AirBnb PLUS option, which claims to feature "verified" properties, you will be wasting your time and money. Nobody seems to verify anything. 8. If you try to call the AirBnb phone number, you will be greeted by a robot in Chinese. 30 seconds into the call, the robot will hang up. No option to switch to English. 9. Messages to and from the hosts, sent via the AirBnb app, get through very slowly (sometimes up to 20 minutes). I suspect it has to do with the Chinese firewalls. However, if you're standing in the cold in front of a building trying to get your access code from a non-responding host, this can be extremely frustrating. Bottomline, the AirBnb you know (and maybe like) on Planet Earth is not the same AirBnb on Planet China. The only thing that's similar is their efficiency in taking your money. Other than that, you're more on less on your own.

The kitchen window lacks a screen so there was no way to get cross ventilation, if you can get the window open. The window shades were very dark. The bedside lamps were on very low tables and did not give enough light to allow reading in bed. Also, they were falling apart. The mechanism wobbled when I tried to turn them on or off . It had all appliances advertised and coffee, cream, honey, sugar, etc. Almost every surface area in the cabin was cluttered with decorative dusty objects. Where do you put your stuff if their stuff is everywhere? How do you plug in your phone, computer/pad and or pod with three outlets in the place and no surge protecting power strips?? To sum it up, the cabin interior was a disaster. The outdoor patio, however was a lovey area. Shaded by a natural tree canopy and festively decorated with outdoor lighting at night. Meanwhile, at every turn, AirBNB is suggesting you become a host, recommend a host, open up your home to guests, etc. They make the barrier to entry as a host so low there is no standard of quality. In my opinion, the term Superhost, means nothing. Based on my recent stay in TX, the reviews provide no meaningful information. Airbnb charged me after they promised they would not. They explicitly stated they would not (twice confirmed in writing), and they did it anyway. I had to leave the Airbnb because the Airbnb host was harassing me. The Airbnb host is not a well-adjusted person. I have booked into six Airbnb's to date and interacted with many others online. My experience is that hosts are difficult people to be around, desperately needing money, are using Airbnb against local public policy (and will note that only on upon arrival), are probably violating rules or regulations for their mortgages or home insurance, or they have other guests that are problematic as I experienced (e.g. poorly behaved, messy, mentally ill, coming and going at odd hours, staying up very late). I find it difficult living in a house with people like this. Also, the terms and conditions of Airbnb protect the hosts and do nothing for the end customer who also takes risks. I have since abandoned using Airbnb. I have found the same hosts advertising elsewhere for much less. But I have since returned to using hotels for the obvious known benefits. With a little research, hotels offer far better value, better locations, and are typically more reliable. For example, I recently booked two months in a brand new Hilton that has an on-site gym, great inclusive breakfast menu, nearby laundry facilities, beautiful view, lots of spaces to work, daily cleaning, etc. It was less costly than what good Airbnb rooms go for. I called ahead to request a room away from the elevator or in a quiet area. They were happy to accommodate. Also, in hotels, it's easy enough to make a request and get the help you want or need to make it a good easy stay. The good hotel people are trained to help out their clients and there are clear standard and rules for all. So, given that hotels are becoming more accommodating (e.g. they'll supply a mini-fridge, etc.) I can't see why Airbnb would be an option for me any longer. Generally, my experience with Airbnb is that they're rubbish and their customers (the hosts) are solely out to make money rather than run things like a legit alternative to standard approaches such as long term stay in hotels, resorts, and so on. The hosts don't identify with what they do. It is just about money. Also, I have always found an equitable solution while working with hotels. Hotels are after all legit regulated businesses with standards and employees who are most often educated in hospitality. I was attracted to the idea of putting my money in the hands of the Airbnb property owner, but I no longer see value in that in any way. I don't think Airbnb is a good company based on their policies and the way they handle things. In the end, I abandoned my room and lost over a thousands of dollars on a single bad Airbnb host.

ABSOLUTELY WILL NOT BOOK AN AIRBNB EVER AGAIN!!! We recently booked a house in LA which wasn't as advertised or reviewed. We subsequently came home, wrote an honest, but ultimately negative review, which a couple of days later was taken down by Airbnb. It seems they give more protection to their hosts than their guests, quoting that they are purely a platform for people to host their homes on. The house we stayed in was filthy, unhealthy and not secure!!! SAID REVIEW: I appreciate that reviews are given based on each individuals personal standards and expectations, so I have tried to give an honest account of 20548 Missionary Ridge Street, Walnut, LA, to try to give a true impression of what you can expect should you wish to stay there. If you’re in LA to visit Disney then the house is ideally placed, just 25/40 mins from both parks, in a lovely area just south of Walnut. If there are 8 to 10 of you, then the size of the property is great - 2 of you will get an en-suite, whilst the rest will share 2 further bathrooms, and there’s room for 3 cars on the drive. HOWEVER… Once you get in the property, things turn a little grubby, especially in the kitchen. I got the impression that the previous occupants, or more likely the owners, do a lot of cooking at the hob, with a lot of oil. - There were splats of grease all over the hob splash back that clearly hadn’t been cleaned. - The hob itself was greasy, with a greasy cooking pot left on it - clean inside bit splattered with grease on the outside. - All kitchen cupboard doors and handles were sticky to the touch - The Venetian blind in the kitchen was thick with dust, stuck to grease, which had also trapped insects by the look of it. - 2 kitchen draws hanging off and being held to the worktop with sticky-tape - The dishwasher wasn’t working… - …which is ironic, as there was no crockery to eat off of, just bags of paper plates and bowls, and a big box of plastic knives, forks and spoons - there was a token gesture of some cutlery, a set of 4 from IKEA still in it’s packaging. - And no kettle - but then there were only 3 mugs, so we took it in turns to drink tea or coffee in the mornings, once we’d boiled the water on the hob. - And no glasses to drink from, just tiny waxed paper cups, slightly bigger than a shot glass. The kitchen was the most disgusting part, but other parts of the house clearly hadn’t been cleaned for a while either… - There was thick dust on a number of surfaces, most noticeably on top of one headboards, the kitchen lights and extractor hood. - There was black grime on some light switches and Air-Con controllers - The TV had a layer of smeared grime all over it. (Personally, I’d sack the people who do the cleaning, because they’re not cleaners - OR, if the owners do it themselves, use the cleaning charge to actually pay some professional cleaners to do it. I would like a refund of the cleaning charge!! …and some!!!!) - Some bed sheets looked as though they’d been slept in a couple of times - very creased around the torso area - Windows, patio doors and mirrors had been wiped, but were left really smeary all over, and hand prints left on them from previous occupants - The mantle piece looked as though it would fall off the wall at any moment. - One of the bathroom sinks was cracked, and was badly repaired - As was a toilet seat in the en-suite - One of the double beds had no base, so the mattress was on the floor, with the bed frame around it, so the mattress subsequently sinks lower than the frame - The TV in the same bedroom was covered in white paint splatters, where they had painted the ceiling with a roller and not covered the TV - In another bedroom, the window frame didn’t actually fit the size of the window opening - I thought my wife had opened a window, only to find a 4cm gap either size of the window between the frame and the wall of the house. - No bath towels in the bathrooms - but found a pile in the garage - The house didn’t feel secure - I won’t go into detail why in this public review though. - There were 4 sun loungers outside, 2 of which had collapsed, with the screws sticking out. - And there was a can of 7 Up left out on the patio, which had clearly been there for some time as the print had all faded. - The BBQ was disgusting (wiped, not cleaned), and even the patio had large grease patches over it Personally, on the whole, I feel that 20548 Missionary Ridge Street needs a good freshening up and clean. It could be lovely, but it isn’t!! In it’s current condition, I would never ever book this house again, and I would advise anyone to do the same - don’t take the very high risk of disappointment!!! In it’s current condition, my view is that this house is not fit for holiday rental.

We had few good rentals in the past in USA thru airbnb. So the trust grew. But come summer of 2018, it all turned upside down. We visited Paris for 4 days. A night away in Netherlands in between resulted into two separate bookings. When we landed in Paris, we messaged the landlord of the 1st accommodation. There was no response for more than half an hour, unlike in the USA where the landlords called us much in advance to make sure we were on our way and had all the directions we needed. We waited for some time in the airport, and thinking he must be busy and a response would follow soon while we are on the way, we boarded a train in Paris subway to reach the station nearest to the property. I texted him couple of times more while in the train. No reply. A bit nervous in the station, we called him. No answer! It was a walking distance from the station to the property, so we walked, 4 of us, with large suitcases on wheels. Soon we knocked on the door, nobody opened. We could see people in an adjoining room, nobody responded to our knock! The fun just begun. Desperately we called airbnb, and asked for help, and she said she would check and get back to us. More than 15 mins later she did call back and admitted of having no luck contacting the property owner!!! "Would you want me to look for some alternative accommodations?" was the offer. We readily agreed, she assured refund. She said she would call back in 10 mins. !0 mins - 20 mins gone, no call came! It was 10 pm, dark by then, and we 4 strangers were standing on a by-road with luggage in a foreign land. A terrible airbnb experience was just starting unfold. We started calling nearby local hotels by then, but nobody was responding, though booking.com, hotels.com and similar sites were showing availability. We started attracting attention of the passing cars, passers-by and people in nearby houses by then, and soon a good Samaritan gentleman from the 2nd floor balcony of a nearby house took interest on us and spoke to us in English, and inquired why we were there. We explained. He expressed his sympathy and said it was not safe for us to stand like this on the road at that hour, and offered to help us by calling some hotels himself from his phone, as calls from his local number might have better chances of receiving an answer he explained. Soon he directed us to a hotel at a distance saying they said they had rooms but a little expensive. Desperate, we soon dashed off in a cab. We were still searching in the cab for any nearby accommodations at a reasonable price if available. My son showed me one, in airbnb, we still did not lose all the trust for one incident and one lady's forgetfulness to call us back. We decided to give it a try. We made a booking and redirected the cab. The neighborhood was desolate, a bit scary to strangers like us, cab was gone after we paid him, and we were not able to find the key for some time, as it was all dark where the instructions said the key would be. In the light of our mobile phones we kept searching, it was beyond 11pm by then. After a long flight from Canada, and all the tensions on the way, we were all very tired. Finally we found the key, made our entry into the property, and realized we were in the shabbiest property of all we have been in our life so far. All the dirty and used towels were heaped on the toilet bowl tank, bedsheets were as dirty as they could be and wrinkled from previous use, ugly all around, the windows did not close as they were broken, the list is long. We could not believe where we were, an airbnb accommodation in Paris!! The perception of class, culture, and sophistication that we had about Paris before coming took a nosedive! We were shocked and in disbelief for couple of mins, and then in disgust. Did not feel like even sitting anywhere in the rooms let alone sleep there overnight. It took us 5 mins, maybe because of our tiredness and trauma, to decide we needed to move out and get going. Soon we booked a hotel and called a cab and gone, at past 12 might by then, and the mistake we did in those moments of pain and shock was not to take any pictures of the shabbiness of the property. So the next morning, when from exotic Paris locations I was still dealing with airbnb over the phone on our nightmarish 'Paris experiences' the night before, courtesy of them, I was denied any refund flat out..... 3 nights later, when we were back from Netherlands and headed to our next airbnb accommodation, which we booked earlier from Canada, our Paris airbnb jinx followed us. Though the landlord responded to our messages this time, he kept the key in a near-by restaurant, and the key did not open the door :)) ... and this time the landlord went unresponsive! The people around watching us, a few strangers, trying to open a door for half an hour at 10:30 in the night was no fun. The door was right on a major road. Later, when we checked in a hotel at around 11:30pm, the landlord's message came in reply to our frantic calls earlier, 'sorry, I just saw your message, coming right now'!!!! We just got back from another vacation this summer in 2019 in Europe, and no airbnb this time, and it was all so good

I first did Airbnb in 2016/17 and it went well and I met good people, earned some money and felt secure and supported. However, having moved to a new area and now able to offer a few differences in the offered accommodation I have just started to offer Airbnb again. What a different story! Of the many enquires received, most have come from recently opened Airbnb accounts with no reviews and no information except the ‘reassurance’ of them having provided an email and telephone number. As a previous contributor stated, anyone can do this without any checks or guarantees. The ‘instant book’ had somehow been activated on my account, so late one night I was informed of the arrival of guest from China who clearly had little English, and was gender-less. Airbnb stated that if I declined this guest there would be a financial penalty and negative review on my posting. I felt trapped into providing accommodation to someone about whom I had NO information for very little financial gain (Airbnb encouraged me to offer 20% discount on my first three guests) with no reassurance or security for me and my family. Apart from one perfect guest and her young son, the other enquires were ‘odd’ to say the least (guests demanding phone calls; pre-viewings of the property; very extended stays; address details etc) that my family's security felt compromised. We are in a beautiful but remote location, and suddenly I am acutely aware of the drawbacks of Airbnb. For us, the risks out way the very modest financial return, and nowadays it would seem Airbnb are constantly trying to get hosts to slash their prices to encourage more guests; I do not remember any of this from my previous hosting experiences. I would strongly advise caution to anyone considering Airbnb using rooms within the family home. In many cases, checks in potential guests are minimal at best, non existent at worst. However due to my work situation, I have used Airbnb entire places a great deal this year and had wonderful, secure stays so it isn’t all bad. I just believe that you cannot be too careful who you allow into your family home and would warm anyone considering this type of Airbnb hosting to be very very careful about which enquiries they accept

We are so sorry that we became hosts on Airbnb. We spend hours trying to please guests who are dishonest (about having dogs with them or having more people on the reservation than they are paying for), do not follow the house rules (noise, parking, security), steal (toilet paper, cleaning supplies, and coffee) and try to get refunds for issues that they report after they've checked out. Hosts need to report a problem before the next guest checks in, but for guests there is no "statute of limitations" and we have to spend the time defending claims. Guests will say they want money back because one of the bedroom doors was locked (we didn't lock it, they never asked us to unlock it during the stay, we have a key on site, and we can't possibly prove whether it was locked or not after they've left). We have a "strict" cancellation policy, but guests are still given a full refund if they cancel at the last minute for "extenuating circumstances"--my favorite extenuating circumstance--our listing is in ski country and, over the winter holidays, we had a guest cancel the day of and receive a full refund for an entire week stay because it was snowing (right, ?). We've had police called because of guest behavior...we get the citation. Guests don't have to provide any proof or any documentation, but hosts are penalized constantly. It is way more trouble than it is worth and people who have short term rentals should go through a local tourist organization to receive better service.

Having had three successful trips I booked a country cottage in consett through air bnb, you have to pay up front which I did only to arrive at a small group of scruffy cottages, the one I got lumbered with was right next to a car park and had a bit of grass to the side of it which several youngsters were messing about on, the photo was nothing like the place we were supposed to stay at , that of course was delightful but in reality it was horrible. I asked to be moved or a refund and of course I was offered nothing, I complained to airbnb and they said that I hadn't made the cancellation in th proper way although I had asked to be refunded? Be very aware that airbnb only sides with the host in a complaint as its in both there interests. I am looking into the legalities of my situation. Please be aware if using this service.
I used to be a host at Airbnb, but not anymore. They keep banning my properties even when i have up with all the requiremnts

HOSTS BEWARE!!! We have been doing multiple vacation rentals for many years with different services. 2 years we started with Airbnb. We were pleased because we got many bookings until recently. We had a nightmare guest. She VIOLATED our house rules/policy. Pets are not allowed by the condo association and the resort where our condo is. We specifically told the guest this 3 months prior to her checking in. The morning after she checks in we get an urgent email from the resort’s Director of Operations and their Property Manager that our guest left a dog unattended in our condo and it was barking nonstop all morning disturbing other guests. This is subject to fines for owners. We immediately contact the guest who doesn’t respond to emails or texts. Hours later when she does finally respond she BLAMES us even though we told her IN WRITING that dogs are not allowed in our condo or anywhere in the complex. We work with Airbnb as this situation needs to be remedied ASAP as we have the resort on our back to fix the problem. The tenant refuses to work with us. Won’t respond to us. After speaking with Airbnb resolution Case Manager, they call her tell her she needs to leave she hangs up on them. Then another Airbnb case manager calls, emails and texts the guest with NO response from guest. We’re told that we can evict her due to the violation and lack of response and we don’t have to refund the guest for these reasons. We move forward with this plan (Airbnb Case Manager calls guest) the next day she vacates then we get an email from a third Case Manager informing us that Airbnb will he giving the GUEST a FULL refund less the two nights they stayed and we get NOTHING!!! Even though they can see she violated the rules, she wouldn’t work with us or them to resolve the issue and we had no choice but to take action. I spent 4 hours on the phone with Airbnb trying to remedy the situation to no avail even though they say we did nothing wrong we followed what we were supposed to do but they can’t help us! And the case manager who overturned the decision (he did NOT read the correspondence he only went by when the guest left) by the other 2 case managers, who actually read the entire correspondence would not respond to my phone calls or email. I warn you DO NOT I repeat DO NOT use Airbnb to host if you value your property. They WILL NOT support you in a bad renter event. Your place could be destroyed and they still won’t back you up!!!! We are pulling our listings immediately and are advising everyone we know to do the same. What a sad thing that they support bad behavior over doing the right thing.

I booked Corey's place in Waikiki Honolulu from July 8th-11th for my family of 4. We took a Lyft and on the way to his place we recieved a message about cancellation last minute. He lied to us about his condo's electric door being broken and advised to give his condo (#3003) a look for proof. I did check it out the next morning and I heard people talking inside the room. The compensation was not enough compared to the stress we had went through during our vacation. He controlled the situation to make me pay additional fees out of my pocket and bullied me to gave a defamatory review. Even after the vacation, the situation with Corey still haunts me, especially with this review, and I don't have a voice. To fix this situation, I request my full refund and my additional fees and remove the defamatory review about me. Corey will give Airbnb a bad name. How can I trust Airbnb and recommend my clients and friends to a service that I've had such a negative experience with? Jessica

The worst. All canned response with no meat. It makes me anxious that these are the people that are supposed to be there in an emergency to help you. They ARE NOT. For the service fees they charge, they need to be our advocates and do a better job of filtering their hosts. They also don't post negative reviews. The reviews are so disingenuous. All 5 stars. Not a trustworthy company. RUN!

Disappointing ! Airbnb deceiving the customers because they offer accomodation for unreal prices with discount but the owners of the flats don't know about it. Then if you book it and pay, later you get from owner cancellation because they are shocked for which price Airbnb sold it. It's really disappointing because they keep your money and you have to deal many hours with that and try to get your money back. If it happend, NEVER cancel the booking on your side otherwise they will not refund all your money. The owner must do it! If I could rate less than one I would - awful service and awful people - try to avoid Made a booking that insisted on instant payment, went through process and made payment, got receipt and 2 hours later and email saying price was wrong and I shouldn’t have been able to book, yet it’s still now on at same price and free to book. Spent the next 7 hours trying to get a refund, they don’t care at all won’t help, are quite rude and take no responsibility.

What a mess this app is!!!! I have booked a flat in Rome 14 days before travel and for some urgency I cancelled 4 days after, and guess what they refunded me only 50%. This app should close down, they are stealing people’s money....

Downloaded app on iPhone and iPad but white screen. Tried to login via app and web but says no account linked to email address but when I sign up says there is an account linked to my email address! Which one is it please? No response from air bnb and cannot contact!

Very dissappointed with Airbnb customer support.
