Their staff is the worst customer oriented people I have ever contacted. They are useless to handle situations and impossible to communicate with. Stay away from these rubbish and use other booking agents. It’s cheap in commission but it becomes expensive if you need help as their staff are insane

Airbnb uses misleading ads and it is impossible to communicate with the host, although the ads give the impression that such communication is possible and easy. Further Airbnb does not include negative reviews on the sites for each property so potential guests searching for the right property never see any negatives - everything is "5 Star" ratings! My stay at the "Playground" in Milwaukie, Oregon (suburb of Portland) was for a family of 10 gathering for 5 nights at $850/night. We left after 2 nights! Dealing with Airbnb is a disaster and I will never recommend them to anyone. Further, my wife and I travel extensively in the USA and outside the USA, with more than 90 nights per year in travel. The "Playground" is way way overpriced and a hodgepodge of construction imposing climbing 20 steep stairs just to get to the main living area with no accommodations for the entire family to eat meals together - only 4 chairs per table and with the tables in separate rooms! There is only seating for 3-4 people for one TV and the other TV is on the third floor with no seating at all!

Disappointed with Airbnb customer service. Terrible experience with a Airbnb in London. Have tried to raise the issue but Airbnb have been very unsympathetic. Would appreciate a better resolution than we’ve had so far! - Area was dangerous - Neighbours listening to extremely loud music until 2am - Check in was late and incorrect key left - Exposed electrical sockets/wires - Back door couldn’t lock - Sofa bed wasn’t a bed, and had no bedding and had half the springs missing - Cracked/broken mirror - Dirty bathroom - People vomiting outside of the house - Cars racing around the street - Wardrobe doors had fallen off - filthy unusable conservatory - plastic cutlery - Very ‘rough’ area with lots of fighting and felt unsafe - especially staying with family, including a 10yr old girl. All this in a property described as a Luxury London House. Paid approx £350 for the night. Totally miss-sold. We complained the day after early in the morning but apparently that was too late to complain to Airbnb. We took ample pictures but apparently non very evidence enough to warrant a refund or an investigation in to the listing. We have spent £1000’s with Airbnb, stayed in over 40 Airbnb’s. this was by far the worst. As a very regular user (we are about to stay in one in Portugal for the next week!) it’s knocked our confidence as to how well checked these listings are, and how well we, as CUSTOMERS, are treated when experiences are far below par.

Careful - you can deactivate but not clear your profile! I was trying to clear my profile in 2018. You can´t do it by your own. I asked the customer service. I was asked to sent a copy of my identification card. I did. I never got any confirmation. My profile is deactivated, I can´t sign in. I still don´t know weather my profile is cleared, or weather I´m still with the statistics. In my long period of membership I visited different homes in different countries. My overall experiences were so far satisfying. When I met problems with the host or the flat (which was seldom but happened!) we solved it (more or less) without AirBnB but with the host. My few personal contacts with AirBnB had been rather stressing because I never got any answer in time, and my contacts changed before a problem was solved. But Airbnb changed. The rooms/appartements offered with AirBnB are actually more expensive than a local hotel. Even if you just book one night you have to pay not only service- but also cleaning fees. The final price is much higher than the price advertised, very annoying! A room in a little lokal hotel, with own bathroom and breakfast is about the same price as a room in a “privat” home booked via Airbnb. Lot´s of advantages with a Hotel: Easy cancelation or rebooking without unexpected fees (just read the booking-conditions of the hotel). Mostly 24 hours reception and somebody to address if something is wrong!

I wanted to book a holiday home through AirBNB. When I finally found a place to my liking, I started the booking process. Doing so I was surprised to find how eager AirBNB is to collect personal data from me. So I dug into the privacy statement of this 'company'. I was shocked to read how they treat our personal data and monetize on it. Also the amount of data they collect is staggering. They would surely demand your first born child and your soul if they could. But worst of all, I did some more research on this topic and found out that AirBNB tells concerned (European) clients bluntly that there's no reason for them to comply with the European GDPR-legislation (online privacy). Once you have made the mistake of giving AirBNB your data, you will have a hard time to get them to turn it over to you again. So one could argue that indeed they DO take your soul... Please don't fall for the temptation! It is not worth it. I found out that AirBNB is actually rather expensive. Other (less intrusive) online platforms offer great accomodations at far better prices (and most of them are GDPR-compliant).

I didn't think a tech company could have this bad of customer service, but I have been proven wrong. This isn't about a particular host. Having stayed with many hosts, I have had, for the most part, good experiences. This is entirely about the company's lack of customer service. My story: I had booked a home for 10 people for three days. The night before our first night at 9:45pm, I received an email canceling the listing. Nothing else was said, no help, just a notice that it had been cancelled. After a very poor night's sleep, I booked a number of hotel rooms to make sure my party was covered. The day of our first night's stay, at 3:30pm, customer service called me to see if they could assist me in finding new AirBnB listings. I mean, what?? It was basically a half an hour before we were checking into our hotel rooms. What did they think I was doing the last 18 hours, waiting for their call? Anyway, they refunded the deposit I made and agreed that they would pay the difference between what I ended up paying and the deposit, providing I sent them receipts. This I did when I got home from the trip. It has now been over three weeks. Four emails and two phone calls later, I have heard nothing from the company. The last information I received was that the refund had to be run by another department. OK. After three weeks, you can't get an internal decision made? I have an Alaska vacation scheduled in two weeks and the bookings I have made with Airbnb for the holiday will be my last. They do not have their act together.

Please be aware guests - if you arrive after 12 am PACIFIC STANDARD TIME and need to cancel due to unsafe or "Not as listed" issues, AIRBB corporate will not help you recoup your reservation $. Otherwise, 98% of the time, AIRBB has been really great due to the hardworking hosts.
Airbnb has horrible customer service. I am amazed they are able to do business. I will never use them over Vrbo or homeaway again.

Beware!!! Host canceled my trip 72 hours before I was to arrive making my family scramble for accommodations. Confirmation was given in April and we were to arrive in July- so here it was July 3 and I got a cancellation. WHAT!!!!! We bought everything for the trip, rented a car, had scheduled our vacations and then just cancel??? They should not allow hosts to cancel so close to arrivals. Because everything was already, I had to contact another travel site and find a house which of course was triple in price for my family. Then Airbnb sends me a 48 dollar credit to use towards another house??? Fat chance that I’d ever trust this site again. This trip was supposed to cost me 1000 dollars and it ended up costing me 3000- absolute bull.
Not the best customer service if problem occur

Beware of units with rates subject to change. We have been looking to book a place in 2020 through Airbnb. Multiple homes have prices listed that the owners aren't honoring the price. This has been going on since at least 2016 and I felt it is time to start making people aware. If you book it now the owner will cancel the reservation or email you with a much higher price. It is a waste of time researching their property only to find out the price isn't valid.
I had a host accept me then give my bed to someone else. I contacted Airbnb but they sided with the host. Both the host and Airbnb were rude to me.

Disgusting customer support. I am a host with several apartments and when I called for help with one of my guests I have been told that my case is not important enough to deal with right now and that someone will call me back. Disgusting support.
Host cancels at very short notice and support will do nothing to help you.

I had two open support cases on my trip here to NZ concerning different issues. One issue was quite difficult as it concerned changing a long term booking. I got a variety of different case managers, which got a bit chaotic. In the end, my case manager Chay was incredibly helpful and made me really believe in the AirBnB experience again. The second issue was more technical than having to do with the apartment itself, but the case manager Tito was also very helpful and kind. Honestly, I feel like if you just bring a bit of patience when talking to support you will be helped eventually and they will do their absolute best!

A bad experience from the HOST after my feedback to airbnb. I’ve recently been to Liverpool on the training and needed to stay in Anfield home for my 2 days training. But my training ended up in one day, so needed to cancel my 2nd night booking. I contacted airbnb if there are any possibilities to refund some part of 1 night (that was cancelled by me) stay, but they said they can try, but not sure. Finally, airbnb contacted and said that they couldn’t refund any part of cancelled night. I just ignored after that. But few days later, I received a feedback email from airbnb to the email using which the room was booked. I provided the feedback ratings as ‘good’ for all the points except the ‘value’ that I gave low rating. My feedback was shared to the host who sent a private message with abusive words, after that I responded for that message, anyway. But the host contacted to airbnb and asked to remove my feedback (quoted with out of policy), and airbnb has now removed it (as per their email communication to the concerned email address), by justifying that the feedback was not provided by guest. The room was booked by my husband using his login and he booked the room, but during that time they accepted the payment and booking. But at the time of feedback which they sent to the concerned email, they said that it was not from guest’s experience. This is not fair. If they want a feedback from the guest, they must have collected my email address (or) accept the review comments that I gave from my husband’s login. The host has hurt me a lot with the abusive words in a private message (after my feedback) using airbnb messaging and I never expected this. The bottom line is, airbnb are supporting and favouring only to the host, but I don’t say they have to be in favour (or support) to me, but they have to stand on both the side and accept the right feedback without any excuse like ‘guest personal experience not shared’ when I gave the feedback. When guests give low rating for any of the criteria that they have, airbnb and the host have now a full control to remove the feedback leaving customers/guests valuable feedback aside, this is unfair.

Has anyone successfully deleted their account with airbnb? I do not want to deactivate my account. I want to remove it entirely from airbnb as I was unhappy with their service. Airbnb then say they will get someone from another department to contact me. Again noboday did. Is it so difficult to delete an account with Airbnb?

I bought an accommodation in south coast ....Just 2 days before check in their host cancelled my booked - paid accommodation. Thanks for quick refund..

Do not count on customer service to provide actual customer service. Airbnb expects hosts to provide this amazing guest experiences and service, yet, at the corporate level they fall short. My new initial experience has not been favorable. THIS IS NOT A REFLECTION ON THE HOSTS. THIS IS A COMPLAINT ABOUT AIRBNB CORPORATE. This has been the second worst customer service experience in recent history for me. The worst customer service experience in the past 10 years has been with Quickbooks. Second worst experience, Airbnb! Would give 0 stars I could. Had reservations about joining airbnb because of the lack of security and accountability for some hosts. I have used VRBO without incident for years. I recently booked 2 reservations on airbnb, one for personal and one for business. There were problems with both. The first I was able to resolve online without too much incident. There was a glitch in the system and I was able to confirm my reservation the following day. No big deal, just a hiccup. The second issue involved payment. I simply want to change payment method after my card had been charged. I attempted to change the payment method before the deduction and could not via the website. I have now been on hold for maybe 45 minutes with customer service just to try to change my payment method. Airbnb sends a very clear message that travelers are not their main concern! Message coming through loud and clear. As a paying customer, my requests don't matter. My request is to change my payment method. That is all I am asking for. As the owner of a business, if someone wants to change the way they pay me money, no problem! Easy.

Airbnb doesn’t even deserve one star. The most disappointed and definitely the worst experience on vacation ever. The rental property was nothing as it stated and with that case the overpayment to rent the property was extreme. The house was dirty and needed to be sprayed for bugs. Our party included 11 family members and 5 of those were children. Would never recommend this company.

Booked a private flat in Zurich. All reviews and photos were perfect. Excellent customer satisfaction. Used Airbnb in Cancun, Mexico during the month of February and a 4 star rating is not enough. We were presented with a bottle of wine and fruits and the place was so beautiful with a huge pool and gym. I will use Airbnb in the future, much cheaper than a 4 star hotel.

HOSTS BE AWARE AIRBNB DOES NOT CARE ABOUT THE HOSTS IF A GUEST WANTS TO CANCEL THEIR BOOKING AFTER CHECK IN, ALL THEY HAVE TO DO IS BREAK THE AIRBNB RULES, AT WHICH POINT AIRBNB WILL REFUND THE GUEST THEIR MONEY AND LET THE HOST BE OUT OF POCKET. DO NOT USE AIRBNB FOR HOSTING! I HAVE HOSTED FOR TWO YEARS AND THIS IS A DISGRACE!

I decided to take my family to Orlando for a back to school vacay. So we booked a house through airbnb the host accepted it and we paid the fees. The host apologized and offered us a discount the next time we came through, This is unacceptable I said as we have already made arrangements through our work except etc to be gone for this weekend. We don't have an additional 600 to book another house nor can we get a refund for our activities we booked in Orlando. So even though the host broke how many rules I don't need the know air BNB could not do anything about it basically told us hopefully your money will be refunded in time and you can book another place. How rude!!! How do I explain to my 3 children and to God children that the vacation we had been planning for 3 months has now gone down the drain? No one at the company with sympathetic they offered as a $43 coupon which 1st time renter gets 55 this is our 1st time so now what now we're screwed. This is our 1st family vacation in 5 years (due to my mom being very sick) and now it has gone down the drain.

This will be my LAST time every going through this company to book a place. My family booked a house in Williamsport PA, for a week and the website overbook the house. I was the first to reserve and put a deposit on the house and AIRBNB is refusing to cancel the other family reservation. Also I am staying for a longer stay. It's 3 days until I'm suppose to leave and have no clue what is going on because the AIRBNB is leaving the decision up to the other family if they want to cancel their reservation. WHO DOES THAT!

IF I COULD GIVE ZERO STARS, I WOULD. During a recent trip to DC (2 weeks ago - July 4, 2019 weekend) we experienced an absolute TERRIBLE experience with HOST CLIFF and Airbnb SUPPORT. **BEWARE** ... IF SOMETHING is WRONG WHEN YOU ARRIVE ... **CONTACT Airbnb WITHIN 24 HOURS OF YOUR ARRIVAL**!! You MUST give HOST a chance to fix it FIRST, however if they don't resolve your issue IMMEDIATELY, THEN CALL Airbnb IMMEDIATELY! **YOU WILL NOT get resolution if you DONT CONTACT THEM WITHIN THE FIRST 24 HOURS**. Make sure YOU TAKE PICTURES. Take SCREEN SHOTS of communication (or lack of) and PRINT THEM OUT. Airbnb WILL SIDE with HOST. They WILL TELL ITS NOT a TYPICAL Airbnb experience AND YET, they WON'T resolve your issue, even when escalated to a Specialist!! We PAID almost $2,4000 for a 4 day stay PLUS $50 more for an additional parking spot. We didn't get the permit until we had been there for 3 DAYS. (We paid for it over 2 weeks before and Host Cliff told us he was on his way to get it the day BEFORE our stay was to begin). But, in Fact it wasn't dated until the day we received it. Our basement BEDROOM floor was FLOODED and Host Cliff told us it was a Holiday and COULDN'T get anyone out to FIX IT, until the next day. We insisted he do something that night ($600 a night and we can't use one bedroom? No way). So, he did. One TV didn't work and it was also 3 days before it was fixed. It was a house for 8 people, but only had utensils for 5!! Imagine our only one big meal together the night before we left, and we had to eat in shifts. There are more issues ... however these were the most important. WE DEFINITELY will NOT USE HOST CLIFF'S houses in the future. However, we also WONT USE Airbnb IN THE FUTURE EITHER. IF YOU DECIDE TO USE Airbnb, then do so AT YOUR OWN RISK. AND FOLLOW THE PROCEDURE ABOVE. We tried to be polite, and not cause our Host inconvenience ... Don't do that!!

I had a few very good stays with airbnb hosts, until this past spring in Seattle, where one of the hosts totally misrepresented her property as a quiet studio apartment in a house. It was basically a glorified room with paper thin walls, extremely noisy people also staying in the house, and mold that made my allergies even worse. I had to cancel and offered to pay for an extra night as well as any cancellation fees. I had to find another airbnb to stay in, which was very nice fortunately. After no reply whatsoever from the previous host, I got airbnb involved and decided that asking for two thirds of my money back was not unreasonable. Airbnb at first responded that they were looking into it, and then nothing despite my repeated follow-up call and emails. Apparently, they have sided with the host.

Similar experience as other reviewers. I once rented a flat in Paris through Airbnb and after I paid and asked how to get in, the owner stopped writing back. I spent several anxious days until finally she condescended to tell me “get the keys from the concierge”. When I complained to her that she could have spent 30 seconds to tell me that three days earlier, she wrote back that she had been too busy to write me earlier. When I got to the apartment, it was shabby and dilapidated, not at all like the photos, and the bathroom was in two separate sections at opposite ends of the flat. Then when I posted a negative review on Airbnb, the owner sniped back that I was a “dirty tenant”. Some people seem to have good luck on Airbnb, but in my opinion now that so many people are trying to let their houses or flats, there is too high a risk of getting cheated, mistreated, spy-cammed, or worse. I wouldn’t ever do this again, and you shouldn’t either unless the Airbnb host has hundreds of good reviews (not just dozens - too easy to fake) for a specific unit.

We stayed a week in a campervan in bristol and found that nearly all the amenities he offered were non existing. There was no hit water like he said and the battery was left next to dead and the toilet half full. Imho said twice we can use the tv to turn up and be told we cant as itll kill the battery. The guy would purposely always talk in person so there was no proof to airbnb. The property was unsafe as we all cut ourselves on a piece of the furniture and found the carbon monoxide detector was faulty. We reported all of this within the week. But because airbnb had taken days to reply it had gone outside of our reservation period. All they had to say was that they cant guarantee anything as holiday is now over. This was there fault. I have spoken to three different people and none care about how dangerous the property was. Because I couldn't prove there was no hot water they didnt care even though the hsot changed his description to saying no hot water. Apparently the host admitting it wasnt enough proof. I have taken a case up with paypal as airbnb at times would ignore me for over a week or two. I will be getting my money back and never come back. The hsot also acused us of taking a pet as there was hair everywhere even though we dont own a pet and we made sure it was clean when we left of which we found mo hair.

I feel completely screwed by Airbnb. My family lost almost 900.00 because of them. We cancelled a trip due to the fact that our family would exceed the occupancy number for a particular property and re booked another place. We received a response that we would be expecting a refund for our cancellation, but never got it and now are told we did not qualify for it. Read all the fine print folks....they have a way of deceiving! Will never use them again and do not reccommend!

This was our first time using AirB&B and was a terrible experience. The property not as advertised. Owner residence attached and backyard amenities shared. Pictures that indicate this information are not provided on listing. Aaron, the Host showed lack of responsibility by not informing owner about our rental requirements made prior to reserving and showed no willingness to address our rental concerns. Owner planned a 4 hour event inviting guests and dogs in the shared backyard without regard to our presence. We were compelled to leave due to lack of respect for our reservation and requested private space. Neither host or AirBnB assisted us in this debacle. We were given minimal refund and required to find a new location on our own. Spent an entire day without a place to stay for our family (several who flew to SD for this vacation), and our two dogs. Paid service fees twice. Lost our 7 day discount. Paid cleaning fees for a house with mildew and urine smell, along with body odor from unclean comforter and mattress cover in the main bedroom. He also informed to me that hosts don't like to cancel the reservations because they can be charged up to a $100 cancellation fee. In other words, Airbnb profited from my misfortune. I was very disappointed with my recent Airbnb experience. My family and I arrived at our Airbnb property on Saturday, the 15th of June 2019 in Santorini, Greece and found the property to be dirty and most importantly, the upstairs bathroom was covered in black mold. I immediately went onto the Airbnb website to figure out what to do and found a hotel on the other side of the island to check into for the night. We messaged our Airbnb host who told us that the house was in fact clean and she thought we were using this as an excuse to stay in a different part of the island and that she wouldn't be offering a refund or amending our reservation. Airbnb's help chat window mentions that their customer service team usually gets back to you within an hour. Well, 10 hours later and still no response, I called the Airbnb phone number to explain the situation. The person on the phone was very helpful and asked if I was in a safe place - I said I was as I had checked into a hotel (which also has properties on Airbnb) and gave her the name of the property. She asked me to send photos of the property which we took and they would get back to me very soon to discuss next steps. The entire day went by and after multiple additional chat messages asking me to provide more details, I still didn't receive a phone call or instructions on next steps. I booked myself a second night at the hotel. First thing in the morning on the second day of my holiday, I called Airbnb again and was told that the person who was managing my case was aware and would get back to me very soon. Finally, 5 hours later, I received a phone call from someone who identified herself as my case manager and asked me for all of the details I had already provided to the other Airbnb representatives. She said she had been in touch with the host and the host said that they painted over the mold and whether we would stay in the property now. On top of the fact that my cousin has OCD and physically wouldn't be able to re-enter the house, we didn't feel comfortable going back to this home after our Airbnb host openly told us they felt we were lying. Airbnb got back in touch with our host and finally agreed to cancel the rest of our reservation. While I'm appreciative that Airbnb was able to resolve the issue, however, there were many elements of the experience which made me feel unsafe: (1) Airbnb told me that we would still have to pay for the nights we did stay in the house (2 full days now) but we never did stay at the property. We were never told upfront about this and there's no information on the website mentioning this. Furthermore, it took Airbnb almost 48 hours to resolve the issue and had they managed this sooner, this wouldn't have been a problem (2) They asked me to meet our host to give the key to the property back. When I did, our host told us we were bad people and liars. I would have felt more comfortable if Airbnb had provided us with a location to drop off the key for the combative host. (3) Airbnb was very unresponsive and uncommunicative during the process - I had stayed at multiple Airbnb's in the past and never had an issue. Now that I have had an issue with a property, it's clear their sub-par customer service isn't equipped to help their customers the way a hotel would. Overall, they did resolve the issue but very poorly.

Airbnb's biased rating system and stringent host requirements, are designed to make us outcompete 5-star hotels and each other. This is all great news for guests who get more, and more, and more for their buck and, as such, Airbnb, who laughs its way to the bank - for hosts, however, this is lunacy. We are being forced to accept reservations from people with nothing but a first name, no photo, no other identifying information. If we decline, our "acceptance rate" goes down and our listing ends up at the very bottom of the search results. Hotels require you to show an ID upon check-in, not Airbnb. Anyone can create an account with a fake name--even change it at any time. As hosts we are required to upload a government-issued ID to become "verified". We are required to have a profile pic. Not if you are a guest. So much for transparency. At the Hilton, if you don't follow the rules, you’ll end up on the street or heavily penalized. If you happen to break something, your credit card will be charged, no questions asked. If you do not show up at the restaurant at the time of reservation, your table will be gone. If you decide to check out early, kiss goodbye to the remainder of your money. Not so with Airbnb. Good luck, trying to have Airbnb help you when a guest breaks something or violates your house rules. Their "million-dollar-host-guarantee" is largely a scam, designed to falsely put hosts minds at ease. Good luck trying to get compensated when something goes wrong.

First off, I've been an apartment rental manager for 50+ 1 bedroom, 2 bedroom, and 3 bedroom units. I've done extensive background checks on prospective residents because it is my personal policy to rent only to people I feel safe with and people I would be willing to have as a neighbor. In 30+ years, I've turned away hundreds of people due to safety concerns (convicted felons, drunk drivers, domestic abusers, disorderly conduct, pedophiles, prostitution, etc, and yes, one convicted murderer out after a 20 year sentence---this in a town with a population of 104,000). There have only been a handful of people I've rented to who I wouldn't rent to again (problem personalities). My units are not lower end, and are usually occupied by professional people, often health care workers, attorneys, engineers. For the most part I've fully refunded security deposits. I loved the rental business UNTIL I listed with Airbnb... I booked with someone who met airbnb's criteria, only to find out this individual lied on his "application", and the lie was serious enough for me to question the safety of allowing this prospective "guest" on my property (and jeopardizing the safety of my current residents) so I IMMEDIATELY cancelled the reservation. I was penalized $100 for cancellation within a 24 hour period of the guests move in date, and I was penalized ratings wise because I cancelled a booked reservation. After a considerable amount of time spent with their customer service reps (sic), $100 was refunded but I still lost $1000 of "rent" that I could have had, if the unit had been booked to a person who was "safe". I consider myself a responsible host and would not knowingly host someone who could potentially endanger the safety of my guests or me, but some hosts would put money before safety and airbnb doesn't screen out those hosts based on where some of those properties are located (believe me, the location stars mean nothing). Oh, and when I realized I was dealing with a potentially unsafe "guest" I immediately contacted airbnb by phone and was put on hold indefinitely so I finally hung up and then sent them a "live chat" message on their site and this "live chat' was responded to the next day, more than 24 hours later. Airbnb has a limited ability to do background checks on guests and hosts. And the hosts have less ability than airbnb to check their guests. A picture id and a credit card just aren't going to ensure your safety folks. And important here, ONLY the guest has been "approved" by airbnb. As a host (and neighboring airbnb guest) you have ABSOLUTELY NO IDEA OF WHO THE GUEST(s) IS SHARING THE APARTMENT WITH!!! (I know of no cameras that provide contact info of unregistered guests). On the evening of Monday, March 18 I made a reservation for a condo in Florida for 11 days (March 29 – April 8) as a birthday gift for my adult son. I explained the fact that I was making this booking as a gift for someone else in the notes section while making the reservation. I’ve used Airbnb before and making the reservation was seamless and easy. I got a confirmation back pretty quickly and my card was charged the $1479.33 required. At the host’s request, I also made an additional payment of $100 to cover daily parking. The host contacted me that same evening saying that since this was a gift and I wasn’t the person who would be on site, then I should upload my son’s ID, which I did immediately. On March 21, I get my final confirmation from Airbnb via email that says, “Pack your bags…”. Sadly, this is where the good news ends. On the same day I got an email from “Lance O” at “response @Airbnb that began with “It looks like you've uploaded someone else's identification!” – I responded saying that I did in fact upload another person’s ID at the host’s request because this was a gift, etc. No one responded back. I figured no harm could be done by also uploading my ID. I did so. The first time there seemed to be some sort of glitch and I wasn’t at all certain that the upload had been successful. I tried again. This time the upload was confirmed. Later that day I attempted to login into Airbnb only to find that my account was locked “temporarily”. I checked again later and found that I was still locked out. I became concerned. I called their 855 #. I spoke with “Jerson”. He said that he couldn’t help me and that a “specialist” would contact me within 24-48 hours. I thought that was too long to wait, so I pushed back. He said there was nothing that he could do, so he prioritized my “case”. At about 36 hours into the wait, I realized no one was going to contact me. I called the 855 # again and this time I got “Amanda” who gave me the same line but assured me that my case had been given “high priority” because the dates for the trip were coming up quickly. I finally took to Google to research the best way to get results from Airbnb since I was clearly getting nowhere. I stumbled onto a long blog where literally hundreds of people had similar experiences, and many had gone unresolved. But one guy suggested DM’ing AirbnbHelp on Twitter. I did that. Someone did respond pretty quickly. They asked for further identifying info. I supplied it immediately. They suggested that I respond again to Lance’s email and re-explain the situation to him. I did that on Friday, the 22nd. Lance or some reasonable facsimile never responded. Twitter gets back to me again to say that I have been assigned a “Case Manager” who would email me “shortly”. Nothing. With each day that has passed since that time, I sent additional DMs on Twitter and several emails to “Lance O.” and I was promised time and time again that someone would get back to me asap. When I reached 120 hrs. since my original call to the 855 # with no one contacting me as to why I’m locked out of my account, I called again. I spoke with “Jessica” who tried more than the others to get a response. She put me on hold a few times to contact the “other specialists” to see if she could get some sort of answer or give me an exact time for a response. Nothing. Again. This is the absolute worst customer service I’ve ever experienced with any vendor of any kind. I’m a serial traveler and have booked many trips with VRBO, HomeAway, PlumGuide (overseas), Relais and Chateau and others. I’ve used Airbnb before too. In the interim, my son began his drive to FL not knowing what he would find. We tried making alternate reservations through another service but all of them required a long lead time to cancel and we didn't want to get stuck with two reservations. It didn't appear that aibnb cancelled my reservation, but I had no way of knowing of that for sure bc they cut me off from the host. They had not reversed the charges to my bank - - nor did I want that to be the end result. I wanted access to my account again and wanted to stop being ignored and treated like a criminal. I deserved an answer as to why this happened in the first place and never got one until I was sent an email message that arrived 240 hours after I was promised a response within 24-48 hours. That was when I was notified that Airbnb didn't allow 3rd party bookings. I could have been told that immediately because I put notes in my reservation request saying that I was booking this as a gift for someone else. They took my money immediately and before I was locked out of my account, the host agreed to allow me to book this trip as a gift for my son. I was 100% upfront about that with Airbnb and the Host from the get-go. They took my money right away even though I “violated” a policy I was unaware of. Why couldn’t someone tell me that immediately and I would have rectified it by having my son book the trip for himself and put it on my card???? Why did I have to wait 10 days for an answer? The most abysmal customer service experience that I’ve ever had. STAY AWAY. VRBO OR HOME AWAY MUCH, MUCH MUCH BETTER IN EVERY WAY.

Long story short, as I write this review I am preparing myself to sleep on the street in a foreign country as Air BnB cancelled my booked accommodation (the agency, not the host) have yet to give me a refund and in 8 hours have not helped my situation one bit. Instead I have been told by several agents how their shift is finishing soon and they don’t have anymore time to help me. Debbie was a particularly awful representative during this process. I always believe that you can only find out the true value of a company are when the chips are down and how they deal with a complaint. Below is the complaint I put through to Airbnb support. They promised to update me immediately. Nothing has happened. I placed a bad review about the accommodation, guess what it hasn't appeared! Read my review, judge for yourself. I will not be using them again and in fact I am setting up my own Airbnb complaint website. As I explained to you, I had spinal surgery Wednesday. I also had planned to go sea fishing Friday and Saturday, before you say anything, my wife thought it was a bad idea! We have been fishing at Penarth several times a year for a number of years and will continue to do so. I have booked property with Airbnb and others and have never had a problem. I believe no hosts have ever had a mark against me and nor I with anyone else. I booked this accommodation last minute but was told no problem and we arrived at about 5.30 dropped our bags and went off to buy some food for the next few days. When we came back, we wanted to make a cup of tea, my friend looked round but found no cups. He opened the dishwasher to a really bad smell. The cups and glasses inside were full of mould and mildew. He washed what we needed and then put the dishwasher on to deep clean. When we started looking round the house we noticed plug in air freshner's everywhere. We believe this was to cover up the smell in the house. I went upstairs to the ensuite room, initially couldn't find the light switch for the bathroom. I then found it behind the wardrobe! Inside the bathroom was a stained floor, the bottom of the shower door was full of mildew and mould, as is on the sides, some in the tiles. The sink didn't drain properly. The dirty blind had slits missing. Into the bedroom. One set of plugs had inserts, there was no lamp by the bed, no sockets by the bed, had to unplug the TV to plug in a charging unit. They seem to like drilling the walls. Looks like they had installed the TV and then kept moving it, leaving the holes behind! Damp spots in ceiling. Same in the other bedroom and bathroom. More slits missing from the blinds in the other rooms. Edges on windows were rusty and needed replacing. I have included pictures showing just a handful of problems, in order to show the full extent I'd have had to spend ages photographing everything. I would have left there on the first night but by that time I knew I didn't have enough time to sort another place plus I was very sore from Wednesday surgery. We were out each day from 6am returning 7-9pm. Hence why I didn't leave, no time to sort out a new place to stay plus as I was out on a boat with no signal I was unable to do anything during the day. You have informed me that the price for the rental is decided by the host plus you never check the properties. That means I can no longer trust any property from Airbnb. I have never complained before, I have never had a complaint against me either. I cannot understand what mindset these people have that they think they can charge this price! If I hadn't stayed on numerous occasions near there in great accomodation at a much better price I might have said nothing except to the host. Someone needs to take them to see other properties in their area to see how a house needs to be maintained. I also said nothing to them because most of the faults require building work to take place and cannot be done in 5 minutes. Some serious money needs to be spent to remove the tatty carpets and rugs, the shabby, cheap secondhand sofa, the wardrobe, put more sockets in, especially the bedrooms, bedside lights, fix the damp and mould, fix the drains, fix the blinds, put hand towels in the bathrooms, in the kitchen. I went to remove a pot of salt and it stuck to bottom of the cupboard shelf! The kitchen hob extractor needs cleaning, badly. Removal of the 2 additional fridge freezers in the conservatory, which by the way stink. The kitchen freezer bottom is covered in mould. Cupboard door hinges need fixing or replacing. Mould under the sink where they have stored the vacuum cleaner. Mop removed from bathroom. Leave the hot water on when a guest is arriving. The electric shower unit in the ensuite bathroom has missing panels in the top as well as mould and also mould underneath. Broken mirrors is another one. How much more do you need me to write??? They should be barred from listing on your site immediately. I am making this complaint because I don't want others to put up with this shambles. I am disgusted with Airbnb for not visiting their sites.

If I could give Airbnb zero stars for the last month of trying to book a rental I would. Let me start this with I have a 5 star rating on Airbnb. I don’t use it often but when I do I have never had an issue in the past ( I also use VRBO/HomeAway when the situation calls for it). It all started when I tried to book a condo for Pride weekend in West Hollywood 2019. I found the first Airbnb (max 3 people, 1 night minimum) for my 2 friends and I in February. This first Airbnb was declined by the host because she was looking for a “longer stay” Her minimum was one night and we requested a 3 night stay (ie someone hadn’t raised their prices for pride yet). I contacted Airbnb, sent a screen shot of our conversation with the host and ask if there was anything that could be done. I received a response back saying that they would move her listing down in search results. Great. So you punish her kind of? But no solution for me. So I started me search over. Found another appartment within 3 blocks of where we wanted to stay. It was a 2 night minimum, 4 person max rental. Booked it. Was declined yet again. This one saying that they didn’t think the apartment would be big enough to accommodate 3 people. . How much space do you think 3 women will take??? I sent him a screen shot of his listing with a 4 person max rule and heard crickets back. Flagged the conversation with Airbnb again. No response this time. At this point I thought well I guess I’ll look at hotels. Looked up a few, but none within walking distance offered more than a double queen single room. So reluctantly I start the search again. Thinking “3rd Times the charm, right?” Found another apartment within 5 blocks of where we wanted to be (keep in mind each time I found a new place to book the price went up). Booked it, was finally approved ( ). I’m thinking FINALLY. Our trip is booked and I can be done with this.... 2 weeks later (now the end of March) get a random text from Airbnb saying my reservation had been canceled. WHAT?!?! We’ve booked flights and Concert tickets at this point. Contacted our host, she said there was a glitch in the system and it would be solved shortly (no response for actual Airbnb at this point). I waited a few hours and it still said canceled so I tried to message our host again. And what do I find out? She’s been removed from Airbnb for charging people outside of the platform. But I had to find this out myself. I NEVER GOT ANY EXPLANATION FROM AIRBNB. Not until I called in the next day and tried to talk to a representative. He explained that the host had been removed from the platform and the reason why. I ask what Airbnb was going to do about our reservation since they had removed our host and he said NOTHING. That it was just bad luck and I should find another listing. . I pointed out to him that this was our 3rd rental for the same weekend and that I had been trying to book for over a month and his exact response was “Yeah, I’m sorry, bad luck. But we can’t do anything about it. We will not issue you any travel credits or vouchers.” Pretty much you are $&!$ out of luck... Needless to say, I hung up on him, got out my credit card for the 4th time (keep in mind I still have charges that need to be reimbursed by Airbnb from this 5 week fiasco) and booked a 2 queen bed hotel room for the weekend. Deuces Airbnb. I’ll be using booking.com or HomeAway from now on.
Just say no to airbnb. Just say no to pmi, maui. Definitely say yes to VRBO. Nuff said.

TO KNOW - Airbnb phone 1-855-424-7262 for cust. svc. You as a traveler generally have 48hours to cancel w/no penalty. LOOK for Super Hosts (people who are very well reviewed and have Good Cust. Svc) If booked way ahead - check HOST policy on Cancels. This is published on site. DO call or chat by email with your host directly ahead. Ask them about cancels etc. AND if they do not contact you after reservation contact them quickly to get a feel. Ask questions. A good host will respond and usually w/in a few hours. RENT a whole home or inlaw appt. etc. - ideally not a room. People who have a whole SPACE are usually more serious- as it sits empty it costs them. People are more casual about a room in a home. Be willing to pay more for a better place. That is life. DO write a honest review the system depends on it. DO read reviews and if none - talk w/host (new does not mean bad). Good luck and if you can - get to host directly, sometimes facebook or messenger works for this as Airbnb will not allow phones shared or direct sites or emails. Better Hosts will save you money by having a direct booking system and it will cost you less. Sites add fees for themselves of about 10 to 23% depending. This is for using the site and customer service. They are a middle man - Your host is your service provider and the key is getting a good one and communication with them Directly. Happy Travels.

Take my advise and book through more reputable sites such as hotels.com, booking.com, agoda, or what ever else, but stay away from this site to save yourself the headache. I have stayed in over a dozen places with Airbnb. In the UK my experience has been OK although not that great. In Spain though I would be very careful since the chances of you having a bad experience are very high. By two biggest complaints are that the locations are well hidden before you book so you only have a vague idea of where the place will be. In Southern Europe this is just too risky. Big giveaways though are pictures of the interior only and random beach photos - avoid these places like the plague. Once you've booked you're going to have a tough time cancelling. Also, the reviews are pretty much useless and I've found some of the worst places actually have the best reviews because they allow a lot of groups and short stays. People are easy to please if you give them a cheap place to sleep for two nights. A lot of reviews may also be from people in countries where noise and poor standards of cleanliness are pretty common - just bear in mind their opinion is coming from a low baseline. In addition, once you've used airbnb a few times, it becomes obvious that there is no incentive to leave a bad review since you'll just look like a jerk to your next potential host. The result, therefore, is lots of insipid comments that don't really tell you anything. My worst experience was when I tried to negotiate an extended stay with one host who offered me a poor deal and said take it or leave it. I left it and got a bad review in return as soon as I'd walked out of the door. We decided to book an Airbnb property as part of my partner's 40th birthday trip to New York. I looked at the rating for the host and his property, of which he had scored 4.5 out of 5 and numerous good reviews, so felt comfortable making a booking. Unfortunately, had I paid closer attention, I would have noticed the handful of negative reviews that would have sounded alarm bells. We arrived at the property at approximately 15:30, and we were disturbed and extremely disappointed by what we were greeted with. Yes, the Airbnb photos were of the property, but they were VERY old. The outside of the property was unwelcoming and off-putting, with overgrown weeds and litter strewn on the driveway. Security was a concern, as the front door was only secured via a single deadbolt, due to the whole mechanism for the door handle being totally removed. Entering the property, we were immediately struck by how tired, dark, and filthy the property was. It seemed like the property hadn't been properly cleaned or repaired in years: lights that didn't work or missing; dirty grubby walls and doors; ceiling fans caked in dust and dirt; a bathroom that hadn't been cleaned since the last occupant, complete with an unflushed toilet featuring a toilet seat caked in what looked like mould/urine; the heating was turned off and could only be controlled by the owner - which he refused to turn this on despite calls and messages; the bedding was dirty and beyond worn, and was only good for throwing out; the ironing board was covered in stains. I could go on, the flat was just DIRTY and a dive. Obviously, we refused to stay here and contacted Airbnb immediately. We expressed to Airbnb the urgency of getting this matter resolved before night fall, as we didn't want to be roaming unknown neighbourhoods in the dark for another Airbnb property we knew nothing about. Our requests were ignored and 5 Airbnb agents and 10 hours later, we were advised to book into a hotel for the night which they would pay for. When I enquired into the refunding of my booking, I was told that I would only be receiving HALF of it, as I had made the mistake of contacting Airbnb first and not the host - I was furious. It was now 12:30am, and after a stressful night with an unsatisfactory result we booked into a hotel. The following morning we received an email stating that our original booking had been cancelled and that we would be receiving a partial refund. Still, a replacement Airbnb booking had not been arranged, and we were left with nowhere to go. We spent another day being passed around from agent to agent with no resolution in sight. Once again, we were left with no other choice and booked into the same hotel for the remainder of our stay that evening. Luckily we were eventually passed through to an understanding agent who went above and beyond to get us a satisfactory result (had we received this service from the beginning, I'd still be an Airbnb advocate to this day, but the damage had been done and it was too late). I took us a week, but we eventually received a full refund, and one nights hotel booking paid for. Booking with Airbnb resulted in us losing two days of our holiday (waiting for correspondence from both host and Airbnb), being pushed beyond breaking point trying to resolve the matter, and leaving me short of £497 (a combination of hotel fees, phone call costs, and transport). Take note, DO NOT BOOK WITH AIRBNB!
