For me airbnb went beyond the call of duty. I think airbnb have responded to criticisms and are more proactive now when things go wrong, however we as users need to be realistic about the limits of what airbnb can be responsible for.

My boyfriend and I stayed at a flat in Barcelona, This was advertised as being 'rented' with only the hosts. When we arrived there, there was another family with a baby. On the second night, two new families arrived at the flat, and the kids were up all night screaming and running up and down the corridor, right outside our room. We had to be up early and didn't get a single hour of sleep. We complained to the hosts and they just said they couldn't help it. We contacted Air B&B to complain as well, and they never replied. We will never be using Air B&B again. A lot of the ads are completely different to what they are like in reality. I'd rather spend a little bit more and get a proper hotel room.

My son recommended Airbnb to me a couple of years ago. I have used them several times now in many different cities and had an excellent experience with them. Prior to this I had used homeaway or similar companies- I prefer this to a hotel/ motel. I have never had a problem with a transaction or with a property not being ‘as advertised.’ Perhaps some people are not doing their homework?

We were supposed to stay in a beautiful 2 story house with pool. We looked forward to it for weeks. We were staying in multiple cities so I booked a hotel, then the house, then another hotel. The house got double booked. So we're in Houston with nowhere to stay and I'm beside myself. We book another property on airbnb that was almost a complete LIE compared to what we saw when we got there!! Airbnb said it could take up to 15 days to refund both charges. Jeez, good thing we have money. I cannot imagine what would happen for someone who needed that money to book another place!!! The good thing is that they refunded all of our money but the experience was so awful that we'll never use them again.

Some of the negative reviews here are grossly incorrect/inaccurate. I'm seeing several people 'describe' how the platform works, and they're blatantly wrong. Long story short, if you don't get a refund/reimbursement for something that you feel entitled to, it's usually because your claim is invalid and you didn't follow the policy requirements. Simples. My advice for those wanting to use the platform is to do your homework. Read and understand the various policies before you travel/host. I've had nothing but great experiences.

They allow host that are poor "Landlords" and lack communication with their paying customers.I made the mistake of booking way in advance. I booked in March and my stay was not until July 25th. They took $568 from me to confirm my stay. After several attempts to contact the host did not give me an address to the location I had suspicions. . The reviews were great upon my initial review. After booking, the reviews began to decline and I decided I needed to cancel as I was concerned for my safety. I cancelled July 5th and was not to arrive until July 25th. No refund what so ever. They say the communication was adequate and I guess getting the address the day of your arrival is acceptable in the AirBNB world. Absolutely dangerous and ridiculous to think this is legitimate business practice!!!

They tolerate misleading listings (e.g. number of rooms). airbnb is opposite of satisfaction guaranteed. They particularly suck in developing countries. I used them quite a bit but when you get in trouble with a fraudulent host they offer zero support

Had to cancel a reservation because the host lied about location, supposed to be 15 minutes from Amsterdam Centraal ended up being 45 minutes (if you're lucky). Booked a new one with another host, who also lied; this time about it being a private room... it wasn't. He also left us with one set of keys and said he'd have to come catch up with us when he's ready to come home because he didn't have his own set. Basically land locking us to his neighbourhood. We called airbnb about this guy to complain. He also showed up 3 hours late for checkin. The airbnb operator told us to leave and he'd set us up with a new place. We waited for 2.5 hours and finally called back airbnb only to be told the guy who was 'on the case' just up and left work. Even after this airbnb said they might not be able to help us out still. After a while on the phone they decided they'd give us a paltry sum, just enough to book a low end hotel. We lost an entire day of travel because of this and a lot of money.

I'm writing not as a host or a guest but as a property owner whose property was used as an airbnb in the past by a previous owner. I was alerted by my city that my address was linked to a listing but of course that listing is not an accurate listing. I have never done an airbnb and never will. The previous owner just never deactivated the listing. Well I called airbnb to let them know thinking they would jump at the chance to review this listing and make sure it's up to date. Boy was I wrong. They refused to remove the listing and according to the city they have refused to for numerous other homeowners. In my city you are required to have a permit to run a short term rental. I let Airbnb know this and they still did not care to take it down. You'd think that this platform would want to double check that all the listings are legal but they don't care. What I was told by the city was that airbnb won't take a listing down until some poor sap books it and arrives to a private (non-airbnb) residence. That poor sap could be you. If you want to book through airbnb do your due diligence but I am telling you that you cannot trust these people. Even when they are notified about non-compliance or a fraudulent listing they do not care. I have everything: utility bills, car reg, business licenses to show that I am the legal resident of the property. I'm lucky to live in a city that is working on my behalf and to make sure that these short term rentals are above board but please be careful...especially if you have kids, are traveling abroad, or are arriving at night. You read tons of horror stories and it can easily happen to you. Even craigslist will take down a listing that has been flagged. Personally I will always stay in a hotel. NOT WORTH IT!

Don't Use Airbnb - unless you're desperate! As a former host, I quickly learned after the first year that is exactly the type of person who will book an Airbnb. In two years as an Airbnb host I met an inordinate number of guests who were liars, religious fanatics, drug users, mentally ill, slobs (one left feces in the bathtub), sex offenders, drunks, grifters, petty thieves, con artists, prostitutes and some who seemed to think I was advertising some sort of brothel as a single female renting rooms in my own home. Airbnb's easy listing service (you won't realize what you've done until you read their policies' fine print) fools thousands into taking a chance as a host or guest before either comes to realize the RISKS involved. It SEEMS like a great way to generate side income and a way to utilize unused space - until it's NOT. Their service has ruined neighborhoods and cities by turning everyone into amateur hoteliers and making home and rental values for locals soar. Be safe and rent a hotel or motel or B&B with commercial liability insurance. Most Airbnbs don't have that and never will, which means you host and stay as a guest AT YOUR OWN RISK.

I can't understand all the negative ratings. All my bookings went according to plan and as described. Was a great experience. They even called the host once to check I was OK in my travels. I had to cancel one due to Venice flooding and they gave the 60% rebate instantly, with no questions. I will definitely use again.

I wish there was a ZERO star for this company. Customer service is worthless. They charged me and uncharged me and then sent me threats to cancel my reservation and then charged me again and uncharged me and then sent me another threat. I have been a supportive customer of this company for years. I AM DONE!!! COMPLETELY DISAPPOINTED WITH THIS COMPANY!!!!

Reviews of the hosts and properties on their platform are nothing but unreliable. The result of the two-way review. When you tried to get a refund, you’ll definitely get robbed. The opportunity to meet a bad host is just too high. Those hosts are still listing their properties. So better not risk it.

We have been hosts for Airbnb for a number of years and had problems every year but the first one. Our properties are ski in/out condos and as such the location warrants a higher rent than other properties in the area. Airbnb takes it upon themselves to lower your rates to what they think is fair if you don't keep your rates advertised at least a year in advance. We have always waited to see what the management of condos similar to ours set their rates at each summer for the following season before we set our new rates. This is impossible with Airbnb. They set your rates and then allow instant booking at rates 65% lower than what you normally charge so that they can get a fee. When you cancel the booking they threaten to suspend you listing. They have changed our settings to instant book and then said we did it. The site is hard to navigate and I have never allowed instant booking. You are not allowed to talk to potential guests until after they have booked as all personal information of the guest is hidden. You don't really know for sure what you are getting (could be a group of kids) even though our personal contract prohibits young people. You cannot contact the company as nowhere is there a phone number or email listed. This should be the first warning when they are not willing to talk to their hosts to settle a problem. Without the host they are nothing. We have taken our properties off of their site.

THIS COMPANY IS HORRIBLE AND WILL STEAL FROM YOU, WITH A SMILE ON THEIR FACE, AND BLAIM IT ON YOU FOR NOT REVIEWING A POLICY FLAW!! I was renting a house for my family in Jacksonville, FL for thanksgiving. The total renting for the house was for 6 guest -$1104. I had to pay 558.00 and the remaining amount on a later date. The host had a strict cancellation policy with a grace period. I booked the house in the last week of October for NOV 21-24. After booking the house, my guest backed out and I had to cancel. I cancelled my reservation the 1st of November, and after reading about the policy of not canceling within 48hrs, I would get a %50 refund of what i initially paid. It sucked only get half of what I paid but at least I getting something back. BOY WAS I WRONG. Airbnb said they wouldn't issue me a refund because i already paid half of the total amount for the reservation, and therefore I was not entitle to getting anything back. They said it was their policy to protect the host. But when I looked up the house again, the HOST already booked the place up from my cancellation. After telling Airbnb, that the HOST didnt lose any money because she had another booking, they refused to even help with the situation of even trying to help give me back my money. So the HOST who they so love to protect took my money and then gained more money from another reservation. Their policy is to protect the host, but what about protecting the customer!

It appears that my account was hacked on AirBnB. Charges were placed on my credit card for a home rental in Ukraine (I have never been in Ukraine and have no plans to visit). The customer service telephone number is cleverly hidden deep with the web site and after finally discovering the number was told by two separate persons that a special person would need to speak with me regarding this issue. No one ever called be back. I then tried to send a message and no one ever answered my messages—it appeared that the company ignored my message and my calls. Recommend that you do not leave any personal data on the AirBnB site.

Horrible experience with airbnb. Beware airbnb has a loophole with their reviews system...its 2 way review, what that means is both parties (host and the guest) needs to provide review before it can be seen online. Problem is if the host knows the guest had a bad experience, amd therefore knows that the review will be bad, they simply won't review the guest.... effectively blocking the bad reviews of their place. So, only there property only gets good reviews... and misleading others to stay at the property. My family and I recently booked our first stay on airbnb. Reviews of the property say "Sprinkling clean". On the day of our reservation, we we to the property and it was beyond disorganized.... the property looked like it hasn't been care for managed in months; the yard looked trash, and the grass/weed was over grown. In the back yard, where we were supposed to park car (although another car was blocking our spot), there was so much disorganized belongings that it looked like a homeless shelter. Not a clean and safe environment we were expecting. The room was not "newly remodel" as they had advertised, it was pretty beaten up. This was not an acceptable environment for my family and we immediately got got of there. I did politely informed our host. We tried contacting airbnb for a refund, because no one should have to lose money if a prooerty had been falsely advertised. My case has been given to a case manager and we have bern playing phone tag for days. He has not provided a reachable contact information as requested, nor have I been able to reach that person when I call Airbnb to discuss my case. Representatives have not provide a clear information about their process or timeframe, just told to keep waiting. Horrible experience! Dont waste your money! I'm sure there are good hosts, but there are scams too. It's a gamble, pricey gamble! Don't rely on the reviews or airbnb for assistance when things go wrong. I would not try Airbnb again nor could I reccomend it to anyone. I would vote/side with communities that are against Airbnb, now that I understand why.

I’ve been an active member of Airbnb since 2013 as an accommodation host, experience host and a traveler and I have never had an experience as bad as this before. I recently rented a private room in a place in Venice Beach, Los Angeles which unfortunately didn’t match the listing. For one thing, we were put in a different room to the one that we described and pictured in the listing. And even worse, we weren’t given any bed linen. We complained to our host who said that we could leave and that she would refund our last two nights. We agreed to do so and found and paid for a new place to stay (through Airbnb as well). We communicated our decision to our host and we left. Later on that day, our host wrote to us that she would only issue us a refund if we agreed to leave her a positive review, essentially attempting to bribe us for a good review. We then chose to involve Airbnb but haven’t been able to get anywhere. Airbnb have also been extremely slow with responses and keep telling us that they are trying but failing to get hold of our host who has since gone awol. We feel that this experience is not on par with the Airbnb standards, that hosts like this should be banned from using the service and we’re seriously doubting that we will be using Airbnb in the future.

First time using Airbnb myself and it will be the last! Just to let you know the fees can completely mess you over and are non-refundable after 48hours of booking. Just booked a 12 day stay (Airbnb fees = $100, 15% of the full cost) and because I cancelled 52 hours later - still almost 2 weeks until the reservation, the fee isn’t refundable. There is also NO flexibility if plans change during your stay. Save yourselves money and just book the old fashioned way - through a hotel. #neveragain Airbnb #readthefineprint #mad

I attempted to book a room for a two month stay in Kennesaw, Ga with a host named Kent. I selected the dates in his calendar and clicked on "book this trip," wrote Kent a quick introductory note and waited for him to accept me or not. 10 minutes later Kent messaged me saying that he was sorry but there was already a guest at his house and that he would have to decline my request. No problem. I thanked him for making his room available and moved on. about 5 minutes later my credit card was hit and $806.00 was withdrawn. I quickly messaged Kent asking him if my request has been granted because my bank account just got hit for $806 dollars. Kent quickly messaged me back telling me that it was an Airbnb mistake and Kent "guaranteed" my money back "immediately." Well the next morning the money wasn't returned to account. I called Airbnb and was told that it would be but it would take between 5 and 15 days to return. I was blown away! Why would it take between 5 and 15 days to return the very money that only took you 15 minutes max to withdraw?????? Remember here Airbnb. I didn't cancel the reservation, you did. Your calendar showed availability, you cancelled the reservation but then immediately after cancellation, you decided to pull the money (illegally) from my account. Talking with Airbnb was like talking to the wall. Cris, the dude paid to read of a script was absolutely no help while he breathlessly and constantly reminded me to remain professional. I told Crissy that I was professional. I did everything that was asked of me. It was Airbnb and Kent who were running the scam. If anyone in the world shouldn't use the word professional it was Airbnb, Kent, and Crissy. Maybe they just wanted the 5 to 10 day interest on my $806.00. Whatever. I just think it was total bad form how Kent, Crissy, and Airbnb handled everything and I'd be very careful booking with them. I certainly won't. And if anybody asks for my opinion on Airbnb, this note is exactly what they'll get.

Airbnb has the worst customer service I ever experienced!!! I do not recommend renting or advertising through Airbnb! If you’re host and have some issues they will never get back to you! Their calendar doesn’t work correctly! It doesn’t sinc so you can get double booked!!! If you are renting through Airbnb be aware!! Their calendar doesn’t work well so you may not have your room when you arrive!! Someone else may be renting it already!!!

I'm really surprised seeing all 1-star reviews here. I'm using Airbnb every time I travel somewhere, which is quite frequent. Last week I had my first major issue with an Airbnb listing, there was a cockroach infestation! I still cannot believe how that host can maintain such a disgusting place. Airbnb support was available through the phone and I knew I would have a refund after my first call. That was very important because we wanted to get out of there immediately and we already paid for a full month! We could not get out of the apartment before securing our refund first. We booked the place for 1 month, in the end, we went out of there immediately. We had our cat with us and it was impossible for us to find an immediate accommodation in London which would accept cats. In the end, we had to spend some days in a hotel (which Airbnb reimbursed a portion of it) and then we got another apartment we could stay with our cat. Airbnb support did not just help until we got our of the apartment, they tracked everything I did with the account and the hotel and make suggestions even before I asked for them. It was a terrible experience because of the only host but Airbnb turned that around!

We had a booking that was organised and paid for for months and Airbnb allowed the host to cancel on us, without consequences for her, so that she could get more money from someone else! I feel absolutely disgusted that we were left in a situation where we had to scramble and find alternative accommodation at the last minute. I will not be using them ever again
Terrible Company! They steal from you. Never trust them!
First of all, they are well enough. But sometimes, the places I stay don't make me feed secure. Their customer service is good though.

Horrible experience. Booked Airbnb for a week in Tokyo 6 months in advance. Airbnb took half of the payment upfront. The host backed out with less than 2 weeks to go. Airbnb did not penalize the host. Airbnb offered to give us $200 to help book a new place (since there was almost nothing available in Tokyo). We found a much worse place at a much higher rate, but had to settle. Afterwards, Airbnb refused to give us the $200 they promised. They rotated us between at least 5 different "case managers" and none of them did anything to help. They hold your money for months interest-free and do nothing to help you if the host backs out. Greedy capitalism at its finest. I will never use them again.

This company must be run by a bunch of kids. I booked a room several months in advance on Airbnb in Cambridge, MA with a host who calls himself FRANKLIN. I needed the room for a required stay at the college. Shortly before the trip, FRANKLIN drops my reservation out of the blue with no explanation. I just a get a terse notification from Airbnb that my reservation was dropped. It's hard to get reservations in the Cambridge area last minute. I got a different reservation for significantly more money because nothing else was left. I complained to Airbnb, and they did nothing but give me the run around. FRANKLIN in Cambridge, MA was given no penalty, no reprimand, nothing. I was not given a reason why this happened and no compensation for the difference on the cost of the stay. I have no criminal record whatsoever, so there was no reason why this was done. I recently went to book another stay in Cambridge, and FRANKLIN is still out there. He's still on my list of trips, and I'm not allowed to give him a review. So, if you choose to book with Airbnb, do not discount that they will pull the rug out from under you at the last minute with no mercy, no recourse, and no fair compensation for it. Highly narcissistic in my opinion. I guess some people (FRANKLIN) are just highly privileged.

By far the worst customer service I have ever felt with. Looking to go on a short vacation for Christmas this year and made a reservation that was relatively easy to do. Then it turned to hell. Received an email the next day stating my account has permanently been deleted due to a criminal record being found when running my name. I find it very hard to believe that since I am a LAW ENFORCEMENT OFFICER!!! Have called over 20 times to resolve to which I am told it’s being handled with some specialty department they can’t even provide a phone number for. Then to top it all off they charged my account and still have yet to refund my money. Oh and they will no help compensate anything in any way shape or form. Will never be using them again!!!

Used Airbnb 2 times, for my first trip the host cancelled due to a flood - fair enough, we then had to find another place in such short notice. 2nd time, the host cancelled for no reason given, and has yet to reply to any messages. Yet again we re-booked (not our preferred place due to it being short notice again). To our surprise under a week to go and the host of this place also cancels, seems he was renting it out to holiday makers when he shouldn't. Went on booking.com found a nicer place last minute, everything was so much more professional and will never use Airbnb again. They're very unprofessional and need to take into consideration, if the host is legally hosting before travelers plan trips from around the world, only to be let down a week ahead of time. As the travelers will be the one at loss if the host cancels! It seems Airbnb do not care about this and will let the host cancel whenever they want, leaving YOU stranded.
Had good experience, you need to look in depth as reviews etc . ' A Min Review' channel has a minute review on Airbnb pros cons & bonus link too. Regards

I've made 5 bookings on Airbnb 3 were a mess. On one of the bookings the host had a total meltdown because we didn't arrive at the time we said we would.(We were in hospital) two of the occassions the host demanded cash outside of the airbnb system. When I messaged airbnb about one of these they just simply closed the case without bothering to respond This support case is closed. Still need help? Visit our Help Centre. Avoid avoid avoid.

The worst, useless, rude customer service I have experienced. I am a host and had guests make a false claim against my property to cancel the booking. We suspect they did not like the area and therefore made exaggerated and false claims to enable them to cancel the booking and get a full refund, at my cost. We spent 20min speaking to the guests who seemed fine, but then contacted Airbnb to cancel claiming the flat was 'dangerous and unsafe for children'. Our previous guests had checked out the day before and gave us a glowing review - something we pointed out to Airbnb. Airbnb emailed us at 11.10pm by which time we were in bed. They gave us 5 hours to respond which would be 4am! Absurd! When we woke up, the booking had been cancelled. We did not receive the rental AND we were charged the fees that the guest had to pay Airbnb! Airbnb did not bother to speak to us before taking the decision against us. We had photo and video evidence to contradict the false claims made by the guests. We invited an Airbnb representative to visit and inspect our property. Instead, we received an extremely condescending email from the Airbnb staff who clearly need training. Separately as guests a few weeks prior, we had no electricity (in France) and the host (a company) had voicemail from 6pm -10am! They only responded to text/calls during 10am -6pm. Even at 6.09pm, they did not answer. We contacted Airbnb but they were useless and simply said 'sorry' - did not offer us the option to cancel and get our money back!

One great experience with an Airbnb host in Longyearbyen - on Svalbard, Norway. Clean, safe, convenient and well-appointed accomodations. Friendly host (in neighboring flat), as well. Ease of reservation, ease of payment, and accurate photos of the flat on the website. I'd be happy to try this again!

Terrible service - which they charge for! They justified overcharging and charging two sets of tax and refuse to accept responsibility for their mistakes. Taking advantage of customers because they think they are a monopoly and 'too big to fail'. I for one will not be using Airbnb again - other similar services are showing up. Stop supporting big monopolies just for the sake of convenience!

Tardy refund process. Booked for Barcelona the other day. Apartment flooded so host cancelled. No problem - these things happen. Rebooked another place today and for some reason they have cancelled just now. The refund from Air B&B apparently takes 5-10 BUSINESS DAYS!!! Absolutely pathetic. One uses these well known platforms thinking that they are well run and the infrastructure is solid. Not so. I will now have to find alternative accommodation AND alternative funding whilst waiting for Air B&B to refund in their tardy manner. I will NEVER use Air B&B again.

Every Airbnb review I've read always reads like it is from the Stepford Wives. It's so generic and so glowing and everyone gives everyone 5 stars. Have you ever seen a rental from them that has not had something wrong. This site is a shame and would never go on their ratings. I've rented from one and it was not as it was told.

After checking out I recieved an extremely rude, accusitory message from a host that was completely making things up. Reported him and airbnb just told me to keep responding to his nasty messages. Eventually he tried getting €250 euros extra for 'damages'. Complete BS, airbnb charged me anyway; I told them I'd be blocking the charge and they can deal with the credit card company. I've heard other people having similar experiences and Airbnb will always side with the host with no evidence. Don't use the site; it is a complete waste of money and energy.

This company is the upitomy of awful customer service... for operating in over 191 countries, you would think they would have a team dedicated to resolving complaints... but I have come to learn two things: 1) They do not care about the law, they only care about their bottom line 2) They definitely don’t care about their customers I am a property manager, currently in the process of evicting a Tennant who has been using their unit for an Airbnb. Our lease explicitly states that this is a breach of contract. This has been going on since September 1st, 2018. I have notified Airbnb three times to ask that they take down the listing. The poor guests who show up are not able to access the building because of our secured entrance and elevator codes... which they were being given incorrect information by the host. When they come to the office to ask for assistance getting in, we ask them to leave because they are not listed on the lease and we are not going to give them access. For those who do end up getting in., we are telling them they may not use the gym and common areas…the use of amenities and facilities are for residents only. If I was an Airbnb guest I would be very upset especially if I were to come to an Airbnb and see an eviction notice on the door.... would you want to stay there? I’ve told Airbnb all of this several times and they could care less. Choose another route when looking for lodging when traveling... they just don’t know a thing about good customer service, and you could be screwed if this is happening elsewhere which I’m sure it is...and from my research and speaking to a few lawyers, it sounds like Airbnb is gaining a reputation for being irresponsible.

There is NO WAY to track where your money went and who refunded it. There are several unexplained charges to my Airbnb account and they can't tell me where they went. FOR PETE'S SAKE, WHAT COMPANY GETS AWAY WITH THIS???? WRONG, WRONG, WRONG. For all I know, Airbnb is SKIMMING off my account.

A treasure hunt in side streets of Melbourne to obtain room key hidden in a letter box in an alley. We had to leave vehicle and go to apartment to obtain garage remote to access parking (during Thursday night late night shopping in Melbourne CBD). Host rude and unhelpful speaking a smattering of English and finishing in an hostile tone of voice in Chinese and then telling me I didn't speak good English! And it wasn't his problem that I couldn't follow instructions. Apartment in 200 Spencer Street was ideally located near Marvel Stadium and that was its only redeeming feature. Toilet floor was "splashed", fake tan on toilet seat, public hair and long black hair on bathroom floor, mould on tiles and more hair under shampoo bottles, kitchen floor was sticky, dreadful smell of tobacco, but the lack of hygiene was fully discovered next day when shower water from previous day would not drain. I cleaned out a cup of a disgusting blockage of several hair colours and lengths. Months of filth! Took photos and reported to Airbnb. They offered reimbursement of cleaning fee and cancelled last day (of fees). My daughter and I packed car so we could have an early get away to drive interstate and went to sleep at 11.30. I woke at 12.30 am to discover a man standing at the foot of my bed and I started screaming and screaming and my daughter woke with a dreadful fright and also screamed. He claimed to be a cleaner (unlikely - a cleaner with a backpack! At 12.30 am) Should have called police. Threw him out and called Airbnb and we were terrified and feared for our safety which they are obliged to protect. In the meantime the host rang and threatened to physically remove us and threatened violence - threats delivered in brilliant perfect English. It turns out that the cancellation offered by Airbnb was not compensation but in fact THEY cancelled one nights accommodation without advising us. What a dreadful blood-chilling experience . Never again. Airbnb have closed case after my daughter requested a full refund. DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY. The intruder could have been a rapist or a murderer and had full access to the security lock. Unwary traveller beware.

I have been waiting 3 weeks to have a simple technical support issue resolved with my account. I have placed multiple calls, I have opened multiple live chats. There seems to be a complete disconnect between customer service and technical support. Whenever I speak with customer support they basically say they have no access to the people that actually need to fix the problem and they only work via email.. but then they won't give me the email address. I wouldn't care, but I have one more trip booked with Airbnb. After that I will never use the service again.

Would give a lower rating if possible Tried booking for my first time and each time they took payment instantly before the owner was informed and each time about a day later the owners came back to apologise that the rooms were not available Why can’t the owners block the dates out to prevent this AND also why is payment taken instantly and refunds a week to come back??? I will not be back here soon!!!!!!

It can be difficult to find a good place quickly so it's important to start looking for a place ASAP. The quality depends on how much you're willing to spend and how many questions you ask the host. Its best to do your research and figure out if your expectations can be met by the host. If you're going for work then you better make sure the host isn't some kind of party animal.

I reserved two airbnb’s for a trip to NY. First host cancelled me two days before arrival, except he tried to bully me into canceling for him. “I sold the house, you’ll get a full refund “ Not true. I would lose all the money I already spent... So Airbnb cancelled and gave me money back. They fine the host $100 when they cancel. While on hold, the call "disconnected." Frustrated, I called back and was connected with a new agent who placed me on a hold again. This call was not disconnected but when the agent came back they informed me that a ticket was created and I would be hearing back from another team with further information. The agent informed me that a ticket had been submitted and I would hear back from them once the issue was being looked in to. They informed me they would give me a call a few hours later or the following day with an update. At this point I was completely fed up and asked if they had a resolution for me. The only way to get my refund according to the agent? Cancel my reservation. WHAT? Called back to speak with a third customer service agent and explained the issue once again. This agent was able to refund my credit card without having to cancel the reservation within minutes. It seemed like my troubles were over and I was on my way to never having to deal with Airbnb customer service again. However, they were not able to figure out how to charge my gift card for the reservation. Again my resolution was to cancel my reservation and re-book the reservation with the gift card on my end. At this point I asked if the agent could do that for me and was told that agents are trained to teach Airbnb users how to use their account, not place reservations. I asked to speak with someone who could further assist me and was told "you will receive the exact same answer." I requested once again to be transferred and was finally transferred. The supervisor was just as helpful as the other agents and told me that there was nothing to do other than cancel the reservation and I would have to go in and re-book. The reservation was canceled and I was placed on hold while they looked into my gift card balance being restored. They had to call me back 15 minutes later when the balance was finally restored. I asked if there was anything they could do for me to make up for all of the time and frustration and was told they would "look into it." I am not hopeful that I will receive a response with any form of compensation. I will be going elsewhere in the future when booking a stay for a trip. I contacted Airbnb and had my situation escalated to a case manager, Randy. He blamed the situation on my check out and check in time, "6PM and 7PM", respectively. However, my check out time was 10AM and check in time was 4PM, which were both clearly stated on their itinerary. In addition, he asked me to contact the guests who were arriving later myself to offer them alternatives. He clearly was not informative nor helpful, but he did finally got the previous guests to leave. I submitted a claim through Airbnb Resolutions Center to ask the guests to compensate for the damages (even with receipts, photos, and videos); they were adamant that they did not cause any damages to the linens and sink, and refused to pay any late check out fees. A day later, they gave me a 1 star review with nasty mentions that were completely inaccurate. I contacted Airbnb again, informing them of the situation and that it could hurt my business, and was shut down with "reviews reflect the guests' experience". At the end, the Resolution Center ruled that the guests only had to pay me about 40% of what they had damaged and did not need to pay the late check out fees (even though it is written clearly in Airbnb Rules and Policies that guests are required to pay late check out fees). The guests who were arriving later cancelled the reservation and I was forced to refund them 100%.

How to get FREE AIRBNB ACCOMODATIONS So I'm a host with Airbnb...and at first, everything was great...guests were happy, I was happy...even earned the status of "Superhost" which helped my ratings and bookings. If there was ever an issue with a guest regarding their comfort or needs, all they had to do was message me and I'd gladly take care of it...problem solved. Things like, can we get more towels, theres not enough toilet paper or can we have extra pillows and blankets...then suddenly, seems like this year... people figured out how to cheat the system. I started getting cancellations, made on MY behalf by Airbnb for issues such as people not satisfied with the speed of the wifi... or because there was a stain on a doormat, the neighbors dog was barking too much...things that may have easily been resolved with a message to ME, the host. But because they went directly to Airbnb and demanded money back, I was left clueless as to why guests left and why they got full refunds, without the courtesy of allowing me to take care of it or at least try. I've had guests tell Airbnb they left immediately after checking in, but managed to sleep in the beds and use the shower and towels, as well as the kitchen... I've had others complain to Airbnb (not to me) 3 days AFTER staying a full week, and get a full refund, and I've had guests spill on carpets, send photos to Airbnb of said spills and say the place was like that when they checked in!! I pay a lot of money every month for cleaning, and walk through before each guest to make sure its ready. But for people with lack of integrity to go to the lengths they do in order to get a free stay is just sad. The worst part, is that Airbnb will side with the guests 95% of the time. So, that being said, if you're a guest looking to book with Airbnb, all you have to do, is maybe plant a cockroach, spill some wine on a light colored carpet, complain about the internet speed or maybe say you didn't find the listing as advertised ..you can get your money back!! Do this every time and save thousands on travelling!!

Just keep in mind that you'll be staying at an Airbnb listing AT YOUR OWN RISK. Once Airbnb has your credit card information, and as soon as you click that REQUEST button, if you're request is accepted by the host, DO NOT EXPECT TO GET YOUR MONEY BACK whether your stay works out or not. Your Airbnb experience will entirely depend on your luck - it's like going gambling in Las Vegas - 50/50. Because Airbnb is the MIDDLE MAN, they basically just hook you and the host up and, other than taking money from you both plus occasionally respond to your e-mail, they don't do anything else for you. If you happen to get a nice/reasonable host, then it's your lucky day, you just pay Airbnb for the booking and have a great stay. But if your host is flaky or just simply a greedy host, they can either cancel your trip last minute with absolutely no guarantee, or they can just let you stay and take full advantage of you by telling Airbnb that you've damaged this and that and, Airbnb will simply deduct the money from your credit card and there's nothing you can do about it. Doesn't matter what explanation or documentation you e-mail Airbnb. The only form of communication you'll get from Airbnb is through e-mail or messaging on their site - you'll never see anyone and you'll never get any sort of guarantee/help from anyone. Plus they don't respond immediately, if you have an issue of any sort, they'll respond to your message in 2-4 days. By then, your disaster may already be over and it's too late to get help. Or, you'll just keep getting the run around from Airbnb AND get your credit card charged anyway, at the end. Airbnb will just keep telling you to "refer to our policy and guideline". So, if you're a gambler, take the risk and stay with Airbnb. Otherwise, spend a little extra (or maybe even cheaper) and just stay in a hotel, or book an apartment through another booking site that uses the method of, you pay locally when you arrive, or allows reasonable free cancellation period ON YOUR END. That way, you won't get charged against your will by Airbnb and their host. Good luck and happy travels!

I normally stay in a reputable Hotel chain managed by professionals and they just want your repeat business. Airbnb hosts just create and account online. Taking the money from my luggage really exposed the underbelly of this business. Of course the amount they took is nothing compared to the revenue overall. DH

I felt I needed to try to redress the balance slightly as I am a little bewildered by the extreme negativity of these posts. I have been both an Airbnb host and Airbnb user for the past four years and based on my own experiences feel that generally, with one or two exceptions, Airbnb offer a great service to both traveller and host alike. HOWEVER - Airbnb can only be as good as its hosts and as good as its users. We have stayed in Airbnb accommodation in the UK, and abroad. When my husband and I travelled across the USA, we stayed almost exclusively in Airbnb properties with host families and with the exception of one bedroom in New Orleans, were generally delighted with the quality of the accommodations, and the friendliness of the hosts. Airbnb was a life saver on one occasion, when, due to flooding we had to make a 300 mile detour. We had to cancel the airbnb we were heading for (the host was wonderfully understanding and refunded our monies), and when we found that every hotel and b&b in the area was fully booked with families fleeing the floods it looked as though we'd be stranded. We checked Airbnb and found a home within 3 miles - they took us in immediately just asking an hours grace to get the room ready! And a lovely room it was too. Even the room in New Orleans was fine - however, in the photos, the curtains to the window were drawn. We found out why when drawing them back -there was no view, just a massive air conditioning unit filling the whole window. The hosts were also quite uncommunicative - possibly because they had such a high turnover they could not be bothered to chat to ALL their guests. As hosts, most of our guests have been lovely and often very interesting people. One or two have been less lovely and have seemed to forget that our home is not a hotel, but they were in the minority. We have an ensuite room in our house, so we are on the premises. Most airbnb issues seem, in the main to centre around properties where the owner is not on site. I am puzzled by reviews that state that the host has the opportunity to vet guest reviews before they are posted. That just is not true. The system is that guests and hosts can do one review on each other. Neither can see the other review until both have been posted or if noly one review is posted, until 14 days have passed. Airbnb will send reminders to guests and hosts to do these reviews during this time span. We always review the guest straight away. In most cases, we receive a review back. We also have the opportunity to leave a public response to a review once they both appear publically - for example, one guest review suggested that our guest accommodation just had use of a bathroom on the same floor. We were able to set the record straight in the public response (our accommodation is ensuite). I do agree that sometimes, Airbnb seems weighted a little unfairly towards the guest - if on the extremely rare occasion we had to decline a booking for very good reasons Airbnb responded by sternly admonishing us to ensure that our details are up to date and meet guest requirements (this after declining a guest who informed us that they were terrified of dogs and might scream when they met ours! Our details state quite clearly that we have a dog that has full run of the house). Airbnb also have a habit of constantly trying to get us to drive our very reasonable prices down further by informing us that other possible guests have looked but booked something else cheaper. In fact, guests have informed us that ours was the cheapest in the area when they were looking! I had a slight shock when I realised how much Airbnb adds to our base price for 'service' which is then charged on to the guests - we as hosts see none of that, just the base price minus a small percentage for administration. To my mind, this large addition of 'service' must drive some fairly reasonably priced accommodations up to an unreasonable amount. It's important that the host keeps photos and details up to date and as informative as possible. The host must also be very well organised with regards to administration - especially the calendar, blocking dates that will NOT be available. That said, when we have needed assistance or advice, Airbnb have been quick to respond. You do have to go through a procedure before making direct contact with them that can be irritating, but I think this is almost certain because so many queries and questions are the same. When we have written with an enquiry or problem, we have pretty quickly had a response back - usually by phone and the individuals we have spoken to have been, without fail, very helpful. Sometimes they appear to be host 'champions' - experienced hosts themselves who are used by Airbnb to assist other hosts. Generally, we are quite happy with Airbnb and would certainly recommend it to other potential hosts and guests. For guests, I would offer the following advice: Study the photos REALLY well! Read the reviews - if there's a negative one, take the others on balance as it might have been posted out of malice Don't be influenced by enticing pictures of local areas. You're not sleeping on the beach! Communicate with your hosts - if you're going to be delayed, tell them. If you've allergies/intolerances - tell them! Be prompt - if the host is offering breakfast and you state a time that you would like it - be there! Don't wander down an hour after the host has got everything ready for you (we had a guest who did that) - it's sheer bad manners. To Hosts Communcation is the key. Get a communcation going with your guests - if they make an enquiry respond promptly. If they instant book, acknowledge, welcome them and ask if they have any special requirements (e.g. gluten free if you are providing breakfast). Be guided by guests previous reviews. If a guest has no reviews and yet they have been with airbnb for 12 months or more, there may be three main reasons - they may have joined expecting to travel and didn't. OR, they may have been rubbish guests elsewhere and the hosts have been too polite to write a review. OR hosts they stayed with waited for them to write a review before responding with one of their own - and they didn't! We have often found ourselves to be the first host that a guest has stayed with so the guest has no reviews. In this case, be guided by the verifications, what, if anything the guest has written about themselves, and your gut feelings. If such a guest instant books but wthout any real information, we have no hesitation in politely enquiring after their reason for the visit - after all, these are strangers coming to your home! If you are in real doubt, and to heck with Airbnb disappoval and your statistics being hit - just decline or cancel the booking. Make sure your house rules are clearly stated in the room - we provide a binder with this info and local info for the guests. However, if all goes well, then you should never have to resort to this. Good luck to you all - guests and hosts alike and enjoy the experience!

Airbnb will screw you over and not even apologize. All they will do is, "understand you're upset." My trip to CA with my kids. Well something horrible happened with Airbnb... We arrived in Hollywood the afternoon of the 28th excited to explore. We booked a stay with Airbnb so that we could walk right out on Hollywood Blvd. No more trying to park and no more traffic! I emailed our host and let him know we were ready to meet for a key exchange. The hosts rely was, "oh there must have been a glitch. My place isn't available tonight". Well after a mini stroke I called Airbnb expecting everything was going to be ok. Well, it got worse... Our first person said oh shoot we will find you something and she attempted to book us into places there is no way I would stay in if I were traveling with a swat team. After clearing explaining why I booked the place we did she said she would have a supervisor call me back. After sitting on the side of the road for an hour with worried kids a callback was not what I needed so I asked that she not hang up but rather put us on hold. She agreed for about 20 seconds and then she hung up. I instantly called back and got someone who frankly was more equipped for customer service and phone calls. She did the same thing trying to book us in places where I just was not willing to stay (everything reasonable was booked, Hollywood was packed). She put me on hold to speak with a supervisor. After a brief hold she said she looked at an affiliated Airbnb hotel and they could not accommodate a party of 4. We held again and she cheerfully had a solution. Find a hotel that could accommodate us, book it, get a receipt the next day and send the reciept. After receiving the reciept Airbnb would refund my previous booking which was now all locked up in debit card processing world and they would send me $200 toward the stay at the hotel we found. At 845pm we were finally in a hotel room... Well, the next day I called Airbnb and they said I needed to set up a payout account with Airbnb. I asked why and they said they cannot just put $200 on my debit card I would instead need a payout account and then I could transfer the $200 to my bank account. The person I spoke to sent me an email with a link on how to setup a new payout method for my convenience. She said once I set up that payout method I should reply to the email with the link in it a copy of my receipt, so I did. Several days went by and people from Airbnb stopped responding so I called today to find out when I would receive the $200 I was promised and that's when Airbnb showed it's TRUE colors... I was told my "request was denied." Ummm I didn't request $200 from Airbnb. Airbnb told me what to do and in doing so I would receive a $200 reimbursement for the overpriced hotel we found. The manager I spoke to was very good at handling me. He clearly worked within his policies. I asked him if personally he thought Airbnb was doing the right thing and he responded that his "moral fabric has no bearing on Airbnb policy". He then asked me if I had anything in writing stating that I would receive $200. I don't so I said no but explained that I had an email with instructions on how to setup a payout account and that showed intent. I also explained that we had a verbal contract and that he could listen to the recorded phone calls. He told me he couldn't sift thru all my calls and listen to them. I reminded him it would be easy to find because it was the second call I made that day after being hung up on. He replied that it wasn't in their policy to go back and listen to phone calls. I then asked why they record calls. He said for training... At this point it was clear Airbnb couldn't have cared less for their mistakes and lies. That call went on for another 35 min or so with me trying to get another manager on the phone and him saying there were no managers available. In the end Airbnb's exposure is $0.01 in all of this. That was the penny they sent to verify my payout account was valid. The payout account they told me to set up so they could send the $200 reimbursement. I have no discounts or coupon codes for another stay. I never even got an email saying sorry but we decided to screw you over. I however lost that one night in Hollywood sitting on the side of the road looking for a resolution. A resolution I had to find on my own. 5 hours of my kids hungry and scared we wouldn't find anything and the frustration of my money being tied up. Shame on Airbnb!

Wow! I booked with Airbnb for accommodations in France. Thought it might be nice to get away from the hotel scene. Boy was I wrong!! I just wish I would have stumbled across these reviews BEFORE I booked anywhere.

WARNING - Do not waste your time with a security deposit with Airbnb! It is totally worthless as they do not pay out. Airbnbs policy is NOT to pay out! I am pretty sure they train their case managers to be as unhelpful and almost obstructive when it comes to making a claim. My blood is boiling as we speak as yet again when i have had to make a claim for a guest issue i have had to fight a battle and lost for no reason . All they do is throw obstacles in your way and constantly change their policies and reasonings. I am a property manager and list 34 properties with them with a turnover of $250K with Airbnb. I have over 360 reviews averaging 4.9. I am not a bad landlord or agent, i look after my homes and my guests but get treated like trash from Airbnb. Airbnb needs to realize that without owners and managers like me they would not have a produce to sell. They would have no business. Their PC philosophy i believe has actually turned 180 degrees and instead of it being there to protect both parties, the host and the guest, it has become very much biased towards the guest. I expect because they don’t want bad reviews from guests saying Airbnb took my money! Well do you know what, in my experience those guests who have had money deducted from them have had money deducted for a reason. In 3 years i have had to probably make a dozen claims. Every single claim maybe except for 1 or 2 claims is like strapping on my armor and heading in to battle. Almost every single claim takes over an hour of my time writing emails to case managers who are not interested in facts, pictures they are just interested in paying out as little as possible and if anything at all. I would not be surprised at all if they are targeted on paying out a percentage of the actual claim. I have had numerous claims that have taken up 3+ hours of my time and effort. The previous claim prior to this one which has made me write this report was for a guest who used the home to hold a drunken birthday party. Even though we clearly state in the advert and house rules no parties or gatherings are allowed. The guest put a hole in one of the bedroom walls and we had hand prints with dirt and blood all over the walls and house. They also badly stained a number of towels. So i claimed for extra cleaning time, 2 towels and a repair to the wall. It was all done on headed paper with the correct amounts. Photos and invoices were attached. Airbnb did not want to pay, they then decided they wanted external quotes for the repair and cleaning. My company is a property management and maintenance company, this is what we do. I quoted $7 for each towel and $35 for the repair to the 3" hole in the wall. $35!!! Airbnb insisted that i get a quote for this, i explained that if i get a quote for this it would be around $75 - $100 for a company to come in and repair this. So i am saving them / guest money. This claim nearly took 2 hours of solid arguing and writing and it was not until i threatened to write to the board that this got resolved. So todays battle against Airbnb is for a guest who trashed a home and it cost an extra $50 in cleaning and they damaged 2 bath towels, they were found in a cupboard covered in human excrement! They also badly stained 2 hand towels and 2 pillow cases. So this time the external cleaning company i use invoiced me for the replacements and the extra cleaning time. This was forwarded on the day of the guest leaving along with photos of the damaged items. Two days later i receive an email from the case manager telling me i need to send receipts and a correct invoice? When i questioned what was wrong with the one i sent she said it was not valid. So i responded that these invoices are valid with the IRS and both my account and the cleaning companies accountant so why was is not valid for AIRBNB? No answer! After 2 more sets of emails i was asked for receipt of the towels. I explained to her that i do not have receipts because i personally did not replace the items as the cleaning company did and that Airbnb will not allow me to claim direct because you want it from an external company, therefor how can i give you a receipt. So i tried to explain to her that the receipt is the invoice, it is a valid invoice stating the price i have paid for the replacement towels. They refused to accept the invoice but wouldn’t tell me why. They kept asking for different photos, even though they had them all. In the end they sent me an email telling me they were refunding me $12.99, because that is the price for a hand and a bath towel from Amazon Basics! That is very nice of them to assume i use the cheapest of towels possible. At this point i receive a response from the guest apologizing and admitting the damage and saying he would pay, he never paid but it is in the message thread that he admits to it. So when i questioned Airbnb that when they can see the guest has admitted to the claim and that the claim covers more than 2 towels, why have they only paid out $12.99. I got a response saying i have not supplied enough information!!!!! Are you kidding me!! I believe that Airbnb purposely make it hard and frustrating to make a claim to stop from hosts doing so. The problem here is that yes it will stop me from making a claim because they will no longer have my business. They have decided not to upset a guest who i have proven has wiped his bum on my towels and trashed my house, but to upset their client who gives them a product to sell and generates $250K with them per annum. I have now listed my homes with as many similar sites as i can possibly find just so i have less booking with Airbnb and eventually all of my homes will be removed and at that point i would have expected to have 50+ homes listed with them generating close to $500K. AIRBNB NEEDS TO RE THINK THEIR POLICY ON CLAIMS

This was the third time I used Airbnb and the last time. Our trip to Philadelphia PA at the PHENIX SUITE Center City East 1BR Was a complete epic fail! If you are going to use Airbnb for one of your trips please take this into consideration. 1. Make sure you are dealing with the actual owner of the place you are renting. It sounds simple enough but beware of FAKE HOST. This can be a friend of the host but Airbnb doesn't have their contact information as a person that is registered with Airbnb. Once I realized I was dealing with a person NOT listed with Airbnb while renting from Airbnb I felt vulnerable and that my daughter and my safety was at risk. She was a crazy lady and very scary. 2. Ask your host if there is a lock on the inside of your door that you can use to keep a host from accidentally/or on purpose, from coming in while you are in the occupying the place. 3. Ask your host about precautions they take on preventing bedbug contamination. 4. Setup a payout preference on Airbnb website NOT from your phone just in case you have a nightmare experience and need your money back. And pack your patience because you won't see your money for a good month. 5. Take pictures of everything when you get there and document everything. 6. If the place doesn't add up to what was advertise start making nose right away! I hope this helps you make the right decision for your next trip. I really wanted to like Airbnb but I see the troubles that come from trying to represent owner and customer.

In the past, I became a host for AirBnB and put several boats I managed from San Pedro on their site and basically had a good rapport with AirBnB. As a host, especially for boats, there were issues and I always refunded, exchanged or in any way tried to please the guests. My experience as an intended guest, however, turns out very different. I reserved a private room in Palm Springs under "Amazing Room Steps From Downtown PALM SPRINGS- Private room hosted by Aden" When I read "Pool: Private or Shared", I incorrectly assumed it would be shared by the hosts if they would be there. I emailed them to see if it would be private, and wanted to know if it would be okay to go clothes optional if they weren't there. The host emailed and said, NO! it is shared by the other people from the apartment complex! I told him I would certainly honor that and began trying to find out why this apartment was on AirBnB. I promptly canceled since I had just reserved it, and got a notice I would only get the AirBnB money back and the host would not refund the money! So, I began researching online and found out this apartment is NOT allowed to be on AirBnB! It is strictly forbidden. I called the management and Consuelo was very nice and informed me no one was allowed to rent to AirBnB. I told her my predicament and she immediately began exclaiming and said she would look into the matter. I called AirBnB and told the customer representative, Kayla about it. She said she would look into it, and when she responded, she seemed very aloof and said because I had cancelled due to the pool issue, my new complaint did not register. I am upset that AirBnB finds out about an apartment not being legal and refuses to refund the money. So, now every guest needs to do their own history search on a place to see if it is legal or you could get evicted from the rental during your stay! I talked to Shane, a guy who said he has the final authority at AirBnB and he said they made the decision and it was final. No refund. I understand AirBnB can't do research on each property listed, but once they find it out, they should be held responsible and refund money to guests who cancel because they are uncomfortable being a part of such activity! Shane told me my status as a former host would be flagged because I was trying to get remedial attention.

Our card was charged without our permission. We hadn't even booked a rental. I live in Kansas and my account was billed 3 times for a property in Australia. I have cancelled my Air BnB account and will not be back. If they would have offered me a free stay I might have considered staying. They offered my a choice of a pair of socks or a mug. Hah! I'm gone. Be careful when you give your financial info to AirBnB. I do not think it is secure.

First time user of Airbnb. HORRIBLE experience. Cannot recommend and will never reuse. Completed online registration. Booked room. Owner writes back that, "I am not comfortable with you." Taken aback as I was listed as "verified" by Airbnb, and he didn't KNOW me so how could he be uncomfortable with me? Then, searched the city to which we were traveling again. Booked. Only AFTER booking do I see that it isn't in the city I was searching but about 30 miles outside the city. Troubled by the fact that the company allows listing outside the listed destination to come up, but learned my lesson. Cancelled the reservation without incident. Next, scheduled again. PAID. Shortly thereafter the host contacts me and says she isn't ready for company and asks me to cancel. It seemed weird, and it was problem 3, so instead of just cancelling as instructed - as a normally would - I did a little research. Turns out, had I cancelled IT LIKELY WOULD HAVE COST ME MONEY!! So, again, very uncomfortable and questionable conduct. Finally, schedule another place. No apparent problems - - until we arrived. Sheets did not appear clean. Beds were unusable - jailhouse issue. He apologized and said he would refund our money. HE DID - AIRBNB DID NOT. We stayed maybe 10 minutes, but Airbnb won't refund the service fee or TAXES. HOW DO YOU COLLECT TAXES ON A RETURNED/UNUSED SERVICE OR GOOD? UNETHICAL AND, I think, illegal conduct.

Let me tell you as a Host on Airbnb it is no picnic. My wife and I do our best to keep our 3 cottages in Hampton Beach New Hampshire in tip top shape. But when a guest comes in and trashes the place, good luck getting any money for damages not to mention the added labor we are charged to clean the puke off all the blankets. Now let me tell you the best part. Airbnb will shut down your listing for 4 days during the peak season of your summer rentals based on someone giving you a low rating. for 3 years we have had 5 stars but someone stayed with us and gave us a low rating which dropped us below Airbnb's rating threshold. Why did we get the low rating ? The air conditioner broke their first day. Did the guests call to tell us ? NO. We called to discuss this with Airbnb support - you guessed it - there was nothing they could do. All we got was a gentle voiced person saying "I understand". I calmly explained that he should open a case ticket and in it state how they lost another host to VBRO. And this goes out to Jerry in a post below: Cancelation costs are Brutal to guests. We have a guest that wants to cancel the day before their arrival. We will lose over $1000 because we won't get those days rented now. They are week days. We were sympathetic however, and only wanted to charge her 1 day out of the 4 that she was staying. $250. Airbnb is charging her $406 for the cancelation.

Do not become a host on Airbnb: -PUNISHMENT FOR LESS THAN 5 STARS - YOUR LISTING WILL BE REMOVED FOR 5 DAYS (even if you don't know about the issue) -IF A GUEST TRASHED YOUR PLACE YOU WILL NOT GET ANY MONEY BACK EVEN WITH NUMEROUS PHOTOS AND RECEIPTS -CLEANING PERSON DENIED MONEY FOR EXTRA HOURS OF HOUSEKEEPING AFTER DISGUSTING GUESTS -THEY ALWAYS SIDE WITH THE GUEST AND NOT THE HOST You will be treated like a second class citizen! We have 3 seasonal cottages in Hampton Beach and have always taken great pride in our response time, availability to our guests and cleanliness of our cottages. Even though we have a multitude of raving reviews, one time we received less than 5 stars from a single guest. Airbnb punished us by "pausing" our listing for five days during the height of summer on our seasonal rental! Airbnb bases their rating of hosts on a numerical algorithm and doesn't take into account the acutal written reviews. STAY FAR AWAY FROM AIRBNB!

I was traveling with my family and a few friends, 10 of us total, in Australia this July and was notified a day before we went to our next destination, Cairns, that our Airbnb host cancelled on us. Well, of course there were no hotels available for our size group a day before and Airbnb only had 5 options left for our size group and so last minute. Either a property that was 7 hours away from Cairns, a vegan basic 2 star bnb, a hostel like room with 11 bunkbeds, or 2 properties that were more than 2x or 5x more expensive than what I had booked 6 months in advance. When I called Airbnb they said book something and to try to work on reimbursement later. Booked the one that was a little more than twice as expensive as my cancelled booking because I refused to put my family in a hostel. After returning to the US, they gave us a $1000 "coupon" but still sticking me with the extra $4,000 I had to pay to accommodate my family because of their host's last minute problem. Their customer service is HORRIBLE and I was passed around or my call was dropped for literally 2 weeks whenever I asked to speak with a supervisor, until they still ultimately refused to offer more to help us, sticking us with debt because the property they endorse dumped us. NEVER BOOKING WITH THEM AGAIN! The worst customer service and business mentality ever. No system to protect customers from these last minute scams, where apparently this host was repeatedly cancelling last minute through Airbnb. Later through research I found the same property on other booking sites asking for more money so they probably double book customers with Airbnb to see if they can get others to book and pay more. Airbnb has no accountability and we were left with terrible anxiety and stress on and after our vacation. Booking with them is a terrible risk!!! SAVE YOURSELF!

We rented an apartment from airbnb.ca and were charged the nightly rate in USD, rather than the quoted CAD. After 20+ emails with airbnb they insisted this was my fault for not reviewing the charges prior to authorization, and refused to refund the difference (30%). Very frustrating considering we rented with them, rather than an independent unit, to avoid such situations. Will not use them again.

I made a booking on Airbnb for a longer period and therefore, a large deposit amount in Euro. Although I had nominated my Euro-denominated credit card for this purchase, the debit went automatically to my A$ bank account, which was not funded for this purchase. Airbnb did not give me the option of reviewing payment for the reservation but immediately debited PayPal, which in turn, debited my $-nominated bank account instead of the credit card I had nominated on PayPal as backup. As the purchase was rejected by the bank, PayPal debited my card with an ADDITIONAL10% of the purchase amount. Both Airbnb and PayPal washed their hands of this convoluted transaction, which arose through their fault, leaving me with a hefty charge. So, be careful when choosing a payment method for Airbnb and don't think that PayPal will be of any help!

I was alone in the apartment as my boyfriend went on travels. My guests came home around 11 and took showers to leave the apartment again - everything was fine. However they came home around 2 am and were super loud, drunk and smashed the doors a couple of times. I didn't say anything because I though they left again. But for some reason they kept walking in and out yelling - and smashing doors. throwing their suitcases around (don't ask me why). At some point I got out of my bed and went to the room - knocked the door and opened it - they were gone. So I texted them on airbnb to please be a bit more quite - also when they check out at 9 am - as this is a shared place. Fors one reason they came back again continuing what they did before for about half an hour and then went to sleep. it was already 4.30 am in the morning. After they had left - luckily in time as the checkout stated - I went into the room and they left it super dirty and had they're alcohol bottles in the room all over - fine. I cleaned it up. This morning I contacted Airbnb asking them to rewrite or even remove my review (if rewriting won't be possible) as I wanted other hosts to know that these guests didn't behave according to my house rules - It's fair enough that we hosts know how guests are that we welcome at our place - which is not a hotel. especially for shared places!) After a long discussion explaining my situation and also explaining that my previous experience with airbnb - and feeling like they don't care about their hosts at all - they stated again: "there is nothing to do about your issue - I'm sorry we just can't" So I asked for their supervisor: Again the same answer - and she kept telling me that I don't have enough prove. I told her she can see the message I was sending at 4 am to the guests asking them to be quite. Still she told me that I should'e thought about it before leaving the review (which my boyfriend left - yes that's my fault but it doesn't change the fact that airbnb several times didn't;t do anything about my requests/complaints) This is not the first time that airbnb just simply ignores my request, or complaints as a host and either hangs up on me on the phone or just simply says "there is nothing to do about your issue - I'm sorry we just can't" This has been happening too many times lately - not only to me. I know other hosts in this town and most of them have the same issue. One of them told me that their guests even brought a secret 3rd guest and left doors open when they left the apartment and nothing was done from airbnb's side - "it simple wasn't possible". It should be fair from both sides - we as hosts are offering our place to guests and put rules, descriptions and pictures of our place and yet when something is not being respected or house rules are being broken Airbnb doesn't care - and like I said it happened a couple of times and not only with me as a host. As a host I always read through the reviews of guests that book my place and ask a bit about there travel reasons - because yes, I would like to know about who stays at my place - especially when it's shared. leaving honest reviews (or rewriting them in my case as my boyfriend - stupidly put a wrong review as he thought everything was fine just like at the 1st night the guests stayed / and like explained he wasn't there the second night) should be possible to make sure that other Hosts are aware of the guests they are accepting. It's only fair to other hosts to know what to expect when a guest comes and stays at your place. Supporting the hosts should be Airbnbs responsibility. The same way they care about the well being of their travellers. The same way the experience is important to your guests it is also to the hosts then run your platform and make it possible for travellers to stay. I'm very disappointed by how I was treated by Airbnb’s customer service the past couple of times.I never had the feeling that I am supported in any way as a host and my place that I am offering on your platform. This is a very disappointing fact - and I'm sure that I'm not the only one experiencing this. And I hope that other hosts also will put some effort to leave a review for Airbnb’s customer service. It's just fair to all of us that our rights are respected as well and it makes me sad that Airbnb doesn’t seem to care. It seems to support illegal activity and I would frankly be scared to death to ever do business with them again.

I recently rented an apartment thru airb&b. To make the story short, the apartment was very filthy and dusty, and the bedroom smelled as sweaty dog.
