Airbnb Hosts Beware As a host who has tried their best to give a good experience to guests I am horrified by the selfish and dishonest behaviour of guests and the customer service of this company. I have now deactivated my listing after only 2 months of hosting because of theft, damage, last minute cancellations and their unfair decision to refund customers who cancel and damage property. Their view of always supporting the guest not the host, despite the unreasonable expectations of guests and Airbnb and reasonable expectations of a host, can result in hosts losing sleep and money. Never again! Airbnb Hosts beware!

Where to begin? 1) I loaned a guest a SIM card so they could make local calls. They didnt return it. I requested that they pay for the card and time to replace it. Airbnb denied both. Now I no longer loan SIM cards to guests, airbnb's 1 million dollar host guarantee is not insurance, and if the governemt tries to regulate them, they officially state they will end the guarantee. JERKS. 2) I had a guest who smelled of cheese, vomit and urine. ALL THREE. AT ONCE. I notified them, and their reply was they can't demand that she clean herself. She had a 6 month booking. I threatened legal action. They said they would find her another place. 5 days later, the position shifted to we are trying to find her a place for 5 months and we can't find any. REALLY? No kidding! I am one of the few who does that. So I informed them under Chicago tenancy laws I will serve her with a formal eviction notice on day 29 of her stay. The next night I was in bed sleeping. I got a call at 10:30pm to tell me she left. She stole a phone battery which I didn't file a claim for so that's gone. Airbnb said I had to pay half the month even though she was there 3/4 of a month, and the reason for her leaving is she smelled of urine, vomit, and cheese. Her feet were so smelly I had to mop the floor with bleach because her sweat just stayed in her footsteps. What a nightmare. Airbnb was useless. BUT I guess I like pain because right now I filed a claim for $100. The guest defecated all over the bed. The homekeeper and host submitted the pictures immediately. The guest apologised, and said she would pay in English. The next day I received a message from her in polish that they won't pay. As far as airbnb: Crickets. Now for the traveling, for which I no longer use them: I booked a trip for my sister that had a flat that had no air conditioning. I missed that in the listing. My bad. However, the host said I can't open the windows because bugs will get in, and that is why bug spray was left on the kitchen counter. Catch 22. I got no money back. I booked a stay with my fiance to a place that the heat didn't work. 1st night the host apologised, the second night it still didn't work. I called airbnb and they said go buy a blanket. It was 11:30pm, and we were in Long Island, NY. I was shocked. I was so upset but calm he then offered a space heater. OMG. REALLY? I now rent 1/2 my bookings elsewhere, and I hope to be fully rid of these 8ssholes by next year. Airbnb call centres are OUTSOURCED. Corporate does not care about these people. Go find them on indeed. They are paid crap, get crappy benefits compared to company employees and the turnover is so high airbnb uses headhunters to replace the workers. airbnb profits pay for company debt service, this is why they didn't go public and the CFO was fired (oh quit right!)... Other hundred of millions in profits pay for developing housing in well to do places like wonderful single family homes in Florida and housing developments in Japan, because you know, they care about the community (uh where?). Oh yeah, they donated $150,000 to house south american refugees because it was cheaper to pump money in to a P.R. campaign than to pay for traditional campaign. It's just calculating unchecked greed. Hey airbnb, want to help the community? Build affordable housing in NYC to help the 60,000 homeless that are on the official record. That will offset some of the families destroyed by your campaign to help families pay bills. You see, it's a zero sum game if people take units off the market, and don't rent to families, thus people are made homeless by your business strategy. Basically ensuring landowners make more money does not help the working class, so please get new batteries for your hearing aid airbnb. As for the avid reader who made it this far, save yourself... use any competitor and you will likely get normal results. Don't chance ruining a great trip to save $100. It is just not worth it.

One day one of my regular guest mentioned that he couldn't rebook due to an error in the app, i called airbnb when they inform me that they will send this case to the specialist department to be fixed. My app froze and my guest were leaving beacuse they couldn't rebook. I called back. Again and again to see whays going on?! Again the same answer " i understand, but its in the specialist department and they will call you" they never did. Then airbnb started cancelling the few guests i had left and refunding them out of my monthly earnings! I had very loyal guests who refuse this offer, they were told they didn't have a choice and said airbnb would be cancelling regardless, they asked why?? Airbnb refuse to tell them why , guests asked me why?? I couldn't tell them because i myself did not know. I suspect it was just a glitch in the app that they didn't feel like fixing or maybe a lie was told we had a guest who we kicked out for opening bank accounts under our adress and braking into my mailbox at the time, i suspect he called and made something up but then again..i dont know..they never call to explain..it wasn't fair and cost me everything , all my hard work and ultimately my home. If anybody ever starts a class action lawsuit contact me please this was not right what this company did to me.

I have been a guest with my account and another person’s account and hosted in my home abroad. I didn’t take guests if I was not committed to certain necessary lifestyle changes in my home. When I accepted a guest, I arranged my life differently to make the guest most comfortable, however, many do not, or do not make accommodations well enough. In one instance, the people hosting were up, active and at loud (at 5-6am), had other tenants living in a rather small home/apt and didn't disclose this fact, ran businesses (such as an overnight dog sitting) without having a separate area for this activity, with dogs barking (at anytime of the day/night), jumping on me, every time I would leave the room, dogs were waiting outside the guest room door and going to the bathroom (peeing) on the floor in the living room and walkway to the room. Too many people are posting rooms out of greed or economic hardship and desperation, to pay rent the next month, but this does NOT make their apartment, or home, personality, or skill set right for hosting. Being a business person (in a host capacity) really requires a certain amount of sophistication and knowledge to know what is acceptable; you can rent a floor with a sleeping bag through airbnb and that's fine with this company, but in actuality- it is NOT. This low or NO standard leads to many issues experienced by the consumer. And someday, someone is going to get assaulted or killed then they’ll wake up and change! Lastly, the reviews do not provide an adequate survey of what the accommodation and stay was like. I have spoken with many who don't put down a lot of the awful details, because they feel bad about writing bad reviews and then the host gets these comments, and can write a nasty review about the guest in retaliation. So many have an excuse, blame the guest or state the guest expected too much. They can't accept a critique to make improvements or outright deny what's being said. And they are guaranteed the money, even if the guests stay was substandard, and the guest can’t easily book another accommodation, on the fly or get their money back, if they decide the place isn’t what was stated. As a note, being a guest is totally different situation, which is actually another issue, but easier to regulate and doesn't reflect the company and the product it's providing. All in all, i have decided no more airbnb in the US, at least, my best and only good experiences have been abroad.

My girlfriend and I booked 3 Airbnb's for a trip to Hawaii. 2 of our Hosts so far seem great but the 3rd requested that we give them our personal email address, sign a rental agreement, and pay taxes via an outside payment method. We felt very uncomfortable about this and upon review at a later date found out that they had breach 14.1 of Airbnb's Terms of Service by requesting payment outside of Airbnb's Platform. We contacted the Host and requested a full refund as their refund policy was strict and would only give is 50% back if we had cancelled it ourselves even though the reservation wasn't for another 6 weeks. The Host refused and breached Terms of Service again by asking that we pay via PayPal. Feeling extremely uncomfortable about all of this, we contacted Airbnb. They investigated the matter and told us that the Host had been misinformed by Airbnb staff about the correct process and was instructed to make all further payments through Airbnb's Resolution Centre. But, despite acknowledging the breach, they refused to process the refund because the Host was a 'valued Superhost'. I have screen shots of Airbnb's verdict where they inform that they do not believe their was a violation before stating that the Host had violate the Terms of Service in reference to 14.1 which states 'request, accept or make any payment for Listing Fees outside of the Airbnb Platform or Airbnb Payments. If you do so, you acknowledge and agree that you: (i) would be in breach of these Terms' They then go on to acknowledge that it is the Host's responsibility to pay any Host Fee and applicable taxes as well as the responsibility to include any other additional payments within their Listing Fees which was not done. The only conclusion I can make from all of this is that Airbnb agrees that the Host has violated the Terms of Service but because they misinformed the Host of their responsibilities (even though they would have had to have read and agreed to the Terms of Service prior to becoming a host) they are unwilling to inconvenience the Host in case they loose a source of revenue. Ultimately, I feel like my rights have been violated and I can safely say I will NEVER use Airbnb again. Hotels may cost more, but certainty is priceless.

Amazing site, straight forward every time and the cheapest around by a mile. I recently had an absolute bargain of a stay at a young gentlemans house over in liverpool. The host was extremely welcoming and took me on a tour of the local area and taught me all about the history between the local 'crocky crew' and their infamous rivals, the 'nogsy crew'. The house was stunning, a 21st century terraced, built to keep you on your toes, if the loose bannister rail didn't catch you out as it departed it's wall mountings when descending the stairs, then the garden fence that collapsed on me as a squirrel crossed it definately will. The toilet, one of my favourite features, my record attempt was 17 plunges of the lever before a full flush was given, not bad seeing as it took me 30 first go. My night's sleep was a pleasent one, apart from the hair clip that managed to impale my shin during the night, it was more or less comfortable. Breakfast was a clear contender for some of the best, dry weetabix. Needless to say, at 17 pound a shot, I'll most definately be back. Thanks again Thomas.
Great website as it was simple to find a place I wanted to stay and allowed me to communicate with the homeowner easily.

Not impressed with this company. They seem to do not vetting of their properties or the people who use them. I arrived on time for my property. There was nobody there to give Me the keys. I literally had to climb a wall to get into the gates community in order to get into the building. I sat waiting for 3hours for the owner to show up. I called Airbnb. They were not helpful, did nothing to offer alternative lodgings. Avoid. Fine when things go ok, but when they do not, they are not at all helpful.

Check and double check every detail, be aware that most air bnb in New York are being managed by professional landlords. It's great when it's actually a home! Firstly it's quite clear that many air bnb are being let by as professional rentals, not as homes for short stays. There are teams of 'hosts' and their friends and they do this as a business. Secondly, check and double check everything: very often the pictures are not representative of the space. In our case, the pictures of the place changed after we made our booking. In New York Air bnb is illegal, so hosts are always very cautious, telling you not to talk to neighbors and to say they are your friends. It makes you feel uneasy and unsure. Cleanliness standards vary, amenities vary. We had no tea spoons and no sauce pans. Only one set of keys. So far, we've had one really good experience in Manhattan, which was actually someone's home. But we've had two bad or average experiences, clearly not homes that were lived in. I would do air bnb again with allot of caution, my priorty would be to find a place through a known network, like friends and family.

Airbnb has revolutionised how people travel! I travel a fair amount and this has been a great experience for me because I get to experience the place from an actual apartment, living like the locals. Hotels are great but I love the sharing aspect!

Be prepared to lose your money or accommodations. The host attempted to try and refund me the total amount and even she could not refund me this reservation fee. Really? Airbnb may be a legal operation but this is a scam. I will look for hotels/motels first before making any attempts to acquire a place through Airbnb.
Absolutely terrible service . My booking was cancelled within 24 hours and refund was 15 WORKING days . My holiday absolutely ruined .

Absolutely horrible unhelpful customer service! We arrived to Charleston SC late afternoon for a bachelorette weekend. There was six of us girls. This has been the worst online experience I have ever had. I have been trying to book a holiday for nearly 3 hours and it keeps sending me in loops. You should be ashamed of yourselves....not fit to operate.

We showed up at dusk to the address (147 11th Street NE, Washington, DC). The host did not specify that there was an apartment A and B at the same address. Most of the exterior pictures of the unit were of the upstairs apartment. We went to the upstairs unit, which was the only one you could see at that time of day. When we tried the door a dog barked at us. I thought we might have the wrong address and had the Uber driver take us what ended up being around the block (where we ended up at the same address). I finally noticed there was a downstairs. It was really dark down there (Sam does not leave the light on for you). I had to turn on my phone and all I could see was a key lock, not the key pad we needed to use. I tried to text Sam, but he uses a one way text, so he can only send me information, and not receive anything I send. I went to the AirBnB rental site, which took a while, because my service did not work well in the city. We called Sam. He did not answer. I saw no other obvious phone number on the rental site on my mobile app that I could call. It was getting later, so we had the Uber take us to a hotel. About an hour later Sam called. He told us to leave the hotel and head back to his place. By then we had checked in, and were ready for bed. There was no sorry for your trouble, or let me compensate you one night and we’ll fix this tomorrow morning. He just took our money, and refused to give any refund. When I was finally able to contact AirBnB that night (their holds are similar to AT&T holds…very long), the first guy passed me through to the second person, who didn’t even try to negotiate a solution. She said we should have contacted AirBnB while standing on the darkening street with limited cellular, and they would have eventually found someone for us to talk to. As I said, I did not see the AirBnB number on the rental page. I did not find the number until I could get on wireless with my computer. Very frustrated, I told AirBnB I would file a small claims court case. They then accused me of extortion. Apparently, you are not entitled to legal recourse in the land of AirBnB. The following is what they wrote: ""You stated, " We will file in small claims court, but if you make me pay I want to write a review." This sounds like extortion. Extortion is not tolerated on the Airbnb platform. Here is a link regarding our Extortion Policy:"" I will NEVER use AirBnB again. I have used VBRO many times, and have never had a negative experience. What I will tell others who want to use AirBnB is that I highly recommend they do four things: 1) Read the AirBnB customer policy (you will find as a renter you have no rights, and little recourse); 2) Call AirBnB customer support on a weekend night and see how long it takes for you to get through should you have an issue with your host; 3) Put the AirBnB number in your contacts; 4) Do not believe ANY review on the site. Negative reviews tend not to be posted (notice that EVERY place is 5 stars). You stated, " We will file in small claims court, but if you make me pay I want to write a review." This sounds like extortion. Extortion is not tolerated on the Airbnb platform. Here is a link regarding our Extortion Policy:

I've used Airbnb twice. I had no problems with an apartment in Italy but I recently had a major problem with a villa booking in Spain. I booked a villa for 2 families for a week in July 2018. I made the booking in January after much searching for the right location and facilities. There were semi-hidden costs on top of the base rental (200e cleaning, 85e electricity costs) but we were happy with the property. Airbnb cancelled the booking with 6 weeks to go with no explanation. The refund can take up to 15 days and alternative accommodation for 10 was by now very limited. We already had flights and cars booked so we had little choice but to find somewhere else. I've had no information but I believe the host decided to list their property through an alternative site and cancel their Airbnb bookings. This isn't particularly the fault of Airbnb but it demonstrates you are entirely at the whim of the owner/host with no protection against last minute cancellations by them. The strict cancellation policies punish the renter but allow the owner to cancel at any point without recourse.

If it goes well, you’re in luck. But if it goes wrong, you’re screwed. I had my AirBNB cancelled by the host 1 week before we were set to stay. I had booked this trip 10 months prior to the trip to avoid any disappointments. AirBnB told me I can either have a refund or £37 extra towards a new booking. The problem was there was nothing available so close to the date and anything that was available was more than double the price. My originally booking was £370, the cheapest available apartment would have cost a total of £780. AirBnB refused to help, they didn’t try and find us anywhere else, nor did they offer to compensate us for additional expenses. It was cheaper at this point to find a hotel instead. Now, I know it’s not AirBnB’s fault if a host cancels your booking but this is what you have to risk when booking with them. And it would be in their best interest to compensate travellers for a stay elsewhere to keep their custom and peace of mind for future bookings. Unfortunately, I’m unwillingly to risk this again, it’s never bothered me before but trust me, it will when it happens to you!

AIRBNB is a horrible company. You have been warned.

I first used Airbnb in April of 2017. I vacationed to Colorado and it went smooth and ideal. I left a positive review for the host and the host did the same for me. Canceled my reservation 24 hours before my flight without notice. Held my refund for two weeks before releasing funds. Customer service was like talking to a robot or computer service. Very unhelpful, staff lacks resources and urgency in fixing matters. It’s as if they are all reading scripts that do nothing but give you the run around. I and my extremely inconvenienced party of 7 will definitely not be using this service again.
The hosts cancel with alarming frequency. Most recently they cancelled 4 days before our trip! Don't use airbnb!

Absolutely awful experience with the company. We found bedbugs in the apartment we were staying in midway through the holiday and wanted to leave the same day. We went through the mediation centre with Airbnb, who gave us conflicting messages about sorting alternate accommodation (and took several hours to do so). We had to arrange our own accommodation for an extra night, and the following day we were told we had breached the terms and conditions by doing so, and they wouldn't support our extra hostel costs. (Even though by taking hours for them to arrange anything themselves, we would have been sleeping on the streets!!) Horrendous customer service and communication, and their system of chat based forums are useless for dealing with emergencies or to get any problems resolved quickly. We ended up with some money refunded, and the promise of credits to compensate for the extra accommodation (which over a week later has still not been received in my account). Having used Airbnb before and had no problems, this is a great service until you encounter a problem, and they will wriggle out of helping you as much as they can.

I had two reservations with airbnb and both times I had to call Customer Service which did not do anything. First apartment I booked was in Paris with a SuperHoset who turned into a Super Beast after I told her that I have to cancel due to misrepresentation of her place. She was furious and somehow I was punished but not her. I canceled within 24 hours of the check-in ...after I was told that I will be sharing bathroom with someone else, while in the description of the place it clearly stated "private bathroom". Airbnb did not take any responsibility and sure did not give me full refund...even though it was written in their Cancellation Policy. The second one was partially my fault as I did not read the Cancellation Policy prior booking...It was very difficult to find a place in Amsterdam and I had to book for my colleague as well so I rushed through to find out later that they do not reimburse SErvice fees if you make multiple bookings....BS if you ask me. Oh well, I learned my lesson and also find out that now days hotels have more flexible Cancelation Policies than Airbnb. So I will stick with the hotels. My recommendation: do not book with Airbnb. I never had a pleasant experience with them and never felt protected.... as in the first case when I ended up on the street because SuperHost lied about her place.

My daughter was made homeless overnight, long story, and had nowhere else to go. We took her in. In doing so I had to cancel 2 reservations, one with nearly 3 weeks notice (the guest was very understanding) the other with 4 weeks notice. Airbnb do not see this as extenuating circumstances, and have stripped us of our Superhost status and fined us. I feel I no longer want to be part of the Airbnb 'family' (now that is a joke) and have one other cancellation, with 4 months notice, that I would have to make - Airbnb will fine me a further $100 if I do this. This is nothing short of blackmail!

Had a horrific Airbnb experience Tel Aviv Israel where the host entered the apartment and harassed my wife and myself to the point where we had to call the local police to intercede. We were forced to vacate the apartment because the host was incensed that Airbnb gave us a refund due to a non disclosed daily noise issue. Host threatened and harassed us on the Airbnb message platform for almost a week. Our dream vacation was ruined and Airbnb did nothing to stop the hosts reign of terror. In fact multiple calls to support showed a definite bias against us and favored the host. The noise problem is not shown on the current listing and my negative review was not posted.

As a host, i had 2 claims against guests for compensation. First one was denied due to lack of evidence (frustrating but understandable) however the second claim i had proof and admittance of fault by the guest however my claim was still denied and when i asked for an explanation two different times, they would not give me any explanation beyond "We have determined that your claim does not meet our Airbnb claim requirements". I do not believe Airbnb would truly back a host should a guest damage or steal anything.
had 2 flights delay, got "0" zero compensation. these are crooks! stay away.

Short and sweet. Let me stranded in the middle of the Appalachian Mountains at dusk with no reservation. WOULD NOT HELP ME AT ALL! Booked and followed all steps. Credit card company even showed a debit. BY my self, no problem. With a wife and three younger children, you do the math.

Airbnb's customer service is terrible. My wife booked our first reservation for our 10th anniversary trip to London. We decided the best way to experience London was to stay with a local. Problems with our stay: (1) address was 1/2 mile from the given address, which is relevant to train location and safety of walking at night. (2) we were locked out by the roommate. (3) roommate answered the door with nothing on top and only a g-string on the bottom. (4) the roommate did not have any idea we were staying there and essentially thought we were an intruder, but did not know that until the second day of what was supposed to be a five day stay. Three strikes and you are out. That appears to be four, so we stayed too long. We told Airbnb we wanted our money back and we were leaving. They want us to try to resolve the situation with the host. I'm not sure what there is to resolve. We are not looking for something cleaner or a light bulb replaced. This is incredible unsafe. What if we were attacked by the roommate upon entry? She clearly was threatened by our presence as a young petite female. You could hear the shaking of her voice. We chose to leave and book a hotel for the next four nights.

Very bad experience, I will never even try them... On my first ever try with them I lost $760... They would do anything possible to circle in HIDEN return policy rules NOT to give you money back... I canceled the same day I booked and 11 days before check in..... To me It is legalized scam, stay away.... Just look other rental way!

Absolutely awful customer service. Host unfortunately had to cancel less than 24 hours before due to the place being trashed by previous visitors. Airbnb advised we were at fault for booking a cheaper place and so had a very low value to put towards somewhere else which with such notice everything was very expensive. Was our fault for not reading non existent reviews and giving a new listing a chance. Left without a place to stay and also shocking customer service

I made a booking on airbnb. My host (Lr Luxury Stay Park Lane) cancelled on me the day before I was due to book in. He only cancelled because I rang to get the address. Other wise I would have turned up to find I did not have a booking. Air Bnb were great in trying to find us alternative accommodation however this booking was made purely on location and the size of the apartment as well as the cost. Trying to find alternative accommodation on the Friday of a bank holiday weekend was a nightmare and very stressful as well as accommodation was now more expensive. This weekend was for my husbands 60th Birthday and has now been spoiled due to these changes. What makes things worse is that air bnb put a review on the hosts page that I am not allowed to change. I think all potential customers should be aware of the whole situation. I also think that air bob should ban any host who cancels bookings especially at the last minute. The host says the apartment is booked by someone else. If this was the case why did he answer my questions regarding parking and a crib that I contacted him about. He had plenty of opportunity to tell me he double booked. I believe he had the apartment on another website and because my booking was only for 1 night, the other site probably had given him a two night booking. There needs to be a shake up on how these websites work. The situation that these hosts put us in by cancelling is wrong. They should follow Booking.com's policy in that if the host cancels then they have to pay the difference of any new booking that is similar in location and type of accommodation. This is the first time I have used Airbnb and it will be my last. I have made numerous bookings elsewhere and I have to say this experience has been upsetting and stressful .

We've had good experiences with AirBnb before but this latest one was bad enough for me to write this review. It is clear from our most recent experience that Airbnb does not perform even the simplest checks for a property's neighborhood crime statistics before putting it on the site. As a renter then, you have no information about the address nor can you do any homework on the property's safety before you accept it (and in the process lose your deposit which happens to be significant). And when we approached customer service, they pointed to the reviews to tell us the property is safe when all public crime statistics show that the neighborhood is in the lowest 10th percentile for safety. Seriously?? And you call yourself a technology company?

Appalling company, someone should take this company to court. I booked a room and when I went there before I moved in and speaking to host realised it's not as described on what was vital for me and which I specifically enquired on, so called Air B&B while I was outside the house for refund and they refused, obviously the host refused as well. There was other major issues with Air B& B how they left me stranded outside for hours while I couldn't enter the house as it was chained from inside on my first night and they still refused to refund and then they refused to refund the hotel and taxi ..........also I pointed out to them about the entire house being still advertised for the same date that I have already booked the room and was already in the room and they did nothing about it nor did they responded. I would be taking legal action against them hopefully for the inconvenience they cause and for the dishonesty.

Worst experience from airbnb. They only like to protect their host and have no regards for the guests using their service. After my stay that I booked through airbnb, I received no message from the host directly about anything but was surprised to be contacted by the airbnb team to pay up for extra cleaning. We had already paid $150 for cleaning at booking time. There was no instructions about cleaning or cleaning supplies left by the host. What could I clean with? There wasnt even a dust pickup tray, we scrambled through the garage to finally find it. We paid the additional fee and I have decided not to use airbnb anymore.

I WISH I COULD GIVE NEGATIVE STARS! It has been over a week now that I have been trying to resolve a problem with airbnb. I am unable to make any bookings and I have never had this issue before. I have called customer support multiple times. At first they said it was a technical problem and it would be resolved by "another team" . After calling the fifth time they then said it was a "trust and safety" problem so I was confused. I kept calling and the customer support staff would tell me they are unable to assist me and hang up. So rude absolutely the opposite of what it was two years ago they had great customer support. update: I was able to get a hold of the customer support this time they were able to help me by advising me to create a new account with a different id and password since my account was hacked into.

Booked an AirBnB in Canada and went through the Webpage. The summary page stated the price in Canadian Dollars. I used a Credit card held in CAD and was charged in UK Sterling which cost me a £15 fee. AirBnB customer service responded with a rubbish excuse. They claimed it was a credit card in Sterling. Then they stopped responding. I am stuck with the charge. So yes, no customer service whatsoever from AirBnB. I am still considering the legal options.

My friends and I started looking for a place in March for an event in August. All of us had nothing but frustration when trying to book a place through Airbnb. On numerous occasions, we were denied a place without a follow-up reason why and there were two times that we booked a home and were told by the owner that those days weren't actually open, they just forgot to mark them as not available -- whoops! One of those times, we even booked and paid in full and were charged extra, per the owner's request (because there was more than 1 person bidding on that weekend at the time), then we're told a month later that they forgot they booked that weekend a year ago and asked us to cancel our reservation and to look for another place. We found a place, not as nice as the first one we booked and had to pay an extra $500, but it was all that was left. Unless something big changes with this company, I won't be booking through Airbnb any time in the future.

My wife and I had a host that gave us a very neutral written review that I could see so I didn't worry about it. Airbnb, after the 14 days, sent me an email that the host had given us an unfavorable review. I called Airbnb and they gave me the actual ratings out of 5 on cleanliness (2), communication (2) and rules (1). We were shocked. Totally unjustified and certainly not reflected in her written review. We have no idea as to why our host trashed us. At this point there was no way to make a public response to her ratings. We left the place as clean and tidy as when we arrived. I still have the trail of communications that show we communicated well. After reviewing the rules after the fact, I realized that we broke only 1 rule, using the kitchen out of the specified time range, just before we left for the airport, between 2:30 and 3:00 am. Airbnb told me to contact the host directly, which I did, but she did not respond. Airbnb ARE NOT specific about how to address a HOST review disputed by the guest but they ARE specific about how to address a GUEST review disputed by the host.

I am a SUPER HOST with Airbnb. I have been using Airbnb for years, since they first started. It use to be so good. Now all I get is rude people picking up the phones and careless people about their jobs. One girl on the phone was having a conversation about someone so loud you would’ve thought they were at home answering calls. This girl was loud and ghetto and I couldn’t believe she was airing her personal business over a phone call.... she later hung up in my face. Aside from that, if I don’t call Airbnb, they will NEVER CALL ME BACK. They will open a order and close it without even handling what I have asked. I still have a water damage bill that hasn’t been paid by Airbnb “1mil” protection plan. This is $1200 worth of damage that a guest did and I have gotten ZERO CALLS AND ZERO PAYMENT FROM AIRBNB. Let’s keep going.......it’s been months that I have been waiting for my registration. It was because I needed to update my address. I did this, but because Airbnb hasn’t updated their system, the city hasn’t received the updated address, making my profile pending. It’s been pending for months and I am subject to getting thousands of dollars in fines by the city. I have called Airbnb numerous times. For over 4 months and still no fix. Airbnb can easily fix this but they give zero care about helping me. I use to love Airbnb but lately I have been so disrespected by this company I am questioning why I ever decided to join. I’m more hurt then angry that I have 100% positive reviews, I make Airbnb money, and yet they can’t even help me with an ERROR on THEIR END. All I get it “were so sorry someone will call you” MONTHS LATER NO CALL. It’s getting to the point where I am going to have to FLY DOWN TO THE HEADQUATERS JUST TO GET SOME ASSISTANCE! This is my main source of income and Airbnb can Care Less. I consider myself a very professional kind individual. It’s sad that Airbnb doesn’t care about their customers or ever their superhosts that are making them tons of cash. It’s to the point where I am so stressed out I am literally losing sleep over something that can be fixed on there end by a click of a button. Even the city hall director tried to call Airbnb with me. I was hung up on because it was a 3 way call. Airbnb is suppose to be a community, where kind people are making a change by bringing jobs to host and safe places for guest to stay. It’s suppose to be fun. Unfortunately it is becoming a huge burden and creating tons of stress in my life.

I signed up to host and had some bookings. It was nice , I signed up to b paid by bank transfer that they said takes 1-2 days,but then air Bnb told me they weren’t going to pay me for THIRTY DAYS!!! HORRID COMPANY!!!!

Airbnb offers absolutely no protection for the customers in case the homeowner decides to cancel the booking. Even if you have reserved your place and paid all the money, there's no guarantee whatsoever that the owner will keep it for you, up till the very day of your stay. In my case, the homeowner of a NYC apartment deliberately cancelled my booking 2 weeks before my $1400 worth stay, so I had to urgently seek a hotel in the vicinity - which turned out to cost me $700 more. On their end, AirBnb couldn't do much, and after a painstaking phone call with their customer representative, the best they could do was to offer me a paltry $15 discount on my "NEXT" stay. NEXT STAY?! Well, they are bold enough to think I will ever go back to their website again after that shameful incident.

Air BnB couldn't care less about their customers! I book an eclectic, cozy, quintessential Austin habitat in Austin for October. The owner took my deposit then realised that she had forgotten it was the Formula 1 GP. After prevaricating for a couple of weeks during which she asked for a further $180, she cancelled on me. Air BnB offers no option to report such an individual. I tried a general feedback form but received no reply and it has now been at least a month. Allegedly, they mark a cancellation against the host but there is nothing showing against her at the moment.

I have tried to use Airbnb for two separate trips, 6 months apart. During my first trip which I planned months in advance of the travelling dates, the owner ended up cancelling my stay a few days ahead of my flight, with no reason nor any form of communication. By the time I was able to book anything else, there were no other viable options available through airbnb and prices had tripled which had altered very significantly my trip (and finances). My second experience is from this week where I have been trying to make a request twice. Whilst I met all criteria for price displayed, property availability and minimum duration the owner didnt reply on time for the first property and my request got cancelled by Airbnb. I then tried to book a second property and this time the owner replied but advised me via messaging that they would only accept a longer stay on the requested period (despite this not specified by Airbnb). In summary, my experience with Airbnb has been horrible. Owners have all rights and do not need to commit to any information advertised, leaving potential guests to pay the price. This App is absolute rubbish and I will never use this again.

It is hard to understand how AirBnb stays in business with their non-existent customer service and total lack of concern for people simply trying to do business with them. I chose an available property, emailed the property owner and submitted my payment information. After giving all of my info, I got a vague pop up notice from Airbnb saying there was some problem in accepting my credit card information advising me to use their HELP desk if I wanted immediate help. Of course I wanted immediate help, I am trying to book a property for a vacation and the clock is ticking. I tried submitting my credit card information again, getting the same error message. I tried using another credit card and got the same error message. I then went looking for the well hidden "HELP" tab on the Airbnb website. Honestly, it's as if they do not want you to find out how to communicate with them. I submitted a message with my problem and about 18 hours later I received an email containing a "form letter" response that had NOTHING to do with my particular problem. Additionally Aivbnb "closed" the case, making it impossible for me to respond to the thread. Their message to me was clear, "We sent you an email, we really don't care about your problem, now please shut up." Coincidentally , about 18 hours later, the property owner started emailing me, telling me the property was available and asking me if I NOW wanted to book it. In conclusion, Airbnb makes it very difficult to ask a simple question and receive assistance, while letting their customers know the company has absolutely no intention of offering any kind of quality customer service. I have deleted my Airbnb account.

I'm thinking this "Trustpilot" has some stock in VRBO or Hilton. These reviews are absolute BS. So sorry I reviewed some other companies with them before I looked at AirBNB's reviews. 80% of them don't make sense as to AirBNB's policies and guest and host guidelines. Somebody at this review site got an ax to grind. Just like at Yelp, anyone with a tiny brain or a "verified" purchaser can tell they ARE 90% FAKE. We have used AirBNB in the States for 8 YEARS and a couple of times in Puerto Rico, and had one host that was a wee bit odd, but nothing much to remark about later. I too have had a host cancel while we were in the air....AirBNB bent over backwards to help, to refund, to call us repeatedly to know if we were satisfied, and to give a free night at their expense. AirBNB deserves all the accolades they have from other less.... shady review sites. From Staten Island, NY to Ocean Beach, San Diego, and all in Between, AirBNB has been a godsend to us, and our family(and have used the referral $ without problems). We wouldn't have EVER been able to see the places we have seen or meet the wonderful people we have without them. God Bless AirBNB.

Got scammed by a guest who didn't arrive on check-in day. Airbnb couldn't give me any decent explanation, the terms of cancellation don't seem to operate as Airbnb took no responsibility for this or for the failure of their system: the guest still has her profile on the site with at least 16 reviews saying she is legitimate. The most worrying aspect is safety as Airbnb makes out that people are verified and reviewed but how can this person still have a profile if she is supposedly a scammer? I also had items stolen by a guest who still has a 5 star profile... They make money off guests and hosts but offer very little in terms of support.

Really bad treatment from airbnb customer service I contacted Airbnb's customer service because I had been trying to use some credit I got for inviting me friend, who had then become a host. I wasn't informed that the credit would expire withing a year, and they told me I would get it back, because I had been trying to use it one day too late. So I cancelled a reservation to be able to use the credit, but the coupon they had given me was only a 10% coupon, which was a lot less than they had promised me (560 dkr). So I called them and they were trying to figure out what had happened. They promised to get back to me within 1-2 hours, and since then I have called them four times, and every time they promised to make the responsible agent call me back immediately. I don't believe he will ever call, and I feel frustrated because I got this credit in the first place from recommending airbnb, and now I feel that they are not there for their custommers at all.
You're not allowed to have any medical emergency once you sign up for something everything is in concrete with them
AWFUL - stay away. I am a host who had a problematic guest - they have offered no help no support, even dropping calls when they dont want to engage with me about the issue STAY AWAY

Terrible company, they tell you they will help you and find you a new property if you arrived to one in bad condition but really they won't do anything but lie and promise open promises. I would never book through them again and no one else should book with them, unless you like staying in places that are full of roaches with zero customer service

AirBnB used to be a great company about 2 years ago, they had a fair and balanced platform, they protected the hosts from fraudulent and scam artist guests that were trying to hurt hosts so they could get a free credit. Now days their host support, payments, and just everything has gone downhill badly. We are actively looking to list our 4 properties elsewhere. They also don't do any type of background check on guests and we end up having some pretty bad people arrive to our house. They have become definitely a company that is not worth doing business with.

I think their business model is terrible!!! Don't use them. About a year ago, I was credited $75, and used that money for a planned trip at another Airbnb. I ended up not needing the Airbnb accommodation and cancelled (well in advance of the cancellation deadline). Airbnb ended up keeping my $75 saying they don't refund credits with cancelled trips. What a crappy way to do business!

Great customer service team! Had to cancel reservations due to realization that the listing requires my grandparents to frequently climb stairs to reach bedrooms and bathroom. Host was understanding. After cancellation, i made another booking for a 1 floor accomodation. But only came to realize that the service charged by Airbnb for the cancelled reservation would not be refunded. So i wrote a claim to explain the reason for my cancellation and 1hr later, Airbnb Customer Service Team replied and called to assist me. Xy and the team were quick to respond and informed me that normally service charge cannot be refunded but understood my reason and thus proceeded to refund me the service charge. Xy was very friendly during our short conversation and im very thankful for their understanding. Definitely will continue to be a Airbnb user for a looooong time!
Of the three times I have used Air BnB it has only gone successfully once. I wont use again,I must admit the customer service for me was always quite good.

Customer service extremely unhelpful. I made a reservation and chose the option to pay 50% now, 50% later. I paid for the initial 50% with my credit card. I received a gift card after I made the reservation and contacted customer service to see if I could apply the gift card toward the remaining balance. They put me on hold for 5-7 minutes and came back saying I could not, I had to pay the rest with credit card. I said that was ridiculous and unacceptable, let me speak with someone that could help me. They said no one could help me. They put me on hold for a bit longer. They came back and said they would have to cancel the entire reservation and rebook it with the seller if I wanted to pay part of the balance with gift card. I had already signed contracts with the owner, etc. They didn't care. On top of that, they are making at least $100 of the $500 reservation in fees, based on the contract from the owner. $100 should by some level of service, but not with AirBnB. First and last time using AirBnB.

Airbnb customer services are rubbish. They discriminate and take biased decision not based on facts. Will not reccmond at all. I hope hosts and guests will make this company closed soon. I can not imagine how a business can work being discreminatory and biased.

Customer service is a group of idiots. They let guests scam the owners too easily. No matter how much evidence i provide, they protect the guests. They stand to make more from travelers than hosts. Disgusting. Taking all my houses solely to VRBO where they care about owners.

Customer service is absolutely mortifying! We got scammed by their VERIFIED host, and all we get when we contacted their support team was "we'll get back to you." No one ever got back to us. They ruined all our plans, and all we get is a delayed refund without any explanation. We tried contacting their support again so as to have them explain the very lousy support to make up for the horrible experience, buy they never answered and just closed our ticket! ABSOLUTE WORST!

I found out 24 hours after I signed up to host that my condo building does not allow these companies. Airbnb is arguing that with me saying their team says it's OK. I cancelled and am relieved to be out.

Recently signed up for Airbnb for a small vacation on a weekend. But I was having a problem with having my ID being verified and couldn’t book the I wanted. Called customer service, who were genuinely nice for the most part, but essentially were useless had me assigned to a manager to “handle” my situation. Well unfortunately, they lied to me almost everyday for the next 3-4 days saying I would speak with one that day. Then when I finally get in contact with one, the individual was just as useless as the normal customer service people. And that carried on for another 3 days. IF YOU HAVE A PROBLEM THEY WILL NOT FIX IT! Going back to TripAdvisor.
F*c*u*k* you Airbnb, you have ruined my holiday!!!

Poor support for hosts and guests. Everything is great until it isn't. We found this out the hard way with a guest who was clearly a sketchball (no real name, even though he claimed to have a verified ID) and tried to stay at our house within 12 hours of booking it. Airbnb said they would call him to help him rebook when we cancelled the instabook. He showed up anyway. Never turn on insta-book or you will regret the control you give away. As guests we have always had good experiences; however, we worry what would happen if anything went south and we needed support or assistance.

Wouln't use Airbnb again. After booking 2 months prior host came back and said they double booked "its never happened before" and offered two families whom whole idea was to stay in the one property, could shift it to two separate properties. I simply don't believe that it took two months to discover it was double booked and we were the second ones who booked the same property, if so why did it take so long to notify us. Further those with STRICT cancellation policies should get reciprocated financial recourse towards the guest whom get cancelled on.

I don't understand how two of the places I stayed at had such great reviews. My experience was so different. Because you are depending on other peoples reviews, you have to trust that you are getting a quality place. I have rented 3 places total in less than a year. What I have found is that the reviews in no way even come close to reality. Customer service can be great to really poor, depending on who you get. Well, I am done with airbnb. It was an excellent concept with a less than satisfying product. It's too bad. You can not do anything about an unreasonable hosts review of you. a.) a host should have garbage pick up, b.) he should have trash cans for each unit, not sharing 3 cans amongst 2 homes with 6 to 8 people in each. Also, when a host has a mud yard with a beige carpet, to complain of dirty rugs is stupid. And when you complain about a place the host writes you a bad review. Just not worth it. Bye Bye airbnb! One rental, and I gave them a good review, had a dangerously slippery entrance, and no lighting at night! Dangerous!

Very poor. It's not really until you have a problem that you realise just how pathetic this company is. The customer service is non existent. You would think that with the ludicrously high fees they are creaming off everybody that they would be able to afford a decent customer service team. Not so. Beware. You could be next.

This is for all the folks that has ever thought about using Airbnb.com I just left a place that was too nasty to stay in. Because I didn't cancel before check in, I only got a sixth of what I paid refunded. Because I cancelled I can't leave a review. Keep that in mind when you see awesome reviews. Perhaps current photos of the bathroom would be wise to ask for in advance. as a disclaimer, my first two experiences were great, the last two has been so awful I will never use this again.

Our trust in what Airbnb advertises on their website regarding their "service" is forever gone. We were in Houston for medical appointments at MD Anderson for a week recently. The apartment we rented through Airbnb was advertised as "Wonderful Medical Center Apartment" (see airbnb rooms/22230166). In the description of the apartment under "house rules" and "read all rules", the "host", who works for Urban Corportate Housing LLC, states: "Potential for noise - The Metro Light Rail runs near the property and is heard several times during the day only." Gross misrepresentation of issues connected with the property! The Metro Rail trains - one northbound and one southbound - run every 6 minutes (10 times an hour times 2 trains = 20 times an hour) not only during the day, but also almost all through the night - ending around 3:00 am and starting up again around 4:00 am. This ground level apartment faces Braeswood Blvd and the trains run down the middle of this street. Braeswood intersects with Greenbriar within a very short distance (the apartment complex is on the northeast corner of this intersection). The trains make a turn at this intersection, so there are gates that go down, with bells clanging, to stop traffic. The trains blast their horns as they approach and make this turn. So, reality is that there is constant noise all day and night long. Result - no sleep!! Isn't this considered a form of torture? (Yes, I'm being sarcastic.) We left two days early when we were through with the medical appointments, and couldn't get away from this place fast enough. This senior citizen ended up sleeping on a blow up mattress in the bedroom closet (large enough to put one in there) for 6 nights. Also, when the "host" never returned my calls, I went to the apartment complex office to see if I could get another contact number to call. I found out there is another rental agency that "subleases" apartments in this complex, and its name is Medical Center Apartments - the Greenbriar. I was gobsmacked. Poor customer service but then rude customer service on top of that. They have offered me a voucher that covers 60% of the total price paid and then closed the case. Not acceptable. I did so but after a lot of back and forth the host finally offered very little (less than half) and was unprofessional once I raised the issue. I escalated to the Airbnb Customer Experience Team - what a waste of time. You have to have photos to prove that the accommodation was unclean despite providing details, or else they take the word of the host over yours, whether they're telling the truth or not. Forget the customer always being right. The customer in their eyes is clearly the host. Also, don't say anything to the host about what you will do if you're not satisfied with their response (escalate or leave a detailed review) - that is considered extortion and disqualifies you from leaving a review and getting an appropriate refund. This company sets things up so they and the host are the primary parties who are protected. The burden for the quality of the accommodation and stay falls on you as the guest to prove how unclean, inaccurate or unprofessional things were and you have to go to ridiculous lengths to give the host the opportunity to rectify the situation as soon as you find a problem...absurd business model. You, as the customer/guest are the one who is inconvenienced when the host doesn't uphold basic standards of cleanliness, safety, amenities and comfort a guest should be able to expect. Know all their terms and conditions before staying in someone's home or you will be out of luck as I was. Better yet, don't use Airbnb!!! The review process is a joke - if you tell the truth about a bad experience, the host can give you a bad review in retaliation so you suffer. And they will only publish your review if the host reviews you in return...hmm, think the hosts know and use that tactic to avoid bad reviews??!! But they don't consider THAT extortion in their strict rules about extortion. If you don't leave a review to prevent retaliation from the host, other guests suffer as I did because we don't see honest bad reviews. This is not real life, folks and is a scam. There is no responsible support from the Customer Experience Team, who does nothing if you have a problem but regurgitate their policies (which unwittingly you violated because they're so arcane). It appears from reading all these reviews that it is a bad deal all around, as both hosts and guests are suffering from Airbnb's poor business practices, which benefit only them. This dodgy business needs to be shut down. I will go back to staying in hotels as I always have because of the consistency of cleanliness and amenities one can expect to find, and having a responsible company to turn to if you have a problem. Airbnb is not professional or responsible and I am done with them. I want to enjoy my nights away rather than be disgusted because someone doesn't know how to clean, sleep poorly and have all this aggravation in the likely event things go awry because there is no real quality control or barrier to entry for hosts. It's all about profit for Airbnb and they make money by protecting their moneymakers - the hosts.

On the 11th of March, I booked an apartment in Poland. The response of the host was that the price was higher for the period (Christmas) that I booked. I filled a complaint at Airbnb stating that the EU Directive for Consumer Rights does not allow traders to change prices. It states: "Traders are obliged to display correct and complete pricing information before a customer makes a purchase online". Additionally, Article 7.12. of the terms and conditions of Airbnb for hosts states:"You are solely responsible for setting a price (including any Taxes if applicable) for your Listing (“Listing Fee”). Once a Guest requests a booking of your Listing, you may not request that the Guest pays a higher price than in the booking request." Nevertheless, Airbnb responds that no sales has been made due to the fact that the host provided me with an alternative proposal. Also, they mentioned that it is unfortunate, that no all of their hosts are aware of the ability to change prices a year in advance. My conclusion: the tools are their for the hosts, the terms and conditions clearly states that hosts are responsible for showing the right price, nevertheless, Airbnb does not protect it's users when hosts violate the law and their own terms and conditions.
