Although you can tell fundamentally the representatives are trained for empathy and professionalism, when it comes down to it... they cant make sense of the transactions page any better then me. It's the perfect conditions and ground to lose track of payments. At the end their reasoning and transaction page platform is worse then any other hosting platform, I have to walk them through every single transaction and guest every time time I speak to a new representative and still not getting answers to the simplest questions and on hold forever. 5:20 typing this and still waiting. My experience as a host has been good generally speaking with people and the the hosting experience as a whole. Nevertheless, being on hold for so long trying to figure things out, the mismatch of information between agents, reps and supervisors and the lose of time and money. I am better of just renting my rooms to a longer term roommate. Its way too much hustle for $21/night that they suggest on my account. Trust me its not worth the hold and the Airbnb customer service runaround on my own property. It is 5:35 still on hold for a supervisor. Its 7:09 pm, been told that my problem is obvious and its being fixed. 9:10 Still on hold now for a different supervisor. From 10:48am to 9:10pm, still waiting for someone to respond to someone so that someone can pick up the line.

Worst experience of ALL TIME. I booked and they took $363 from my account for a bungalow in Panama that was ALREADY booked and the gal that owned the place CANCELED - when it was CLEARLY listed as AVAILABLE on AIRBNB. I had no money left to rebook anything so had to pin up in a hostel since AirBnB cleared it from my account. They tried to give me CREDIT instead of a REFUND - I attempted to book another place they had listed as AVAILABLE - it took 2 DAYS to get a response that this place was ALSO BOOKED and they ALSO CANCELED. WHAT A NIGHTMARE - ruined my trip. AND THEY HAVE STILL NOT REFUNDED MY MONEY. They cleared my account, caused so much added stress and wasted time, and have done NOTHING in return. They still have not refunded my money and it has been OVER 10 days now... NEVER EVER USE Airbnb - SAVE YOURSELF -
bad bad bad, especially their website. confusing and impossible to find information. If you like your home, don't use airbnb.
Worst Customer Service. Arrogant staff. Non Host friendly. List your property elsewhere.

Appauling customer service. My account was hacked last week and about $800 dollars were spend on a holiday I never booked! I must’ve sent about 30 emails and called a dozen of times and my money STILL hasn’t been refunded! I’m unable to pay rent, there’s no updates on my situation, I am in disbelief and how shoddily this company in run.

We booked my wife into a flat in Israel which was advertised under an entirely false description. It stated "private entrance." A lie. Afer we had booked and paid our deposit our son-in-law checked and found that there was no "private entrance." My wife was expected to share a flat with a man. The "private entrance" meant each bedroom had a door" Gee, I never expected a bedroom door (!) There was hostily when the booking was cancelled and the renter failed to return £56.37 of our deposit, despite his false description. Further, trying to contact this organisation is virtually impossible-you just get a set of idiotic standard answers which do not fit. They are not intereested. My letter to the Tourist Authority may wake them up!

Our place in Whistler, BC was booked 6-7 weeks ahead of time and then canceled 8 days prior to check-in by the host. Airbnb offered little assistance in finding a new place. The prices doubled between the booking time and the time it was canceled. We finally got them to pay the difference of the cost to book a place in a similar location but that took an entire weekend and into the next week to get them to do the right thing. The place we ended up in turned out to be close but moldy and dusty. There were visible dust bunnies under the furniture. And a leaking ceiling. It was warm and close to our destination at least. Poor quality control on Airbnb’s part. Airbnb was a mess and we will be using hotels even if the cost is higher.

We booked via Airbnb platform 3 bedroom cottage in Sainte-Adele, QC, Canada, We booked the entire house, paid through Airbnb and received a confirmation. Upon arrival, we discovered that 2 bedrooms in this cottage were locked. We contacted our host, Tommy **, and asked him to unlock the bedrooms. He explained that we need to pay more money to him directly if we want to unlock the rooms and also additional money as a fee for opening bedrooms. We contacted Airbnb support team with no results. My husband tried to sleep this night on the couch, no linen, no blanket, nothing. Our next vacation day we spent talking to different members of support team and finally to case manager Arianna. She did not explained our options but gave us guarantee in words that the situation will be resolved by the evening, the host should come and open another bedroom. Then it was a second sleepless night on the couch. Next morning we cancel this reservation. Airbnb punished us for cancellation, but not the host for cheating and extorting money from us. Be aware, this company support host's cheating and money extortion from the Guests, don't count on their help, they would only waste your time and your money.

Horrible customer service and support! They allowed an owner renting out 2 bedrooms in her house at the end of a hallway as a entire standalone guesthouse because it had a door to the outside. You call and try to sort it out and the response is that it’s consistent with their definition. Basically you are on your own! No interest to address, adjust, correct or otherwise. Never ever again!

To keep a very long story short! Host cancelled the day before holiday despite having booked 3 months previously stating that she had double booked. I was contacted by Airbnb case agent which was great and they made a lot of promises about looking into the additional costs of my accommodation and emailing me to get my feedback, but really it was a sales call to try and get me to book my accommodation through them again and once I informed them I had booked elsewhere I never heard back from them again. If all goes well, then its great, but the minute you have an issue you are pretty much on your own. Their policies favor their hosts and the guests get no compensation when it all goes wrong. I did receive my refund, but had I been the once to cancel at the last minute I would have lost all my money. What happens to the host? They get $100 fine which goes to Airbnb and then you can't even complain directly without lengthy phone calls or using their online process which once you have filled out your feedback basically tells you not to expect a response, but thanks for the feedback! It is a road to nowhere. My accommodation costs doubled due to the last minute cancellation at peak holiday time. Who is helping with that, certainly not Airbnb! I will NEVER use the service again and I feel sorry for this as I am sure there are a lot of reputable and honest hosts out there. Perhaps they should consider using a more reputable and honest forum for advertising their properties. Not so short after all!!

I wish I had seen this site before booking with Airbnb..... will never happen again! As with most others here we were stuck in another country and a host who double booked his condo.... what does Airbnb do? Re-book last minute at double the price!! This or be stuck in the street in another country. Customer service Eric laughed in my ear when hearing my demand they fine the owner to pay the difference in price for our last minute lodging problem. So basically yes they get Airbnb fees from us when booking and fine the owner while we are stranded with no where to go with NO compensation for this VERY bad experience. IF you do choose Airbnb be sure you have all info and contacts for the owners.... I feel like they don’t even do background checks to see if there owners are legit. Way to ruin a vacation guys! Airbnb will fail with this lack of support to clients using their system.

Booked a private room in a house on the Gold Coast, Australia for 10 days. I messaged back and forth with the home owner who represented herself as being retired and that she and her husband rented out rooms in their house on Airbnb for extra income. She indicated that she had grown children who had long left the family home and it was just her and her husband. I was travelling with my daughter who was 11 at the time. I had paid close to $1200 for the 10 day stay. When i arrived at the property, I was impressed as it was in a lovely street and the house was large and well maintained. We were shown to a room that was clean, bright and overlooking the garden, very lovely. Bathroom was a combined shower and toilet and it was also clean and well stocked but the owner pointed out that there was no lock on the bathroom door so had a little hotel style sign to hang on the doorknob to indicate bathroom was occupied. This immediately made me feel a bit uncomfortable, who has no lock on a toilet/bathroom door? After showing us to our room, the owner decided to introduce us to "John" a family friend who was apparently living at the house also and in a room right across the corridor from us?! Nothing was mentioned about this man during the initial conversations about who lived at the house. This man was around 50 years old and his room was a mess, it smelled weird like stale body odour and he had clothes and belongings strewn everywhere. He laid in his bed in his boxer shorts and just grunted a hello when introduced to us, his whole demeanour gave me the absolute chills. The homeowner explained that he was "a lovely guy" but had some issues and was currently unemployed?! My heart sank as I realised that as well as no locks on the bathroom door, the bedroom had no lock either and we were going to be sharing the entire upper level of the house with this man. I was furious that the home owner did not divulge this information to me about this "family friend" and i decided there and then that i would not be comfortable staying 10 whole days in the house especially with my young daughter! I made this clear to the home owner in as diplomatic a way as I could and she immediately became very annoyed and indignant and accused me of being judgmental and unfair. When i contacted Airbnb it was a nightmare, i was back and forth with them and the bottom line was that as far as they were concerned, the homeowner did nothing wrong by not disclosing who lived at the house and it was at the home owner's discretion as to what refund i would receive?! I would never, EVER use Airbnb again and I can now fully understand why they get such consistently woeful reviews! Pathetic customer service, this "business" is a joke.

Booked and paid for a place only to arrive there and not be able to contact the host. Airbnb could not reach the host either therefore cancelled our booking. We had no choice but to stay in a place double the price as we needed beds for the night.

I booked a place under the "Flexible" cancellation policy (the most relaxed). I thought that meant I had plenty of time to cancel should the need arise, and when I went to cancel only three days after booking, I was dinged the AirBnB fee. It turns out you have to cancel within 48hours to not pay the fee. This is total crap - why should AirBnB get a fee for doing nothing? If the host gets nothing, nor should AirBnB. Beware! I will be thinking twice about booking via AirBnB again.

I signed up to rent our home and had difficulty with the website letting guest book auto with out contacting me first. Changed it many times and it would always go back to auto booking. Problem to sink calendar with another website. Never did get it to sink. They paused our listing and thats fine with me. Not paying us till guest arrive was another red flag. Never could get the security deposit the way their website is set up. Someone didn't put enough thought into this. Very unfriendly to home owners. Not enough protection if you have damage. I think the reviews say it all.
I have used this many times on personal travel and everything worked out well.

Sadly, AirBnB are being extremely obtuse and bloody-minded by refusing to give me and the other neighbours in my block the information we want and need to know - i.e., whether two recent listings for an apartment on our floor stated that Parties and Events were permitted, or were NOT permitted. It's a perfectly simply and reasonable request, and it would help us resolve a very inflammatory dispute between neighbours. The issue is that both the tenants renting the apartment next door and the people who rented the apartment for 2 nights from them claim different things. Neither wants to acknowledge the blame, so the tenants are saying that the listing specifically forbade parties, while the AirBnB clients claim that the listing said it was OK to hold parties and events. This is obviously AirBnB's way of trying to protect everybody, including themselves, and helping nobody. They just act as a clearing house, passing on messages and ask everyone concerned to be nice to each other and apologize profusely, as if we were all little kids in kindergarten and everybody had to kiss and make up, then be friends again. I am very disappointed with them. They are raking in money like nobody's business but their customer service people are highly unethical and cowardly.

My boyfriend rented a room for a month in LA. Mind you he texted them prior to showing up and the owners failed to respond. He got there late in the night and the owner says to him “uhh how long are you staying here again?” THEY WERE OVERBOOKED AND HE ENDED UP PAYING ALL THIS MONEY TO SLEEP ON THE COUCH ACROSS A RANDOM PERSON SNORING ON THE OTHER COUCH. Needles to say, this is an unreliable company to work with.

The Airbnb was not acceptable. The building was not maintained. The beds was horrible the water cuts off the TV never worked. The rooms was dusty and dirty. One of the room had bed bugs. The beds are small full sized. The owner scammed up by marking up fares on tours prices. No WiFi connection as advertised. The elevator did not work. They did not replace Toilet papers nor cleaned the rooms unless asked. This place is not suitable for 9 people and it’s not suitable at all. The host should not be trusted. The place is unsuitable don’t be deceived. The place has no closet and can hardly accompanists your personals.

Airbnb called me the at 8pm the nigh before my check-in to inform me that my host had double booked my house. This was after I received my payment receipt and check in instructions. The call was at 8pm on Valentine's Day 1/14/18, the night before we were to fly to Florida. There policy of allowing the host to cancel at any time without notice stinks. To make mater worse their mobil phone email network was down. When I arrived in Florida on President weekend with no place to stay, they did nothing to help .I was on hold for 15 plus minutes each time I called. I spoke with 4 different reps, each had no knowledge of the previous call. One rep Cindy finally helped and found a room for the night. They finally sent me 4 options, 3 were booked and one was 60 miles from my original reservation. STAY AWAY FROM THESE GUYS. THEY DON'T CARE. They allow the host to cancel at the last moment. I'm guessing the he got a better deal. By the host was Joshua and his property 40 Via Floresta Dr. Boca Raton Florida 33487. I'd stay away from this guy also.

I have just had a great holiday in Spain but there were somethings wrong. My gripe is I went to leave a honest review but until the host replies then it doesn't get published. 3 weeks later it still isn't published. Some of the remarks I left ( Not bad but about the location ) need to be seen by people who are booking this place. Also there were good reviews about the area in general, but no one will know until is too late if the review is not published. Trying to get hold of Airbnb to find out about this is a nightmare.

I have had the WORST experience with Airbnb. I have had an ongoing case with the company where my things were essentially robbed in the host's apartment (massive security issue). They claimed they had insurance/filled a police report and would assist with rectifying the problem. I also filled a case with Airbnb- now roughly 2 months later my case has still not been resolved. I received no sympathy from the Host or Ainb, no follow ups at all despite my calls and email. They even hung up on me TWICE, ignored my messages. Despite being very polite just wanting a solution. I am absolutely APPALLED with the customer service, lack of communication and lack of empathy. I have received nothing 2 months later. I am filling a police report and reporting this to the financial ombudsman. Never again AIRBNB, this has been the worst experience ever.

Airbnb is NOT customer friendly. I have two small coupons they gave me for a TERRIBLE experience I had in one of their international homes. They only allow one coupon to be used at a time forcing my family to book two Airbnb’s if I want to use both of my coupons. They will not let me combine the coupons on one stay. This one trip is the only vacation my husband will get this year, so we can’t book another and the coupons expire in June. A company with great customer service is one that makes decisions based on what’s best for the customer, not the company. Be more customer friendly in your policies. Until then, Airbnb has lost this customer.

DO NOT BOOK WITH AIRBNB. We booked a reservation with a host SEVEN months in advance. We went to confirm our stay with the host a week before leaving and they said they were not going to honor our reservation. Apparently they were not allowed to offer Airbnb in the residence anymore. They failed to tell us that. So we call Airbnb and request a refund and compensation to pay for a hotel (as we are 4 days from the trip - Spring break in Cancun) they offer TEN PERCENT of the original stay. Trying to find a place to stay in this location and time is IMPOSSIBLE AND EXPENSIVE. I guess their customer service thinks that an extra $40 is enough to pay for a last minute reservation. THEN the refund was supposed to take 5-10 days when we leave in 4... Only after talking to 4 customer service reps and a manager was I able to get an extra $100 (which I’m not even sure I will be getting). So now we are stuck trying to find a reservation 4 days before our trip and we can only afford the less-than-decent accommodations now when we had booked a luxury location. Airbnb failed to help us in any useful way (sure, they sent other Airbnb listings - but no way in hell I will ever trust them again). Had I not tried to confirm my reservation I would be stranded in Mexico with no place to stay. They claim the amount needed to reserve decent accommodations was “out of their budget” yet neglect to think that it might be WAY oiut of my budget too?! Thanks to YOUR host I now have to pay an additional HUNDREDS of dollars for this. Do not ever trust these people. They take little to no responsibility for the actions of their hosts.

Horrible!!!!! We rented a place that looked wonderful on line. When we got there, it was a dive, AND it was unsafe as a sliding window above our first floor bed unable to be secured. We had paid over $500 for three nights. We had to stay the first one as it was late and there was nowhere to go. Left early in the morning after a sleepless night . Notified the host AND air b&b before 8 am that we had checked out, and why. Host refused to give be us back money for our remaining 2 nights( gave us $55 back) air b&b would do NOTHING!!! Had to pay for the dump room and also an expensive hotel for the remaining two nights. THEN, I left a review, saying I thought I must have been in the wrong place because other reviews were so good and the place was awful. Well, my review was never published, and when air b&b finally responded to my repeated inquiries, they said it couldn’t be published because it didn’t meet their guidelines?!?!? Really!?! There was no profanity or names mentioned, it was just an HONEST review. They also told me, I could not rewrite it as it was too late!!!!!! So THIS is why there were not ANY , even slightly negative reviews! They only publish the ones they want to. What a bad experience! Lesson learned!

I have reserved a house on airbnb but the price were different when I pay it. Its 30euros difference of total 466euros. I contacted airbnb and no response. Then I message to airbnb facebook. Customer support contact me and explain this is a currency problem however, the currency would be at least 1.0 different rate which is unusual. Then they turn around to say because of the host. The host have fully control with the price. Before I contact airbnb, the host already said he has no idea and didn't change the price. Anyway, airbnb used to be a good company but now they increase their service charge poor services. This is nothing about the host, its only the company.

They lie... I made a reservation that stipulated I could cancel with a full refund of fees if I did so before 7 days out from checkin. I canceled 3 weeks ahead and did not receive a full refund. I called in - difficult to find the number, long wait times - but the person was nice and offered an immediate discount on the reservation I did hold and the refund of the balance of what I had paid for the reservation I canceled. The discount was supposed to be immediate and the refund a couple weeks til it posted to my credit card. After 2 weeks and no refund, I called them back and was told there was no record of an agreement to refund the balance if what was owed. I am told someone will review the case and contact me. Issues: they don't honor their refund policy, their CSR's make promises that they don't keep and don't record in the notes. I'm soured on this company. It's easy enough to check out whether the places are decent, but if there is any issue with Airbnb - refunds, or host cancellations etc, good luck. March update:I never received the promised phone call or emails from the escalation, only an email asking if the 2nd CSR had resolved the issue. I now have filed a dispute with my credit card and the next day received a survey email from AirBnb. Still waiting...

I love their platform and interface. It is very user-friendly. Also, they offer the option to review your guests. That way the guests are conscious of what they write about you too. They want to leave a good review for the hosts in order to receive a positive review. That is my personal favorite feature of this site. My wife and I have been running a hostel for 4-5 years now and we have had little or no issue with the site. Follow their rules and all will be well...

I am beyond fed up, and outraged over experience with this LOUSY company. I had a so-called guest (one with serious emotional issues who should NOT be allowed to use the site) complain because I have dogs (yet the ad specified that FACT before she booked) - she complained constantly, and then when I left the house for an appointment, she went into my kitchen and EMPTIED MY FRIDGE OF ALL FOOD AND THREW IT OUT. sHE made such a huge mess it was impossible to dig through a huge trash can full of food so I let it go, but then when I left the house a second time 2 days later she finished the job removing EVERYTHING (sealed containers of cheese and butter, juice, fruits and veggies, meat, all nature of items, including medication for my dogs, microwave popcorn packages, cookies, crackers, nuts etc. I confronted her, she got huffy and left the next morning. Airbnb arbitrarily decided to give her a refund (she was booked for a month, left in less than a week) - stiffing me for an entire month. Then, in a scramble of empty words, I am 'given' a partial refund for groceries, which in turn was deducted from the month's rent - leaving me with NADA, except out several hundred dollars! Of course, try to get access to anyone online - impossible. So I called, and got a run-around of more empty words, with lots of "so sorry" - but the bottom line is I got screwed twice -- and the wretched b***H who created the problems? She was not inconvenienced one iota! Further, they allowed her to post a negative review of lies - in which she called my house a house of horrors! That despite constant positive reviews! The rules and nature of operations for airbnb sucks - it puts hosts at risk, in double jeopardy should they get a nightmare wretch like the one I just got rid of, and further, they have insurance for liability to it costs them nothing but platitudes! I have decided to do NO MORE business with these people - there are too many problems not the least of which is that they have too many properties in all area so bookings are down; they put pressure on hosts to keep lowering prices to the point of a no-win deal, and as for unruly outrageous guests - they protect them and they get off scott free! I AM TRULY FURIOUS -- BOYCOTT THIS CRAP OPERATION!

Airbnb will never take the side of the host. Remember this if you want to host your property. They will always take the side of the tenant even if they make lies or destroy your property. When you go to call or contact them they will ignor you. The only time when they will be willing to listen if you make a small claims through the court. Then they put their head in their backside and submit like a dog LOL.
absolutly horrible customer service.. NEVER NEVER more

We will not use Airbnb or this host ever again. Airbnb is, in our opinion, very HOST focused. My husband and I have traveled often in the past 10 years. 3 times to Hawaii and then to many other places as well. We have NEVER experienced such poor quality of customer. Our experience with the host and Airbnb has been far from acceptable. Within two hours of our arrival... I called the host right away about the size of the property... was told to move stuff onto the patio outside. We could barely fit two suitcases, a stroller and a pack and play in the room. Followed up with Airbnb and she told me she would look into it. I also told her the room lacked cleanliness and items that were said to be in the property were not. I then submitted photographs in support of my claims. After doing that, I researched and waited to hear back. When I did I received the “run around” with the same answers over and over again. It has made me feel that we are not important as guests. Cleanliness is a reason that a guest can cancel according to Airbnb. On the website it reads: “at the start of the Guest’s booking, the Accommodation: (i) is not generally clean and sanitary (ii) contains safety or health hazards that would be reasonably expected to adversely affect the Guest’s stay at the Accommodation in Airbnb’s judgment, (iii) does not contain clean bedding and bathroom towels available for the Guest’s use, or (iv) has vermin or contains pets not disclosed in the Listing.” The property was dirty. We were told that we could find someone to clean it and they would reimburse us for $50. The room needs a deep clean... not just an everyday tidying up job. We were also charged an additional $38/day for an additional guest (a 5 month old infant). We were not aware of this charge. Due to the dishonest nature from beginning to end, I highly recommend that people NOT use Airbnb or this host. Airbnb is about the host and will back the host and leave the guest to deal with any issues. It is in my experience that the customer should remain the priority. We have not received that. After traveling for 14 hours with three tiny ones I would have hoped to have a warmer inviting greeting. Instead we’ve spent that time trying to deal with the issue I presented above only to receive a response of “that’s too bad”. All we want is a refund so that we can move forward and find somewhere else to stay during our vacation and they’re not willing to even accommodate part of that.

One of the worst companies to ever work with. Not only were we denied our requested amount refund due to a poor stay with our host but were sent in a run around to try and get the customer service to help us receive our refund. Has been over a month and counting since we returned from our trip back in January. Utterly horrible, customer service reps said they would call, never did, wouldn't talk to me about it because it was my boyfriend who booked the trip even though I was included on the itinerary. SO unprofessional. Seriously a horrible company and poor hosts.
If I could give zero I would. I stayed in an airbnb drugs den which gave me an epilepsy seizure. Since then they have ignored every single complaint and deleted my review of the property
Shocking customer service. I had problems with the site and my profile and their only solution was to repeatedly send me the host's details. They don't control Airbnb emails. Will not use again
They will not reimburse hosts for damages caused by guests. They proudly claim they will pay with their insurance but this is not true. I am extremely disappointed.

OMG!!! Shocking experience - Booked Villa and then the owner cancelled our reservation and said the prices were wrong and tried to increase it by another £1000 for a week. Have called Airbnb and so far have been cut off 4 times.

I have had nothing but great experiences with my Airbnb rentals when traveling. We save a ton vs staying at hotels and my family loves the extra room we get from staying at a house or condo. It’s also nice to be able to cook some meals vs eating at restaurants for every single meal. I always read the reviews especially most recent, check out the picture and communicate with owners or property managers before booking so I know exactly what to expect. If you do this you should have no problem. It’s always a nice touch when the owners stock you up with snacks and waters for your stay too! It’s my family’s preferred way to travel for sure!

I feel like a fool for giving them a copy of my driver's license. Next thing I know, they've already accessed my email contacts list & want access to my phone via the camera so I can take a "selfie" for verification! They now want a credit card number before they will delete my account! This is just creepy and not safe! DO NOT Trust Air BnB!

Host cancelled the same day, after the check-in time and about 30 minutes before we were about to arrive (5:30pm the day of arrival). I reserved Lindsay's place for Saturday and Sunday of a long weekend (after another host had cancelled a few days before a trip). I reserved 1 1/2 days before our arrival; the next day I had not heard anything regarding how to check-in, so I messaged her again on AirBnB. Still did not hear anything (we were en route, driving through sleet), so I texted her at the phone number provided. About 15 minutes later, I get a pop-up message from AirBnB that the reservation had been cancelled. She did not message or text to apologize or to explain why; we ended up having to stay in a crappy hotel out by the airport because everything was booked. I've never had a host cancel last-minute like this, but apparently there is no recourse and my $310 still has not been refunded :( I spent about 45 minutes on the phone with customer service before the system hung up on me, then I got an email from my "case manager" apologizing and suggesting other AirBnB rentals - but 90% of those were not even available for the weekend. I still (3 days later) have not heard back from them.

Not sure what happened to airbnb but their service has gone done the drain. It's pretty much a nightmare to work with this company now. We need a better solution with the fees they are charging, it's crazy.

What a joke. Sit on hold for 20 minutes. Spoke to someone who lied to me 30. Was told a case was opened and should be fixed in 1 to 2 hours and they would call back. No call. I called again to find no open case. Also at that point they magically had no record of my call. Bunch of people who just lie to their custimets

DO NOT US AIRBNB or VRBO. Same owners We booked a place and received a confirmation and noticed that they had ended the trip a day earlier than we booked it for. Understand we are there for a tournament and don’t get to choose the dates. So we had to stay another night. However, when the condo owner called us about this she said she didn’t have us booked at all for the condo that it was someone else. So we didn’t have a place AT ALL but we’re charged for it. And they want refund us because they are basing it on the original refund policy. Which would make sense if we actually ever had the place. Called them and they were rude and not helpful and wouldn’t even allow me to speak to a supervisor. Also, we can’t find a place now. Everything is booked!! the worst business ever The whole time things that showed available were not. DO NOT USE! They SCAM!!

We did not stay the night at a property that a property listed in Redfern in Sydney. The house was infested with too many mosquitos, flies, cockroaches and night beetles. I handed the keys back to owner assigned this contact as we have checked into a hotel even though we had paid $1606 FOR 5 NIGHTS!!! I understand that by Airbnb agreement I am not entitled for any refunds but I hoped we can work something out as the house was not habitable. Broken windows in the room upstairs made it impossible for us to protect ourselves from the mozzies. Thinking that AirBnb would help me out with my troubles I contacted your support. And they got back to me with an email from the owner of the property accusing me of lying and being late for check in. I CAN NOT BELIEVE THIS IS YOUR RESPONSE TO MY PLIGHT: "You reported that the listing was infested with too many mosquitos, flies, cockroaches and night beetles. As a guest you run the risk of being robbed or worse. 5. Even if you manage to book a place, the host may cancel on short notice to accommodate a "better" guest. 6. I travel 270+ days a year for business in the tech industry. I thought Airbnb would be a good way to enjoy extended stays at different projects. I am a contractor so I am responsible for my own expenses. One of my favorite travel perks is my American Express Platinum Club membership; I use the points for everything. When I saw I could link my card directly to Airbnb and use points for my stays, I said to myself, “What a great convenience!” My first Airbnb stay went great. I rented a penthouse condo for a week. Then the nightmare began, I was on business in Costa Rica to build a system to run a large call center, which would end up keeping me there for two months. I booked a few places to kind of Goldilocks my way around to find the best deal. I booked three locations, saw they were charged immediately to my Amex card, and went to sleep that night looking forward to a day of meetings. When I woke up the next morning, I turned on my computer, only to see my account had been suspended due to verification. I immediately contacted Airbnb support. They asked me if the email had been from someone at customer support. When I said it was, their only answer was they would expedite a response. Half way through the day it got worse. Since Airbnb suspended my account, I could not access the location of the host where I was supposed to stay that night. I called Airbnb and they told me they could not give me that information, and I would still have to pay for the nights I reserved. Having been a business traveler for over 30 years, I could never imagine reserving a hotel room, paying for it, then the hotel not giving me it’s location. I contacted American Express Platinum Services and they said that Airbnb had not tried to verify my account. Then things got bizarre. Airbnb sent me an email three days after this started asking for a picture of my Amex Card. I immediately called Amex and they informed me merchants were not allowed to ask for this kind of information. It has been two weeks since this incident and Airbnb has still failed to contact me or remove the suspension on my account. Don’t get me wrong, I would never use them again, but I worry because they have a copy of my passport on their system and I am worried about identity theft.

Before you use Airbnb you need to be aware that this is NOT a letting agent. It is a software company acting as a "middleman" for hosts and taking a large commission in return. This company has no interest whatsoever in guests. We used Airbnb for some of our stopovers whilst visiting Australia from the UK this year. All the accommodation was booked and paid for by February 2017. We left the UK on 1 October and the week before we sent courtesy emails to our hosts just to let them know that all was on track and we were looking forward to our stay. Three replied but one didn't which caused us slight concern. We contacted Airbnb - the reply was astonishing!! We were told that this host had ceased operating from June. Nobody had told us this and Airbnb tried to make out that it was up to the host to inform us. THIS WAS NOT TRUE. The ONLY way you can contact a host is by going through Airbnb who monitor all emails. Airbnb actually control which emails get to the host and which ones don't. It was legally their responsibility to contact all guests of that particular host to tell them of the change and, MORE IMPORTANTLY, to refund any monies paid. Airbnb didn't do this and were quite happy to keep our money (and no doubt that of others), presumably in the hope that we simply booked somewhere else and forfeited the money. We had to book alternative accommodation just 4 days before we left the UK. At such a late stage the accommodation cost us almost double what we had paid back in February. Airbnb VERY RELUCTANTLY refunded our money (it took them almost another month!!!!!) but wouldn't entertain any compensation. We informed our hosts at the other accommodations we had booked and each one of them said they had experienced problems as hosts with Airbnb and a couple said they were owed considerable sums of money which wasn't forthcoming. Use Airbnb at your own risk. I am now considering legal action.

Finally I am able to hail a taxi with a phone charger so I can get the address and return to the house. We make it back to his place and go inside. Being my friend is drunk, I had a few drinks myself, and it was 2am, we decided to hunker down for the night and leave that place first thing in the morning. An hour passes and I hear him come home so I get up and let him know we made it back and we were leaving in the morning. At this point he apologized for his behavior and seemed fine. I could sense someone was in the room. I sat up and saw his shadow crawling across the floor. I yelled "WHAT ARE YOU DOING?" Along with a few other choice words. He tells me he is looking for his dog (who was white and very clearly laying on the edge of my bed, very visible even in the dark). I tell him to get out, along with a few other choice words. I then lock the door again and prop a chair up against it. As I am trying to process what just happened I pick up my phone to see the time and notice it isn't charging, thinking maybe he unplugged it while crawling around I feel it is still plugged into the wall. I then go to turn on the lamp, it doesn't work, neither did the other two. It hits me this man has literally turned the power off to our room to prevent us from turning on the light while he was in there. Now I am in survival mode. I pack all of our belongings and get my friend out of bed in about 5 minutes. We make a plan, jet out of the house, and out to my car and speed off. We call Airbnb emergency number and initially they are great. They paid for us to get a hotel for the night and refunded our money from the host. They also told us he was blocked from the website and they gave me a $300 credit to use within the year. I tried 3 times to use the credit. It always said error contact customer service, which I did. This is my horror story from my stay in New Orleans with my sister. I will preface by saying that both my sister and I have traveled the world, been to many different countries and have stayed in hostels many times but never had an experience like this. We booked a room in a house in New Orleans. The house stated that it was on Frenchman Street – for those of you who are not familiar with this area, it’s a popular destination in New Orleans, lined with bars and restaurants where all the locals go to listen to live jazz music. Unfortunately, Airbnb does not disclose the exact address of the house until the day before your stay, they give you a radius to give you a general idea of where it’s located. Well, when we arrived at the house it was on the very far end of Frenchman Street, not at all in walking distance to that area as described (nor would it have been safe to walk, day or night, male or female, EVER). It was in a very bad, crime ridden area with bars on many of the windows and doors, and wood paneling covering windows that had been blown out. The house was not at all how it was described in the ad. We stepped outside for a moment to contemplate if it was safe to walk just around the corner to Walgreens, and within a few minutes someone made an attempt to rob us. I will spare the long details of this but luckily we escaped the situation unharmed. When we ran back into the house we discovered that someone left the door to the back patio unlocked. This was a shared space, meaning other guests were staying in other rooms just down the hall. Luckily no one had entered the home from off the street but we feared that if the guests accidentally left it unlocked again, that someone could enter the home in the middle of the night and rob us… or worse. Also, there were no locks on our bedroom door, leaving our belongings at risk while we were out exploring the city. I realize that New Orleans suffered awful devastation from Hurricane Katrina and is still recovering… and it’s really sad, but, Airbnb should be more forthcoming about the state of these houses/rooms. This place was completely misrepresented. It said there was a “porch overlooking the yard as well as street… and two sets of french doors that open up into Frenchmen Street, letting in plenty of light and allowing for prime people watching.” The french doors in the kitchen were bolted shut, and the only view from the porch was a very tall fence that separated the back of the house from the street, we couldn’t view the street as stated. In addition, the house was unsanitary. The pillows were stained brown (very brown, spotted, DISGUSTING), the towels that were folded and placed on the bathroom counter were damp and smelled like mold, the toilet wasn’t completely bolted down to the ground, etc. Unfortunately Airbnb has a refund policy that protects them from just about anything. We contacted their customer support line immediately and worked with a case manager in an attempt to get a refund but they refused. They said that they cannot refund due to neighborhood factors, only things pertaining to the house itself; so we sent the pictures of the house and everything inside that was dirty (including those nasty pillows) but they still refused. We were also shocked that there were no reviews about any of these things which leads us to believe that perhaps the negative reviews are being deleted. After the incident I decided to do some more research on the company, and found that other people have experienced the following situations (also without refunds): door locks being broken when you arrive, getting kicked out of the house by disgruntled ex-spouses, cancelling people’s stays hours before their reservation, hosts openly using drugs in common spaces, getting kicked out by HOA reps because the host doesn’t have rights to rent, not refunding people who were supposed to stay in Napa Valley during the devastating fires… just to name a few. I don’t care what their policy states, they should operate by what’s right and what’s wrong. This company has no moral compass whatsoever. It sounds like just about anyone can qualify to rent their space through Airbnb and misrepresent it in their ad. I would highly advise against using this service.

I asked for documentation of the ‘personality conflict’. Neither company is properly licensed or authorized to be making these monetary decisions, but they have so far been totally unchecked by the state regulatory authorities. They purport to be a pier-to-pier in order to escape having to be regulated, but the reality is that they are brokering rental transaction. How can the industry be deemed pier-to-pier when the website in the middle of the transaction is acting to strictly regulate and restrict the communications between the provider and consumer? They are collecting security deposits and are making decisions about the claims against the deposits they are collecting. They are engaging in illegal and unlicensed real estate brokerage activities and if not for the various governments wanting to collect the associated tax revenues this would never be tolerated. In short, homeowners and consumers are being tortured and abused all because large companies are chasing returns for their investors and any type of government protection has failed because the governments have become complicit due to the need to expand and protect their tax revenues.

AirBnb: This is MY business! I work HARD at it. I requested to book, including details of our party and requirements and the booking was accepted. I paid £808 in January and have spent the past six months planning and anticipating our trip. A couple of weeks ago I noticed that the property had been unlisted and the host's feedback seemed very strange - there are apparently over 550 reviews but if you look through them carefully there only seem to be around a dozen individual messages which are just duplicated over and over. I drew customer services' attention to this but the guy said that they weren't the same, just similarly complimentary! Anyway, I finally got hold of the host two days before we were due to travel. I had requested details of check-in and parking etc. He replied with the check-in info and property details and an apology because the property had no parking after all! He recommended an NCP which turned out to be 37 minutes walk from the house. I replied that I would never have booked the property if it hadn't advertised a parking space, I explained that our budget had not included the cost of a week's parking and the long walk would be very inconvenient. He offered a contribution towards meter parking on the street but it would still have cost us around £100. Plus, we'd have had to keep topping up - exactly the sort of hassle I'd hoped to avoid by booking a place with a parking space. In the end my family and I decided that we had lost all confidence in the host and the system - imagine if we'd driven for six hours and arrived on the doorstep to find that they wouldn't accept the dog?! The host offered a full refund but unfortunately it couldn't be paid back to my card for 5-15 days which left me no money to pay for an alternative trip - there was nothing remotely suitable left on AirBNB. So we have got a week off work but no holiday to go on. I am utterly disgusted with the entire situation. I was offered a £100 AirBNB voucher as compensation but I strongly doubt this will ever be redeemed. I had pre-booked tickets for London Zoo and exhibitions at the NHM and V&A, I am trying to see if I can get a refund but I don't know how likely that will be. Our much-anticipated holiday has been completely ruined. Thanks very much!

I did not see two older reviews where the guest had listed concerns about the house being cluttered and messy - the host's replies were insulting and nasty. When we arrived, the home was relatively clean and neat. However, the host had not made any accommodations for having us take over his home. (He lives in this home and usually rents out one room) ONE bedroom had empty closet space. ALL of the rest of his closets and dressers were absolutely full of his belongings. All hall, bath. laundry, linen, and utility closets were stuffed full. The host had emptied 1/2 shelf (and pushed things out of the center of another) in the refrigerator, though he had specifically asked and been told that we would be preparing most of our meals at the house. The drawers and shelves were stuffed full. All the kitchen cupboards, including two full wall pantries - were stuffed full. The kitchen counters were covered with appliances and condiments (and there was no place to move them out of the way.) In the host's listing, there was an empty game room - perfect for storing out hiking and golfing gear, and other extra stuff. Unfortunately, that room had become the junk overflow room, and was totally full of excess stuff - including a full sized nude male manikin. We realized we could not stay, and we left the home. Eventually, the host and airbnb agree to return 10 of the 11 days (after literally 10s of hours of communication.) However, Airbnb kept all its fees and auxilary fees. (They also kept almost $700 in housing taxes for nights that had been refunded until I involved the Attorney General's office.) Though their "receipt" shows a total of "0", I actually lost $791 in fees.

I am a host and have mixed feelings about Airbnb. Some of the guests are great but we've had more than our share of bad ones. It seems like people who want to smoke, bring their pets, or fit way too many people in a house use Airbnb. Recently, we had guests use our grill without pulling it away from the side of the house. I guess I should just be grateful our house didn't burn down because Airbnb's million dollar guarantee probably would have covered nothing. **Update 7/12/17**Airbnb's policies do make it difficult to collect for damages caused by guests. AirBnB is okay with no working heat??? We recently stayed in Seattle for two nights at a place where, it turned out, the heat wasn't working. It was a cold Seattle night and we had our 7-year-old daughter with us. We had to spend the whole first night without heat. The next morning, we reached out to the host, asking him to let us know if he could get it fixed -- otherwise we wanted a credit for the second night, We needed to know right away so we could find another place to stay. When he didn't respond quickly, we contacted AirBnB's resolution center. They said they would reach out to the host but were required to give him time to fix the problem. We were concerned that we'd once again end up with no heat and by then, it would be too late to find other lodgings, but it seemed as though we had no choice but to wait so we did. The host then promised to fix the heat but when we got back after sightseeing around 6:30, it still wasn't working. Or at 7:30... 8:30. By this point, it was time for our daughter to go to sleep. Once again, she had to try to sleep while freezing. It was terrible! We reached out to AirBnB and the host again. The host said he would check on it. The heat finally came on at 9:30. It seemed ridiculous to us that we had to spend any time that night or even the night before without heat! The host should have credited us for our visit, but instead, he gave us a partial credit of $78 for the first night. We paid over $460 for both nights. Does that seem fair? Does that mean a hotel can charge over $400 and not provide heat??? In addition to that problem, there were no sheets to put on the air mattress the first night. We had to use a blanket that who knows how many people before us used. The bathroom sink didn't drain -- seriously, the dirty water from us brushing our teeth and washing our hands was still in the sink the next morning! The shower had a window in it with no covering and it faced a courtyard that had windows opposite. In addition, the window had no lock. The lamps and microwave that could be seen in the photos on the listing were there but none were plugged in. Why? Because there were no plugs anywhere near any of them! And there were no extension cords to connect the plugs to either. Maybe worst of all, there were giant metal garbage bins just outside the windows of the place. All night, people were dumping trash into the bins, often big bags or boxes of glass bottles. We know we could hear it all as if it was happening in the room with us! I'm guessing that restaurants use these bins because there was an inordinate amount of trash dumping and glassware. The second morning, the garbage trucks began coming by. It was one after another starting around 4 a.m. You can't imagine how loud it was! Do you think the listing mentioned any of these deficits? Absolutely not. The place was a total dump and we felt like we'd been duped. We had tried to get out of the second night but then got stuck there and were just as miserable as we'd expected. The main things we mentioned to the host at the time were the heat and the sheets. He brought sheets the second day, but we shouldn't have had to ask. After we got home, we saw that we'd been credited the $78. We quickly reached out to AirBnB's resolution center to say that this was not satisfactory. They never called us back for 10 days, despite many calls to them. We then tried reaching out to the host through AirBnB to let him know about all the issues and ask for more money back. We felt like the first night should have been free -- who should have to stay somewhere with no heat? He didn't respond. After 72 hours, we were able to escalate the problem to AirBnB's resolution dept, which promises to help mediate if the host isn't being fair. Three more days went by -- nothing! I called them again and again and finally, one of the floor managers promised to escalate this matter and have someone get back to me within 24 hours. She asked if we had documentation of all the issues -- we did not, other than some texts. We had no idea that we needed to photograph all these issues! She said not to worry, AirBnB has policies in place for first-time users who don't know you need documentation. Okay... The next day, we got an email from AirBnB asking us for documentation. I wrote back explaining that we didn't have it. We had no idea you needed to do that. In addition, what would pictures show? Could you see the heat not working in a photo? Or the sink not draining? You might see water in a sink but wouldn't know that there was a problem. Even if we took pictures of the lamp, how would we really show the plugs are not plugged in and there are no outlets nearby all in one shot? I said I had texts between us and the host and would be happy to share them. I included my phone number yet again, imploring the person to respond. She finally called, but only to say that AirBnB couldn't do anything without documentation. They couldn't consider the texts because they were not done through the AirBnB platform. We did have some through the platform, the last one around 4:30 on the second day. I pointed out that even if she didn't believe that the heat wasn't fixed till 9:30 that night, it still wasn't fixed by 4:30. Isn't that unacceptable? No guest should have to spend a night in a place where the heat is not working! She said they had already contacted the host and he feels the amount is fair, so end of story. While I was still trying to question her about it, the connection was lost. Did she hang up? Who knows, but she didn't call back and I had no way of reaching the same person. This whole experience was maddening! AirBnB's position is that they're just the middleman so they can't be responsible for what a place is like unless we send photos. But they are advertising a place and profiting from the daily rental of it, so doesn't that put some of the onus on them? And it seems as if they didn't mediate at all on -- they simply accepted the host's opinion and that's it. How does that protect guests at all? When we talked to the resolution center while still on our trip, we mentioned some of the other issues to them -- why didn't they tell us at the time that we should document these things so we could show them? We had no idea. And why, really, can't they accept texts between us and the host if they were on our phones? The texts clearly show that we are talking to the owner, and they clearly spell out that the heat wasn't fixed until 9:30. I'm guessing a court would say it's reasonable to consider those valid. But who has the money to spend on a lawyer? It's just terrible customer service, and terrible that they would be okay with any guest having to stay the night without heat. I understand that they need to allow the host time to fix a problem, but overnight? Ridiculous, and unfair.

I failed to inform the host about it, but I did not deny the fact that I was the one that broke the rail and owns my action. Little did I know, the host extorts me by demanding to pay $2100.00 to replace the whole bed instead of compensating for the single piece of the bed. She then files a claim with Airbnb Resolution Center to sort this problem, and she had won the case without further investigation and have simply relied on the pictures provided by the host and a new price review base on the price of a new bed that she would purchase in order to replace the current one. Do note that 1 piece of the bed broke and it is fully functional as a bed and it does not cause the visitors to have any safety issues. I simply received a letter from the resolution team that this matter is no longer debatable and that they have made a conclusion that the bed must be replaced for $1759 CAD. Guest Side: Never book an Airbnb listing if it does not have 5 stars (Superhost) and more than 20 reviews. Read all reviews and ratings for each section. It's the only way you can not fool yourself: Airbnb makes no checks on apartments and / or owners before posting a listing. Assistance in case of problems will not do anything. Airbnb service is also bad as owner's point of view. Being Host for more than 5 years with 4 apartments, Superhost in all, I can only be ashamed of the bad service received despite paying thousands of euros each year for Airbnb commissions. The service in recent years has further deteriorated. Be aware, know by heart Airbnb's terms and protect yourself with strict rules, so you are able to respond to the assistance. As they understand you are a newcomer the fool you. Italian Support is available only daytime dabasis. At night you end up at foreign assistance of no help. They try to push you to accept to repay the traveler for anything. Even against their own terms. They insist because the owner remains waiting for travelers far beyond the check-in time, threatening to withhold payments to help the guest find another accommodation. Yesterday I was awake at 2am when my check-in time was by 22pm and the guest had to arrive at 7pm (meeting time at the apartment). The guest was insistent and wanted at all costs getting in at night. He refused to take a taxi as I suggested to get there before. I asked for help for the assistance that, apart from the phrases of circumstance, did nothing. In fact they made me realize that if I was not flexible I would have to bear the cost of another accommodation for the guest or lose the reservation money. To which I have made mention that there are rules on check-in times and it was not my fault if the guest is late (I repeat: 2 at night !!). They tried to call the guest but they said they did not respond and so they could not do anything. Too bad that I got caught calls and messages until 2 o'clock by night by this unbalanced. By now, Airbnb is the platform of people who do not have the money and demands services from 5 star hotels as well as abusing everything in the apartment and the owners' availability without the slightest respect. With Airbnb that encourages these abuses without laying down rules or clear limits to protecting the hosts. As owners you are constantly under blackmail and driven to be servile and accept everything, every absurd request by guests, otherwise you get a bad review from guests (and on airbnb given the competition, you will only work if you have great reviews) and no: Airbnb refuses To eliminate unfair reviews even though they are clearly retaliating guests who do not accept rules. Or they claim free services or things that by announcement are unavailable (early check-ins, delays, lingerie change which in Italy is also forbidden in tourist rentals, the most absurd appliances that the paying host hostel price pretends, luggage storage and porterage ...). And beware. Airbnb does not collect any deposits that you own (as well as forbid you to demand damage deposit to the guest) and also does not block the money in the guest credit card (which could make you a deterrent for damages). In fact I hope you do not have any damage or the house left blank because the extra cleaning is never paid (even if you send photos) and for damages they try not to repay anything contrary to what they claim with the "host guarantee". Assistance uses only sentences of rite and it is impossible to have clear answers on any problem. Indeed, on the guide on their site and in their Terms, unfortunately frequent cases are not unclear: No one in Airbnb will tell you in detail what really happens when you get damages and how much you reimburse you are entitled in what cases. No one tells you what protection you have in case the guest is harassing. Or if the guest is late behind any decency. The absurd thing is that you are obliged to host him anyway if you do not want to lose the gain. The new cancellation policy in Italy allows the guest to cancel until the last minute, creating an economic damage to the owner (loss of earnings = loss at your own expense). To not menition the "extenuating circumstances" that will make you loose the money anyway. Their "smart prices" suggest you to rent at hostel prices to feed this downplay game and war between the poors. In fact, abusives who can offer more competitive pricing (they do not pay taxes !!) are incentivated because Airbnb does not verify the legitimacy of the ads: anyone who operates in a completely abusive way can place an ad on Airbnb since no information is required before to post the ad. Be careful not to squeeze it out of Airbnb and not be tempted by their rhetoric ... the first time you get a problem you'll make it with...

Double checked our dates were available and booked. First thing happened was our credit card was debited and we got a message saying we were on our way to the holiday. Then 20 minutes later we got a message from the hosts CITY LETS saying the property was unavailable, but they offered a more expensive, less suitable property. I declined and tried to message the host...they failed to respond. I then tried to contact Airbnb directly but couldn't find a way to do it other than a FAQ route. I eventually found the refund our money bit, this involved contacting CITY LETS for them to refund our money. After having to wait 24 hours for them to respond, we got an automated message saying our money would be refunded but we may had to wait up to 5 days. This meant we had to wait even longer to get our money back to book another holiday...obviously not through Airbnb. Having thought back, we thought the original property seemed cheap compared with others offered in the area and we had wondered why it was still available, but it was perfect so we booked. I have been using Airbnb as a host for five years and I am in general very happy doing business with them and never had any big problems, I hosted hundreds of guests and only a small handful were troublesome but this can happen anywhere. I am surprised that the great majority of reviewers on Trust Pilot give it one star. Airbnb do make mistakes and there are no doubt rogue hosts and guests (checking reviews on Airbnb helps to identify them) but most are decent, well behaved people so where are all the higher markings? I suspect this skewed marking is done by the enemies of Airbnb who write bad reviews one after the other to give the impression that there is nothing positive about it. If Airbnb was as bad as made out here it would have collapsed long ago.

My friend and I used airbnb for a week as we travelled the East Coast (6 places total) and we will never use them again. We were surprised by how some of the places we stayed at had such good reviews, which we thought were highly inaccurate when we got to the places. The breaking point was when we arrived at a home and the windows (easily accessible) had busted locks that didn't work. The neighborhood looked rough, so we looked up crime statistics; we were staying in a town with a crime rate 120% above the national rate, and the area we were staying in was the most dangerous of the town. I tried to resolve with the host and then called Airbnb as their refund policy states that if an Airbnb is "unsafe", you get a refund. Airbnb offered me a 50% refund which I told them no. The host even agreed that we should get a full refund (he wasn't aware of the broken windows), but they are dragging their feet. It's been a week and I've had to call twice for updates. Book at your own risk! Also, we're from Chicago, so we have a pretty good idea of what a good vs dangerous area of town looks like. I'm appalled that I'm even having to fight them on this refund. The house is not secured! How could we feel safe sleeping or leaving our belongings there during the day?

I recently visited Boston to assist a friend who was relocating to my home state of North Carolina. My friend lived in the downtown area, several blocks from Fenway Park, so naturally she couldn't find any rooms for under $300 except through Airbnb. (The Red Sox were playing that night, which didn't help.) The room itself was clean and acceptable, and the people I communicated with via text and phone seemed friendly, although we had to play several hours of "phone tag" to finally settle things. When I reached the building where the room was located, and attempted to gain entry via intercom, I was told, by a gentleman who sounded very indignant, that the building was a private condo, and that residents were not allowed to use Airbnb to "sub-let" rooms. I finally got in when a maid or service person took pity on me. Obviously, my hosts were/are playing fast and loose with the house rules. I did not appreciate being put in the position of staying where I was not, by policy, supposed to be. My friend and I made no attempt to get a refund. She booked a bed, I got a bed, so we don't exactly feel cheated. But we do not make a practice of dealing with unscrupulous people. I will not use Airbnb again. In this case, it would have been less hassle to spend the night in the airport lobby.

On April 21 2017, we reserved the master bedroom of Alex's appartment in Hollywood. The listing claimed the following : All amenities included. APARTMENT FEATURES: - you get your own master bedroom with a private bathroom, closet, balcony - Sleeps 3 (third person can choose to sleep on living room couch or airmatress) - FREE WiFi - Central Air Conditioning and Heating - Hardwood Floors (carpeted bedroom/walk in closet) - All brand new furniture and apartment - Dishwasher, Microwave, Full Size Stove - Laundry Facilities inside the unit (modern washer and dryer) - Cleaned by professional maids - Full Kitchen - Extra Comfortable Mattresses, 600 thread count sheets, High Quality Comforter Sets - Chic and modern design - Stainless Steel appliances Before booking, we asked for more pictures, because only one was provided in the listing. A woman claiming to be Alex said that she did not have any at the moment. When we saw the apartment, we understood why she would not provide pictures. We did have our own room with a private bathroom. However: • It was very sparsely furnished -- just a bed and a TV. No bedside table or lamp, no dresser, no chairs, and no sofa, contrary to what was shown in the picture. • We had to ask for the air mattress, which was stored in a pile in the dirty living room. • It smelled like cheap perfume in the room, as if someone wanted to hide a bad smell. • The bath, sink, and mirror were dirty. • The only linens that were provided were 5 face cloths and a hand towel. • The blinds did not work properly, missing many slats • The balcony was cluttered with stuff belonging to other people (and Alex responded that he wasn't responsible for the comings and goings of the people in the apartment!) • The room could only be locked from the inside, so we could not lock it when we wanted to leave. Furthermore, the front door was always unlocked. Alex only gave us the key to the building, not to the apartment, claiming that there was always someone there. Therefore, both the front door and the door to our room were always unlocked, so we could easily have been robbed. When we confronted Alex about these problems, he made up excuses and said he would get the air mattress (which he did) and extra linens (which he didn't). One needs to be very careful when attempting to book any accommodation on offer via Airbnb - They state that after you enter your dates which show the Accommodation of choice to be free to book for your dates, that you can click and Reserve this accommodation - Airbnb clearly state that they do NOT take your funds from your cc or if you are using Paypal, until the Accommodation is confirmed by the Host. This is NOT correct - In this instance it appears that Airbnb take ALL the funds and this is NOT a pre-authorization, as the actual total amount is deducted from either your Paypal account, your cc linked to your Paypal account or directly from your cc account as a straight out authorized transaction before any booking is confirmed. Then, if the Host of the accommodation does not accept the booking, even if their calendar shows availability for those dates and the ability to proceed to booking and then If you have proceeded to booking and paid via Paypal your payment has in fact been processed. If the Host then declines, Airbnb will probably notify Paypal of this cancellation of the booking, however Airbnb do not return the funds they have already received at this stage. Paypal appear to act as an intermediary to draw your funds from your bank account on behalf of Airbnb & then Paypal send these funds directly to Airbnb however the Bank linked to your Paypal account does not release those funds upon Airbnb cancelling this Transaction with Paypal for up to 10 business days because Airbnb have actually TAKEN the funds using Paypal to draw the funds from the potential customer's bank account and Airbnb are still holding them or they still have the potential to draw them from the customer account as there is a hold on those funds by Airbnb. So potentially, you could have a substantial amount of funds held by your bank for up to 10 business days and therefore cannot use these funds to book something else. Airbnb do little to assist you to resolve this situation, accept to insist that this is a Paypal issue if you have paid by Paypal, or if you have paid direct by cc, Airbnb claim it is a Bank issue. It is however actually a Airbnb issue as they are acting unethically by deducting the full amount pre the booking being confirmed by the Host, and on their Airbnb site it clearly states they do not do this. Then Airbnb can hold onto these funds or have the ability to draw these funds from the customer's bank account until the customer's Bank can legally release them back to their customer after 10 business days. I have spoken with my bank at length and they have explained that accommodation places such as Airbnb do this all the time and then the funds are held against the customers account by the bank until the Bank under their policy can release them as unclaimed and/or finalized by Airbnb, or, Airbnb advise the bank that they are releasing the customers funds as the booking is no longer required or other - THIS IS 10 BUSINESS DAYS - the bank have also said that these sorts of Accommodation places seek an authorize payment to be drawn from the customer’s account and this is not a pre-authorization. Accommodation places can send a Fax to the Bank to release the customers funds and apparently this is done quite often according to the Bank who have a special area to deal with this scenario, and that many Accommodation places do sent faxes as normal practice after taking a holding deposit or taking an authorization; However Airbnb WILL NOT do this and have even stated it is not their problem and they have NO facility to sent a Fax nor will they do this, EVER. So in effect, it appears that the customer has to wait until either Airbnb do their banking and reconcile their accounts and realise that they are still holding customers funds on a cancelled booking and then they must release them, or, Airbnb can send a fax to the Bank to release them earlier than the 10 business days that the Bank is legally required to hold them before they then can be released back to the customer. I am not sure how a company like Airbnb can run a business without proper and ethically financial structures in place in Australia, however it seems that they can - Also the fact that Airbnb are quite a big organization only adds to this concern! That their customer service department do not understand how their payment system works and have little knowledge on procedures of dealing with any Bank or Paypal is perhaps indicative of the skill of those running Airbnb. Therefore do not make a booking, send an enquiry always to the host and ask questions and then agree between messages on the possible booking, then ask the host to sent the confirmed booking slip or pre-approval email back to the customer and then and only then, give your cc details when an actual booking has been confirmed by the Host, irrespective of whether their date calendar for the Accommodation of choice shows a vacancy for your dates - Otherwise you will be chasing your money for up to 10 business days because Airbnb will not assist you to get it back. Your Funds could possibly sit in the Airbnb account earning Interest for these 10 business days and if the Bank has not been notified by Airbnb, after 10 business days the Bank can legally release the funds back to their customer. Ring any of the four big banks and confirm this procedure as this is what I did after spending days trying to explain this to Airbnb, who stopped answering any of my messages lodged through their Customer service message service. Also DO NOT cancel your booking if you happen to have made a request for a booking through the request to book link, even if the Host declines, because you could possibly end up with cancellation fees irrespective of whether the Host has declined - this is because the booking has definitely been made by Airbnb as it would appear they take their funds from either your cc or your Paypal account and find some way to show this at the bank end as being an authorized transaction. This issue makes one wonder what would happen if the Host cancels the booking at some stage prior to the customer's arrival and how this is reflected in a refund? Will Airbnb return the payment immediately or will they wait until the 10 business days to return the Customers funds? There is also the question of what would happen if you arrive at your paid accommodation place, to find that this is not what you agreed to purchase or worse still, is not even there! - how would Airbnb handle this, or rather the question may really be - Will Airbnb handle this? After my experience and the customer service I have received, I would have very serious doubts, and also think it possible that Airbnb would do little to assist a customer! It is also extremely difficult to use the Airbnb site if there are any issues, and to actually find any Help link that works as a help link. Airbnb's emphasis is on the Host not the customer in relation to getting in contact with Airbnb - although I am reading that some Hosts are also unfortunately faced with difficulties. The other issue with Airbnb is that it is very difficult to book 6 months ahead in Australia because hosts often do not want to be committed so far ahead, however do not adjust their dates on availability on their Adds for Accommodation and their calender's show free dates however if you happen to make a booking, firstly your funds are deducted and then the Host comes back and declines because its too far ahead - then you have to get your refund back from Airbnb! Hosts should state they are not taking booking for beyond 2017 or the year in question, and Airbnb do not appear to enforce or suggest this, so one can spend hours looking for suitable places, then send an inquiry only to have the majority of Hosts decline if it is more than 6 months away - then one is back to square one. My experience with one booking is now into the third day of searches with many many messages sent and many being declined by hosts for reasons that 2018 is too far away or I have had a number of message inquiries unanswered. Overall my experience with Airbnb has been dreadful, time consuming and a 'bashing one's head against a brick wall' scenario when attempting to deal with Customer service. Good Luck if you happen to go with Airbnb, just remember don't book anything until you get a Pre-approval from a Host and be very careful giving Airbnb your cc or paypal details and lastly 'heaven help you' if you are owed a refund by Airbnb!

AirBnB randomly asks people to upload an unedited copy of their passport, through an organization called Jumio, a for-profit organization. Three problems with this: 1. It's not a hard requirement, until it is. You can randomly get picked to do this (for instance on your 5th booking, which means that on your first 4 it's not an issue). But once you have been picked, the system won't let you off the hook, making any future bookings impossible until you provide them with an unedited copy of your passport 2. In the Netherlands (where I live) it's against the law for any company other than the government, banks or your employer to ask for unedited forms of ID, and to provide this 3. According to Jumio's privacy statements, they can share all your information with anyone they consider a partner or contractor AirBnB has been made aware of this years ago but doesn't seem to give a hoot and happily goes on asking their users to break the law. Shame on you AirBnB. This is not how you treat loyal users.

I have used Air bnb as a host and as a guest and the people and company have always exceeded my expectations. I have met the nicest people. The app has everything you need! Such as: cancelation policies can be flexible, moderate or strict depending on the host's preferences. I am also given many areas to write info about my specific living situation. Read them!
