As a customer of AirBnB I've booked accommodation a couple of times without problems or complaints. Until now though. Because of a new policy of theirs (probably to protect the owners against bad customers), you are required to provide a full copy (including your social security number) of your ID before you can make a booking. This is illegal (at least in the Netherlands)! This information is obviously susceptible to fraud en identity theft can lurk around the corner. The only companies where you are legally obliged to present your full ID is are the ones who are connected to the goverment and banks etc. Not a booking company! They cannot provide the security that is needed to protect my personal information and they have no legal reason whatsoever to knowing my social security number. I'm not going to book with AirBnB, unless they resolve this issue and I'm advising everyone else as well to be cautious when sharing your personal information.

It is only possible to contact the host. The communication is still ongoing - you can request money from the host - but airbnb can only be contacted directly after fu***** 72h !!!!! Airbnb - to me you have shown to be the biggest scam since the invention of penis enlargement pill advertisements. I will never - and I mean never ever - book anything via this uncaring and irresponsible portal again!

Airbnb has not published my review - which in all fairness - was mostly positive. The negatives of my shortened stay were enough to not publish. I just needed a small room. My question to the host about sharing a bathroom with other guests was met with a response of 'perhaps you would be more comfortable in our master bedroom' - which was advertised as a master suite on the host's site. Both of those terms led me to believe that there was a private bathroom in said room. I did not need to be up-sold to then also have a shared bathroom situation. I would have just kept looking to find the right situation for me. Because of my 'misunderstanding' I booked an 8-night stay at a house in Whittier, CA. So, upon arrival, I see that there is no private bath with the 'master bedroom'. Okay - my stay is not that long - the place was clean - I can do this, I tell myself. That night, the hallway outside the room I was in (note: all 4 guest rooms are off this same hallway) absolutely reeked of marijuana smoke. Smoke knows no boundaries and that is what I got to smell all night. I don't personally partake, and don't really care what others do, but this was just too much. I am extremely sensitive and it was several days before I felt okay. I contact my host the next day (note: this is within the stated complaint policy) and explain the situation - asking what my options are. He never responds to me - but, because airbnb can see all of the communication, I now have a 'case manager' responding to me. I have now filed an official complaint. How can I possibly continue to stay there? Well, odors are not a provable complaint, according to the case manager, Janelle. I can't photograph smoke - I could just be complaining because I don't like something. Yet - I am pushed to make a decision to stay or go. I choose to go, despite the 'strict' cancellation policy. The host has decided that there will be no refund for me! So special! I arrange another place to stay - that actually has and enforces their non-smoking policy. Then I go and quickly pack my things and leave the key right where I found it. I let the case manager know I have vacated the property. There is some generic communication from airbnb - you cancelled - do you want a refund? YES! It is all BS. They have denied my refund request. Never heard another word from the host. I don't know which room the smoke was coming from - but I could have gotten high just being in the hallway. It was that bad. Honestly, if it had been a bit earlier in the evening, I would have made other arrangements for that night, too. I have rented whole houses many times on VRBO and HomeAway, all without incident. I am respectful and responsible. This is not the way you treat your guests. So, when you see all of the 5-star reviews (the only ones that seem to get published), consider yourself warned. There could be just as many unpublished 1 or 2 star reviews. Never again!

In disputes they side with hosts to protect their revenue source. We have had mostly good experiences with AirBnB hosts, as opposed to AirBnB itself which we do not trust with a ten foot pole. We had a bad experience in California with a house that was way overpriced for its condition and neighborhood and an uncaring host. The kitchen was devoid of appliances except for a two cup coffee maker in a house that sleeps 8. Cutlery was stuck together in the drawer and the carpets were stained throughout. The bathtub would not drain. There were no hangers in any of the closest. Windows were not locked before we arrived and had we not checked each of about 15 windows we would not have noticed the three that were unlocked. A terrible experience with a rude host. Host actually agreed to pay us back $60 per night for three night stay but reneged and AirBnB did nothing but say they would not hold host responsible. They are just a booking agency and not responsible for the condition of properties. We were told that there was a coffee maker available (true) so we should not complain about its size. What emerges from this experience is succinctly summed up in the letter we received from AirBnB: "I do want to take the time to clarify a bit more about what Airbnb is. We are a payment processing platform that connects hosts and guests together and processes the payment between the two parties. We try to resolve any issues that may arise during the reservation by mediating between both parties and assisting in the rare situations when a problem arises outside of either parties’ control." In other words it is a computer program with a payment mechanism attached to it. The risk is truly all with the customer in this wild west shared economy created by AirBnB -- beware and AirBnB will under no circumstances refund any portion of the booking fee they charge you, even if you have to cancel the reservation and they make another booking fee on the same place at the same time. This practice is disgraceful Best to go into the arrangement with the host with all eyes open. They can cancel on you at any time. AirBnB will not help you and will want to side with the host as the host is more important to their revenue stream. Many times you will have a good experience because you meet a genuine host (95% of hosts are in this category which is what makes AirBnB work) but one bad experience like this will leave such a bad taste that you will never want to trust AirBnB again. I would hope that seeing how much demand there is for AirBnB's service, another more ethical and customer friendly organization would step in and offer better service both to hosts and guests.

I would suggest that you go with Homeaway or Tripping.com rather then airbnb. They don't really care about you as a renter. They protect their hosts and not the guests.

AirBNb seems to be fine from the host point of view - they get paid in advance, no one verifies that their often exaggerated quality of rental property is what it's claimed to be - and hosts are not required to give any refund for dissatisfied clients. The poor tenants/guests have NO rights, NO redress against dishonest hosts, and NO way to even contact AirBNB. There is apparently a hefty insurance for hosts in case their property is damaged, but NO chance for guests to be refunded or moved if property is not as advertised. We are renting a place in Milan for over two months when here for work and it's pretty bad, shabby, dirty, loud, dark and poorly equipped. The landlady tricked us into leaving three days early so she could rent for a conference. Why can't AirBNB be contacted? What are they hiding? Lousiest customer service ever.

I'm sure there is a warning somewhere on the Airbnb website but I don't believe they make this danger clear enough and they certainly washed their hands of it completely when we contacted them. Luckily the bank suspected that there was a problem and did not process the transfer. The second time I made another booking and this time the "verified host" said all the right things like paying through Airbnb etc, however the listing mysteriously disappeared before I have the chance to do so. I contacted Airbnb support who told me as I suspected that this was "100% scam". No doubt the next communication with the host would of been an excuse for the faulty listing and a nefarious link to some other payment method. The point is we hit scams in two out of two attempts. I'm sure the vast majority of listings are fine but surely Airbnb should vet the host listings and take more responsibility for entries they allow on their website! Will not be using ever again.

When my friend and I arrived at the rental cottage, we walked in and about fell over from the smell. It was filthy. The host advertised providing wine and snack foods, so we checked out the kitchen. I don't eat half eaten food, do you? There were open packages of lunch meat and cheese, open packages of dry items in the cupboards. Ugh! We quickly left and called the hostess to let her know we could not stay. She said, sorry, you will be charged for the day our arrived and then I will return 2 days rent. Huh? We had paid for a week, and no refund? Call Airbnb quickly.........we will call you back. This went on for half the day. Can you spell STRESS! After some time, we will refund about half of your fees, but only after much discussion. Bottom line, read the cancellation policy very carefully and be willing to live with it should the rental not be to your liking. Even with extenuating circumstances like a filthy rental, they helped little and that took many hours to resolve. Any monies we saved was quickly lost and monies spent was magnified by twofold. Live and learn.

I have been in the vacation rental business for over 20 years and with Airbnb since 7 years. At the beginning, we were not doing much business with them because of the low standards of their accommodations and they couldn't provide us the renters who had a sufficient budget, as compared to VRBO/HOMEAWAY/TRIPADVISOR. However, after 2013, they considerably improved their website and they came in the leading position. We had a successful and happy 2 years with them, in 2014 and 2015, but things started to deteriorate in 2015 and in 2016 their prices went down again. That's largely due to their pricing policy and to all the sublets, of which the renters really don't care about pricing. Now, recently, in 2017 we faced a total disaster at the price level and at the level of their customer service. We had an issue with a guest who came with a group of 14 to overoccupy one of our properties and the resolution of that issue by their customer services took hours of disconnected calls after 40 to 50 minutes of waiting times. It may take up to 2 hours to reach these guys, depending on the hour and the day, because of the long waits and the disconnexion. As a result, we lost $1,400 entirely because of their poor customer service. At this time, it's simply not worth it to rent with vacation rentals, one will do much better with long term rentals and avoid a lot of trouble.

My experience is same as others, they work for the guest and not the host. We have over 200 listings and on mulitpul iccasions they have cancelled bookings and given guests full refund even if they have stayed and have not reimbursed us for damages and loss of rent payments. Very frustrating! This year we has lost out on around $20k total from Airbnb refusing to pay out money owed to us.

I couldn't be anymore disgusted at Airbnbs response to the damage a guest caused to my apartment and Airbnb refuse to help !! The guest left a trail of red paint throughout the apartment, completely ruining the carpet in the room. I took detailed pictures of the damage submitted them to Airbnb only to get a response from Airbnb they had closed the case because I did not submit any evidence ?? I filled the claim !! Then several phone calls later trying to speak with the case manager Hannah she still refused to speak with me!! Disgusting !! I've been a host for 5 years and trusted Airbnb to support me as a host on their platform!! I am now having to report this to the police as criminal damage and the police so they can take the witness statements from my neighbors who saw the guest dragging this red paint on his suitcase, which Airbnb don't seem interested in at all!! Disgusting

(e.g. lower transaction fees) I have posted tickets on all kinds of subjects with the header *** EMERGENCY **** About five days after I posted the thread, I was contacted by an agent who offered me help to make a new booking for my last remaining 2 days. It was not totally clear if this new booking would be for free or not. I was staying with a friend those last few days. So, all in all, no compensation offered at all. Even when I did get contacted by the service department, they dont care about doing anything to compensate me or fix the situation. Hope next guest doesn’t lose some fingers in the freezing weather.

You can not contact anyone from airbnb if you make an online mistake. Your money is taken, then if you realize there is an error you can not amend it because you can not contact anyone. Companies like booking.con do, and will at least try to resolve the case, and will even contact the provider for you. It feels like an unregulated company that has no responsibility when things go wrong.

City: Rancho Santa Margarita, CA First of all, it is quite apparent that Airbnb does not have as much protection for it's guests compared with it's hosts who are it's source of income! Therefore, it cannot be a fair organization. My host was allowed to cancel my reservation on me after I had spent a lot time and money to select that property back in January. This was a shocking revelation to me that hosts can do such a thing even after payments are taken from my credit card. In my case, it was not even an emergency. It was just that another guest had offered my host a longer reservation (6 months) which conflicted with my booking. The host canceled my booking and took the other guests. Does this seem to be morally acceptable to you? Secondly, Airbnb customer support was not there for 3 days when it was needed most to help me out! The person assigned to my case (Alex G.) was out of the office for 3 days and no one in the office would take care of her cases. Apparently, this is not Airbnb policy to reassign customer cases! While I was looking for another property to switch to, my repeated emails to Alex remained unanswered. When I called customer support line, I was told that I have to wait for Alex to return, and yet they would not tell me when she would come back to the office. How frustrating is that? Thirdly, Airbnb does not really care about customer support. Why, you may ask? Well, here are a couple of good reasons: 1) There is no phone number to be found anywhere in Airbnb web page to contact customer support. I had to find it thru Google! If there is one in Airbnb web site, you have managed to hide it real well! 2) There is no obvious link in Airbnb web page to leave any feedback. I had to ask your customer support to get this hidden link. Don't you want to know what your customers think of your services? Why isn't there a clear feedback link right in your main page for people to provide feedback and rate your customer support? Note: This is not for the property. The feedback is for Airbnb itself. I wonder if this feedback is going to bit bucket or if a real person is going to even read it. I am going to remain optimistic for a couple of days to see if anything results from this feedback. Farid

So basically if I would have booked thinking I'm paying 1318 host would have wanted another grand. Seems shady to me, plus host was kinda rude about it. I am still trying to get back money from December when the unit I rented had roaches, flying insects, filth and doors that did not lock. Host declined my refund but thank God Airbnb did do a partial refund. However, it's been over 40 emails and two months later and I am still trying to get the case fully resolved. My first advice to you is just get a hotel. My second advice to you is if you do go with Airbnb and have a problem, involve your bank or credit card company right away to file a dispute for you. Airbnb may never answer your emails. Phone calls are basically just a waste of time explaining the situation over and over again to a new person every time, and leaving messages for a case manager who never calls you back. I would only recommend Airbnb to people who I don't like.

I hate these so called vacation web sites. When you try to find out information it's like pulling teeth. First they want you to enter your dates that you'll stay. They have pop ups in the middle of what you're looking at that are plain annoying. Who the h*** puts these things together. There's not one good web site for booking a vacation. They all make you want to stay home. I've only found one site that's worth looking at for room rentals and that's BBCanada if you're looking for a bed and breakfast somewhere in Canada. Outside of that I've given up trying to book on them. VBRO, Air B&B, Trip Advisor, they're all the same. There in it to make money for themselves not their clients. I don't know why any of these companies post their rentals on them. C. W. Newsham

Let's say that after my first experience with airbnb, I'm One and Done! I checked into 65 Hendricks Isle # 4 in Ft. Lauderdale, Fl on Feb 4th and had to check out immediately. The place was absolutely disgusting. There were 2 industrial strength blowers going at full speed in the bedroom of the unit. I asked why wasn't told about this situation before i got there, and they said it wasn't an airbnb problem. When we tried to contact airbnb they were nowhere to be found and to this day I don't know where they have offices or a contact number with which you can talk to an employee. The host double booked her place and we were left out in the cold, we had to scurrying to find a hotel room and again airbnb had no support system. I called them for and explanation and was given the run around by one of those contract answering services. I was told that my case would be put on high priority and I would receive a call from a case manager. That never happened. I wish I could do that but I have no idea why they took such action. Customer service is non-existent and they couldn't be more vague or clandestine if they tried. The worst company hands down that I have ever had the displeasure of dealing with. Hopefully they will fade off in the sunset and never be seen from again. Sincerely, David Ventura

After posting the first review I finally obtained a phone number and was able to contact a real person at Air B&B. They processed my request for a full refund with no argument and were very helpful, (also gave me a credit voucher for future use). 1. I wanted to change my date and the trip itinerary did not have my dates as pending, so how can I change if there is nothing pending? No contact number. 4. If I were not desperate for a place I would not use Airbnb. Scott Lobato

Airbnb provides almost ZERO customer support to hosts. I've been renting my house through Airbnb for about three years; all was well for most of this time, but over the past few months, suddenly I am getting TERRIBLE guests. And the support at Airbnb is practically non-existent. First of all, there is no email or messaging system to reach a staff person. You cannot find a phone number on their site, though you can find one by googling, but then they put you on hold for upwards of 20 minutes (I don't know how long, actually; I usually give up after 20 minutes. The other day I called them at three different times of day waiting 20 minutes each time and never got through). The only recourse you have is to go to their resolution center and ask the guest for money. Of course they don't agree to it. Then, if you can figure out how to do it -- quite a challenge -- you can ask to "involve Airbnb." Then you never hear from them. A day or two later they send you a message saying your claim has been closed. No reason, no explanation, no way to contact them. I think you can reply to the message (it doesn't actually say that), but your claim is already closed. I have had three terrible guests in the past few months. One just kept my neighbors up all night with noise. The other two broke things, so I tried to get money back. With one, they broke my stove, pretty obviously by dropping a pot on the open oven door. They claimed it just "popped." This cost me $172, for which Airbnb reimbursed me $72 for the parts but gave me nothing for the labor. (That is their policy, apparently. Did you know that?) The other time, although I submitted multiple photos of damage done -- a huge wine stain on an upholstered chair, one of a pair, which it looked like they either didn't try to clean at all or cleaned it perhaps with WINDEX, anyway they destroyed it -- and four dark wine rings on my marble coffee table (on which I provide piles of coasters). Replacing the chairs, even if I bought used chairs, would cost me around $500+, but Airbnb only holds a $300 security deposit, so I asked for $300. I figured the coffee table was a lost cause but I could put $300 toward the chairs. Airbnb said they wouldn't reimburse me anything without my providing receipts for the replacement furniture. I told them I needed to know how much money I was going to get before I bought replacement furniture. So they closed my case. Did not contact me as I asked and refused to work with me. They did nothing about the fact that the guest, as well as a previous guest (the one who kept my neighbors awake past 1am) then started sending me rude harrassing emails because they were upset about my reviews (no concern for the damage done, of course). I'm actually trying to sell my house now, rather than continue to work with Airbnb. It is that bad. WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE OF ANY COMPANY I DEAL WITH.
Website is awkward and confusing. Verification process excessive. Site would not take credit card, without copy of monthly statement, and getting that downloaded on Air bnb website was impossible.

I recently paid a premium fee to stay at a rundown old nasty apartment in Honolulu. It was expensive and I was unhappy about how much I was paying just stay in such a poorly maintained space. But it was my vacation and it was difficult to talk my husband into spending the money in the first place and so I wasn't about to complain. However when the owner claimed my entire security deposit to fix doors that had not worked the entire time I was there and Airbnb sided with them and gave them that deposit I was and am furious. I will never stay at an Airbnb rental again. They do not care about the customers or consumers.

Waste of weeks trying to get them to recognise my email, new password set with them dozens of times. poor clients no business..poor guests no accommodation, rude conduct. pay for decent service..give airbnb a wide berth,

I have used them on several business trips, and was very lucky with (most) hosts. My theatre company booked an apartment in Edinburgh through airbnb last year and they cancelled last minute! My family stayed at an Airbnb rental that had a KNOWN NATURAL GAS LEAK!! The six of us are fortunate to have survived. AND, Airbnb wouldn't even talk to me about the issue. If anyone asks us, we would highly recommend NOT patronizing this company. Your next of kin may regret your decision if you do. If you use this site with respect for its methods and rules, not much can go wrong. After over a hundred encounters, we have never been ripped off, never missed a payment or a booking. Moreover, I found more new friends there than on FB. At least, through Airbnb, you see people IRL. Of course, some people on the internet just lurk for prey, and they try to abuse just any site that has to do with financial transactions. But wouldn't it be a bit unfair to blame your shop, your bank or a site like Airbnb for that? Phishing is everywhere. Besides one big inconvenient (they are almost impossible to be reached directly - I give them "only" 4 stars), I think they are very safe. Their Superhost program, their rewarding for it and their algorithm to determine wether you're Superhost or not, however, is a big joke. The figures are different on a PC, on an Iphone and in the final evaluation. That is jus lousy IT.

Tried to call, have been on hold for over an hour and then got disconnected. Tried again, and again.....endless hours wasted, no result. Not a pleasure doing business with you. Very unprofessional. Contacted a host through Airbnb site and they turned out to be fake and made us transfer them $700 us to an account in Portugal. When we contacted Airbnb they refused to take responsibility even though we found the listing on their site. They should control the hosts on their site.

I unsubscribed from this company, will never use this service, and will proactively seek to make sure no one I know does so because of it's choice to not support our president. They are disrespectful and un-American. God bless America, and President Trump.

My daughter & I used Airbnb to book lodgings in Budapest & Venice. Both accomodations were clean, bright, roomy & in convenient neighborhoods. In both cases, our host & hostess were gracious & helpful. My daughter has booked through them on at least two other occasions (Paris & Brussels, I think?) and was pleased. We have booked rooms through Airbnb for our trip to Athens this Spring, because we have been happy with our previous bookings. It is like a home away from home!

They do not care about their hosts at all. They do not have a direct email address, you can give them a call, but you need to wait 15 min to talk to someone. No matter how many reviews you give them, they do not respond. They simply don't care.

Like many of the posters below, I am host with a number of listings on Air BNB. A few days ago my account ask hacked (my own stupid fault for not having a virus checker on my smart phone). The hacker was able to change my password, change the email and phone number and list numerous scam adverts! How can that be? We were informed by email that the email address had been changed, but the scammer had access and the time to attempt to scam numerous guests. There is something seriously wrong with their system that can allow that to happen. To rectify the situation them became a nightmare. There is a customer service number, but you can rarely get through. After 2 days the account did get blocked after finally speaking to them, but the promised link to reactivate it was not forthcoming! I tried for days to email all the email address that I had and NEVER got one reply. Eventually we got thought to someone on the phone and did get the right code. Following that, I emailed again several AIR BNB email addresses asking for an explanation and some reassurance about the the future and so after another day has gone by and the fact that they obviously don't care about security I am resorting to this post. I am very concerned about the loss of confidence that the numerous guests who enquired about the scam properties have had no communications from AIR BNB and further more I am very concerned that the site is not secure. We advertise on Holiday Lettings, Trip Advisor, Home and Away and booking.com. There is no way such a serious breach of security could happen with those portals, so AIR BNB need to get their act together. They need a dedicated hotline for reporting fraudulent activity and account mangers to deal with problems, as all the big portals have. I really like AIR BNB as a website and the guests they attract, reviewing guests and hosts is the way forward, but this has rattled me and my staff.

Read the fine print. You get fined a 50% fee if you cancel, but the host gets slapped with a $50 fine for cancelling. We searched for weeks trying to find a place in Scottsdale for this March. We booked it 2 months ago and got a notification today that it's been cancelled. No explanation. So they've had our $1,200 for 2 months and now we're going to probably end up spending double to try to find a place for our stay. Never again!

I am a property owner and got my first Airbnb booking today. I needed to send the guest an attachment with maps and photographs of how to find my property and that of my caretaker. I could find no way of sending such an attachment on the Airbnb web site. I spent an hour this evening listening to their hold music and still did not get through. Does anyone have ant secret numbers or is there no one in the call centre. Les Sherry

As an owner I chose to list with Airbnb and have been so happy with my decision. The customer service crew has always been helpful and courteous to me and all my guests. I then tried to contact Airbnb but the site is certainly not set up to allow feedback or even review My advise, don't use this site. I hope their properties remain empty !!!!

My account was disabled for an unknown reason while I was on vacation in an AirBnB that I booked for two weeks. I made AirBnB aware and customer service told me they were unable to help, that the issue had to be escalated to team that did not have a direct phone line and could only be reached through an email alias. I also made them aware that a guest had booked my own apartment for 28 nights and that I was unable to get in touch with him and that they would have to liaise with him until the issue was resolved. Low and behold, this poor Frenchman shows up expecting to have a place to stay for nearly a month in one of the most expensive cities in the world and I have no idea what to tell him. I spend my day at work repeatedly calling AirBnB to get this sorted out, meanwhile they still have this guy's $2800 and he has nowhere to go. The issue was escalated by at least 4 different customer service reps and still no one reached out. I don't even know where that guy ended up going. Now I'm trying to book a place through AirBnB and call customer service back to see if there's been an update they forgot to share; but there hasn't -,-' The customer service woman I spoke to (her name was Meredith) told me that there is in fact a direct line to the Community Defense team but it's used "only in the event that your host is trying to kill you or something like that." She belittled the entire situation saying that she could warm transfer me over to the Defense team, but that them disabling my account unexpectedly & unjustified, essentially robbing me of the $2800 for the French guy's stay, being unresponsive to my 5 emails and preventing me from creating a new account was not a dire issue. I recently completed a 2 week stay through AirBnb. Overall I think I got good value for my money, and it was a good trip. However, I was very careful about making my choice, and I think you should too. The reason I give them 3 stars are: * The trip was fine and the place I stayed was great. However, as soon as I checked out I got hounded by text messages from the "hostess" why I "didn't leave the place as I found it." Which I didn't understand because I did. After a few rounds back and forth I still didn't know what she expected. I offered to reimburse for a professional cleaning if that's what she wanted, but she didn't take me up on that either. * Airbnb lets the "host" rate the customer as well. This is ridiculous. I had no problem finding a place without any reviews. Why should I? I am putting out the money. I was going to give this place a 5 star review with lots of detail. But in the aftermath I found myself basically being harassed, and with the rating system as a pressure tactic it's just not what I need. I want to remember a good vacation. As a customer I feel that a "good rating" does nothing for me while a "bad rating" would be, well, bad or at least unnecessarily stressful. * I solved this problem very simply which is that I just deleted my Airbnb account. I very rarely take a trip like this and it's just not worth the stress. Maybe it was just this host but I get the sense that it is not, but I think she is in denial. They do not want to see it this way but like it or not these people are now in the hospitality industry. For certain with a much lower expectation of service but still with an expectation to be treated with courtesy and that as a service provider cannot complain to the customer. * So this advice I would give. If you use it once a year fine. I personally would not rent someone's home that they live in. I was looking for someone who has a business income property and that is what I got. I would stick with that. I do not think that people should rent out their own homes to strangers and with that I think Airbnb needs to raise its bar and view itself in the hospitality industry. * I would advise you to take the trip and then immediately delete your profile so you don't have to deal with ridiculous harassment and pressure. * If you plan to use the site on a regular basis, I would advise against that. Stick with Hotwire for those one night or two trips. * So I would use the site again say next year if I take another vacation. I would just sign up again and delete after. I will stick with Hotwire for deals in the meantime because to stay registered leaves you open to harassment by "hosts" (who I consider hospitality suppliers, whether they like to see it that way or not; that is what they are) If you use it carefully and just every now and then it can be worthwhile. Just don't expect to use Airbnb for your regular travel all year round,.

I then texted and got no response. I then called and got through, but was told, quite calmly, that she was in a meeting and would phone back later. No return call. More texts with no reply and then phoned again. Call disconnected and then I couldn't get through. By now it was 5 days before the date we were due to stay. So, I called AirBnB, who said that it was not normal for the address to be incomplete for booked dates that had been paid for. No attempt to cancel the booking by the host, so I had to go back to AirBnB to get them to contact host to verify her cancellation and get a refund. If there was a bereavement that is tragic. However, out of 10 reviews on AirBnB this person had cancelled four other people's bookings (this was not the case when I booked). One was cancelled the day before they were due to arrive. After this cancellation I tried looking around AirBnB for an alternative. I was in a hurry so I snapped up a similar property with parking (there were hardly and, and those that were available were disappearing fast). Booked through my phone, which meant it was harder to check details. Well, this time I messed up. I requested some more details from the host, but they sent back two word answers that didn't make any sense. So, smelling a rat, I went to check the address in google. The area seemed OK, with a mix of shops and residential, so I went up and down the road checking numbers on Google streetview. Outside a gleaming building was a tiny sign with a street number that matched my booking. One problem was that although the building looked like residential, it turned out to be the head office of an engineering company! Another call to AirBnB, who apologised, said that it wasn't a "scam" because the money was with them and could be refunded. No explanation of how a listing could be created using a false address. OK, maybe the host wasn't going to get the money, but had I not checked, I would have been standing in the middle of London with nowhere to stay for the night. Maybe it was someone having a laugh, maybe it was a prospective scammer looking to test AirBnB's payment system, maybe it was a thief? Who knows, but certainly tit was not a real listing and if AirBnB took its operations seriously it should not have appeared on the site. Booking cancelled by AirBnB, host account suspended and listing removed. Good news, except that I am still waiting for a refund via PayPal. I know I will get it, but I am a bit ticked off that my money went to AirBnB in a nanosecond, but I have to wait 48 hours to get it back. In the end I gave up. It just wasn't worth the pain and stress. I didn't want to end up with another cancellation or scam. I did, however, spend ages searching; spent most of my time reporting dodgy looking hosts or listings. What this all tells me is that AirBnB doesn't do enough to check listings or hosts. They take a nice chunk of cash in commission but they don't proactively check their hosts and listings. They make a big thing about "creating a community", but in the end this is just a pile of hippy nonsense. AirBnB is a business that makes a lot of money by acting as a go-between for people who want to book short stays. All we want is reliability; you book, you pay, you arrive, you stay, its nice, you leave. Maybe you go back again in the future. Its a transaction, not a relationship. Because money changes hands, clients commit themselves to travel & hosts let people live in their property this cannot just be just about "trust". Some people are crooks, some are just selfish or inconsiderate. Improving the system would not be that difficult. For a start, emphasising to hosts that this is a business. They make a commitment to provide a place to stay,, and they must take that commitment seriously. If they have a problem, they should have a backup plan to help the client (finding someone else to drop of the keys is not exactly a massive effort). The most basic requirement should be that AirBnB checks every listing to make sure that it is a real residential address. Then, after a booking has been paid for, the full address of the location must be visible to the client. Hosts that cancel bookings, leaving clients without accommodation, should have their accounts confirmed & restricted (stopping them from accepting other bookings until they have given assurances that their remaining existing bookings will be honoured). Repeat offenders should be shut down or legal action taken.

My girlfriend and I have used Airbnb several times and everything has always gone well, until now. We booked a place in Adelaide, South Australia called the "Grange," and when we got there the place was absolutely filthy. The bathroom mirror was covered with stains from soap and/or toothpaste, there were half empty water bottles on a dresser in one bedroom and a dirty towel hanging on the bedroom door, the hand towel in the bathroom appeared to have been used. The kitchen sink and drains had food particles stuck on them and the drain in the laundry room was full of hair. Every piece of furniture and all of the window sills in the place were covered with dust. There were stains on the sofa and love seat, the carpet hadn't been cleaned and, worst of all, there were a bunch of bodily fluid stains on the bedding in the master bedroom (on a memory foam cover). Every single Airbnb place we had stayed in prior to this had been great, so we were shocked to see this level of neglect. I contacted the owner twice but he was unconcerned and insisted that the place was clean. It was late and we had no other place to stay so we actually cleaned the place ourselves - dusted the furniture, vacuumed, washed the bedding, cleaned the bathroom, etc., then stayed the first night there. In the morning I contacted Airbnb via their website to file a complaint. It was awesome. The system asked me to explain the problem and upload photos if I had them (which I had MANY). Once that was completed it said the owner would be contacted and he would have exactly one hour to respond and work it out with me. Well, exactly one hour later I got an automated e-mail from Airbnb asking if I still needed help. I responded "yes," and then was given the option of cancelling with a full refund or continuing to stay there and getting a partial refund (which was just a return of the $30 cleaning fee). Obviously, we chose to cancel and get out. So at least we got one night free for all our trouble and for cleaning the idiot's place for him. Airbnb refunded our full payment and offered an additional $50+ credit toward a different place. We found a much better place within the hour and moved over there. My only complaint is that since the reservation at the Grange was cancelled, there is no ability for me to review it on Airbnb's site. That is just wrong. People need to be warned about this place so they don't end up in the same position we did. Note on filing a complaint at Airbnb - you have 24 hours after arriving at the rental to do it. After that, you have little recourse. We did not know that but just happened to check into it after being there about 18 hours. Phew!!

I am property manager specialized in vacation rentals in Dominican Republic. I am so disappointed by TRIPADVISOR/VRBO/HOMEAWAY GROUP that it's easy to say why you should do your deal with AIRBNB. 1) first an apps which is great for owner and travelers, you can do many things on it without using a laptop or computer. It's really well done. You can modify your adds and stay in contact with your guests everywhere and anytime ! Information provided by Airbnb regarding payments and other things are useful. 2) a transaction safer with the guests, less fraud and thief tentatives on this website because they check for owners the reality/quality of the guests. You can decide by yourself with an option that you want they check the I'd of the guest before instant booking, and also refused badly rated guests automatically. It's really nice. I have experienced these last months many frauds on homeaway websites (they really don't care...) and I am really glad to say that I have much less pb with Airbnb. 3) rating of guests can warn you regarding the experience of previous owners.. very interesting. It's not just stars like homeaway it's also written reviews which is very important to me to avoid bad behavior guests. It's great because bad guests doesn't come back... they are evicted of the Airbnb system and they find refuge on homeaway... among other defraud and thieves. You can also let a hidden feed back to improve experience with others... 3) payment are made regularly and are quick, it's very important to me and owners. 4) they manage the damage deposit, if you are multi property owner or manager you don't have to worry about it. But if you have pb, you have to manage claim with them, this is not a good point for owners as you should not have to justify if you have damages... Overall, a good experience with them, and I advise you to be very selective with your guests and use extensively ratings to avoid bad people. Then you can run your business without too many troubles.

The house that came up had 4 rooms, but we did not realize that because the house it said it sleeps 10! We did an instant book rather a request and everything went through immediately. Today we were looking at the house again and we realized it has 4 bedrooms instead of 5! So, we asked the host if we could cancel and he said no AirBnb cancellation policy is that we lose 50% which would amount to 1800 US dollars for us! Mind you this is the next morning and we are more than two months out of our travel date. So, we thought that would not be a problem. Not only are they allowing management companies to let out properties but they do not support their clients. Terrible company
Would recommend!
It's a great service, but if your plans change due to unforeseen circumstances the cancellation policies are awful.

Airbnb's site is very confusing and because of that I accidentally booked a reservation in the Bronx that had a strict cancellation policy. I only meant to inquire about the booking not book it. I noticed this mistake when I saw a message saying that the host accepted my request. I immediately contacted the host and told him the mistake. The host at first said that he refused to refund because of the penalties he may face for cancelling. Airbnb contacted him and told him that he would not penalized. When I told the host this, he still refused to refund my money and ignored my messages. It took a whole week and a half for case manager to get back to me! And all they said was that the host refused to refund my money and nothing else! The host should not be keeping the money at all especially if I did not stay there and told him that the booking was an error! He even had the nerve to say that he wanted me to pay extra cash in person or else I couldnt stay there! Its very bad that the company lets people get away with stuff like this! Also do not believe Airbnb when they say that they cant do anything about your issues. They can do something! They just do not care about their customers! Be very careful, learn how to book on the site, and make sure that you look at the hosts booking policy! Stay away from any booking with a strict cancellation policy! Better advice would be to not book with this company at all because the problems that can arise is not worth your time or money!

For all of you who are considering traveling and booking place to stay, please read following. I had recently traveled with three friends to Paris, France. First time ever we have booked an apartment through Airbnb. This is our experience and after sending this e-mail to Airbnb, I have yet to receive the response. I do not believe that they screen their landlords properly. In my previous travels I have always used House Trip and was never disappointed with them..... To whom it may concern I was one of the 4 guests registered under I..... P......My name is Sonja Ness and I was not sent an e-mail to submit my review. Never the less I would like to say a few word about Eduardo's Place at 32 Rue Montorgueil, Paris, France, Staying at Eduardo's place was, to say the least, most disappointing experience. Other then location, which was excellent, nothing else was enjoyable. Place was unclean, dirty water in the bucket from floor washing was sitting in the kitchen smelling and attracting mosquitos, dirty windows, film smudged glasses and dishes and linen did not smell like something that has been recently washed. There was no telephone except the one to answer and open door for visitors. TV did not work and neither did coffee maker. The worse part of all of this was that the apartment is flea or bed bug infested. At first we thought we were being bitten by mosquitos, but soon found out the bites were from fleas and more likely bed bugs. I, alone have at least 30 bites on my arms and just as many on my legs. This apartment should not be rented to anyone else until it is fumigated and clean. I feel that I did not get my money worth and if anything should be compensated for being exposed to such terrible conditions. First day that we arrived we have e-mailed some of our complaints to Eduardo, but in six days that we were there, we did not get any reply. The bites are still very visible on my arms and legs and if needed I will be happy to provide you with the photos of them. At present I am trying desperately to make sure I did not bring those insects into my own home. Washing everything and spraying my home is an added agrevation i did not need. I have traveled extensively and have stayed in hotels, private houses and rooms, bed and breakfast places in many different countries and cities and have never encountered conditions like this. I feel that this issue needs to be addressed immediately as to prevent other visitors from same terrible experience. I am so upset with this that i will be posting my experience on social media to worn other travellers. I do hope that you will, as well, address this problem with the owner of above property. Sincerely Sonja Ness

My airbnb is not as described and i wanted to move out. it was advertised as a private room in a 2 bedroom apt, but the hosts rent out both of their bedrooms and they themselves live on the couch. Moreover, the kitchen is an office to them. I called Airbnb, the customer service was so rude to me and insisted that they cannot refund anything.

I booked with airbnb for the first time. I had no problems arranging check in with host who was lovely. I met up with host at accommodation and he was very helpful and showed us everything we needed to know. When I started to clean (which I don't think I should have to do as a guest) I started to notice there was a lot of dog hair even in the fridge and drawers. Also the house had unfinished flooring and everywhere was filthy. I have to give the host respect as she had bought new bedding and tried to tidy the place up as they said they had been sorting the garden out etc, it was also the first time the host had let her property out. I called airbnb as I didn't want to tell the host her house was filthy, I got through after about 20 minutes on hold. I spoke to a customer service assistant who then put me through to a lovely lady called Kristina, this lady literally could not do enough to keep me happy and try to make a positive situation out of a negative. She gave me 2 options: 1 being a full refund; 2 being transfer the cost to another host with 10% extra towards it. I managed to find another host. However I still needed to pay £87 towards the cost as it was more expensive i got back in touch with kristina who refunded me the £87 back. She also said as it was late on the night when I arrived at my first host it would be hard to find a new host so told me to book a hotel and she refunded me the cost of the hotel also. I hope that Kristina gets an appraisal for this as I will definitely come back to airbnb due to 10/10 customer service. However when I arrived at my second host he was not there so I made another call to airbnb and they managed to get in contact with the host who explained he got the dates wrong and he was there within half an hour. The hosts are lovely people but the standards are not very high at all for the accommodation.

I got to the place and it was dirty, moldy, and just terrible. I was not able to take picture at the time and they are siding with owner and not even allow me to leave a comment where owner is took my money and refused to refund my money back. My first time and my last time. Shame on your Airbnb.

The host canceled on me for 24hrs prior to arriving to Vegas for a conference, the conference also happened to be on a weekend of 2 major music events in Vegas. Now I am a little type A so I booked on Airbnb about 3 months in advance and got a great room that had about 60 positive reviews and maybe two negative ones over a long period. So 24 hrs before arrival my host cancels. You first get an email from host, saying that you have been canceled, then you get an email from airbnb, which says they are sorry and want to help you find a replacement and they offer full refund or 10% additional credit toward new room on airbnb with the help of their concierge service. Now I had a nice suite to myself for this week that I was gonna be in Vegas and when I booked there were lots of options in my price range, but 24 hrs ahead of time, there was nothing in my price range even with 10% credit (80$ in this case). So I emailed this to airbnb, and didn't get an immediate response, but it was also overnight on a Thursday, so wasn't expecting, the next morning, I had a few hrs before I had to go and booked at the Palms Place (coincidentially the same place where I had booked before through airbnb), but on my own, not through airbnb, it was more expensive, and I wrote a followup email back to airbnb, that booking through them 24hrs before an event was not possible on a busy weekend in Vegas. Ultimately, they encouraged me to send them a copy of the final receipt, and they paid the difference. I would have accepted a credit, but they paid the difference between the original booking and the new booking. So that said, I am angry with the original host, but thankful airbnb had my back. So I give the host a 0 stars, and airbnb 5 in this case.

You seriously would have to try to be this bad at handling customer issues. I purchased some gift cards worth over $1000 and uploaded them to my account. I made a reservation, which on the day of - Airbnb cancels it! I call and I am told I have to email and wait for a response. No one ever responded. I finally open a BBB report. Airbnb finally contacts me over a week later (my money in limbo the whole time) and apologizes and gives me $100 coupon in compensation as well as re-enable my account. Two weeks later they disable my account again for no reason. I have been trying to get an answer ever since and its a month later. Seriously... the worst. I loved the site, traveled to several countries using them, that was up until I experienced their complete lack of care for their customers.

I booked an AirBnB for a recent business trip to Dublin. As a woman travelling alone I prefer to rent whole apartments, and searched accordingly. A 'boutique Georgian studio' came up and I booked it. To my surprise it turned out to be a bedroom + ensuite in a house where the owner both lives, and offer multiple rooms for let - all of which are accessed from the same shared hallway. This was not what I was expecting. I was concerned about the security of the arrangements, and as the room was freezing cold (despite leaving heating on for an hour) I decided to cut my losses and head to a hotel. What happened next was interesting. I suspect I am not the first person to be disappointed by the room as the owner had the leaving conversation and follow up down pat. No apology, no offer to help..just 100% a** covering and BS hairsplitting excuses about the 'technicality' that allows her to use the word 'studio' and tag it as 'whole apartment'. Outcome - I got 50% of my money back in exchange for a cancellation which meant that I could not leave a negative review. Cancelling AirBnB on the day is not easy - especially when you are jet lagged and frantically trying to find a last minute hotel. You're on your own basically. While this whole experience was inconvenient, it took place in the middle of the day, and I'm in the fortunate position of being able to absorb the cost of the 'cancellation fee' and last minute hotel costs. Not everyone has that financial safety net, in fact many people use AirBnB because it is cheaper than a hotel. By allowing hosts like this to continue to advertise rooms in a shared house as separate apartments on a dubious 'technicality' AirBnB is putting traveller safety at risk. Any host who has multiple guests leave on the day of arrival is doing something very wrong, regardless of whether they fulfill AirBnB site criteria or not. I'd also like to see AirBnB collecting information about why travellers cancel on the day post check in, and following it up with hosts.

We love our stay at John & Kara's Historic Pioneer Rock Cottage in Mendon, Utah. (Mendon Rock Cottage). We stayed an additional 8 days!!! Excellent host!!! The views were breathtaking!!! our cottage was immaculate!! We will return! Airing excellent company!

I boiler about 7 trips in total with AirBnB and until the last one all were fine. However, when I had a problem with the host during the last trip, the service received from AirBnB was appalling. They were completely dissinterrsted and only replied with a very generic quotation of their terms, without even taking into account what my complaint was about. I had complained about a relatively minor incident, where the host was unfair in her review so AirBnB's dissinterrst did not affect me much. But if this is representative of their general attitude towards traveller problems things could be a lot worse if a more serious issue arises. I will avoid airBnB in future as this experience left me without any confidence that there is any sort of assurance or customer service should there be problems on a trip.

I feel like they were hoping I wouldn't notice and that they never had any intention of communicating with me regarding this. The fact that the transaction was completely missing from my transaction record is incredibly disturbing!
Horrible service provider to use - never again. Do yourself a favour and book accommodation using anything but airbnb.

My boyfriend and I used Airbnb for Johnny's place in San Deigo, Ca. The place was not like the listing seemed. We contacted Airbnb and they only gave us $140 (one night refund). We still had to pay $400 for a crappy place that we left at 1:30 in the morning on the first night we got there! Lost money, lost sleep, lost time. No real refund. We will never use or recommend Airbnb ever again. It's not fair we lose so much of our hard earned money over this (we are in college and barely could afford our vacation let alone paying for a place we didn't even stay in on top of a nice hotel). Stick to the chain hotels because at least their concerned enough about their customers to right any wrongs that happen, and give refunds where they are due. Don't use this app unless you have no care for your own protection. I want to make sure I also leave the complaints we had with the place we stayed, as we can't even leave a review for the host we had when all this happened. This is the message we sent the host: "You have two complaints about street noise in your reviews, (Phil and Andy). We had to hear the noise as it was well over 80f last night, and your fan barely functioned. We knew about the lack of AC, but the fan was completely useless, even at it's highest level it was still extremely under powered. While I realize you cannot control the weather, we expected that the fan would at least be somewhat useful. As for the spider, I am not sure what to say. At roughly 10pm Ashley closed the window (as we would rather be hot and uncomfortable then have to deal with the cars outside) and laid back down. At this point she felt something crawling on her, picked it up, and threw it on the floor. I turned on the light and found a large brown/black spider (looked like a wolf spider) on the floor. I killed it and flushed it, but have a bite on my arm now. Would be glad to provide pictures. There was sand all over the bathroom floor and the shower. Ashley wouldn't take a shower unless it was clean so she cleaned it with Lysol and water. Involving the sprinklers - We came back from some families house at 9pm. We stepped out of the car and got completely soaked. We should not be deterred to come back to the place at 9pm. This also left water spots on our car (would be glad to provide pictures) and soaked my shoes / pants. Involving your neighbors(?) [the people directly above us] around 12 there was really loud squeaking of a bed from above us. While we could deal with this and understood it happens, not a minute later we heard some really loud moaning that lasted roughly 10 minutes. This made both Ashley and I really uncomfortable, and was the final straw to us leaving. The bed was extremely squeaky and firm as well. The unsolvable heat from a useless fan + being bit by spiders + sand all over the floor + getting soaked by sprinklers and water-spots on our car + people having loud sex upstairs + a terrible bed completely ruined our first time experience with airbnb. We left at 1 am as there was absolutely no chance of us being able to sleep there. We did not do a thorough investigation of the apartment as soon as we got there. Either way it would have resulted in the same conclusion - us leaving. For what we got we would have had a much better experience at something even as cheap as motel 6 for much less money. While I do not mean to come off as rude - this was an extremely frustrating experience. Especially as we do not have much money (In college) and had to find another hotel room at 1 am in the morning." Our host then replied tough luck. Never again.

I have been using airbnb for many years. I never had any problems since I read every single review. That has helped me a lot. This time, I traveled to Istanbul, Turkey. The apartment was just terrible, I could not understand how every single review was so great. I stayed at the apartment for 5 minutes and immediately left for a hotel. I don't know what proof they are asking for, more than my word, the word of a client that has traveled around the globe with great experiences. Airbnb wrote an email saying that exceptionally, they would refund just one night, almost as if they were saving my life. I honestly am very frustrated, humiliated, and angry at airbnb. They have 0 customer service, very tough to get in touch with. I will never use airbnb again, no way they are getting my business.

I strongly recommend that you avoid using AirBNB. Here is my experience. o About a month prior to my visit, I booked a stay in a foreign city through Air BNB. o 5 days prior to the stay, the booking is cancelled by the host. o Day 5-3: 2 days are spent trying to book a new property. Effort results in mysterious emails, direct from host, requesting that we wire transfer funds to an account in the Ukraine. We determine this is fraud. o Day 3: I post a question through their “help” section of the Air BNB website alerting them that I think one of their hosts is actively using their site to commit wire fraud, and I am advised to post a review on the hosts’ website. o Day 3-2: attempt to book another location, but host rejects in order to accept a different booking request. o Day 2-1: limit my search to bookings that are instant. This greatly reduces options, and requires some inconvenient compromise, but I request a booking and it is quickly accepted. I am asked to go through a “verification process” which includes a lot of personal questions, and it is my understanding all is well and accepted. o Day 0 – notified that our booking is cancelled due to “We’ve discovered that the payment method used for reservation XXXX isn’t valid.” I check with my credit card and there are no issues, so I have no idea what this means or why I am now without a place stay. Search on other websites indicates that AirBNB has had to implement some stringent credit card verification, due to high rates of complaints about credit card fraud. Guessing my booking was caught up in this? I have sent several emails asking what happened, and have yet to receive a reply. o Day 0 – try to login to AirBNB help center to see if any other support is available, and find out my account was disabled. I requested that the account be enabled, and I have never received a response. So, I am left stranded the day I arrive in a city in a foreign country by Air BNB with no access to account support, no place to stay and no answers to questions. Question: I have great credit and my credit card was checked and was clear. This was my first booking with Air BNB. I am completely stumped as to why my account was closed. Was my account inactivated because I complained about fraud? My biggest concern: Air BNB, to the best of my knowledge, has never investigated or made any effort to remove the fraudulent host that requested a wire transfer of funds, since the only follow up I received from them was a suggestion that I post comments on the host site. I find this very concerning since the host is clearly perpetuating fraud through their site. Since my account was inactivated, I cannot post a negative review.

I have used Airbnb for about 5 to 6 times from Australia, Malaysia to Hongkong. Reading alot of lousy review from here make me laugh. First, cancel policy is set by the owner. And it is stated clearly in the page wether they have strict cancel policy anot. I believe some hotels have this policy too. Lousy experience or lousy stay?. Do you read reviews on the apartment or host before deciding where to stay? There are alot of good host and apartment out there. You need to do research before even making a booking. Factors to consider, location, cleanness, host. Credit card fraud? Obviously your credit card details have been stolen. It may due to spyware in your computers or public wifi. Just happen your credit card details are being used to purchase in Airbnb. My bet is that the hacker is a host in Airbnb and use it to get your money. Call the bank immediately and change a card! Airbnb is good on cost saving and experience living like the locals. But having that said, research is needed to have a good experience. Unlink hotels you could just stay in "branded" hotel where not much things could go wrong, of course you pay a premium.

Fraud company.... I booked with them after getting host approval and paid to Airbnb. I paid to them 30 july.2016 and Airbnb cancel my booking after 2 months. Now no one is ready to speak. They don't have India contact number. I called them on US number and waste my ₹1100 more but no resolution.

This is a review for the service I've had at Airbnb - not of a place i've rented through Airbnb. I phoned them - note - you are unlikely to find an email address for the site as a whole - there is a phone number on their website - I rang them and got through pretty much straight away. I was requesting a refund under special circumstances. I explained my reason and was told a specialist team would be in contact. I received a a follow up email that day and and then a further email which was sympathetic and asked for some documentation (which I expected). I booked an Airbnb accommodation for Munich, Germany which will be my last Airbnb reservation. I normally do not write bad critiques or any at all but this one had me fuming. I thought listing my beach house on Airbnb sounded like a great idea. There is NO HELP available for you as a HOST. My first experience with Airbnb was recently August 27 2016. We were moving from Honolulu to Albany, NY. After 20 hrs of being in airports we arrived at the B&B at 8 pm on a small unlit back street. The house was totally dark with no one to greet us even though we paid in full on July 30th by credit card. (This host was rated highly with 5 stars.) At first we thought it's a scam. Then my husband struggled with his pen light and we used my cell phone to call the B&B host. He didn't answer. I managed to access my email where I read a last minute email posted by the host giving us a code to get in back door. After we got inside he soon called my cell and threatened us. He said we had to change our reservation to a more expensive room or he'd throw us out. So we agreed. The next day I noticed the tv ain't working. I called him. He didn't answer. At about 3 pm another guest arrived, letting herself in the back door, claiming she had paid for the entire house. She was angry at us. She called the host but he did not answer. At that time I had complained by cell phone again to him that the tv was not working nor was the Internet. He said he would have his property manager come by and fix it. No one came. I called him and said no one came. He said I was a liar and someone had already come to fix it. I said I was there all day and nobody came. He called me a liar. He said he had surveillance videos in every room of the house and he was watching me all day. He bragged about freely watching me. We moved out of the B&B that day, the 29th. I made a complaint against Airbnb on the Better Business Bureau website. I wrote a letter to the CEO of Airbnb including a copy of the Attorney General complaint. Now I am now taking the B&B owner to court to get our money returned. I took photos of everything in the house, by the way, before we left. I photographed the surveillance equipment too. Airbnb was provided with a lot of documentation including photos and cell phone records and still no assistance from them. I am taking copies of all my records to court with me. This has cost us $1,280.00 but it's but more than the money. I have spent many hours, at least 40 hours filling out reports and organizing documents, to file complaints. I am still gathering cell phone records to show the judge on my day in court. Nightmare!

She also told us where everything was and was happy for us to use her stuff to cook with etc and even left is towels. From speaking to the host and also evidenced by what was in the apartment it was clear this was her usual home and she was staying with friends/family whilst we were staying in her home. Second, more recent experience was in June this year, at the Apartment Marina Novalja. Again for a girls holiday, host had several apartments and lived in a larger apartment/house on the same site. There was a pool etc, towels provided and he even stocked a fridge around the pool both alcoholic and none alcoholic drinks. Again met us on arrival which was very late in the evening and showed us everything we would need to know and also outlined a few rules. Perhaps ever so slightly more stict than your normal holiday apartments, but this is understandable as it forms part of his permanent home and he looks after all the additional apartments involved between him and his wife. Both great experiences, clean, good value and welcoming places to stay. So far my experience has been very good and I would certainly recommend.

She is "not prepared to explain or argue with you about this". The booking is changed and she has no obligation to do more. What transpired is that she was (sub) letting an apartment illegally in a building and that the owner/building management had blocked her access. She had been doing it successfully for some time and had good reviews but now was caught out and barred. Obviously the assurance she had given Airbnb was falsified. When I raised this with Airbnb they said "we have hundreds of thousands of hosts. We can't verify all their claims". Airbnb cancelled the booking and helped us find another that we had to accept with just 4 hours notice. It is a long bus ride out of town and is on a very busy highway. Our holiday is completely ruined. What is my complaint? Airbnb say Nicole told them she had a last minute hiccup and they accepted her excuse completely They agreed it was unacceptable but they had absolutely no plan to do anything other than help me find alternative accomodation: she was a successful host (aka she made big $ for Airbnb). I was told this really did not happen often and I was unlucky. I was told 4 times that Airbnb took great care to look after their customers and that my experience was unusual. The bottom line is that Airbnb will keep Nicole/Ashleigh. She is a valuable source of income to them. They understand what has happened looks dodgy but if she tells them she is OK to offer an apartment then they will take her word for it. Airbnb's model is set up to facilitate scamming and they know that and believe that they can "manage" victims when they emerge. It's a buyer beware portal. So BEWARE. Post script. Airbnb sent us a charge for cancelling the first booking!

It was a dark and stormy night at the end of August. I checked my bank account, and having just been paid I didn't feel the need to cover my eyes like I usually would. How wrong I was - £800 down on frivolous weekend getaways with AirBnB. I was 99% this was not me nor my drunk counterpart, and henceforth my tale begins. I spoke to Paypal, who had actually already flagged the transactions as suspicious, but these were the only suspicious charges on my account... why would a criminal only need a weekend getaway? Why not clear my account? Why not treat themselves to a nice trip to the zoo while they were there? And so the mystery deepened. I spoke to my bank, who told me the same. They cancelled refunded me and cancelled my card "just in case" but told me to take up the initial breach of my confidence with AirBnB as that is where the mystery began. Down the rabbithole I fell... I phoned AirBnB, who told me they'd email me. I gave them the information they required to "look into it further". And look they did, but in the wrong place. Repeatedly and relentlessly, and infuriatingly. I lost track of the amount of times my account manager, Elizabeth the Inept, told me that they couldn't find these transactions and to take it up with my bank and Paypal. "But Elizabeth," I cried, "I have. I've been refunded. All I want to know is why and how my details have been mishandled and my confidence breached!" "An apology for the hassle caused also wouldn't go amiss," I added. But Elizabeth did not care. Elizabeth stopped replying. I assume she was off wondering around with her head in the clouds, possibly booting a puppy or two on the way. So I took to twitter, who said they'd fix it. My hopes were raised again. Perhaps finally, I thought, the mystery can be solved and this tale will have a happy ending. But Elizabeth struck again. We can't find these transactions she told me. Maybe take it up with your bank she, unhelpfully, suggested. And the final blow, "we consider this case closed and will disengage from further discussion." Do you remember at the end of Sopranos when the screen just goes black and you're left to decide whether Tony is alive or dead except it doesn't really matter because nobody will ever know? Well, I am sad to say the ending to this story is much the same, if not more traumatic. I have tried to tweet again, and email again, but nothing. Just a never ending Sopranos finale. An endless void of AirBnBs lack of f**ks to give. The moral of this sad story is a simple one, and much better said in the infamous words of Dr Seuss: "You have brains in your head, you have feet in your shoes, you can steer yourself any direction you choose." Which is to say, if you're thinking of booking with AirBnB - don't.

I do not see why once an investigation is opened, a review can still be left reflecting that. The only reason is simple, they do not want hosts (or guests) to open investigations because it causes them more trouble. They want you to accept your losses as your own and not start an investigation. "Be a good little customer, and there's no bad reviews and no trouble". It is that simple. They deterr you from support and their guarantee as much as they can. I have now done so, and received negative reviews as a result. This is a direct result of their support team's advice, and they do not consider it an issue that this is easily possible for reviews to be left in the wake of open investigations that they have told me to open. The review does not directly state the entire issue, but does most certainly make reference to it. As Airbnb policy states a review is disallowed when there is "Content that refers to an Airbnb investigation". It most definitely does refer to it. It is not hidden. And it is through their support that this has occured. Contact with AirBnB has been meaningless at best. They will not honor their guarantee, they will not honor their own policies when their policies support you, but they will take 20% of the total booking income, and do their best to make it look like they don't. I think they need to seriously rethink their policies and staff training.

Generally speaking, Airbnb is a great service...when things go to plan. When they don't and you are forced to interact with Airbnb customer service, they are truly terrible. I've never experienced a customer service interaction like Airbnb's. Long story short: I booked a place that listed "moderate" as the cancellation policy. I've never booked long-term before, but I booked the room for close to two months. I didn't realize that if you book for over 28 days, Airbnb automatically applies a long-term cancellation policy regardless of the host's stated policy on the listing. However, this information is not openly provided, and I only found this out after I had booked the place on my billing receipt. I sought to address this issue with the host the same day I booked the room (a month before my rent was to start) and he himself did not know about this automated policy and insisted that no such policy existed. Once he realized that it did, and that he stood to make over $800 for less than a day of lost potential guest bookings, he essentially stonewalled me and shut down all communication. Given this, I tried to enlist Airbnb's customer service to provide advice and assistance. The first-point of contact was extremely nice, but had absolutely no power over or knowledge on what could be done. Airbnb essentially insulate themselves such that the customer can never speak to anyone who holds any real power. Eventually I managed to strike up an email exchange with a Trip Agent. I was repeatedly sent badly worded stock messages essentially outlining that Airbnb had no culpability etc etc. Their main point was that the customer enters into an agreement with the host, and they must honor the terms of the agreement set by the host. However, they eventually (I think somewhat accidentally) admitted/conceded that I was in fact subject to Airbnb's terms and conditions (automated long-term cancellation policy), not the host's. Eventually, after many unanswered emails and after I submitted a refund request, Airbnb arranged for the host to refund $134. After informing me about this refund, and stating they would credit it to a visa ending in the wrong numbers (I'm still yet to hear from them as to whether they've changed this to the right credit card), the Trip Agent stated, "Please note that i have also made this my final decision and we will disengage from further discussion on this topic" followed by a BS stock response about valuing customers etc. Just like that...the discussion is closed down. They have yet to answer any of the multiple points and questions I raised in the email exchanges (I really mean that they answered none of them). Not least, I've asked 3 separate times for a contact person or department to issue a formal complaint against Airbnb. Ultimately, I've lost over $600 because of misinformation. Airbnb have essentially created a situation in which a host has made $500 for less than a day of lost business and over a month notice to find a replacement guest. But more than the money, I've been shocked by Airbnb's approach to customer service. I know I'm a tiny part of their massive business, but they made me feel incredibly disempowered and exceptionally dissatisfied with their service. Perhaps I won't get much sympathy from people, but I feel like I've been extorted, and Airbnb have not just sat idly by and done nothing, but have actually participated in this extortion.
