Sofa beds are not suitable for my 75-year-old parents since they have some health problems. Accordingly, I cancelled the reservation right away. ( I received the confirmation email at 9:52 pm and the cancellation email at 10:28 pm). I got the refund of 2 euros. I thought that something was mistaken, but still after 5 working days, I got nothing but 2 euros of refund. Now Airbnb says that they cannot give us the refund no matter what as the long stay policy is applied, which means they will take the whole first month payment. I would have understood if I had cancelled 3~4 days before the actual check-in. Airbnb says that long stay policy is to protect hosts in case guests cancel their stay with such a short notice. However, in my case, the check-in is not until the end of November and the reservation (and the cancellation) was made in July. That means, the host has enough time to take other guests until then. (Actually, he said his house was reserved right away I cancelled, so I cannot reverse the cancellation.) Then, who protects guests in this case? Not only did Airbnb refuse to give us the money back, but the staff working in Airbnb office threatened my husband that they will take the whole 3-months’ rent from my credit card, which is 3545 euros. How come Airbnb makes long stay guests believe that they actually can cancel the reservation and make the whole month’s rent slip away from their pocket for nothing? What are their roles if they fail to solve this kind of problems? Why do they take the commission fee from both sides in the beginning? I strongly demand the full refund of what I paid, 1194 euros.

Just returned from summer vacation - an expensive experience richer - and therefore a WARNING to all others who might come in the same situation using Airbnb. Our four teenagers, my wife and I suddenly had and need off an apartment in Cannes due to some private housing issues down there. We downloaded Airbnb’s app and found a home, which we booked. It all went through Airbnb’s page with their logo. But when we got to the payment page, we were guided to a page that asked us to make a wired bank transfer ... (DO NOT IT !!!). We made the wired bank transfer of € 1,750 for HSBC bank addressed to Airbnb, as we were told. Everything was so professionally made. Airbnb’s logo, mail address and bank account was in the mail, the payment and confirmation, so we knew nothing of fraud/Scam. Even Airbnb subsequently announced that it was so professionally made. But when we got to the address, the apartment did not exist. The location there was just a little old hotel. Olga the host, who we had booked the apartment with, and who had been verified by Airbnb since 2012 with good recommendations from other tenants did not exist. We called Airbnb, sent them mails and have been in contact with them countless off times, but they disclaim any responsibility. They recognize that it is professionally made, but for their guidance, where it says that you must NEVER pay with a bank transfer. Unfortunately, we didn’t have the time to read all Airbnb´s instructions carefully enough. Who has that, by the way, in an urgent critical situation With no housing, no Olga - ONLY FREUD/SCAM and frustrations - we as a family think that it is hard, how Airbnb can look them self in the eyes, and live up to their slogan: one network built on trust, confidence, good behavior, authenticity and reliability!! Airbnb disclaim any kind off responsibility for that on their website, that there was (she is now deleted) an Olga, who rented apartments, who actually rented/hosted apartments in Cannes, at address that did not exist. They are actually totally indifferent, so no help from them at all. HSBC bank is handling this case in their fraud department, but our money has already been transferred to the person (OLGA). So in our mindset, there are minimal chances that they will be returned back to us. We had to find another apartment through Airbnb (which, however, went well this time), pay once again (€1.340) and use our vacation, writing mails to our bank and Airbnb. So all in all, a less fun and really expensive vacation. For us € 1,750 is certainly more money for us than for Airbnb, who will not compensate us for our loss. Airbnb, should screen every hostess, with passport, bank no, social security number, and get all verifications in place, before you can rent out your home. So remember if and when booking at Airbnb: Stay on their web, never leave it! Never pay wired bank transfer! AND read all their guidance thoroughly, before booking!!!! Thanks for reading this. Kind regards The frustrating family

I have been a host with Airbnb for several years and always had good experiences with them although I was aware of all the bad reviews. All that changed with my current booking.The property is in Rio de Janeiro and I have always charged and received in the local currency, the Brazilian real. The current booking was made in August last year and covers the period of the Rio Olympics. Since the booking was a long one (more than five weeks) and the guest was a single traveller I made him a special offer in reals. Imagine my surprise when the first month's rent payout was considerably less than the amount of 7,824 reals which shows as the payout amount on the website. In fact, Airbnb credited my Paypal account with US$1,996. At the exchange rate of 3.25423 on the day of the transfer, this converts to 6494.44 Brazilian reals, about 17% less than I was expecting. I have had numerous contacts with Airbnb and they continue to maintain that I received the correct payout. Their logic is that the dollar amount sent corresponds to the amount in reals they collected from the guest on the day he made the booking in August last year. In other words, in the intervening period the real has devalued against the dollar and so, notwithstanding the fact that all the negotiations were in the local currency, I have received the amount I would have received if the payout had been in August last year. In other words, Airbnb has had the guest's money for 10 months without assuming any of the risk for exchange rate movements For me, Airbnb's reasoning is inherently dishonest. Since they allow their hosts in Brazil to charge and receive in the local currency, the expectation is that the host will receive the agreed amount in reals on the day of payout. I have asked Airbnb where it states in their terms and conditions that their hosts in Brazil who choose to work with the local currency may not necessarily receive the amount they were expecting. I have also them if, following the same logic, the change in the exchange rate has been in my favour, would I have received more than the amount expected in reals. I haven't received replies to these questions and don't expect I ever will. I've reluctantly come to the same conclusion as same money others that Airbnb is just another money-grubbing corporation that's only interested in making money for its owners and shareholders. Trying to deal with their customer services people is an education in itself - they're evasive, they pass the buck, they muddy the waters, in short they do everything except assume any kind of responsibility. This kind of culture in a company doesn't just happen, it comes from the top. Anyway, this current booking will be my last.

We have a three bedroom holiday property in Wales that we have successfully rented out for the last 10 years. We pride ourselves on the maintaining the property to a high standard and ensuring that all our guests have a great stay. I did have some reservations about listing it with Airbnb but, after several recommendations from friends who have used the site as travellers, I decided to create a profile to see if we could pick up a few more short stay bookings during the quieter months. To cut a long story short, after listing my property it became apparent that I could not switch off the 'instant book' feature which would mean we had to accept bookings from ANY travellers who met the limited criteria I was able to set up (e.g. ID verified, no smoking, no pets, no parties or events). In the 10 years of renting out the property there are very few potential guests that I have followed a gut feeling about and not rented to but, as someone who needs to protect our investment and the goodwill of our neighbours, I totally reserve the right to do so. After several emails and phone calls - which were both time-consuming and stressful - I have finally established that I have been unfortunate enough to be one of the selected new hosts who apparently have to accept instant book on any listing I create. I categorically refuse to accept this and have therefore unlisted the holiday property I was intending to add to Airbnb's portfolio. I am extremely angry about this for a number of reasons. I spent several hours on creating the listing and was told - by a customer experience rep. that I initially queried 'instant book' with - that I would be able to edit it once it was live. I was then subjected to a degree of stress after the listing went live because I couldn't disable the function. All the time I was unaware that my profile had effectively been 'locked' into this particular lack of functionality which the reps at Airbnb knew perfectly well. To me this shows a complete disrespect for other people's time and well being. I understand that numerous other prospective hosts have been affected by this 'experiment' and have also refused to list because of it. It would not be impossible for a software engineer to spend a few hours writing the code to enable us to have the same tools and features on our listings as all the other hosts on Airbnb. Or are they really not bothered about us and happy to see us go? If it is the company's plan to make instant book mandatory for all, do they not realise that hoaxers, scammers and those who just see an opportunity to make a quick buck out of travellers will be more than happy to accept it, whereas responsible hosts are much less likely to? Those of us who care about our homes, and the experience of our guests, will always reserve the right to have the final say in who we welcome into them. Airbnb should also be aware that this policy could have legal ramifications. Some local authorities are very concerned that unscrupulous individuals are effectively using Airbnb to set up unlicensed hotels, without any reference to regulations. neighbours, fire safety etc. Making instant book mandatory, even if only for a small percentage of listings at present, would seem closer to a hotel style model than one that claims to be offering a personal home-from-home arrangement.

I'm a huge believer in AirBnB. Putting aside all the wider issues of "should people be allowed to rent out their homes?", AirBnB as a company do a brilliant job of facilitating the connections. The website is one of the most fluent and seamless user experiences I can think of. It's so intuitive, and flexible enough to let me tailor bookings to individual days. When I travel, AirBnB is usually the first place I look for a place to stay. I've booked around 20 nights in 13 different cities over the last couple of years and although every stay is different (by the very nature of the site this has to be expected), they've all been positive. As a host, I've only had 1 negative experience, and this was with the guest, not with AirBnB. In fact AirBnB stepped up and assigned someone to the problem ASAP, were professional and quick to give us assistance, and thankfully, none of it was necessary because it all worked out in the end. What we thought was a fraudulent booking turned out to just be a guest who wasn't very computer-literate. I don't understand why someone would pay more to book a hotel, when they could have a fully serviced apartment, and all the perks that go with it. I think AirBnB would always be my first choice for holiday-stays, and renting an apartment out with AirBnB has been a great income as well.

What do you do if the landlord locks the door and there is no way to get in? Well, we did everything but nothing worked and therefore had to sleep on a bench outside. We called the landlord and sent him messages but to no avail. Then, we rang the bell and knocked the door for hours. Neighbors woke up but never our landlord. By 4am, we were freezing cold and called AirBnb to inform them of our circumstances. 30 minutes later the AirBnb's representative (Laura) called us to confirm that the landlord was not answering. Laura suggested we move to a hotel (with the $70 that AirBnb pays in such cases). But where? How could we if our credit cards and IDs were in our luggage? AirBnB could not help us. We did not want to disturb the whole neighborhood further, and we started walking until we found a bench in a nearby park. There we tried to sleep. The night was cold and our clothes were light. We felt homeless. A few hours later, we located another lodge where we were well received. We returned to the first lodge to pick up our luggage and left. Our landlord thought we were sleeping inside and locked the door. He was very sorry. So were we. Will AirBnb do something? A terrible night going cold and fatigue on the street and one day less of our trip.

The result is : - customer service doesn't answer all the time. - they don't have people to answer in your mother tongue. - AirBnB makes it hard to contact and wants hosts and guests to solve issues on their own. - even though AirBnB has no idea what happened (because they're in an office far far away), their decisions can't be debated. What AirBnB does (other do that too but AirBnB managed to kill the competition) is take the money and let you down as soon as any problem occurs, guest or host. Everything would be much better (and not that much risky) to do things without them but unfortunately, their big money managed to annihilate that much healthier and more straightforward option.

I am floored by some of the reviews here. With the poor reviews, there are no specifics, only flippant negative comments, which makes me wonder if they are being written by hotel/motel owners. We stayed at 4 different establishments on our trip to Africa. Every single one was wonderful. The caretakers were extremely kind and communicative, they went out of their way to make sure everything was just right, they were happy to oblige our needs and were automatic "in's" with the culture and events in the area. Granted, if you are looking to be "pampered", and don't enjoy the warm, quirky intimacy of staying with new friends, this is maybe not for you. The prices are amazing and from what I can tell, Air B&B only charges a minimal amount (like 3% or so) of the asked amount from the rental property. If you are considering Air B&B, by all means, do your research and look at the other reviews from people who have stayed there, but we have found it to be an amazing experience for all involved. More than anything, we love the new friends we have made in new parts of the world.

I've had great luck with hosts - good prices, nice people, etc. That part of this organization works fine. But their idea of account security is Draconian. It's easy to get locked out of your account because you can't take a picture of your ID from your computer. Why can't we upload it from a file like normal people? If god forbid you try to log in from an unknown computer (like when you're traveling, maybe?) and your cell phone doesn't work overseas (happens, you know) good luck getting a timely response. I wrote 3 emails over 5 days and nothing. I finally called their customer service number and the nice man spent 30 minutes trying to help me do something as simple as UNLOCK my account so I could use. He couldn't do it and had to send it up the chain. When I asked to talk with them I was told they only communicate "internally." Seriously. Why not just throw your customers out with the trash? Very poor model for customer service, security and functionality as a whole. I would be embarrassed if this were my company.

Horrible experience. Guests moved in (a lot of them), forged some photos as if I had dirt in the house, submitted them to Customer Service and they got a refund and a free stay at my place. Anybody can do that and a get a "free ride" at host's expense.

I'm just at the end of a 2 week (4 different AirBnb's used) adventure across the USA. The fairest way to describe my experience using it is a bit hit and miss. Booking to begin with was awkward, you wait a day hoping to hear a response to get rejected or ignored, whilst other apartments in the area are being booked and there's nothing you can do about it. I just went for the instant booking ones in the end. My greatest frustration is in the fact that when you read the reviews for a host, they're full of what I can only presume are false niceties, either that or the places have gone really downhill in the last month or so. The first 'apartment' I stayed at had nothing but fantastic reviews. In reality it was just two rooms off the side of someone else's apartment, not private at all as it had no lock to the allotted rooms, and no mention of the fact there is no door BETWEEN the two rooms. Was staying with a male friend, it was a bit awkward with the lack of privacy. Found hairs (head and otherwise) in the bed, yellow sticky stains infront of the toilet (we can all use our imagination to figure out what they were, but cannot be certain), makeup on the pillows and also a cockroach. How can this have only positives? However my next room, in Hollywood was exactly as described, host went above and beyond and let me chill in the lounge in the house because I had a late flight. The last two, were as described but let's say they must have used some strategic angles when taking photos of the rooms, one I didn't even have room to open my suitcase. So this really is my point, in none of these reviews was any of this mentioned or I probably would have just gone with a hotel. So I'm curious if the negatives are removed or people are too scared to be honest. For every room I booked I did read each and every review, so I did manage to avoid anything too disastrous, or being cancelled on, but for what I spent on flights and being on holiday I truly believe it's worth the extra to not be dreading going back to your 'base' at night, I feel a bit like I've wasted money and would rather have had a very short but sweet holiday for the same price.
NEVER USE THIS SITE!!!!!!

We booked an apt. in NYC with 'Al' and paid UP FRONT over $900. We were supposed to be there 6 nights but by the 3rd night realized that a massage parlor was on the mezzanine level of the building we were in, the '2 security doors' didn't work and we ran into a guy in the narrow stairway who was stoned out of his mind. At that point we were thinking 'how could be this be?? We were at 138 W. 46th and if you google Spa 138 or 138 Spa (and look at the google street view) you will see the spot where we were!!! Just look at the door with ALL THE YELLOW CRAP ON THE DOOR and then pan UP (wish I had before I stayed there!!!) and see the photos of massage above. My daughter and I don't remember them being up there because we were too concerned about the travel up those narrow stairs. The sites on google list it as a 'Happy Endings spa' so if that's what you want . . . . then great. It's a great neighborhood, with the exception of this place in the middle of the block. And don't believe Al when he tells you 'he's not sure what the name of the restaurant is next door' because THAT is a lie. I'm sure he knew and he just let us believe that it was the cute little french place to the right of this awful 'yellow door.' There was a VERY swanky boutique hotel called The Muse to the left of this place and a couple of really nice pubs and to the right a really nice french eatery. So you are probalby wondering why am I complaining here? Because when we let Al know that we had been fine with the apartment in general. We weren't there most of the time, but we had increasing concerns for our safety and for the heat that was 'on' and the weather had gotten hot but you couldn't shut it off because it was 'for the building and the pipes were still hot'. And we just couldn't sleep in an 80 degree place so we moved as night 4 was about to commence. He offered us a refund of $300 and I told him I didn't think my husband would be thrilled about that but I'd check with him in the morning. It was almost midnight and we were about to head to bed and I'd let him know. By morning he had contacted AirBnB and they had decided to give us a little over $200 for our 'last 2 nights' (and I'm sure a 'cleaning fee' they kept as well). We figured well, we'd write our review and let people know this place is NOT safe for women to stay!!! BUT, AirBnB has decided that 'canceled' reservations are not allowed to write reviews even if the people stayed for part of the time and MOVED OUT FOR SOLID REASONS!!! BEWARE of AirBnb's is all I'm saying. And DON't stay in the spot listed as Location, Location, Location in NYC on AirBnb! Feel free to contact me if you would like more information before you book. I would have written a review if I could have. Won't be staying at any other AirBnb's if you can't write a review because you moved out for valid reasons!!!

If you want to temporary rent an apartment as a tenant,beware of Airbnb : Airbnb is the most abusive system for you as a tenant and you can not make your vacation plans based on a deal with them. The facts are as follows : The landlord can cancel the deal at any time and the only commitment Airbnb has is to give you back your money for the rental that you had already paid 100% in advance and there is no compensation for the time ( may be weeks or months) that they have your money for free and for the trouble they cause you like having to star over looking for an apartment or worse as in my case having started my trip and getting notice on the way that my rental in Lima -Perú-that I had already paid for was cancelled and I had nowhere to stay . If the tenant cancels the deal damages to the owner on an unknown arbitrary bases will be established but if the owner cancels the deal no damages are considered . As you can see there are no equal parties when renting with AIRBNB .

I recently coordinated a trip of 19 volunteers to do community service near Lafayette, LA. A suitable house was located and the reservation was made and paid for. With 2 weeks to go before the trip the host canceled the reservation. While there was a refund, AirBnB still kept several hundred dollars as a service fee. Being desperate, I located a second AirBnB rental and host agreed to accommodate our group and the reservation payment was made. Shortly thereafter the host began setting unreasonable conditions such as requiring our group to not being able to keep suitcases in the house. When it was clear these conditions would not work for our group I canceled the reservation. Sadly, only 50% of the reservation cost was refunded. In the end the host charged our group of volunteers over $800 for the five days the reservation was place two weeks for the trip was to begin. Not a very nice thing to do to people volunteering their time to do community service. AirBnB was unresponsive to my request for help. Despite these negative experiences, the next location worked out perfectly for us. The facilities were great and we rented out additional space from the host. We ended our trip by renting a house in New Orleans and this was also excellent. The host was attentive, we were very happy with the facilities, and it was a great place to stay. In the end, it is clear it is important to talk with the potential host at length and make sure you understand their refund policy.

I've had extenuating circumstances which have resulted in an unpleasant experience with my first (and only) Airbnb experience. I was told one thing by one customer service agent, then I called again later to double check and was told something completely different by another agent (regarding a refund for a "Change in Reservation" versus a "Cancellation.") I'm honestly still confused, and their legalese/terminology is hard for me to understand; and, I'm American and speak fluent American-English. The website layout is exhausting and confusing, which is the price they pay for looking flashy and trendy. While a lot of my negative experiences were due to my host, neighborhood, and other extenuating circumstances, I found the process to reach a resolution to be anxiety-provoking and exhausting. I've stayed in almost 40 airbnb's over the past 3 years. The GOOD: A good selection of property on the site everywhere in the world. Savings compared to staying in a hotel. No need to pay when leaving, as payment is automatically taken when booking, so check-out tends to be smoother than in a hotel. The website and app look pretty and work very well. airbnb messaging means there is no need to pay for text messages to communicate with a host if connected to wi-fi. The BAD: High fees usually > 10% of booking price. The fee % does not seem to decline much for higher-value bookings, meaning you can end up paying a 200+ euro fee to book an apartment in a European capital for a month, while the work involved in making such a booking is surely no more than a 3-day booking where the fee is 20 euros. Customer service can be pretty useless if you have any kind of problem. For example, in one apartment I rented, the host didn't want to provide me with sheets to start with. I complained to airbnb and they told me to try to see it from the host's point of view... No possibility to search for property by square footage. (Very important!) Reviews of properties are almost useless because airbnb tacitly encourages that negative feedback is left privately. No star rating for Comfort or Luxury in property reviews. Difficult to gauge the true standard of a property in advance. No easy way to gauge reliability of a review because the number of reviews a reviewer has left is not displayed (experienced traveller = more valuable review). Risk of ruining your holiday if a host does not let you in the apartment (happened to me once) / apartment is much below expectations. Only happens < 10% of the time but when it happens it's catastrophic. And when it happens I don't see how/if the host is penalised. So overall, airbnb has created a new market and should be commended for that, but their customer service and quality of information about properties on their site are pretty bad. Therefore I rate airbnb 3 stars, and hope that they will have more competition in the future that will focus on the quality of the customer experience.

I had an unfortunate experience with a poor quality apartment rent in Vietnam, and was letting the owner know about it via a professional email exchange (I genuinely respected him, but pointed out that I felt mis-sold by his apartment, and that it was not worth what I paid. I booked my first trip through this site. The reviews for the host were all very positive. The place appeared to be safe and clean on the website. I received a text from the hosts saying I couldn't arrive until late.....something they did not disclose on their site prior to booking. I arrived after dark and learned just why I was asked to arrive late. It was a complete scary dump. The reviews could not be legitimate. This is a fraud and I contacted the AIRBNB customer service line and they basically sided with the fraud hosts. This company appears to be facilitating fraud. No refund? Seriously? Never, ever again!

AIRBNB BUSINESS PLATFORM IS HORRIBLE. The guest and property owner/HOST can not speak directly until the reservation is booked. Airbnb charges the guest - over and above the rental fee, an additional 6% to 12% to book through airbnb - this is based on the rent amount per week. They also charge the property owner a 3% booking fee. I'm okay with the property owner booking fee but the guest fee is outrageous! They also do not pay the property owner the rental amount until 24 hours after the guests have arrived, which means they can hold the guests and the property owners money for up to a year or more if the booking runs that far in advance. GUESTS, PLEASE book through VRBO or HOMEAWAY! The property owner pays them a yearly fee to list with them and the guests do not pay an extra thing. BEWARE!!!! if a cancellation on the guest's part is necessary, Airbnb will hold a huge part of your money as a cancellation fee. USE VRBO OR HOMEAWAY!!

The nicest thing about using them is your almost making new friends with the gusts as your communicating often and can get to know each other before deciding to allow them to stay. I've had good experiences so far.

I chatted an Airbnb rep to find out why guests could not reserve my listing after I canceled on a guest for that particular weekend. (I now know, of course, that is your punishment for canceling.) My issue was that I put my ad live but forgot to set certain dates (Mardi Gras weekend; I am in New Orleans) at higher rates. Almost instantly, someone booked the Friday and Saturday of Mardi Gras at the regular rate. So basically, I was a brand new user and made a mistake and was hoping Airbnb would at least allow me to list the place for Mardi Gras weekend, to that same user at the correct rate, or to someone else. The conversation was pretty brief, but she did take the opportunity to lecture me on business ethics: Kat: Airbnb has a policy of only wanting people who are serious about keeping reservations to agree. We cannot bend the rules just to make money. Are you still with me? Me: Yes I'm just trying to figure out how they hired such an unfriendly person to be a customer service agent. Kat: I'm friendly enough sir, you just don't like the answer. Kat: We cannot waive the penalties in this case because the pricing was not what you wanted. It's not fair to the guests you cancelled on. Not fair to the guests....what about not fair to me? It's fricken Mardi Gras weekend! If I had accidentally priced my place at $1.00 when I meant to price it at $100.00, would it be "not fair" for the guest not to get the place for $1.00? It's called making a mistake, a**holes! Thanks for listening.

Moreover, they will find any reason not to pay you. I've had guests openly threaten me on the phone and Airbnb did nothing to help.

- You agree your dates, pay your money and think you have it all booked. Oh no you don't !! - The owner has a virtually-free one way option on you. You make your plans pay your money and you are committed, but he isn't. He can cancel until nearly the last minute. The penalties are pathetic. - If he still wants you, fine - he gets your money. But if he changes his mind or gets a better offer, you are on the street. Sure you get your money back eventually, but you have nowhere to stay. - Worse, when you have arranged your time off work, or if he gets another prospect for your dates he can blackmail you for a higher price - or start an auction. That happened to a friend. The guy's excuse was that he made a mistake with the price. Either you pay what he demands or you lose your accommodation. If you have already paid for your flights you are really at his mercy. - Stick to proper letting agencies, (preferably ABTA members so your money is safe), and a binding contract. It is no more expensive and you get a proper service.

I rented a room where the host said he would clean it after he got off work at 6. Check in is at 3, but I didn't feel like I could force him to come back earlier so I planned around his schedule. When I came back around 730 the sheets were dirty and there were dirty towels from the previous guest. The toilet had urine on it and the apartment smelled bad. Airbnb wanted him to come home and remedy the situation instead of reimbursing me. When he was not home by 9 they finally agreed to reimburse me. Which is great, but I had to go back and forth with them for almost an hour and get a supervisor involved. They also agreed to pay up to $150 for my first night in a hotel. So I get a hotel for 2 nights thinking everything will be ok. Then this morning I find the case manager has sent me 2 emails between 9 and midnight stating she needs the receipt and then that she is not paying for the hotel anymore. When I call back i'm told I just have to wait for her to return and they can't give me a timeline. Way to ruin a vacation! I wouldn't have been upset with the dirty room if customer service had responded to the situation quickly and fairly and I was able to put it all behind me but I'm still having to deal with them.

My experience is a strange one, as I am neither host nor guest. I work at a establishment that rents rooms on both Airbnb and other sites, and feel I am qualified to write this epic horror story. Some weeks ago 2 men aged mid 30s rented a room in one of the houses listed by my boss for 2 nights over a weekend. The guests in question, I don't remember their names, seemed mild enough on check-in, and the first night went off without a hitch. There are several rooms in the house, and it being a busy weekend I stayed on site in a spare room to keep an eye on things. The second day of their stay things started to get weird. One of the gentlemen seems to have left the residence in the morning and I never saw him return. The other seemed to wander around the house in a semi-drunken/drugged state muttering to himself. At this point I had one of my children with me, and he immediately started talking to my son and rubbing his head. Parental instinct had alarm bells going off in my head, not because I felt this man was a pervert, but just too intoxicated to know where he was. I politely made small talk and rushed my son home, not feeling comfortable with his drunken familiarity or repetitive verbal utterences (lClassics like "I made a deuce!" And "are you ok, you're freaking me out!"). Regardless, I assumed he would go to sleep eventually, wake up later and be sober, or at least half coherent. I relayed info of my encounter to other employees and the owner to be on the safe side, and thought nothing of it. Boy, when you're wrong, you are REALLY wrong. I received a call at roughly 2am from the employee who was staying on site that night. She reported several large bangs downstairs and requested someone come over to make sure. Living only a few doors down, I got ready and headed over to face who knows what. Upon entering the house, I could see a light on in the bathroom and hear the showering running. The door was wide open, the shower curtain open, and nozzle directed onto the floor. In the shower I could see soiled boxers, and EVERY surface in the entire room, walls, sink, toilet, floor, mirror (yes, the mirror!!!) had been dabbed or splashed with human excrement. Water and faces also formed a trailed from the bathroom, down the hall, thought the kitchen, and finally to the bedroom. The bedroom door was closed and I was already beyond horrified at what I was witnessing, so dared not knock. Stepping up, I did what any true soldier does and cleaned up the disaster (took almost 2 hours, and this is at 1am). And went home to steel myself for the next day's dramatics (I.e. Cleaning the room). By the time I arrived at work the next day, he had left (I'd hope fled but fear he'd not come back down to earth yet) and in his wake had managed to it himself as well, and a small section of a large house needed to be completely sterilized. The loss in bedding was close to a hundred dollars, and considering that Airbnb payout for my employer was only about 130 dollars for the whole weekend so this is truly and epic failing of community rental. Due to problems my boss had already had with Airbnb (inability to get assistance when even the tiniest thing goes wrong, being delisted for violating a federal law that we hadn't violated, was really because Eugene didn't like us) he cut his losses and never filed a damage report, though I wish he had. This is far from the only crazed Airbnb experience in had, and I'm sure not the last, this is just by far one of the worst. The random occurrences of rooms nasty, guests showing up with pets even though we have a no pet policy, stolen food, damaged linens...... For every 1 conscientious Airbnb guest there are 3 oblivious and one totally destructive. I've never had this problem with any other rental site we are listed on, so got to be individual to the Airbnb "community". Cheers A.M.

That was around 8pm Friday evening. That's when things started going pearshaped: there was a giltch with the website, so I phoned customer service and they said they would get it resolved. I got an email on the following day (Saturday afternoon, approximately 2pm) providing a hyperlink saying that I'd need to try the booking again... this link took me to an Airbnb webpage that wasn't working and referenced a 500 error (whatever that is). When I tried accessing it through my potential host's listing, it returned an 404 error ("file/page not found" for those of you not familiar with that error code). Around 3pm, I got an email from another team member saying that they were having problems with my payment method... the same payment method I had been assured was prefectly acceptable by previous agents. The agents kept assuring me, "Oh, this is easy to fix - I'll have it up and running for you in no time!" **Airbnb, please do NOT make promises you cannot fulfill!** It it now Sunday morning aproximately 12:05am, and what I have been through in the past 24 + hours has been an absolute nightmare - a total living hell! Is my reservation going to be completely approved? Will I get a confirmation? I'm a nervous wreck!! I'm to the point of saying, "Screw it! I'm going to stick with my hotel and Airbnb can go to blazes for all I care!!" Because even though the agents I spoke to were very polite, I really got a distinct impression that they'll promise ANYTHING in order to make a sale! It's capitolism at its worst, and it comes off as heartless, soulless, insincere, and almost sadistic. Please, save yourself the heartache and *don't* book with them, especially if you're trying to use Paypal to pay for your reservation.

Recently rented a house through airbnb. There was an electrical problem with the pool cover which was fixed during our stay. The problem was power to a switch that was no fault of ours. They enabled a dishonest person to steal money from a customer because they held the deposit. There is no transparency or available line of communication.

The whole purpose of Airbnb is to protect the guests and hosts. If they fail to do that then everything they purport to be is unrealized and there is no longer a need for them. I feel that I can not trust them to protect me based on my experiences with them so I now due my own due diligence on the guests and require IDs. Hopefully, this will weed out the criminals and I will not need protection from Airbnb which they did not provide. They said they had my back, but when it came down to it, they let me down big time. The whole aura of safely and protection is a facade. They do not care about the hosts or the guests. VRBO doesn't offer you the false sense of security. You make your own contract and do your own do diligence. What they do offer is the insurance that the guest buys, and if something goes wrong you file a claim with the insurance company. I have heard many stories about hosts charging a deposit which actually does not go to the host and then airbnb will not use the deposit to cover the costs of the damage. I think I am going to change my account to no deposit and require the guests to give it to me upon check in and I will have a contract stating they get it back when they leave. Kajsa F- You must work for airbnb. Who would use a company after reading all of these bad reviews. That is a sure sign the person writing the review works for the company they use after reading all the bad stuff about them.

I use Airbnb as both a Host and a Guest. It's a great idea but obviously it relies on individual hosts and guests to respect each others requirements. If you get a bad host or guest, then of course it is not Airbnb's fault but that is the risk you take. It is the same risk with booking a regular hotel or B&B, you can get bad ones as well as good ones - it's down to the people involved! This site opens up unparalleled opportunities to stay in someone else's home or holiday home, giving you a unique experience and unbeatable choice in terms of price and location. You do need to have some common sense when using Airbnb however, so always check out your host's/guest's reviews and make sure that the communication is as you would like. You can always go by your gut feeling too, however if you never try it you will never find out how it works! In summary I have had mainly good experiences with Airbnb and if you are clear on what you are offering and know what you are booking, then you will enjoy a nice experience 99% of the time. Well done Airbnb, keep up the good work!

If you have a problem with the accommodation through Airbnb they will no doubt refund your fee but you will be denied the chance to comment on the experience so the feedback is biased towards the host. I won't be using them again. They have lost my trust and potentially they are colluding with bad hosts to promote bad/dangerous accommodation. You cannot be sure about what you read.

Our host Blaine on 206 Revington street newyork is very mean and unacomodative.She was not nice at all. she is kicking us out of her apartment right now. She also tried to kick us out in the middle of the night last night. We got here yesterday. Only spent a night and she's already accusing us of destroying her house and restricting us from using the things in the house. I advice that Airbnb look into this and caution her because BLaine is one of the people that tarnish the image of Airbnb company.

When we arrived to the location we were astonished to see the number of homeless people sprawled on the street.The host would not come outside to welcome us, but waited at the door for us to come. It should have been the first warning to turn around, go back into the car and leave. Unfortunately, we went ahead and followed her upstairs to the apartment. There was no place for a key, only a keypad, making us very suspicious and nervous---Not to mention, the key for the external door worked for other doors on the block. The interior of the apartment was as expected and eased our minds slightly. However, before getting a chance to leave for dinner, a stabbing occurred just outside. The building was in the thick of the crime scene. We were unable to leave for hours and were scared to do so at that. When I called Airbnb to cancel and attempt to get a refund, I was told they would have to contact the host first. When I finally did hear back, they needed proof of the incident, such as a newspaper article. What this indicated was that neither Airbnb, nor the host was willing to admit the occurrence happened and did not truly care about the safety of their customers. The next morning we woke up to look out the window and see a homeless woman shooting up. I would not recommend staying here as it is in an incredibly dangerous area. Airbnb will not support you if you feel unsafe and the host is in denial that the area is bad. If it helps, this apartment is a couple of blocks away from Tenderloin --- a place to avoid at all costs. All in all, we left scared and in a daze. Save yourself the trouble and find a nicer area. Unfortunately the crime has not been reported yet, so there is no way to prove that it happened aside from pictures we had taken ourselves. As the area is dense with crime, there is no newspaper article regarding the incident. There was no other resolution or trust in their customer’s word. There should not be listings in such dangerous areas. If this happened to us, it is likely to happen to others — or worse, others may find themselves in the thick of it. Two of my friends staying at the Airbnb were minutes away from being outside where the stabbing occurred. They were fortunate enough to have their departure delayed a few minutes, thus narrowly avoiding a potentially life threatening occurrence. The fact that there is no screening process for the locations of the Airbnbs is astounding. If there is one in place, it is clearly not effective. We woke up nervous and scared — rightfully so, as we looked out the window and saw homeless people shooting up. When we left there was a trail of blood along the sidewalk, with crime tape left behind. I am baffled that the customer service is more concerned with finding proof that the incident happened rather than trying to keep it from happening in the future. At the end of the day they care more about business than they do their customers.

We booked thru air bnb for 2 nights in Vancouver and really looked forward to staying in the same bldg as our nephew . Paid and confirmed . Use this site a lot both as traveller and host and find it reliable. Although the app is a bit creaky.

About 2 months ago I tried to complete a reservation on Airbnb for a 6-day stay in Paris. I tried 6 different "available" properties and none of them was really available. All hosts, but one, responded that the property I selected was not longer available. What a waste of effort and time!! After one week of asking hosts and trying to complete a reservation, finally one host accepted my reservation, the charge to my credit card was made in full and everything was running smoothly. However, just this last Saturday I received a 1-line email message saying "I am sorry but the property needs a repair" cancelling my reservation, No more explanations and only the option was to reserve another property with Airbnb. Here I go again fighting against the turbulent waters of getting a reservation approved on Airbnb, now with much less available properties to choose from and at significantly higher costs. I tried 3 more alternatives: the first one was a fake announcement. It disappeared the day after I requested more info and asked for the reservation. The second was again "available" but finally unavailable (I do not understand why such a mess with calendars in Airbnb!). And finally the third was accepted by email, but after 2 days of waiting for a formal response via Airbnb again a 1-line email saying "Sorry but the property owner has decided not to rent the property on those dates". Again what a WASTE of TIME and EFFORT. And the clock ticking for my trip to Paris!!! Finally, I got tired and I decided to go like in the "old days", I took my iPad, opened the Booking.com application, selected a property (30% Higher price than my original search 2 months ago: Thanks Airbnb!) and completed the reservation in 5 minutes. I will never try again Airbnb. The process does not comply to world class service standards, as they do not really qualify properties and /or hosts (or potential hosts). It is a waste of time and the risks of being cheated are high. In my perception, Airbnb is completely useless to busy travelers. You spend more time trying to get a trustable reservation, than really planning a good itinerary. -G

the problem is a challenge to describe, basically a host who did not respond in a timely fashion, and no way to get help from airbnb. the website sends you in circles, sending you to a page that has no resolution and with no options offered.

This is not is a review of Airbnb per se. It is a review of a vacation rental that was booked through Flipkey (TripAdvisor). There was no problem with the booking process through them. After this review the owner canceled her ad Flipkey this review taken off. The ad is on Airbnb. This shows what kind of people advertise on Airbnb. Pro: Kathya (cook and house) 2 thumbs up! Cons:rules signs everywhere, 3 rooms w/tiny AC, 2 rooms no AC, no cots, filthy broken plastic furniture, USB finally after 2 days, broken antique tv, no satellite or cable, insects inside, 2 spoons, no microwave, no seats on toilets, when sitting on main bathroom toilet a person has to put feet over shower parapet, 6 towels for everyone, tiny stereo, kitchen stove does not work properly(Kathya had to cook some food on the grill, because the stove would not burn hot enough). trash all over yard, These amenities are items the owner was grasping at straws trying to improve the ad: private fishing lake/river (no), ocean views, waterfront, water views Duh, the house is a oceanfront . All of the of above items were inconsequential in our decision to leave after only 2 1/2 days into 8 day booking. When we arrived the pool looks like it hadn't been cleaned for weeks. Ezequiel(pool boy and garden) told us that there was a broken pipe. The next morning he ran the pump all day and the water cleared somewhat. He never cleaned the filter or the bottom or sides of the pool. The next day he didn't clean or run the pump. The pool water was never clear and the sides and bottom were slimy. Our party consisted of 12 adults and 4 little kids. All of the kids and some adults spent a lot time in the pool. Some are suffering infections. While eating dinner the second night the owner's dog was chased away from the table by my husband. The dog left. After dinner we were sitting around the table and the dog returned. He received several pats on the back and my brother even removed several ticks from him because he was loaded with them. My husband whistled at him and he came to him. My husband petted him then the dog growled and nipped at him. He then left. The next day the dog was running around and no problem. After lunch one three year old boy who was standing still by the table was bit by the dog with no provocation. The boy's father and my husband went after the dog. In the meantime Ezequiel (who told us the dog was his) stayed in his house instead of getting his dog. My husband caught the dog and was bitten several times before the dog was hopefully dispatched by him. The owner of the property and the dog was only concerned about receiving money for losing the dog. The boy will possibly have trauma for the rest of his life. My husband is undergoing rabies shots and awaiting surgery on his hand. There are many great vacation rentals in El Salvador stay away from this one.

I was a bit apprehensive approaching Airbnb with my issue seeing these negative reviews but I was positively surprised by how professional and helpful they were. I had booked an entire apartment for my boyfriend but the host ended up staying in the apartment occasionally during his stay which made him very uncomfortable. After talking to Airbnb and specifically Sandra from their customer service, they contacted the host and we received both a refund from the host and a sum from Airbnb. They called us back several times to check that we were okay with how they were dealing with the situation which we really appreciated, as it can be quite awkward dealing with a host in person. Overall we are extremely pleased.

Having used Airbnb on 4 occasions, I have been impressed not only with the hosts but with the customer service of Airbnb when our last apartment wasn't up to scratch. We booked an apartment in New York and was told by the host the day before that cockroaches had appeared in the bathroom and that she was getting rid of them. Having backpacked before, I was used to this in hot climates, so a couple in the bathroom wasn't an issue. 2 days after our arrival, there were many in the bath and under the bed, so we told the host. She was amazing and offered a full refund. I didn't even have to contact Airbnb as they had been informed and sent the refund straight to us, not only that, but as we had to move into a hotel for the remaining 3 nights (which was considerably more expensive), Airbnb offered to pay the difference and were very good in answering our questions via email whilst we were travelling. Massive thanks to Emilee F at Airbnb, who sorted all this out for us without us having to ask! We will definitely use Airbnb again.

I have been hosting on Airbnb for four seasons now, renting out lovely room in my own home in Tuscany. I have watched the company become more corporate and less host friendly. At this point there is no longer any way to contact someone who works for Airbnb to make a simple query, but they bombard me constantly with orders about how I should behave and act with my guests. I wish there was an alternative.......

Before starting my complain I want to warn the reader to read one article in New York times published on 14th Aug, 2015 since posting link doesn't work here. The article is about how a traveler was sexually abused in Madrid by its host keeping him locked inside the room and the corresponding worst ever customer service provided by airbnb. Let's begin my story. In this 2015 summer I and my husband travelled to Mallorca. We booked an accommodation reading the good reviews there. But the problem started after the reservation. I made several phone calls (may be 30 times or more) to my host to arrange the subsequent travel plans but never was succeeded to contact them. I repeatedly complain about it to airbnb and they kept on assuring me that they are contacting with the host and everything will be all right. After that the host contacted with me for only 1 time with very poor english language skill. It was impossible to communicate with them. Now the worst part later just 3-4 days before our journey, I tried again to communicate with the host regarding late check in time, taking the keys etc and was not able to communicate. Reported about the problem at the last moment and airbnb said..'ok we tried to contact too and we are also not able to contact with your host. So we can offer that you cancel your reservation and you will get a full refund your money (the cancellation rule was strict which is the reason i didn't cancel my booking earlier). You can now search your accommodation and we will support you with 10% extra cost than that of your previous booking' What the hell! This was said to me just a day prior to my journey! That time almost all accommodations were overbooked and every possible accommodation was way expensive (may be 5 times) than my previous booking! If this is the case then why airbnb did not suggest me to cancel my booking earlier? why they kept on assuring me that everything is going in right direction? why the day before I had to think whether we need to stay in middle of the street? If they would have suggested me earlier, I would have cancelled my booking sacrificing the 50% loss due to the policy and found something cheaper. At the last moment this is just not done! Next time onwards I will never go through an airbnb booking and neither shall I recommend any of my friends or family to go through this type of non co operating services. At the end, I must appreciate the airbnb's customer care executive who really helped me a lot to find a last minute accommodation as soon as possible. But there was no need of this last minute tension paying almost double the price compare to my earlier booking if they would not give any assurance earlier rather suggested a cancellation with 50% loss! I rated single star only due to the last minute help I got from the customer care executive, otherwise, airbnb doesn't deserve a single star from me at least! Regards, Suranita

I had a great experience with the support team and with a long vacation ordered on Airbnb. Long story short - I had a billing issue, and received a refund after chatting to a rep, so that I didn't overpay fees due to a billing issue on my side. That was a fair solution and I was pleased. It seems that there are a lot of bad reviews here, especially regarding refunds, but I'm guessing that not everybody reviews the refund policy of the various hosts. Thought it's worth mentioning.

Air bnb is fantastic- but do your research- I think all the negative reviews here are from prople who didn’t choose wisely. As with all accommodation- research the area you'd like to stay and the home you'd like to stay in- ask questions of the host. I both host and choose to stay in airbnb accommodation. I have always been pleasantly surprised by the quality of the Airbnb homes I’ve stayed in- I've stayed in over 50 airbnb to date!)

People should remember the TrustPilot reviews are extremely negatively biased. Airbnb is so commonly used, and many positive reviewers won't review here because they've already done so on the system itself. I still can't believe the system ranks airbnb this low! I've used airbnb over a dozen times in half a dozen countries, and every experience has been excellent. I no longer bother looking at hotel booking unless I absolutely have to. And I don't know anyone personally who has had a negative experience. I faced one minor disagreement with an airbnb renter which did not affect my lodgings or the cost of my stay. This disagreement was resolved.

I have had a really bad experience with AirBnB and would urge anyone, who is considering using this company, to stop right now. I booked one night with six of my friends for my birthday, in what was advertised as a "Delightful Town House in Central Brighton" (UK). The reviews were glowing so I paid the £336 on my credit card two months before the due date. When we arrived in Brighton we realised that it wasn't central at all and was in the student/ bedsit area, on a very busy road with all-night pizza and kebabs shops opposite the house. The house itself was horrible and hadn't been cleaned in a while. We ended up going to the Co Op across the road to buy antibacterial wipes before we touched anything. There wasn't enough beds for the seven of us, despite the advert stating "sleeps 9 comfortably". None of us could sleep at all as it was so noisy all night with the takeaway restaurants outside. The following morning the host texted me asking me to vacate the property by 11am - I texted her back to say we left at 8am as we were so disappointed. She then called me and I politely told her how dirty and noisy it was and asked for half my money back, which she refused and put the phone down on me. I then wrote a review to AirBnB telling the whole sorry truth but I was shocked and distressed to get an abusive review back from the host accusing me of being "a Professional Cheat, who goes around staying at people's properties and then complaining in order to get the night for free!". I was shocked by her aggressive and defamatory comments and asked AirBnB to escalate my complaint. Since then I have had emails going back and forth totally ignoring my complaint that the house was not "Delightful" or "Central Brighton". The case manager assigned to me said she can't help me as I didn't follow the company rules and make a complaint with 24 hours and even said "I cannot see from your review that you had any problems with your host". If it wasn't so frustrating and distressing to me it would be laughable. This company haven't supported me one bit and their website is still putting up glowing reviews on this house. I am going to try retracting the £300 through my credit card company as I'm not going to get anywhere with AirBnB. This is the first time I have ever used AirBnB and I will certainly never use them again.

I booked a week in a room in San Miguel de Allende Mexico. It was listed as a Casa D'arte; a room in an artist's house which looked bright & colorful. The artist said she had 2 friendly dogs & 2 cats. Instead when I arrived I found 3 dogs including a full-grown, untrained golden retriever who jumped, bit me ever chance it could, and barked like crazy. The artist was more of an unemployed wannabe jewelry maker who got by on (guess what) renting her spare rooms to airbnb. She slept 'til noon, drank from 4 on and hardly spoke to me, anyway ner dogs were sheer hell. They barked for hours, left a [trustpilot will not let me use the word for 'fecal matter'] on the hallway outside my room, then I got fleas, the house was messy and she did nothing ... I complained to airbnb who of course did not respond, told me to talk to her but she was either asleep or out buying more booze and ignoring me. The dog ran away with my underwear one day -- no lie -- and she shrugged it off. My last night the noise was unreal -- she and her boyfriend talked loudly until after midnight, then made love next door to my room to the sound of television ... I felt like I was back in college. Again I complained to airbnb who had me write letters, communicate with host (who said well dogs bark in Mexico that's what they do, and that I was a dullard who didn't drink) and finally airbnb closed by case (I asked for a partial refund from this lying artiste) saying I hadn't followed proper communication channels. The airbnb service rep I talked to was so lame and useless, and he said that his Supervisor had said it was my fault for not following proper channels and that I needed to 'move forward' and learn to communicate more efficiently. I now have a huge infected flea bite which measures 4 inches by 2 inches on one side of my cheek which I got at her house; but again I guess in the fine print of airbnb's contract it says the guest is responsible. How outrageous -- if you stayed at a hotel they would respond to your complaints, but airbnb won't. They don't regulate standards or legality of hosts or hosts' spaces, so as a guest that is part of your job also ... to be the regulator, to report back, then to deal with their slow, incompetent customer service. I'm going write again, sending photos of the flea bite (which is gross and green and is now felt in my lymph node), then talk to my credit card company about refusing the airbnb charge for this horrible week. I will never use airbnb again, or any short-term rental agency. I've traveled for most of my life and have always had great luck finding local great places, because I speak 3 languages and make friends, not by clicking on a white yuppie app from the US. Prices are much higher now that airbnb has reinvented travel for the middle-class travelers, and the travel experience is much worse, in terms of being dirtier and less dependable with some of the space case hosts, and also the 'foreign' experience is much more Disneyland and less real world now. If you travel on your own, and take local accomodations, or rather, travel like a member of the country you are visiting, you will always learn more, have more fun and save money. I hate airbnb. Seeing what they've done to New York City, San Francisco, Paris and other big cities is stomach-turning: rents are now at least doubled while local taxes for social services are down, and local neighborhoods have lost their real feeling, instead becoming islands of wannabe cool visitors. Plus workers in local businesses can no longer afford to live in these cities and must travel long distances to get to work. Airbnb's uncaring customer service has energized me to take them on in a bigger way.

I have had my property on AirBNB for a few months now and if lt looks like I will probably lose more money than I have made.
