HATE the system.
No ABTA and no ATOL. It is not unusual for hosts to cancel your booking the day before you arrive. Just be aware !

We rented a house in Redmond WA for five weeks and it was super expensive--the host completely misrepresented his property. It was "barely" furnished and what it did have was dirty and stinky bed lines and pillows. The kitchen had almost nothing in it, things were broken, shoddy, and the host was a control freak. Our kids have autism and we were in the seattle area for a special camp so "moving" to a new location and getting a refund was not possible. I alerted Airbnb of the issues in the beginning, they said they have "guidelines" but no real "standards" hosts must adhere to. So we made the best of it, had to buy so much to furnish the house we had to rent a uhaul to return home....of course the host was completely unreasonable asking for thousands of dollars in damages. We went through resolution center and offered what we thought was fair for the things we know we did, minor carpet stains, a broken door stop, etc. The host actually tried to bill us for removing a lightbulb from a lamp! and he also wanted us to pay him 36K for new carpet...airbnb sided with our intitial offer to settle but my problem is that while in resolution we exceeded the 14 days you have to write a review (we had no idea of this policy) and they WILL NOT budge on making an exception. we thought after we settled we could then write a more honest review instead of the "this host is insane" narrative....but airbnb??? BIG FAIL.

I booked a "Charming Historical Home" for vacation with family in Cape May, NJ. We found the place utterly lacking in charm, and poorly maintained and furnished. Kitchen was dirty w/ leaking water under sink, trash in cupboards and drawers, and 2 dinner plates for a house that slept 9. Closets were dirty, baseboards were missing, and, when a doorknob fell off in my hand, the host told me "It's a 105-year-old house, you know", and left without fixing it. Beds looked slept in, linens and dishes were of questionable cleanliness, and furniture was broken. I was extremely distressed and did not stay more than an hour. I was fortunate to find a last minute rental elsewhere. I contacted Airbnb, and told them I had to leave, as the place was not habitable for 450.00/night. I wrote a letter to Airbnb and attached pictures. I was told they would not refund my money because their policy was to give the host 24hrs to correct problems. This host was so annoyed when I pointed out some of the issues, he left and took back with him the courtesy bottle of wine! And where was I to stay while he 'addressed' the issues of cleanliness and disrepair?? Never again.

Stayed in a Brooklyn apartment booked through Airbnb. Old and neglected was sold as "charming." Could not sleep in the stuffy, uncomfortable space. Left after two nights and requested a refund for the third, supplying Airbnb with photo documentation. Got the refund, but Airbnb removed our review because our reference to an Airbnb investigation violated Airbnb's protocol. Airbnb refused to allow an edited version of our review to be posted to their site. It seems to be about money at all costs rather than fair information to be available to prospective guests.

I made a reservation and then cancelled within 12 hours.. Clearly they said we get a full refund when cancelled before the 24 hours of check in. I cancelled one place to reserve another and for that they took $29 from my refund. I think that is such bs. And I feel that is not right at all. I do not recommend airbnb.

We rented from Airbnb this month. The place was ok but many problems. You really take your trip into someone else's hands when you use this option. Sometimes it works out, other times??? Not recommended for families because you never know what kind of a place or an owner you're going to end up with. Airbnb lies about the cost, gets you to commit, then jacks you with fees at the very end. They never reply to a request or question. There's no way to reach them. Caveat emptor!!

Hello, just wanted to share a bad experience with AirBnB I rented a flat in Lisbon-Portugal for a few nights in August , Small apartment but it had a pool and my kids wanted a pool. On the day prior to our arrival AirBNB warns me pool will be out of service for one day. Upon arriving I am told the pool is on maintenance for several days, therefore ruining my stay in Lisbon ... I paid in advance for a service that can not be provided to me Owner seems to understand, apologizes to me and offers to cancel and reimburse. What choice do I have??? So I leave the location without even stepping in this flat I find a 4 stars hotel with rooms and working pool, (in fact cheaper than the flat... and breakfast included) Afterwards I get about 60% refund, without any comment or explanations Far from being acceptable so I tell it to AirBNB, who nicely offers USD100 coupon instead of the 200eur I claim for ... like I was some begger, this was so insulting!!! I am now trying to get full refund but AirBnb rejects my requests for total refund and does not even publish my review on this rental I watched through the reviews for several apartments, and it is surprising to see there is no negative comments, none at all ! very strange....but so convenient Anyhow I lost about 200eur on this 'organised' fraud I am therefore going for local tax authorities to leave a complaint about the local owner... AirBnB will probably pretend they did their job, but they are just getting money and not taking responsabilities or recognise their own mistakes So boycott AirBnb and be carefull with your rentals, particularly in Portugal !!!

I booked a room in Paris with flexible cancellation. When I went there the room was very small and the toilet was in the kitchen. To top things there was dust on the window and the host's husband was there which made me uncomfortable and was not mentioned in the room description. I left immediately. The host will not refund my money nor will airbnb

rented a place at the beach. The house was nice. But we were charged an extra cleaning fee and then airbnb charged us almost an extra night stay as a fee! Ok. Our first experience and hit the ok button too soon. We then realized later they charged us a security deposit but added it into the nightly fee. Nightly rate was to be 715 they charged us 928 a night and NOW say they didn't charge a deposit and that was the nightly fee. We shared screenshots to prove. The customer service rep even agreed that is what she sees and confirmed it was advertised at $715 nightly YET she cannot help us. They basically admit they overcharged but we 'agreed' by hitting ok so tough luck for us! So exactly what is that airbnb for? They caused this problem themselves and we are out $1500. Never again. I will go to VRBO.com as I have always done.

I recently booked a place in Portland Oregon for 2 nights, paid airbnb $485 in full, in advance. I show up and the place looks nothing like the photos, plus they lied about parking on the premises and there was a cat in the apartment, plus litter box. I called the owner immediately, he seemed to be nice and said he would refund me but I had to go through airbnb, so I locked the apartment and left. I called airbnb and they said they would refund me ONLY what the listing party agreed to. Sure enough he changed his mind and decided he would keep $245, including taxes and cleaning fees. I got nothing, zero, zilch, and paid $245! I can't even leave a bad review for this guy! Airbnb allowed this, even though the place looked nothing like the photos and was not as described. I told them to go and look at what they are advertising, they did not. I would never use airbnb again!

We used airbnb to arrange what we expected to be lovely cottage accommodation for family visiting for our wedding. With less than a week to go our booking was cancelled adding huge amounts of stress - I had been recommended airbnb by a friend but wish I had read this sights in advance as had I known this could happen I not have used airbnb. Airbnb offered an extra £100 towards another booking but with so limited notice of the cancellation any remaining accommodation in the area was either too much or unavailable. We had a great wedding but the whole experience would have been much more pleasant had we not used airbnb. I am sure you can get great value accommodation if you are lucky but I believe that our experience shows it cannot be relied upon - please avoid our mistakes.

I tried to book a night at a small bnb in Melbourne. I didn't realise the cost was for per person as the add was not clear. When I tried to get a refund even though I had not accepted the higher fee I was charged an administration fee. They have refused to refund me the fee despite the fact I did not accept the booking. Totally dodgy company to use for booking a place to stay!

AirBnb has worked perfectly for me since the beginning. I have used it as rental and rent out myself and not once have i had any trouble. Its a perfect way to get a little extra $ when i am on vacation. More to it, it has always been such good service if i needed any questions answered. ps. Thanks to Stevie from customer service :)

I booked an apartment in Paris for a week in July. We were traveling with family including a couple in their late 70s. Although one week prior to leaving for Europe, the host told us construction was going to start and could get noisy and offered to extend a discount based on the amount of disruption. We had no choice but to stay their since we couldn't find another apartment to sleep 8 people with limited stairs in such a short time. The construction noise was during the day when we were out - no big issue. However on the 4th day we returned to the apartment to find that the handrails for a spiral staircase had been removed plus the wall on one side was completely gone. This was a Friday, the female member of our family (78) had to climb the stairs on hands and knees. The male family member (same age) who is recovering from a broken him was to arrive at 7AM on Saturday. We had no choice but to get a hotel for them just down the street. I contacted the host (Tom) who said he had said earlier he would give us a discount and would reimbsurse for the hotel. There were other issues with the apartment that we were willing to overlook because the location was perfect. After we left, I contact Taom about the reimbursement for the hotel, he requested a copy of the bill which I sent numerous times , but he always said he didn't receive and then just stopped returning my calls, texts etc. I spent a number of hours trying to locate Airbnb's phone number,l when I finally did and provided the information to them the final resolutions is that the host has refused to reimburse us, airbnb said they will cover up to 50% of the bill, but we should have notified them within the first 24 hours of a problem (the problem occurred on the 4th day) they wanted to see videos of the stairs with the railing and without (why would I have taken a video since I didn't expect the tailing to be removed). Airbnb is hiding behind their poilicies if possible. I have raised an issue about being able to provide a review but since we are past 14 days they don't allow it - plus they have no intention to dealing with the host for lying about the situation. If you are looking for an apartment in Paris and see one by Tom Schlemby on Blvd Beaumarchais - ignore it!!

We recently stayed at an AirBnB home in Seville, Spain. Three days after we left, the host notified us and wondered if we had experienced any allergies or bug bites. I responded back that no one in our party of four had experienced a single bite. Fast forward, she has now filed a claim against us for infesting her entire home with bed bugs in the three nights/2 days we spent there. There is no way we are responsible for this. I even contacted the hotel we stayed at after the AirBnB home, and they brought in professionals to check the rooms we stayed in and found NOTHING. I am waiting to hear back from AirBnB. They sent one response, but have not followed up with me since. There is no way we are reimbursing her for the fees incurred to disinfect her home. In fact, I am planning to file a claim for reimbursement of the monies we spent staying there. We spent 345 Euros per night to stay in this home and it most definitely wasn't worth it. It was our first experience using AirBnB, and if they don't resolve this, it will be our last.

Airbnb is in principle a good concept, however it does not offer ANY protective measures against FRAUD, which makes it a very big no-go. I tried to rent an appartment offered through Airbnb, but the apartment does not exist, and payment was offered through private bank account, with prepayment before i could get the keys.... I can add 2 and 2 together, -surely this is a scam. However Airbnb does not offer any measures, to ban this advertiser Anna Harper - or this appartment. This swindler can freely continue his/her activity on Airbnb. This was the payment information I received from so-called Anna Harper: Deposit information: Rent with confidence with Airbnb Payment Information Account Name: Negreanu Corneliu IBAN: ES48 0081 0130 0900 0687 0896 SWIFT Code: BSABESBB Bank Name: Sabadell Country: Spain 1. Go to your local bank. 2. Payment by bank transfer with Airbnb representative information.
I used airbnb several times already. Every place I stayed was great, often better than expected. Hosts were nice and hospitable. Prices are often better comparing to hotels/hostels.

Can someone give me the email address for customer service inquiries? I didn't find one and now their site has me locked into their agree or disagree page. Won't let me maneuver through site. When I called, they said that's the way it is. Booking error and I immediately requested correction. Made inquiry to owner and it booked me as I had credit card on record. Not easy to contact anyone who can authorize correction, they'll call you back. Meanwhile host hasn't removed booking and his listing is showing the dates I inquired for as booked. Will update and post review when situation is resolved. Hoping I have something nice to report.

Sadly to be an Air bnb Host is NOT a good experience. Poor customer service and assistance from air bnb, site that malfunctions, they require you to pre approve or decline within 24 hours of initial contact even if you are still discussing with the booking guests. If you decline too many times then they deactivate your account or move your listing further back so that when new guests are looking they do not see yours! if you pre-approve and the guest changes things up or you have another reservation request for some of that time it makes it difficult to decline and penalizes you too. I have 5 star reviews and a ton of hostings however I could wish a better company would come along with better policies that allow this to be a smoother and more profitable process.

My 79 year old mother does not have a Facebook or Linked In account. Who knew that would be such a problem in trying to get her a place to stay to visit her brother. She spent six hours alone working on jumping through all the other hoops, and then I drove down to her house in another city from where I live and spent two more hours. Apparently Air B and B is great for the hosts but God help you if you try to navigate their website as a potential guest. They supposedly want to prove you are who you say you are, and a link to Facebook would do that. Without Facebook you have to upload a picture of your drivers license or other government ID, post a video (this was where we had trouble-the site was malfunctioning and you can't call them) introducing yourself, and give payment information. Enough to have them steal your identity. Scary right there. If it weren't for the potential host communicating with her, who eventually got an Air B and B person to call her, she'd have lost her reservation. They have s time limit to reserve and it's not enough for host and guest to communicate and make arrangements without being vetted by the company. They have to get their fees somehow. Hopefully not by preying on very active and mentally sharp but computer shy 79 year olds like my mother!

The worst customer service ever - stole my money - we never checked in because apartment offering accommodation for 8 people tuned out to offer 3 single beds! Here is correspondence: Hello Joan, This is Kristine over at Airbnb again. Thank you for getting back to me although I am sorry we weren't able to find you a suitable listing. If you were able to book another listing, we would not be able to transfer the payment as the cancellation was made on your end. I have reached out to Jordi to speak with him regarding your refund, but am awaiting to hear back from him. As I mentioned on the phone, the quality of the beds does not qualify as a hosting standard violation. Therefore, Jordi is not obligated to issue a refund. I do, however, want to try to find a middle ground that will accommodate both parties. As soon as I am able to get back in touch with him, I will reach back out to you. I look forward to speaking with you soon. The apartment owner does not return my calls or text messages for 2 days now and it is unclear when and if he will respond to you. As fas as the payment is held by your company I hold you fully responsible for the full and immediate refund. I have spoken to Jen in your company and she could not confirm 24, 48 hour or any response time frame by your company at all. Dealing with this situation while being stranded abroad with my wife and kids, away from my home and office in Los Angeles is extremely difficult, I need a prompt response from you now. Otherwise I have no choice but to give this matter to my office in Los Angeles to deal with which will only complicate the matter further for all parties involved Regards, J.P. Capacity is one of the valid reasons for the full refund. I insist on the full refund immediately regardless of your conversation with the owner as the listing policy has been violated. Furthermore the owner has finally contacted us and, per his statement, it is your company that holds the funds and it is solely up to Airbnb to issue the refund and the matter is out of his hands. At this point I am taking it very personally because it is not how I spend my vacation time by arguing with you about the obvious. I have people in my office who are ready to take it over. I have already experienced tremendous inconvenience and substantial extra expenses due to mis-information on this listing and the lack of resolution on the matter. This is your sole responsibility at this point.

I am surprised to be hearing such poor reviews after the writers limited exposure to the company. Identification verification is a good thing for all involved. It gives both the host and the traveller a sense of security. If a potential guest balks at going through a few security loops I honestly won't feel comfortable hosting that guest. A company like Airbnb is worth billions and doesn't need to sell your ID to make money. That is just silly. It would annihilate what they have so successfully built up. To mention that the hosts don't care is rubbish. I'm a host and we go beyond the call of duty to make our guests have a memorable and enjoyable holiday. To stay in a home instead of a hotel is the only way to touch the community of where you are visiting. Hotels are completely impersonal and are just a room in a new location. I have used the site as both host and traveller and I think it is the best thing to happen to travel. They've created a site that is actually fun to use and make travelling so much more personal than it used to be. I will be surprised if I ever stay in a hotel again. It would be near impossible to run any sort of global site like this without some bad apples spoiling some experiences but this is not the fault of Airbnb so they take all the steps they can to prevent this from happening and those very steps are causing complaints. You can't have it both ways people. Would I recommend the site? I do! Time and time again. Well done Airbnb!

I rented my cabin through Airbnb last month. My cleaning lady went there to clean it. She texted me right away to alert that the guests smoked weed/marijuana inside the property and the whole house is in a bad condition. We could not rent the place for a few weeks as a result of weed smoking of Airbnb guests who were absolutely disrespectful. I contacted Airbnb to compensate for the damages. Airbnb do not require deposit and guests literally can do what they want. If you want your $250 000 to be ruined for a few bucks of rent AirBnB is the way to go. Save yourself from aggravation and disappointment and stay away from Airbnb

Tried to book a place through Airbnb. Went to put in dates. All dates--every single day--through August 2018 (that's 3 years from now!) are grayed out. Beyond that date, the calendar is non-active. So does this mean booked, or the place is no longer for rent, or what? Tried "contact the property owner." Can't be done without selecting a date; can't select a date since they are all grayed out. Tried "help." Non-existent. Tried contacting a fellow-user "expert." The "expert" suggested contacting the owner. (I suggested that the "expert" read my email, in which I had explained why it was impossible to contact the owner.) Suddenly a popup: now, suddenly Airbnb wanted a photocopy of a photo ID and some other documentation. So suddenly, I am supposed to start sending personal data and info to them via internet, even though there is nobody to contact with a basic request? Really? Looks like a scam at worst, and very sketchy at best.

I am a Landlord. A "guest" took a picture of my room which he is now advertising on Airbnb for profit. he has no right to do so and obviously I will not be honouring any bookings. I have told Airbnb many times both on live chats and by e-mail. The best they come up with is that if I write a letter of complaint they will bring it to the attention of the "host" (who is of course the criminal!). The entire situation is absurd with Airbnb. Avoid this company.

they took my money; later they emailed and said place is not available. 16th day passed still didn't gave my money back. false advertisement, talked to service department couple of times more than 10 hours i spent just to taking them. no help.bull sheet. this company definitely sucks. if you care about your family and your money donot book or use them to plan for your lovely vacation . They will ruin it .

I tried booking a cabin first on their website and then on the terrible app they have. I had to make a profile and tied to book the cabin. My booking didn't go through. When I tried to call, "which it's nearly impossible to find a number to call" the wait time was over 30 min. I never got an answer to any of my emails. I will NEVER!!!!! use this site again. If you have a property to rent find another site to list it! This one SUCKS!!!!

I bought a plane ticket and room in Martha's Vineyard, but 2 days before the trip as I'm getting ready for work I find out...airbnb abruptly canceled my reservation and asked me to verify my ID!! I verified my ID with passport, but then my account was closed. I didn't know what to do, because all the hotels were booked. They never gave me an explanation, but luckily my gf was able to find another bed and breakfast. If they had called me ahead of time or given me an explanation, I wouldn't mind so much. I guess this is the way airbnb does business.

I've had good & bad experiences with Airbnb, mostly good to excellent. The first time I tried to use it, the host pulled out half a week before a big weekend in San Francisco -- too late to find anything affordable in the city. That host had no reviews. I have since stayed in a number of great places for the money, both in the U.S. and in Europe. Airbnb saved my family's European vacation this last summer (2015). No way would we have been able to find affordable lodging for 5 people in regular hotels. We had a major mishap in the last place we stayed in, where it seemed like pipes had burst while we were out, resulting in water leaking into the floor below and into businesses on either side. Because the plumber found nothing, the owner tried to blame us, but with the help of Airbnb, we came to an agreement where I got reimbursed for half of what I had requested. Airbnb's follow-up was good, including personal calls.

Just had a pretty bad experience trying to use air bnb for the first time. We found a few places that we really liked and after speaking to a few of the hosts we chose one place. It was in budget and had all the amenities that we wanted. Knowing that the fees may change depending on the time of year, I double checked with the owner that the fee for a weeks stay that was on the listing was the same for the week that we needed to stay next year. He confirmed the amount and also said that if I requested the stay that he would accept. So...I request the stay and the request expires. He's in Italy, so I figured with the time change maybe he just missed it, so I sent another requests (this puts two holds for the total amount on my bank account). I get a response 12 hours later saying that he is sorry for any confusion, but the rate for next year is going up $300. I told him that is out of our budget and if he could please reconsider keeping the rate what he had already quoted U.S.. I did not get a response other than a declined request notification. I contacted air bnb, knowing there was probably little they could do and I was right, they did nothing. Just responded to my email with a list of steps for successful booking which I had already completed. Needless to say, I am not happy. I thinly they should allow you to review hosts even if you haven't stayed so that everyone is aware of the issues that they have had and not just the good stays. The other booking websites I have used have been so easy and stress free. Now I am stuck searching again and not on air bnb I might add.

I booked a loft in Montreal for this coming long weekend... 3 months ago. All went well, host was helpful and payment was taken. Fast forward to last week, I got an email reminder to get in touch with my host to make sure everything was good to go, so I did. 3 days later no reply from host. Send her another message. Still nothing the next day. Now I'm worried as I see she had cancelled on someone the day before their arrival date in June. I use the verified cellphone number to text her (multiple times/days) and email her as well, to no avail. I email airbnb, they call her - no answer. "Give it another day and you'll hear back from us soon." Nothing. I call airbnb the next day - raging mad as I'm now two days away from my supposed check in date with no where to stay (this is a long weekend in Montreal with their massive Osheaga music festival happening - ie good luck finding ANYTHING for any kind of decent price or distance to where we want to go). They tell me they are going to try and call my host and see what happens, and again, "get back to me". I tell them I just want a refund, they give me the standard like "In order to prevent paying cancellation fees...." and my reply "EXCUSE ME?! I am NOT paying to cancel when my HOST is the one who is unresponsive!!!" Long story short, I am due to call airbnb back today to see what my next steps are. I will not give up on this until I receive a full refund. This is outrageous. Airbnb NEEDS to better screen their hosts. Unreal. Ridiculous. Only wish I saw this website BEFORE making this booking ***UPDATE*** Have received FULL refund (including airbnb service fee), as well received $60 voucher for "next use" Airbnb ended up being very helpful in this matter despite a couple of waiting periods. It's just the HOSTS you need to really watch for!! USE WITH CAUTION

So, what I can say about my Airbnb experience as both a guest and a host is nothing but wonderful things. I feel like a lot of the reviews from the people on here don't completely understand how this community works or are completely computer illiterate. Their customer service is beyond exceptional. Any time I have an issue and need to contact them, 95% of the time it's not just some robotic type response, and they are extremely personable and friendly, especially compared to most any other company's customer service dept. The people who don't understand the whole "providing ID" thing are ridiculous! Would you want to stay with someone or have someone staying with you who may possibly be a felon or a sex offender? I didn't think so. Airbnb has always paid me out on time, it's just THE BANK who takes forever to clear the money, and claiming they don't have it, while as a bank employee, I know for a FACT they have that money, and just hold it as long as possible to collect the interest on it. Luckily tho, I've had no damage done to my property, but my brother, whom is also a host, has had damage done, and after provided proper documents was paid out accordingly. As a guest, when host's cancel, I can understand that things come up. It's not as frequent a thing as people are portraying it to be on here, and Airbnb was very helpful finding me another place, even going as far as providing me with a little bit extra for a place that was more expensive than my original booking. The other time I was cancelled on last minute, and I couldn't find a place so was booked into a hotel. I don't see how this is a bad company or poor customer service. These reviews from the others make me feel like this just may not be a community for them because that's exactly what Airbnb is, a community, and should probably just stick to staying in hotels. I love this website and highly recommend it to anyone looking to try something out of the norm when taking a trip. There's a reason why this company got SO big SO fast, and it wasn't from being poor to the users in their community. Use Airbnb!!

Last May I rented an apt in Washington DC. All went smooth. The place is what I expected, a bachelor pad for my son and I to spend a night at, while attending my other sons military graduation. I didn't have any problems with payments or contacts. The host left us snacks and the place was clean. I was going to use AIRBnB again...but not sure why so many bad reviews! If I go on my own experience, there were no problems at all.

I signed my property up to Airbnb 10 months ago, all was going well until a guest damaged items at my property. The guest refused to cover the damaged items despite the items being blatantly broken and in need of replacement. Since the damage deposit is held by airbnb and not the owner I referred the matter to Airbnb's resolution team for assistance. After all, I had proof of the damage as well as what it would cost to replace the items. Surely they would side with the owner who's property was damaged? Wrong. This was literally the worst thing I could've done. Despite providing replacement cost evidence and point by point details of what happened. Airbnb said "Thanks here's 61% of the actual cost" They gave no reason for their decision, zero feedback on my requests and I'm out of pocket on replacing items in my own home. If there was a zero ranking that's what I would give. For a $10bn company this is unacceptable. I'm still at a loss for words.

We booked a place in London and the host cancelled on us. Airbnb did give us some compensation towards booking another place, which we duly did. Low and behold, the new place was cancelled on us by the host, 3 days after he had accepted and we had paid him. This site is overrun with unreliable, unprofessional host who are dipping their toes in the water for a few extra pounds. When it suits them, they will accept your booking, when it it doesn't they will cancel your booking and the hosts don't give two hoots about ruining your trip and plans. I have spent a total of 6 hours on the phone dealing with this nightmare. In the end I called a hotel that was cheaper and took me 5 minutes to book, GO FIGURE!! TAKE MY ADVICE, STICK TO PROFESSIONAL RELIABLE HOTELS AS YOU HAVE ALWAYS DONE AND SAVE YOURSELF THE AGGRAVATION AND RISK. I would sooner sleep stood up in a field than go anywhere near this idea ever again.

I booked a recent family trip to Yellowstone through AirBNB. I was enticed by their cheaper rates vs VRBO for similar properties. BIG MISTAKE! One condo was canceled two months after I booked it (about three months prior to the trip) and I had to find another place at higher cost. I'm a reasonable person, I figure these things happen. Then the second condo gets canceled LESS THAN ONE WEEK PRIOR TO OUR ARRIVAL! Both times the listers gave some excuse about "management issues" or some such. Absolutely horrible horrible business practice! AirBNB obviously does not screen their listers nor hold them accountable for these kinds of practices. I will NEVER EVER book through them again and I would encourage others to heed my warnings!!!

I had a problem with my paypal account, another story, but I am unable to change my payout preferences for Airbnb. So, this is the follow up: Well, they finally fixed it and I like them again. Customer service personnel really don't know how important their jobs are. They were even kind enough to give me a free affiliate link. I put it on my website for a donation to the NGO I founded in Nepal. It's called Kay Garnay for Nepal. I've met a lot of nice people on the site.

This is my first visit to this site. I and any of my friends and colleagues that I've ever talked to about Airbnb have, to a person, had excellent experiences. The technology works. The selection is amazing. The hosts are genuinely interested in the sharing economy and the good experience of their guests. The last person complained that he had to use a photo ID for proof of identity. That is a ridiculous complaint. It's a simple security measure for everyone involved. Let's get a little real here. I question the credibility of Trust Pilot when an amazing service like Airbnb has a rating of Bad.

You only find out that they need photo id to book after you have spent hours searching through the property. Why do guests need to do this - after all they have the credit card details. I did go through the ID verification process only because i had spent hours on the website. I am worried that this will leak and be used for fraud . Also very difficult to ring them

Forget about using this website !! Landlords will have money sent to airbnb before we have seen the apartment or been given the keys. And afterwards we would receive a refund if we did not like the apartment - yes, hello..... Stay far away from this website !!

I am not a clever person when it comes to the computery things and Airbnb is freaking me out! Whilst once I was able to send an e-mail requesting their help, now it seems impossible to get any direct contact. When I had a technical issue, a customer service representative made contact by phone and was friendly and helpful and it turned out that my Safari and Firefox are out of date so I have to use someone else's computer to access and reply to B&B enquiries. I have specific questions: one of the amount of commission they are charging per booking; the second and third questions relate to what was recommended by the customer service person I had spoken to - on the matter of there having been NO response to my friend's application as photographer (for this region) and that a fellow host and I cannot work out how to give each other reviews - it seems impossible to work out! And a question which relates to a recent potential booking: I got three of the same messages to my phone several days after our first correspondence. I thought she was going to make a booking but this was obviously delayed by Airbnb, and thus she cancelled. IS this organization a big sham? I find it frightening that one can get no personal customer service when they brag about how many jobs have been created here in Ireland. All this is taking up far too much of my valuable time. Who and where are these people!???? R. F.

My experience with Airbnb is from a hosts prospective. All the website glitches and extreme difficulty contacting them are the same as all the other reviews. My recent experience is with payments that should have already been paid by the guest are several days late, within 24 hours of the guests arrival, with no sign of any problem according to Airbnb. Traversing their maze to customer service leads you to customer service reps that offer no sense of trust at all. It actually feels like their threatening if you cancel a reservation THEY WILL CHARGE YOU...and it's more than a guest pays for a day. So, what do you do? Continue to spend money and prepare for guests without any TRUST that Airbnb will forward the payment from the guest? Shared economy ONLY works when there is trust...AGREE?

Airbnb has completely useless availability information that ties up your money. - Home shows AVAILABLE for your dates - You pay through PayPal for a reservation - The owner notifies you the home isn't available - You're money is now tied up for 6-10 days while PayPal waits for your bank funds through ACH (even though they're deducted from your bank balance) before they show the refund on your PayPal balance. - Then, you need to initiate a transfer BACK to your back; another 3-5 business days. All of this because Airbnb doesn't have correct availability information!!!!

I booked an apartment for a family of three people and a baby. I was given a room with a double bed, on a flat shared!! I contacted airbnb and they replied automated messages! I paid in advance and no way they would give me any money back. I have now contacted my credit card company, I hope I get a refund for this RIP OFF!!!!!!

I booked an appartment in LA through airbnb. It was cancelled about a month before the trip. Annoying, but I found another place via airbnb (not least because they offer a tiny sum towards the next booking). That second place was cancelled less than a week before we arrived!!! This just shows that airbnb does not screen its hosts! Airbnb has a nice website, cashes a solid fee for a booking, asks you to pay the full sum right on booking.... but in my case delivered nothing but cancellations! STAY AWAY!! And the worst is: there is no possibility for me (or any other guest) to rate a host who has cancelled a reservation. Thus no way for me to check whether a potential future host is reliable or also prone to cancel reservations on (very) short notice! So obviously airbnb wants to make its hosts look better than they are... not quite what I would expect from a trustworthy company!

When I offered proof from the credit card company they weren't interested. When I asked to speak to a manager they said he would call and never did. The credit card company offered to do whatever necessary to satisfy Airbnb, but it appears Airbnb is of the opinion that they are special people and their clients are lowlife. Then I came to this site where it appears most people have found this company to be of trashy nature and realized my experience was widespread. Then I found out their charges might be excessive. I don't know for sure, but that is what I read in the reviews. Based upon the number of reviews it seems they don't care. I think as customers we should avoid companies of this nature and renters should as well. I found other accommodations and hope the renter will not be empty on the days I wanted to book. It would be a shame for both the renter and the rentee to both face such difficulties. I now wonder what Airbnb does with all that intrusive information. I would give no stars but Trust Pilot doesn't go as low as Airbnb Goodbye Airbnb.

I have hosted with airbnb some 30-35 bookings already, all of them without any problem. Also I have used airbnb as a guest some 4-5 times, and also everything went smooth. The problem of sites like Trustpilot here is that whoever made a bad experience would immediately report and post here, whereas the 99% happy guests or hosts would not report their good experience here. That makes somebody who has never used airbnb before scared to book after watching all the reviews here. Airbnb will pay the owners of advertised houses and apartments only 24 hours after succesful check-in and shows furthermore a hotline where eventual "surprises" upon check-in could be reported to. I find that this is more than enough time to ask airbnb to withhold the payment to the host. Overall I would say Airbnb is a perfect working booking-platform for vacation rentals and I can recommend to anybody to book there however only those hosts that have at least some 3-4 nice feedbacks.

We booked an apartment but decided to cancel our booking, which we thought was fine, since the cancellation was "flexible" ... this however means that you loose the fees charged by AirBnB, which was a steep 16% in our case. That means AirBnB cashes in twice here, once on the owners side and once on the visitors side ... which I guess is between 20 and 25% of the price. This is worse that booking.com (which have 12% on the hotel owner side) ... but my question is: What is the service you provide for this very steep fee. The unfortunate answer is: None.

I recently used AIRBNB for the first time. Host was very friendly and the place was clean, but I soon realized that while the host was pleasant, the very positive reviews for this place didn't mention some very key negatives. For instance, location was next to a major freeway and railroad tracks while windows had not been upgraded for noise reduction. Extremely noisy through the night. The curtains were white linen, with no shades to block out sunlight. There were eight bedrooms upstairs with one bathroom. Host did say they monitor this closely and rarely, if ever, book all the rooms. Fortunately, this was the case for me that night. I also discovered that AIRBNB charged me twice for a cleaning fee which the host said they would clear up with AIRBNB and credit my card. To date, while I have been billed for the original charge, I have yet to see a credit. Overall, a very underwhelming experience. I reccommed avoiding AIRBNB.

I been robbed on AIRBNB !!! 5760 EUR!!!! I do not trust them and cannot recommend them. Their validation procedure includes taking hold of your Facebook account - "managing your contact details" and looking at your metadata (read the small print), and thereby it seems that they hi-jack your login and password. The customer services team will not respond to questions about this.Some aspects of this 'snooping' are almost certainly not legal in the European Union. Other aspects of the validation process are disproportionate, even accepting the primary need for ensuring the security of hosts. AirBNB also seems to censor emails with hosts, by removing any web addresses, email addresses and possibly, phone numbers. When you get an acceptance for a booking - and before you confirm it - the full cost is charged to your credit card immediately. So, don't make too many tentative enquiries because you will find you run up a big bill. In all, this is a lousy system. Many of the hosts that I have spoken to find that AirBNB is greedy: they take commissions from both parties amounting to some 12% - or more - in total. The guest ultimately is paying for this. AirBNB is unresponsive and inefficient. The customer service staff are arrogant, and do not fully read emails. If it works for you, great, but it doesn't work for me - and the whole experience has been truly dreadful. ========================================== To illustrate the cavalier attitude of AirBNB Customer Support I am now attaching recent correspondence with them. RECENT EMAIL EXCHANGES WITH AIRBNB CUSTOMER SUPPORT 13 June 2015 - To Gloria at AirBNB who contacted me after the AirBNB website crashed multiple times during validation (although they did get my credit card details!!!!!) Alternative means of validation via Google were poorly explained. As part of that process I was informed that AirBNB would "manage my contacts" and also look into metadata, without any further explanation. This is totally unacceptable on two counts: firstly, there was no information what "manage my contacts" meant. Secondly, I cannot allow anyone to manage my account in such a way. Indeed, Google contacted me with a security alert! That sort of snooping is almost certainly illegal here in the EU. Alternative means of validation also asked for my Social Security Number. That simply cannot work in the UK, unless you have an arrangement with the British Government, which I very much doubt. On the whole, I found the experience deeply worrying and very, very unsatisfactory. It seems that your security procedures are disproportionate. Certainly the personal security of hosts is of high importance, but your procedures appear to me to be unfocussed. I really do not 'get' the idea that a host would like a profile and a that a video will aid my verification, but the host won't see it . . . it seems rather poorly explained, or possibly not really relevant. I might have taken a different view if the website had not frozen, but that has really soured the experience for me. It is very unlikely that I will use AirBNB in the future, or even recommend it to any of my family of friends. I am going to be away from home for several weeks but I do expect AN IMMEDIATE RESPONSE on this specific point. 7 July 2015 - To Gloria at AirBNB [Three weeks later!] Still waiting [for a reply to email of 14 June]. 9 July 2015 From AirBNB [A reply at last] Hello My name is Stan, I am a Verification Specialist with the Trust and Safety Team here at Airbnb. I hope this email finds you well. I am the case manager assigned to this matter. Furniture is bus station level. Cable tv has 1960's antenna and 3 stations but even these stations are broken with "snow." Texted host and she said she would take care if it. Small condo with no place to escape strobe light. Texted 2 hours later to host that light was still on but this time no answer. My family has booked 8 different AirBnb properties with no problems at all. I noticed some reviews on issues with cancellation and refund. That's not the case for me at all. Just this past month, I have to cancel my booking right away (Note: Not "Instant Booking") due to some changed plan. I was refunded immediately in that case as the host has not confirmed my booking yet. When another host declined my booking the other time, I got my money back as well. I had no issue with picking the right hosts as well but I had been super careful in picking my hosts and all of them have been good or excellent. Here's a few criteria I looked into this hosts: 1). Reviews - I read through a lot of them. The rating system doesn't tell you much. You can learn much more about the host's hospitality, etc by reading the written comments. Also, every guest has different standards, one's perceived excellence can be viewed as "hell" for another person. One can only find out from reading other's written reviews. Also, watch for frequent cancellation from the host. It may mean that can happen to you too. 2). Look for authentic pictures: having tricked by problematic pictures on pamphlets and websites of hotel/hostel/motels before, I have learned to be caution with pictures. Do they have a lot more pictures of the surrounding areas of the unit than the unit itself? Chances are they are doing that because their unit is really crappy. Are the pictures more like pictures of a model unit or stock pictures? Chances are they are pictures of model unit/stock pictures they use from other sites because their units are sub-par. Pictures on these units can look nice as hosts can hire professional photographers, but when things look too perfect, be really cautious. 3). The Types of Unit: I have the next experience staying with hosts who are renting out extra rooms or cabins on AirBnb. When it is setup that way, the hosts have less valuables and personal items around so we were less worried about breaking them or being framed for property damages. It also allows us to have a better boundary with the hosts: they were still availanle quite readily but yet we would still have our personal space. A unit sets up as timeshare or vacation unit is my second choice. Hosts usually separate their personal/valuable items a lot better. The boundary is setup a lot better in that way. The only downside is the hosts will not be as available. Personally, I found it least enjoyable to stay in units which are the host's actual home. The hosts usually just stayed at their friends'/family's home when we were visiting and would return to the unit later on. In all of these units, the hosts would have a lot of their personal and valuable items scattered in the unit. I found myself tiptoeing around the unit when I was there - worrying that I would break their stuff or be framed of breaking or taking their stuff. Don't get me wrong, the hosts for these units are still amazing and hospitable but I personally preferred better boundaries and space from the hosts. Since I am really big on boundaries and space, I always stayed away from rentals of sofa bed or beds on AirBnb so I can't really comment on that. I hope my review can help others who are considering the AirBnb service. In my humble opinion, it is only a good service if you know how to use it.

We have been hosting on Airbnb for three years now. During this time, we have had great guest and great reviews. We have also used the service as a guest and have never had a bad experience. We also usually avoid the property Mgt people with multiple listings. I like dealing with a owner that is available if I were to have a question or problem. Also, individual owners usually are very helpful about suggestions and directions. The reviews that I am seeing here do not reflect the majority of both host and guest experiences. To avoid problems, you must do your research. First, read the listing and the actual reviews. Reviews (within 14 days) are done by real Host & Guest before they are posted. If only one leaves a review, that is the one that will show up. At first, only go with listings that have reviews and are star rated. The reviews will usually tell you if the place is clean and other useful information. If you only go by price (cheap) and photos, then you have not done your research. Cheap price probably will end up being a disappointment, unless they have a good record. Regarding Photo's, you should look for 'verified photo's' which assures that the photo is accurate and not from a travel brochure. When you sign up, get a Verified ID, like Host are required to have. Host are usually renting their personal property and what to know who they are renting to, which is part of the trust & safety policy. The minimum ID requirements are: a photo of you, not your cat or dog, email, phone #, profile and offline ID, which can be a Driver's License or Passport. Only contact information is disclosed once the booking is make. If you skip any of these steps, then they may ask for additional information which may seem intrusive and frustrating. Also, asking to rent with only an email or little info about you may result in a decline. I rent to many first time users because they have completed the Verified ID, completed a profile and communicated with me their plans and who they are traveling with. Message the host and ask any questions that are not covered in the listing. Keep all conversations on the site message center, so there is a record. Make sure you read the host cancellation policy. A Host does not have the luxury of a Hotel in re-renting dates quickly and sometimes not at all, so be sure this is the right rental for you. When you check in, be sure to report any problems to Host immediately, and if they are not resolved, then contact Airbnb, and if the issues are serious, they will re-home you. Hundreds of new hosts are signing up every day, and there are bound to be some scammers. The company tries to stay on top of this and remove them when red flags appear, or they are reported. If you follow the above suggestions, you are more likely to have a positive experience. Happy travels!!

I've been a host on airbnb for almost 7 years, so I have had a front row seat in witnessing the growth of the business. It's been both exciting and frustrating. The fact of the matter is airbnb has been growing exponentially for the past 2-3 years and they do not have the resources (customer service personnel, proper testing of apps/tools before they're launched) to keep up with the demand. That's problem number one. The second problem is with this growth comes fraud. There are hosts who are shoddy and misrepresent themselves and their listings. There are guests who are fraudulent, who rent and trash rentals, who aren't who they say they are and use a property to operate an illegal business. The third problem is that all of the players (airbnb, hosts, guests) are new to the business. People are attracted at making extra money by renting their room but keep a filthy house or are oblivious to what innkeeping is, or they are a criminal renting out phantom properties. Guests looking to save money rent a place on airbnb and expect paying $50 for a bedroom in someone's house is going to be the same experience as paying for a room in a hotel. And airbnb is scrambling to keep up with the demand, trying to hire people with actual hospitality/hotel/guest service experience while operating a business that seems to double in size every six months. Hosts need to provide a detailed and accurate description of the property and provide lots of photographs. Guests need to read the entire description and photos to make an informed decision. There's nothing wrong with hosts vetting guests and guests checking out their hosts. It's called doing one's due diligence. And you always can decide not to book if you're a guests and hosts can always turn down a reservation. My opinion on how airbnb can improve? Put a foot on the brakes when it comes to growth. You don't need to spend any money on marketing and advertising. Focus on your current guests and hosts. Happy guests and hosts are the best marketing and brand ambassadors you can get. Improve your infrastructure when it comes to customer service, hire more people and don't give frustrated people who call the party line. Help them fix their problems.

We have been great fans of Airbnb since our first guest experiences in 2011. We have used airbnb in many places across several countries: Australia, Italy, France, Germany, Ireland and here in the UK to name a few, and without exception we have been delighted with our Airbnb homes and our hosts. Crucial to this working is establishing good communications with where your prospective hosts, READING the details about a property, and making sure you have a realistic expectation. If you pay 15 pounds for a room, you cannot expect it will be the same as what you might get for 90 pounds for maybe a whole apartment. We now host ourselves and have very happy guests, some returners who love our space, and we pride ourselves on our five-star reviews. Your Airbnb experience will be only as good as the individual properties - and their owners - so you need to put in the time to find that space within your budget AND that gives you what you want and hope for. With that effort you can spend around the same as a hotel room - but get so much more (but with different expectations on you as a guest). I Have recommended Airbnb to many family and friends who now also enjoy richer experience of independent travel at prices they can afford. I recommend the service to you - but remember not all properties are equal!

I recently spent two weeks traveling through Japan. My accommodations included hotels, ryokans (traditional Japanese Inns) and a machiya (a traditional urban house) in Kyoto that I rented through Airbnb (title: Gagakuan traditional & modern Machiya, owned by a host named Mako). This was my first time using Airbnb and I had high hopes for a positive experience. However, my experience was, I'm sorry to say, not good. Here's why I won't use Airbnb's services again: 1. Airbnb charges too much. Before you click to charge your card, check their fee. It is, in my opinion, too high (and I believe Airbnb also charges the host a rather high fee). This company seems to be making a lot of money per transaction. That's good for Airbnb (check out images of their nice offices in San Francisco) and its investors, but not so good for its customers, I would suggest. 2. Airbnb allows hosts to have harsh cancellation policies. In the case of this Airbnb machiya, if I had to cancel for any reason, even long before my arrival date, I would forfeit 50% of the total charge for my stay (in my case, about $800). Compare that to the hotel and ryokan booking services which typically have much more flexible cancellation policies. While I can appreciate the need to protect the host from last-minute cancellations, the prospective guest should be able to cancel well in advance of the intended arrival date without having to pay a substantial cancellation fee. Airbnb should require hosts to conform to a consistent and fair cancellation policy. 3. Airbnb purposely makes it hard to contact them for help. Take a look at their site and see if you can find a customer service phone number. Go ahead. Take a look. You won't, because as of this writing there isn't one listed. It's even hard to find an email address without having to dig deep into their circular menus. The only way that I know to get their phone number is to receive an email from Airbnb after you email them and wait for them to email you back. Their site is not customer-friendly. 4. If you do finally get through to an Airbnb customer service rep on the phone (which I did after spending too much time digging through their circular menus and having their phone number finally emailed to me) be prepared to have them hang up on you. Twice. This was my experience. Though I consider myself a professional (senior executive and corporate officer) I was twice hung up on by two different Airbnb customer service reps. In my many decades on this planet, and many hours spent speaking to an untold number of customer service reps of various companies over the years (an experience we can all share) this is the first time I can remember ever being hung up on by a customer service rep, and I had it happen with Airbnb. Twice. I wasn't screaming or swearing or calling anyone names or getting personal in any way. I was just voicing my concerns and frustrations with their service and policies. Everything I communicated was done so in an even tone. I was so shocked on being hung up on the first time that I assumed it was an aberration with that one person. I was sure it wouldn't happen again. It did. Two different reps, same result. I guess Airbnb doesn't like constructive criticism. 5. Airbnb has a much-too-rigid review policy. You are given a strict two week window to submit a review. If you miss it by a day, you're out of luck. Period. They will not budge. Even though I took notes during my stay, wrote my review over a couple of weeks upon my return (I had to squeeze in the writing between many other many obligations that had piled up while I was gone) and really wanted to submit the review so as to help other prospective guests make a good choice based upon accurate information. My motivation was primarily driven by my having found the information about the machiya on the Airbnb site to not be accurate and/or complete when I was making my initial decisions on where to rent in Kyoto. Important information was missing. For example, one major issue with this Airbnb machiya is that it has some cross beams that are at about 5'8" in height. I'm talking about the beams that are part of the ceiling/roof support system (American homes have cross beams that are typically eight feet or higher). As such, if you're about 5'8" or above you have to bend over or you're going to bump your head in this machiya. If you're over six feet tall, like me, you will invariably bump you head and, in my case, draw blood a couple of times. After a couple of days I found myself walking hunched over all of the time. The height of the beams is not listed on the Airbnb site. I was going to share this important information, along with other important information, in my review, but when I tried to submit it on the 15th day after my return, one day after their deadline, I was told no. I had missed my window. When I asked why there was such a short window I was told that it was primarily to ensure that the experience was still fresh in a guest's mind when writing a review. When I assured each customer service rep that the experience was indeed still fresh in my mind, I was told no, the policy is set in stone. When I told each customer service rep about the dangerously low beams, that it was very important to get the information out to others and that I couldn't believe Airbnb didn't have an effective policy or process by which to do this after the end of two weeks, I was told no, that the policy is set in stone. Nothing could be done. Period. Then they hung up on me. Not good. It makes me wonder if a) Airbnb customer service reps don't feel empowered to escalate viable concerns to management, so they just give up by hanging up on customers, b) a number of employees are just biding their time, not really caring about customers, until the company has an IPO and many of them become twenty-something millionaires and move on, and c) a large number of important reviews are not being posted on the Airbnb site. Each time I was hung up on I was sent the following automated email: Thanks for reaching out and submitting your feedback. We're collecting every bit of advice that we can, and we greatly appreciate your input. If we have any questions about your suggestions, we'll be sure to follow up with you. If you have a specific question, please contact our Customer Experience team at [link deleted]. Best wishes, Airbnb I wanted to email back: "But I did contact your Customer Experience team, and they hung up on me. Twice." But I didn't since it was automated email, the kind sent by a company that would like nothing more than to automate every component of their service process so that they can maximize profits for the company and its investors, rather than provide true customer service to its customers. Contrast the above with my experience with various hotel booking services, such as [external references], all accessed through [external reference], which included lots of helpful reviews to help me make an effective choice (hmmm, for some reason their review policies don't seem to be as strict as Airbnb's - I guess their customers are able to remember things beyond fourteen days), flexible cancellation policies and, typically, easier-to-find contact information (I even called a customer service rep of one of the hotel booking services via the phone number clearly listed on their site and we had a helpful conversation - and she didn't even hang up on me). My experience with each of these services was efficient, pleasant and positive. My experience with Airbnb was, from beginning to end, frustrating and unpleasant. I will not use Airbnb again. There are better options out there. Mark M

I have been a Real Estate investor/landlord/agent for 40 yrs. I was contacted by Airbnb who found me on a free nationwide online website 6 yrs. ago when they were just a starting out, asking if they could list my rentals on their new website. I agreed. I was a loyal airbnb host for 6 yrs. I took total strangers from all over the world into my private L.A. & L.V. rentals & accepted 1st time guests from all over the world who had no host reviews. I took their pets. I did this because Airbnb offered me a false sense of security, by holding guests security deposits and offering a host guarantee insurance policy which is currently $1,000,000.00. Yes, a million dollars! Lets talk about the "Bad" guests. They ranged from irresponsible nuisances to shrewd con artists. There were the ones who broke or stole a few minor items, the ones who violated our common sense/common courtesy rules, or the ones who required "special services" but didn't want to pay for them after. The worst guests included necessary police intervention or major theft caught on CCTV cameras. There was the group of "squatters." They were wolves in sheep's clothing who came to me as short term vacation rental guests. Visualize "The Beverly Hillbillies" in a pickup truck with their dogs. They came off sweet as pie (landlord 101: beware of overly nice prospective tenants. No one is that nice! They are usually desperate people with bad credit, no job, who can't get anyone else to rent to them!) He even took on the job as handyman around the apt. bldg. They were able to drag out their stay, doling out breadcrumbs by paying a few days at a time. When it came time for them to check out, these predators who apparently support themselves by "working the system" refused to vacate the premises screaming "permanent tenant rights" in the grand scheme of things to con me out of $13,500 in re-location fees and to be able to extend their stay for one more year under the cities rent control laws!!! As if this wasn't bad enough, I also got sued by the city who extorted me for nearly $16,000 in perceived TOT fees, which ended up costing me nearly $5000 in attys fees (who took my money and resigned from the case after doing nothing) before I ended up having to pay the city nearly $10,000 in fines. THIS IS WHAT BEING AN AIRBNB HOST COST ME. And what support did I get from airbnb? Now lets talk about airbnb. They come off syrupy sweet, calling you an "awesome Superhost." They act like airbnb is all about "sharing space" and "making friends." If I were looking for friendship, I'd join a social club. Lets get one thing straight. It's renting out space. Real estate. Real estate is a business. Bottom line, you are in business to make money. AIrbnb is in business to make money. They take it from both ends- their hosts and their guests. They block out parts of hosts and guests email correspondence if they suspect it includes sharing contact information. Don't let them kid you. They expect hosts and guests to trust them with total stranger connections, lodging, and finances, but they do not trust their own hosts or guests to be able to communicate with one another in fear they will get cut out of the deal. As airbnb & their # of hosts grew during the past few years (as did their negative reviews which began popping up all over on various websites) due to their mass marketing campaign, they appeared to care less and less about their hosts and guests. The 1st big scandal I read about was the host in California whose home was totally trashed by airbnb guests. That's when airbnb came up with their "$50,000.00 host guarantee policy" to provide panicked hosts a false sense of security. Most recently was the home in Canada that was totally trashed by airbnb guests. Airbnb upped the ante to $1,000,000.00. To be eligible for that type of host coverage, I suspect the entire family would need to be brutally murdered. I am a professional, honest, trustworthy, "to the book" type host. I never once went behind Airbnb's back to try to cut them out of their original booking commission because I believe in karma and I believe everyone is entitled to their fair share of what they contributed. Also, never once did one of my guests ever make a theft claim while staying in our rental units. That speaks volumes for my honesty and integrity. Many guests don't realize that when they book through airbnb, all payment is handled directly by airbnb. They never allow the host to be in possession of the security deposit. So when a guest commits damage, theft, violations of rules or requires special services, I exercised my host rights and filed a claim with airbnb under the guest's security deposit. To avoid having to process claims, airbnb will attempt to discourage hosts by running you through the hoops. Think boot camp! 1st you have to go through the "Resolution request" (asking your guest to pay you.) This link is nearly impossible to find on their site. Once you have found it, filled out the form, and sent it to your guest, the guest will usually deny the damage/theft, etc., get angry that you "accused them," refuse to pay, then leave you a false negative retaliatory review. If you don't hear back from the guest or they deny the claim, you have to mark your calendar to remember to contact airbnb to "get involved." (if you forget, you are out of luck on the claim as the deadline has expired.) In order to involve airbnb, they will require photos, witnesses, original receipts, and/or comps. As a real estate investor with multiple fully furnished properties in 3 locations in 3 states, I would have hire someone to pull dead files out of storage and spend days going through thousands of receipts through the years to find one for a towel, mug, pillow or whatever for the damaged or missing item(s) in question! Once you have completed the form & provided the "evidence" (they do not trust their hosts word, despite the fact the host trusted them to have these strangers in their home who broke/stole their personal property items!) you wait to hear back from airbnb. None of my claims were what I would consider "substantial" amounts of money. Some claims were processed, but as time went on they were either denied, reduced, or ignored. When a guest flooded my unit, I filed a claim for $2,500.00 for my out of pocket costs. This was my and only claim that came under the $1,000,000.00 Host guarantee policy. After I went through airbnb's claim "boot camp" process, they said they were only willing to pay $500 firm (20% of my claim,) Final decision, no appeal. Shortly thereafter, with no warning they deleted all of my listings and cancelled all of my bookings for the rest of the year. They told my future guests that it was I who had cancelled their bookings, so I had angry guests contacting me not realizing the truth, that airbnb had lied to them and that I was as much an airbnb victim as they were! I still have approx. 1/2 dozen minimal claims airbnb ignored and never paid over the past year, along with the one and only claim I filed in 6 yrs. under the $1,000,000.00 Host guarantee claim for $2,500.00 that I was never compensated for.
