We have used AirBnB on numerous occasions, in a variety of countries and have always had a positive experience. When we've had to speak to AirBnB we have found them to be very helpful and friendly, dealing with our queries quickly and efficiently. We have been lucky to have some amazing hosts and stayed in some fantastic properties. We try to use AirBnB for every trip and we recommend them to all our friends.

The Airbnb technology is great, but there are some major potential "gotchas" to be aware of. We recently made plans to visit the San Francisco area and booked a townhouse via Airbnb. However, before our trip, the reservation was cancelled because the Home Owners Association (HOA) for the townhouse found out the owner was taking Airbnb reservations and forced him to stop. Basically, almost any property listed on Airbnb that is a condo, townhouse, or single family home in an HOA is at risk of being cancelled if the HOA finds out. I have never heard of an HOA being open to short term rentals like Airbnb provides. Additionally, anyone trying to sub-lease their apartment on Airbnb or similar site is likely violating their lease (I don't think may landlords would want their tenants taking Airbnb reservations on a rental apartment).

What a load of rubbish, tried to book some apartments in London, in the area where we were looking there were quite a few available so sent a request for 1, which came back cancelled due to none availability. Sent another request for somewhere else, came back cancelled due to none availability. Found one that said 'instant booking' so we went with that only for the host to cancel saying not available. Finally made an enquiry on the 4th apartment only to be told that too is not available!!! Whats the post in advertising apartments that arent available... also each time you do a 'request to book' the funds are taken from your account so we had 3 lots of money taken from our account which actually put us over our overdraft but fortunately had money elsewhere to transfer back into that account... and now were waiting for the money to be returned to us. Airbnb dont even deserve 1 star!!!

I have been with them for 6 months, and not ONCE have I had a single issue or anything but the best experience with AirBnB or with the guests they have send. However, having said that, I could understand some of the issues that have been posted here, but the reasons why and how are what is important. First, I am a host that says and delivers exactly (if not more) than what I say on AirBnB. In fact, I never pre-aprove any Inquiry until I write anyone interested in my place and answer ANY questions they may have, BEFORE they book, to make sure the place IS what they are looking for. Only after the potential guest is totally satisfied and comfortable, would I 'Accept' their request and for ONLY the dates they intent to want to stay. I understand fully how AirBnB ~can't~ totally guarantee that the potential host is a flake or an outright hustler, nor for them to guarantee the guest is also a whining flake. I do look up the guest reviews - always. Before able to join them, they were very careful before accepting me, now I see why. There are a lot of unscrupulous people out there hustling to make a dollar without any form of integrity. The same could be said about guests who do not take any responsibility to make sure what they are booking is what they want. READ THE REVIEWS on hosts people, and yes I could see that sometimes glowing reviews can be 'created' by hosts via their friends that are nothing but fraudulent. This is not an easy system to pull off, you are dealing with two entities (hosts and guests) that may range from superb individuals to low-life scamers. IF a guests is not satisfied with my place, the day that ever comes up, I will refund their money immediately (if already paid by AirBnB) and move on. End of story. It is no one's fault, it is life. Then no one could complain. This is a fabulous service and a fortunate opportunity for REAL entities to get started, before building their own repeating clientele. And I consider AirBnB the best of the big three, by far: Air BnB, VRBO and a distance third Flip Key. Good luck all.

I offered a room for a week starting from Monday, since I was invited to the interview on Tuesday. A day before my arrival, I contacted a host to let him know then I arrive around 10 p.m., but host replied that he is not able to let me in until 12 p.m., so I should wait outside for him and if I am not happy with it, my booking can be cancelled, what he had done later that day. As a consequence my trip was ruined, I lost my flight ticket, and of course a change to get a job.

airbnb threatening a host if they do not accept in a given time. but where in gods name is the accept button, certainly not within the same frame as the threat. give these people(airbnb) a big miss if your going to threaten your clients(hosts) with punitive sanctions your business model will go down the pan very quickly.

I've used airbnb a few times in the past with no trouble, however my latest booking experience wasn't great. I was trying to book a weekend in Berlin, the first apartment was apparently available for the weekend I'd chosen however it was rejected with no explanation within a couple of minutes of the request. My profile has two good reviews so I was a little confused. The next three bookings I tried to make were simply never responded to and after 24 hours the request expires. The next booking was rejected, the host did actually write to me to say that the apartment wasn't free, though it did show as available on the website. So on the 6th attempt at booking my credit card was declined - my credit card company had suspected fraud as so many payments were sent to and returned from airbnb within such a short space of time. I finally managed to book an apartment with an immediate booking confirmation. I think that airbnb is a great idea, however hosts seem to be unreliable and unchecked by airbnb - surely if the website is showing that the apartment is free then it should be! Also I think that if hosts simply do not respond to requests then that should be shown on their profile. I also think that payment should only be taken when the host has accepted the booking - otherwise credit card companies get worried and stop cards. All in all a fairly stressful, unpleasant experience and I will certainly look for othera ways of booking accommodation in the future

I'm an airbnb host. My experience with the guests has been great, a totally different experience from vrbo guests. However I'm prompted to leave a negative review as it's the third time I encounter poor customer support. The first time a problem arose (as a guest) was when I tried to use a $30 coupon I received from airbnb. Their system did not accept it and I was afraid of losing the booking so I proceeded with the payment thinking they will apply it and refund the $30. They didn't, according to their policy once a reservation is made you cannot apply any kind of coupon code. It's understandable if it's the client's fault but it was their glitch. The worst was that they refused to refund the booking fees. This escalated to a supervisor who reviewed it and responded with a very nice and apologetic letter and I was refunded the booking fees. I wrote this off as a negative incident overlooked by all the positive benefits. Now, I have a similar situation but on behalf of my guest. I received a private inquiry and I directed them to book through airbnb and to off set their booking fees I offered them a $25 coupon that we have access too. They never received the coupon but proceeded with the reservation. It was embarrassing for me and I promised to contact airbnb on their behalf. I spoke with a Senior Case Manager in the Trip Experience team and she advised there is nothing they can do after the trip was booked. Once again, due to their glitch in their system the coupon didn't apply and she refused any further help. Indeed she suggested I offer my guests a $25 off. She was borderline rude. These are guests that came directly to me, I get 3% less to cover the airbnb credit card fee, and I should offer them a discount?? Maybe only I see this as an absurdity? Then I found out it happened to my other guests as well that I referred to airbndb. Additionally I have referred 2 other families to book through airbnb instead of going directly. I thought the benefits out way the 3% fees but instead I receive less rental fee and I lost face. The Senior Case Manager's reply when I asked why should I ever recommend another private guest to book through them instead of going directly? "Because it's a good company". Is it?? You get less rental and lose face. I had to follow up with the guests, it was embarrassing. Next time I will do all of my private reservations directly and I will not recommend the company again. If they write their own policy their must be able to overwrite the exceptions when mistakes result from their own mistakes.

They are very very rude. If there is any problem, they will use all evidence (emails, messages) to make you think you are stupid yourself. They think there is absolutely nothing wrong with their service. I talked to one gentleman and NEVER want to talk to them again, EVER.

I opened an account with air bnb and never used it, then on the one occasion I tried to use it they blocked me and I had to email several times to find out a week later when they FINALLY replied why, then to be told I had 'violeted' the terms and conditions and they don't need to explain why, still have absolutely no idea what's happened as I have never used the site, the whole thing left me confused and annoyed. really wouldn't recommend this site to anyone

My husband reserved an apt. at Calle 75 1/2 Este Panama, Panama. 1. It took 3 taxi drivers to locate the unit. 2. We arrived at 2am Thursday 5/07/2015 and left before 3pm.....why? Because my husband received an email from Claudia that "Just to let you know, there are additional guests arriving at 11:30pm." We were NEVER informed we would be sharing a 2 bdroom with COMPLETE STRANGERS! The unit was OK...nothing special, and definitely not cleaned. We didn't mind the lack of cleanliness, as everyone has a different standard of "clean". What we did mind was the deceptive behavior of the host. I attempted to contact Claudia with no success. Her phone does not have voicemail. She never attempted to contact us, so I am fairly certain she knows why we were calling. I assume their friends are writing reviews or others scheduled 1 day stays, so they never encountered the "shared apartment" issue. We will NEVER use airbnb again! We will stick to hotels! Good thought, but too many untrustworthy people.

On a 57 day trip in Europe I planned to use Airbnb extensively but have now discovered them to be ruthless when it comes to refunding money taken without authorization on the flimsiest excuses directly from my credit card. I have tried to contact them with no success and can't find a phone number or email. That can't be an accident. Are these guys simply crooks or do they have a business plan based on screwing their customers? Never again!!!

I booked a room via Airbnb for 3 nights at 16 Fairfield Road, BS6 5JP in Bristol, UK. Olivia is the host. I checked out on 1st May at 11 am. I asked Olivia if I can leave my luggage in her flat and pick it up in the evening. She said this is OK. I returned at 7pm in the same day, picked up my luggage and left her the key. No issues at all were raised by the host. Two days later, on 3rd May and after I had left her a positive online review in the previous night, she emailed me complaining she found a stain in the duvet. She said she didn’t see a stain when she made the bed after I checked out and that she only noticed it two days later. She took a picture then, 2 days after my departure, and said this is the evidence! She claimed £60 ($90). I replied her I have not left any stain and that it was her responsibility to report anything on the day of my departure. Airbnb charged my card without asking my view!! This is against their own terms & conditions. Airbnb policy says they also ask the guest and wait for a response for 48h. I never authorized a card payment, neither Airbnb consulted me. They also haven’t provided me with the photos. I have emailed Airbnb many times asking for the photos and why they breached their terms & conditions. They don’t reply me. Airbnb steals guests money, don’t value their opinion and provide no safety net at all. I will never use Airbnb again. Anyone wanting more details, please contact me via Twitter: @Ilias_Energia

Sellers often advertise rates only to find out that they are really higher once the reservation is requested. This is a bait and switch in my book. Unfortunately, AirBNB is no help at all. This is infact acceptable in their book. There's no accountability for hosts or protections for renters. Save yourself the headache and book a hotel. At least they honor advertised rates.

Used the service several times, liked it overall. But all the pros are for my hosts, not the airbnb personally. I was the lucky one to get the wonderful hosts. A couple of times the apartment was not like on the photos - smaller and dirtier, but I never complained, as it is the same as with the hotels - they look great on the photos and then you find out the truth. Neverhteless, it was never terrible. But they created the good service, anyway, great idea of sharing. Also I had some issued with hosts accepting my requests - sometimes it is very hard to get the approval - you have to write 10 different hosts. So it is better not to pay immediately but contact the host first by the message.

There is a clear cancellation policy on my terms and conditions and if guests cancells 7 days prior to there reservation and they didnt give me any payout for the same as i got last minute booking. This is not done as airbnb will never pay me when i am loosing on prime dates but still its rare experience everything else is amazing on this website

My husband and I love airbnb. As hosts we know to do our part. We make sure our casita is perfectly clean; sheets and pillow cases ironed, windows and blinds clean as well as everything else. To be a successful host, you need to know what people want. For sure, a comfortable bed is vital. Also, information about where to go, what's in walking distance and don't forget snacks, large amount of water bottles and our guests favorite alcoholic beverages. Since hosting, we have made extra money and new friends. It's been the easiest money I've ever made, and what's more, it's been fun. I wouldn't list with anyone else.

AirBnb is trying to do something very interesting. What they are trying to do is actually rather difficult to do. So if they were a sensible outfit they might just make it work, but it would be difficult. As it is I find this company so deeply obnoxious that I cannot imagine it will survive (except perhaps by the good graces of its customers). I have used them a few times. All the places I stayed in had very strong reviews. The bathroom was never clean. One host was a little sad but doing her best. Two were ok. Two were excellent. All in all I don't think I have done badly. There were signs of promise. All the reviews I received were very kind (which is, after all, always nice). I was able to leave some pretty strong reviews too (friendly, thoughtful people certainly compensate for dirty bathrooms :) Despite an enormous time expenditure to organise these stays I probably would have given AirBnb a try every now and then in the future all things being equal. But AirBnB seems intent on making life more and more difficult, not easier, and that is the nub of the problem. When you book they take the money straight away (but don't give it to the host until after you start to stay). That's not a hold, they actually take the money. Free interest is fun, no doubt. Even if you cancel within the time allowed, they keep their substantial booking fee (Booking.com does not, for example, do that). They force currency exchanges to occur within their system, accreting further quiet but material fees to themselves (Booking.com does not do that either). Basically every little thing is set up not to help customers but so this corporation can gain some little advantage here, some there. When one tries to communicate through their system, they censor the messages. Whether or not hosts wanted it, AirBnb kept threatening to make me send over an electronic copy of my passport or driver's licence which they wanted to keep on their system (sending something like this to a commercial enterprise to store on its servers is, of course, crazy). They also tried to make me give them access to my Google drive account (yes, I'm not joking) and to manage my contacts (perhaps they would like to add in some new people and see if I can spot the difference?) When I said what they were asking was inappropriate, and despite the fact that the host I was trying to book with at the time wanted me to stay (we had been able to vet each other's identity to our mutual satisfaction), they attempted to stand in our way. They were not interested in conducting a reasoned discussion but rather intimated that I was "leaving their community" (like not using them was akin to being exiled or some such nonsense). They come across as a weird, manipulative, even odious, operation. Lots of other people have similar concerns. The web offers many interesting newspaper articles and blog posts on AirBnb, in addition to all that is written on this website. If you do use them, do it on your own terms, and go in fully prepared to have a struggle with - what I found to be - a bizarre, faceless behemoth.

I put my house on AirBnB. One of the first bookings I had was for a family of 4 visiting to have a quiet weekend. I was not able to meet the guest when he checked in and left a key. This person threw a massive college keg party/crawfish broil for 100+ guests according to neighbors. There was close to $2000 worth of damage from a $700 booking. I opened a case with Airbnb's resolution center, submitted the invoices and was reimbursed $300 out of the $1000 security deposit. I have been trying to call Airbnb and speak to a supervisor for over a week and cannot get anyone to return my call.

I've used Airbnb for some time as a host and as a guest. If you choose your guests well, you shouldn't have any trouble at all and it's generally been a great experience. Only once have I chosen a bad guest, and it just proved one should always act on one's instinct. I accepted a last minute booking as the I was due to be away on the dates requested by the guests. As I was about to take off from the airport, the guest called and said that he wished to check out early, and didn't want to pay for the rest of his stay. Under Airbnb's rules, I was entitled to keep a percentage of the guest's payment (on terms the guest had agreed to) however the guest became very threatening over the phone, and it was at this point I called on Airbnb to assist. In all honesty, they were not helpful, offered little advice and I was left to pay out the guest who was in my home for fear of him ruining the place. The next time I had cause to get in touch was via email (only an international phone number seemed to be available on the UK site) was when a payment wasn't paid out. I emailed in to ask where my money was, and heard nothing back. I emailed again, got nothing back. My payment was finally sent 6 days after check-in, as opposed to the 1 day, and to this day I've received no reply to my emails and no explanation as to the delay. Despite the above points, I've still given 4 stars as these experiences have been the minority. Just be careful with your choice of host / guest, find out as much as possible before agreeing to anything, and you should have an amazing experience.

I had experience with this website both as a host and as a guest. First I booked an apartment in Italy for my vacation: the host claimed it was right on the beach. It turned out that the apartment was 10 min drive away. Airbnb didn't take any responsibility for not verifying the listing address, and I never got my booking fee back. Second negative experience I had as a host: a guest left my apartment without even telling me, and then filed with airbnb extenuating circumstances. It appears that any guest can leave like that and then file for a refund, claiming an emergency, and then get 50% of the remaining nights back. This is just plain wrong policy, catastrophic for any small business homeowner, and encouraging fraud. I will be removing my listing from airbnb and won't recommend it to future guests and hosts. Airbnb collects far greater fees than vrbo/homeaway, but it doesn't bother to verify listings, management or ownership documents, the actual address, which leads to many host cancellations.

We booked a place and the host cancelled last minute. Everywhere else is booked and we are left with expensive flights and no place to sleep. It's impossible to get through to anyone at Airbnb that is actually authorised to do anything. Would never use again - not worth the stress.

Traveling back east this summer for my son's wedding. airbnb was suggested for a reasonable price. They are the most intrusive company I've ever dealt with wanted all kinds of personal information and access to my facebook, linkedin, etc. Are you sure this isn't a branch of homeland security? Just read my emails and check my phone calls please! I'd feel less violated.

We booked a small house for a family vacation. Once the reservation was confirmed by the host and she sent us all the info about the house, we booked our flight. The next day our reservation was cancelled by the host with no explanation, just a generic email from Airbnb. Now we have to wait a week or two to get our money back, which we need to make alternative accommodations. We'll never use them again, very unreliable service. Save yourself a giant headache and book a hotel...
Poor customer service. I had ants in my apartment and they would not give me a refund for the apartment. I lost $1000.

We had a terrible experience with Flipkey and decided to switch to Airbnb. So happy we did - so far.... My advice with Airbnb is 1) look at the host - do they look like they understand hospitality? 2) Problems - contact them immediately. They don't pay the host until you arrive so if you don't complain early than you are sunk.

I booked and paid in full for Paris Apartment which was offered at a discount. The host did not appear, and Airbnb said their site was hacked and I lost all my 1000Euros. There is still hacking and scamming on their site and they are not interested in fixing the problem for the innocent guests. Airbnb deleted my messages, blamed the hackers and then over 10 days of my trying to contact them they said CASE CLOSED. They never responded to my calls or my emails for over 3 hours when I was stranded with my daughter. Please stay on my link as I have more to report to you tomorrow as I need to get police protection on this one Collossal scam!!! My advice - avoid Airbnb, book through booking.com or hotels.com for safety, finance and cleaning fees - if you do indeed find you have somewhere to stay through them.

This company is bad news- they have such problems with their mobile app responses (which they freely admit but won't shut down the app) that my response rate has been reduced to just 20% despite replying to every inquiry I recieved! Their customer services have currently taken six weeks to "look into it" via email only as they won't discuss it on the phone and won't believe my side of it as their system is telling them otherwise. As a result I am right near the bottom of the search list due to the 20% they've applied to my account and obviously I have no inquiries for my Hong Kong apartment. This is appalling and they need to face facts and fix it-do not use the mobile app if you are on the move to reply to inquiries as it doesn't work and also don't bother them at customer services as basically they won't be able to do anything (although they'll be terribly polite about it) as they are too busy with the myriad of other complaints they receive and do nothing about! What a shame - a company like this which is so popular and profitable really shouldn't be able to get away with treating hosts so unfairly and creating unfair response rates like this!

I've both hosted and been a guest on Airbnb, and provided that both parties have decent intentions, it's a fine service. However, I traveled internationally recently, and my host tried to downgrade me between properties twice--once a couple months out from my stay (claiming the original property had been closed by the landlord due to an unexplained "incident" caused by a guest), and again less than a week out. I complained to Airbnb, and their customer service team cancelled the reservation and granted me a full refund. Luckily, after the first switch, which struck me as suspicious, I made a backup reservation at a hotel, which was cancelable until the day before. Had I not thought to do this (as I highly recommend all travelers do--check those no-fee hotel cancellation dates carefully, though!), I would've been out hundreds trying to book rooms at a hotel for me and my travel companions at the last minute, as Airbnb offered me only $60 extra in credit for the host cancellation. I understand that Airbnb doesn't want to alienate hosts, as they make money off of them, but there needs to be either a per-incident fine or three-strike policy for incidents like this, where hosts cancel on their guests or don't provide lodgings at the original property reserved. The guy who I rented from (Nori, in Tokyo) runs tons of apartments through the site and is basically operating as an Airbnb slumlord. This is a host with 150+ glowing reviews who totally screwed us over. Had my previous experiences with Airbnb not been positive, I wouldn't be inclined to go through them again.

I booked an apartment in Jerusalem on Airbnb 6 months in advance. On arrival I found the apartment misrepresented and dirty, stained mattress, sheets, blanket and pillows. Place smelled musty, moldy, dusty and there was evidence of bed bugs on mattress. Window broken and front door of building difficult to open with key. I did not stay and Airbnb gave me almost a full refund, except for $70.00 Canadian. I see that the listing for this apartment is still on their website. These problems can't be seen in the photographs they show. Airbnb gave me a $140 coupon to use on next booking. I requested my $70 instead of the $140 coupon and they refused. For this reason I would not book again with them. My trip was partially ruined because I had to scramble to find last minute accommodation which was frustrating, wasted time on my trip, and cost me more than I had budgeted for. I book an apartment at least once a year and Airbnb will not get my future business because they withheld $70 which is a miniscule amount of money for them, but not for me. This small refund was all that they had to do to restore my faith in using them again.

I actually had a good experience with the flat and the host I rented from and wanted to write a positive review about it. But when I got back from vacation I had a ton of backed up work so it took me over 2 weeks to get around to clicking on the "write a review" button on my email from Airbnb. And when I clicked on it I got a message saying "you can't modify this comment". So I'm like what? I didn't make a comment... that's what I want to do. So after investigating I see there policy of 14 days to write a review, which I think is stupid, but even more stupid is that I didn't get that explanation instead of "you can't modify this comment". So I want to send an email expressing my displeasure, but seems that is either impossible or incredibly hidden. And no phone number either... So what started out as a desire to share a good experience has turned into a bad experience.

I used Airbnb twice now for weekly business trips. Both hosts were very polite and accommodating. Rooms exceeded my expectations. Never a problem with payment. I will definitely use Airbnb again for future travels and recommend to my friends and family

I have been using Airbnb for years now. All over Europe, also in South America, China and now in Fes ( Morocco). Always been pleased with the company services. Even in China, where we had a very unpleasant experience and Airbnb returned the money. Last week I produced a report on our Fes accommodation, a lovely well presented place , arranged with great gusto, a host with a superb way of communication, but with a very low standard kitchen facilities and safety . Safety must be a paramount affair any host must consider. For that I gave three stars to the place in relation to amenities. Otherwise highly recommended. As Airbnb has not as yet published this review, I lost some confidence on Airbnb. Although, it does not matter to me Fes accommodation any more; it will matter a lot the reviews I want to rely on.

I booked a flat in Discovery Bay, Hong Kong. Reservation was accepted and paid for in full. Less than 2 weeks before the trip the booking was cancelled without any explanation. I will not use airbnb again.

It seems that we only ever hear how wonderful this site is for cheap accommodation, however my opinion of them has just plummeted big time! I recently tried to book a place in New York but the request was refused. Airbnb nevertheless charged my credit card for the FULL AMOUNT of the stay (a charge of more than $2000.00) and is not going to return it for a full 7 days! The only way to contact them is by email and they have responded saying that the bank is holding the money. When I verified this with my bank, I was told that it was Airbnb who were withholding the funds. What kind of scam is this from a company who aspires to be honest and trustworthy? "Don't stay at a hotel. Airbnb is a global network of accommodations (sic) offered by locals". It's a much easier way of getting scammed! And just try contacting them to get your money back! Good luck with that one!!!

Terrible! I submitted request for booking, they charged my card for entire stay over 90 days before the reservation. Owner contacted me via text for discussion about appropriateness of the rental. I quickly determined it was not going to work then during discussion I get an email saying rental confirmed. I send another text saying NO, I just cancelled. Then I immediately get a receipt that my card was charged. They claim they can only refund 50% on a reservation that should never have been made! Their final decision was to charge me $50 for the inconvenience of a reservation cancelled within 5 minutes that never should have been made in the first place. Forget poor business practices, this company lacks common decency

FIRST: DO NOT STAY WITH DE LONTA IN LOS ANGELES!! HIS BOOKING IS LISTED AS "PRIVATE ROOM, SAFE, COMFORTABLE IN HOLLYWOOD" I booked his flat for a night, not only did he give me a FAKE ADDRESS, he simply stopped communicating with me the day of the booking. I tried for 8 hours to reach him and to get AirBnB to straighten out this problem. Now he is STILL LISTING HIS FLAT. AirBnB says that they "are working with him". How is that the right thing to do? I don't think someone who gives a false address and then disappears should be allowed to continue to profit from AirBnB business, do you? How many other travelers will have the same problem I did? SECOND: AirBnB should have a plan in place to make sure their hosts are reliable, and honest and "safe"! All I got was a refund and they think I should be happy about that. My trip was completely ruined. Too bad, it's a great idea but not backed up by a very good business plan.

Many people believe that airbnb is a cheaper way to book an apartment or a place but this isn't actually true. On booking.com you can find even cheaper hotels/apartments - don't know if this has to do after airbnb arrived and have taken some of its share so they managed to lower their prices as well. Something else really annoying is the high service or cleaning fees they charge, a basic reason why the prices are really high! I have booked 3 times with airbnb. I didnt have any problem until 2 weeks ago I had one cancellation the last moment from a place that I have booked but that wasn't actually airbnb's fault. The person who owned the place has given the keys to someone else who called me 4 hours before arriving and told me that he lost the keys (!!!). So I had to find an alternative from booking.com Unacceptable but... that's the risk you take when you trust common people and not professional hotels. Airbnb offered me a voucher for a discount because of this cancellation which was a nice gesture but I couldnt find a host 4 hours before my arrival. But I have to say that I appreciated that they even tried to help. From the other side if you hate the machine-style hotels, airbnb is not a bad place to find a more human-friendly place to stay. And if you have a big group of friends (5-6) I guess you can find a place that will cost cheaper eventually. PS: I had to remove one star as I have done the same mistake multiple times and it seems that many people have done the same thing. Sometimes when I booked and had to cancel, I did not pay attention to partial refund so I lost a bit of money..... Thats an utterly shame!

We have booked an apartment in Tenerife, that turned out to be horrible: smelly, dirty, old furniture, the host never showed up, so on… We claimed for the money back in the first 30 min we got there, together with photos for prove,but it wasn't enough for Airbnb evaluation team??? who decided that we don't have enough reason for claiming the money back!!! We didn't use the apart. at all and paid for 1 month! Never again Airbnb!

BEWARE OF AIRBNB...Airbnb should scrutinize and thoroughly access the accommodation they advertise. Have just stayed in accommodation in Rome, this was not cheap and yet the worst place I have ever stayed in, my bed was a cheap bed with 4 wobbly legs, kept me awake all night and I ended up sleeping on the floor. Very disappointed, the place also had plumbing problems and smelt of faeces all the time.

I rented a house via airbnb. It turned out to be a scam. Airbnb does not give a refund for the rent I paid. Airbnb does not guarantee the trustworthiness of the properties listed on their website. So Airbnb in the end is not a trustworthy website. Beware!

What happened to me is that I booked the first place but after one day, the owner cancelled it so I have to book it again. I went to a cheaper one this time because I did not pay that much again. When I booked it, the price was cheaper than the first payment and I paid it. Next day, the second payment has to be refunded. So I checked the site and I found that Airbnb changed the basic rate of the second place and charged more. And Airbnb said that they offered kindly the coupon and kept the original price. I contacted the customer service and the first representative said I was right. But Airbnb did not refund the money back again. I followed up again and again. At the end, Airbnb admitted there was a system error and changed the attitude saying the first customer representative made a mistake. They did not pay back the differences. This system is really cheating. Please do not trust this site.

People look for a place to stay on airbnb because they think it will be budget-friendly, however it turns out to be anything but. - Rather expensive: the hosts charge like 75% of a decent hotel. Together with all kinds of fee, it sums up to a hefty amount. - Be careful with the photos: they look wonderful, nice, cozy house, fully equipped. 3 photos of the kitchen, but in the description, you do not have access to the kitchen! What the point of uploading them if the guests cannot use it? Check, double-check, triple-check what you will have in the description, confirm it again with the host. You'll be surprise how often there will be something listed there but cannot be used "for some reasons". I commented with a host that his swimming pool is nice, but a bit small, only then he said to me "oh sorry the pool needs cleaning & maintaining so it cannot be used, sorry for that" - The site urges you to enter a lot of personal information, and urges you to enter credit card number. It wants to charge money as soon as possible, and when things go wrong, you will have to go through hell to fight for that money back. The most stupid thing is when the host changed their mind right after the credit card was charged a huge amount, now how can you continue booking for another? Happened to me: the host set it as pre-approval, and the site continuously prompt me: hey let us charge it so you will have it firmly booked. Since that a lot of money: more than 2300 EUR, I was reluctant and wanted to ask the host for more details and more assurance to our side....30 hours after our friendly discussion, she declined! She said sorry, but still have to declined due to "some reasons"... I feel so relieved I didn't pay. - Spend a day with the site and the host, it's hard to find a good place. Hosts declined, changed their mind after, not sure about the amount, pretty much different experience with other site such as booking.com. For your peace of mind and to minimize the chance of your long-waited holiday becomes a disaster, consider very carefully before booking on airbnb.

I found accommodation in Barcelona that was suitable and was available on my dates. I requested to book and paid the full amount. The host is then given 24 hours to accept or decline your booking. However BEWARE because if they then decline which is what happened to me (they said they now had family visiting at that time) airbnb doesn't wait the 24 hours to take your money it is taken when you make the booking so you dont get it back in your account for 7 business days so if you need that money to make another booking you have to wait a week! Why can't airbnb just wait the 24 hours and take the money only if the booking is accepted?? SO ALWAYS contact the host first to check your dates are available before you book. I have used owners direct for years with no problems as you pay a deposit then cash on arrival BUT airbnb do give the cheaper option of a room in someone's apartment which can be good value and a good experience if you get a good host It is a gamble

Please be carefull when you book a place via Airbnb. Read the cancel policy well. Even if you cancel 3 months in advance, you only get 50% of your amount. Just lost € 541 as the host refuse to refund. So be carefull when doing a booking via this site.

Searched Airbnb for a 3br house in Austin, TX for mid-October 2015, for a Thurs-Mon stay. (we also made sure that that particuar weekend that there was no big festival going on in Austin, because that does drive up pricing). Found perfect place, perfect location, perfect price, which was listed @ $200/night. When I went to book the price per night surged to $475/night. When I inquired to 'Lauren, the owner', about this I was told it was the weekend price. I responded by saying that I certainly understood price surges for Austin weekends during SxSW and ACL, but there was no indication whatsoever on the web page of a "weekend price", and since when was Thursday considered a "weekend day", and pricing should be adjusted accordingly. The response from 'Lauren' was that she had "no control over the pricing, that Airbnb set the pricing..." When I responded again about why then wasn't the property listed at $475/night instead of the $200/night listing, I received a response back the the "property was unavailable for my requested dates". This is pure Bait and Switch...Do yourself a favor and look for other resources.

I have tried to book an apartment thought Airbnb and had a bad experience. Most owners do not reply promptly. I requested to book an apartment which was available for the dates that I wanted and the owner replied saying that these dates don't work for him. It would be good it home owners simply updated their calendars, instead of wasting people's time. About Airbnb website. It is simply the worst website! I have hears that they recently invested millions of dollars to improve it but I don't see it. * Booking was very complicated - clicked "book" after entering my credit card inormation and nothing happened. No email, or notification is the booking went through * No phone number to call anywhere on the website. They make go through some ridiculous FAQ page where your problem isn't listed. Then they make you start a chat, but... the chat with customer assistant doesn't work. You type your question in the chat, and the message pops up saying "you are out of this chat" * Your wish list is by default public which means that everyone can see it. When you change it to "private" is stays public, no matter how many times you make you change. It is very frustrating that you can't easily call customer service. I booked my apartment on homeaway.com and had great experience. Airbnb seems to be run by a group of young, inexperienced guys.

I found the 'verification process' for AirBnB to be a nightmare and I still don't understand the need. Eventually got through that and booked a place 6 weeks before trip. Then. with less than 10 days to go before the trip, I get a message from the hoster that my reservation has been cancelled (not something AirBnB has control over and something they strongly disapprove of). My initial attempts to get through to their customer service went unanswered and left my very concerned and stressed, no reply to email and phone call went unanswered, I tried again via phone after about two days of hearing nothing and did get through. The person I was talking to was very helpful and responded to future emails quickly. They offered a fairly considerable credit towards finding another place and made some suggestions for improving chances. I did find a place that cost about 25% more than the original booking and AirbnB paid the difference! Overall, despite a slow start, and an unfortunate cancellation, I would deal with AirBnB again

I stayed at one host's pool house and after 3 days the toilet exploded. The host's claimed that I had damaged the toilet and therefore had to pay the $2,000 repair bill. I contacted Airbnb and they were no help whatsoever, so not only was I out of pocket on my first holiday in years, but it lead to a very tense remaining stay at the pool house. I decided to use Airbnb again for another trip, 4 days before I was due to travel I was informed that my reservation was cancelled, I immediately contacted the host and he confirmed that he did not cancel the reservation. So I called Airbnb and they confirmed that it was cancelled on Airbnb's end, I asked why and they said due to privacy reasons they couldn't disclose the reason why. Distraught, because I had no accommodation, Airbnb said they will reimburse my expenses, as well as an extra $500. Well, when I got my refund, it was the expense I had paid minus the refund. When I contacted Airbnb they said that they don't give out money refunds and instead I can use it as a credit on their site. That was the last straw, I will never ever use this website again nor will I recommend anyone in using it.

I've used Airbnb 4 times, with 2 out-of-the-country and 2 domestic rentals. Overall, my experience with Airbnb has been disappointing. After looking at great property photos and reading multiple glowing guest reviews, I have found inaccurate representations of properties, problematic communications with hosts, incorrect rental information, stained bedsheets, and filthy apartments. My first and only less-than-positive rental review was not published as the host did not review me in time. My most recent experience included an apartment which hadn't been cleaned prior to our arrival due to a cleaning service mix-up; the host didn't respond until the next day. In the meantime, my husband and I did laundry and dishes and cleaned for nearly an hour after half a day of traveling. Airbnb refunded us the $60 cleaning fee, and thus resolved the issue. I do not feel the Airbnb provides consistent, high-quality service. I feel duped after several Airbnb interactions, and do not plan to recommend or employ Airbnb services in the future.

When we arrived in this house in melbourne in 546 flinder's street, it was good as he gave us early checkin. When we walked in the one who greeted us was his cleaner/ mate/ or i dont really know. His name was Martin. He was friendly. The studio apartment was small but it was alright. We were really tired so we did not really notice the abnormalities in the house. When I woke up, I saw under the pillow had blonde hairs in it. So I was thinking maybe it wasn't washed. So I washed it in a near by laundrymat as the dryer inside the building was broken. When I came back, I saw a ball of blonde hair in a cupboard. Again, I cleaned it... The bathroom had hair all over, so I cleaned it because I did not want to have a shower in a dirty bathroom. When I went out the balcony, one of the mats had dog poo in it. We took a photo of it. We were so patient and thought it wouldnt mind us, we got a good deal anyway. After 2 1/2 days we told the owner and he promised a refund. After a few minutes, he took back what he said and told us to follow policies of the air bnb... We called air bnb and the operator was being sympathetic at first, maybe that's just her being plastic... Because after that, she told us that the poo was nothing and not a big deal... In conclusion, when you rent a house, photograph everything!!! Also, don't use air bnb as they are just after your money. Hotels are better with good service. These hosts in air bnb especially this Jae is just trying to make a few bucks and does not care about his reputation.

Hello my friends, i am host of airbnb ,currently running 3 listings and accepting dozens of guests per month! I read carefully your reviews here on truspilot and i have to say that i believe you. It's completely logical with millions of reservations done every month in the platform of airbnb there must be some that don't quite work well!I also have found my self in some diffucult situations like the guests leave my place a mess but hey! i had over 300 guests the previous year and only 1 to 3% left the place a mess .So what i did is left a bad review at them although they left me a good one and called the cleaning lady telling her that she ll work overtime! When i started my airbnb i had only my extra bedroom listed but now i have 2 apartments right in the heart of Acropolis and i can say it is better than an average salary with so little work! I welcome the guests, i show them my website where i have put much information about Athens and help them with any questions they have!Everyone leaves SATISFIED. So summing up airbnb has been the best platform for me because of the people that i met, the money that i make, if any problem comes up costumer service is ALWAYS there. Literally the guys are trying their best! My profile has over 160 reviews and all my listings are book 3 months ahead!Isn't that awesome for a 22 year old dude? So basic things for guests 1) Check Reviews 2) contact the host to see how fast he replies. I always reply within minutes or if it is night and i am sleeping first thing next morning 3) Address him your questions or concerns, if he doesn't care go to the next host who will! 4) Provide arrival time and double check how the check in is going to work ! :) 5) RESPECT THE PLACE......This is no hotel so mind your manners and don't act like vandals or 15years old in their first vacation. Making the place a mess ends up to a dissapointment for the host so in order to cover up his expenses he will raise the cleaning fee for future guests. 6) Be always clear with what you are going to visit and probably ask some advice. Many of us are more than happy to give you! That's all folks All my best to all of you who want to travel through airbnb and enjoy being among locals! Best wishes Chris meli

Avoid to use Airbnb, I have tried to reserve using the web site for three years during summer and I had bad results. Lot of people have declined the reservation or canceled the reservation after payment.

Places are not always available on requested dates , even when listed on Airbnb. So please be careful when making booking without emailing hosts first. If you have requested a booking on available property but declined by your host for any reason, the full booking amount still will be taking out from your bank account and kept by Airbnb for approximately 7 days before money will be returned back to your bank account. Basically you won't be able to use your money again for your next booking if the first booking is declined by host. Happened to me three times in one day. I would highly recommend to contact your potential host first to confirm the place availability before hitting the request booking button.

I book a place that looked good on AirBnb, but when I arrived the key was not in the mailbox (as the host said it should be). In the end I lost the full $245 for a single night stay that I didn't have. I checked the side door, basement door and the patio door in the back. Nothing. I looked again, thinking that I missed it. Nope -- the key is nowhere, not even under any of the mats. It turns out that the back patio door was open and I was able to get in. It felt like I was breaking into someone's home. There were clothes strewn all across the bedroom (this was a 2 bedroom listing that sleeps up to 4 -- I told them that I will need both rooms). I did a double take to compare the address and pictures with what was in front of me. It was barely even the same place because the furniture was nothing like the pictures and because it was so messy. Did I mention that throughout this process the host was nowhere to be found? She did not answer her phone and did not answer her e-mail until the next day. I decided against staying at the place since I had valuable luggage and did not want to be in a place where the only way I could get in was through the accidentally unlocked patio door (I wouldn't leave my stuff there while I went to my meetings...someone could steal it). Long story cut short: I called AirBnb and they said they can do nothing since I didn't call them right when I found out that I couldn't stay at the place. I contacted the host and she said that the keys were in the mailbox (Bull -- I checked at least 4 times and was extremely careful and thorough). The host said "Too bad" and AirBnb just disappeared off the face of the earth when I needed them.

I wanted to make a reservation at the site and I asked too many personal details This is the list: The last 4 numbers of my social security number Date of birth Street Address deireccion mail credit card and even did charge my account facebook and others data I gave ALL and then I get these messages: "We're sorry to Say That We Were not reliable to send your reservation request Because You did not finish verifying your ID. We've Canceled your reservation request and voided your payment authorization. , Although your payment cancellation Instantly OCCURS-through Airbnb, your financial institution May take several days to process the transaction. "

As a host, I depend on my airbnb income to afford my monthly expenses. I rent out 2 rooms in my house and have enjoyed my experience of hosting people from all over the world. I'm the very kind of host that Airbnb markets as a justification for why the service is amazing. However, people in my city are getting fed up with people trying to capitalize on the Airbnb model by renting out multiple properties they probably don't even own. It's exacerbating our affordable housing crisis and these "hosts" have no regard for the types of people who they rent to. So now earnest hosts like myself are lumped with these greed-driven hosts and now I have a negative reputation to manage in my own neighborhood. I'm afraid my city will outlaw Airbnb. I've reached out to Airbnb multiple times asking for assistance communicating with my local government but did not receive a response. It seems to me that Airbnb only cares about their bottom line. The least they can do is address the concerns that many stakeholders have and put a limit to the number of units a host can rent out. They should get rid of their automatic booking option. Potential investors need to see the writing on the wall and put pressure on Airbnb.

I have listed my property with Airbnb one year ago. I have enjoyed working with them. When I call them, I speak to someone immediately, I am not sure if they route my call based on my phone number but the people I speak with always speak my native language. Any issue that I have had they have taken care of immediately. I receive an email confirming our conversation from the rep the I speak with and I am allowed to respond back. It is not an automated message. I had an issue with a potential guest harassing me and it was handled immediately. In fact, I was told that Airbnb is looking at changing their policy so that a guest can't request a booking until their identity is verified. If this happens it will solve the only issue that I have had with booking which occurs when a guests identity can't be verified. My payments always arrive on time and in full. My experience with their rival FlipKey has not been so great. I am considering removing my listing from that site.

I had payed one booking with my credit card. After some month a was looking around and wanted to send an request for another place to stay for another vacation trip. I thought that I just send one reguest but my credit card number was still registered in their files and the whole became an complete booking. I did not understand what had happen until I got and mail that said that airbnb had charged by card. I directly mailed them about the mistake but they had no understanding at all and said that I had to pay their service fee and would only get 50% back of the cost. I have to pay 500 euro for this mistake. They charged my card without me understand what was happening. I will ever never use them or recommend them to anyone else again!!!!! They are no better than thieves.

These guys are a racket. Paid significant money to stay at 2 places in Maui, both with beds that were not beds. Host in one was a drinker, wouldnt talk to me or answer emails. I used AirBnB "Resolution Center". This is nothing but a time waster. She took the info, said get documentation, but when I asked specifically what, she wouldnt answer. She came back a few days later and said time is up, case closed. I didnt have a chance. As a customer I was nothing, AirBnB wont look into it again. Devious, manipulative and no customer service. I would advise people not to use this site.

I had a first time experience with airbnb. Although largely the experience was fine and my review was a long detailed one much the sane as posted on TripAdvisor in past. I see the whole point of these experiences is to share the good and bad. Everything about my hosts mother who took care of us n was in flat and the flat was great. Except for the host ... She basically had taken payment for breakfast and then said she hadn't. I did the calc to prove it was paid. Her mother was fine and provided it no issues. So I said in the review this was sorted. But in my review I also had a v negative review of airbnb for not making charges for admin service and card/PayPal conversion fees obvious and transparent. I also said I'd be complaining to them as the host said they never received the extra money I'd paid airbnb for the breakfast. So air bnb is pocketing extra cash. I told her to also complain. The next thing you know my post doesn't get posted and there is only one line posted of 4words which is only the title I gave the review! The 4 words were positive and a 4 star rating. Although I would use again airbnb are cheating consumers and hosts in monies earned and in terms of describing actual experience. Thus you could end up staying somewhere which is rubbish but as airbnb doctors the posts or hides them u wouldn't know any different! Responses from airbnb are ... "Maybe you hit post too soon" or "you forgot what you posted" nonsense like that. Or "you had internet issues" Absolute nonsense. They are doctoring things for sure. Be suspect of any short reviews and any place that has no negative or balanced comments. What is the point of reviews if they are edited/hidden! I'll tell you what ... More money in air bnb coffers! TripAdvisor/trust pilot/other review sites ... - please open up the ability for users to add airbnb hosts and apartments to trip advisor.so they can be independently reviewed! A disgusted airbnb member!!!

My young adult daughter was relocating to L.A for an extended period of time. She had a room lined up but needed temporary housing until her permanent lodging was available. She chose to use air Bnb and her host was initially very helpful. About 7 days in the host disappeared. She then phones my 22 year old daughter who knows no one in L.A. and tells her she she is having personal problems and my daughter must leave now. She gave my daughter literally 2 hours to pack and get out. When we called customer support we were told "we have to speak to the host before we can do anything". Next they said we can put her up in a Super 8 hotel for a few days until we figure it out. Mind you at this point she had already paid 2,000.00 and was now out of the money and a place to stay until Air BNB could figure it out. After we told customer support that Super 8 was not quite appropriate for a young lady by herself they offered $250 reimbursement for a hotel of her choice but she had to pay for it initially. Now she's out 2,000 plus the cost of a hotel stay why they "figure it out". . $500 more hotel dollars later they place her with another host. Guess what? This host calls a changes her check in to 4 hours later. Now my daughter checks out of the hotel waits around only to be contacted again to move her check in to another 5 hour delay. Air BNB then offered my daughter a $100 reimbursement to walk around LA until they could find this host to see what was going on. As I am typing she is trying to check back in to the hotel we had to find her 3 days ago! This experience has been horrible for my daughter and for the Mom of a young lady in a city alone.

We had a reservation for a lodging in Dublin and the persons who owned the property canceled on us, in an untimely manner. FIRST, Airbnb offered us a $300.00 coupon to compensate for our additional expense in finding a new reservation, which we used for lodging in another region. BUT!! We received, about 2 weeks later, a notification that OUR ACCOUNT WAS BEING PERMANENTLY CANCELLED, AND THAT AIRBNB HAS THE RIGHT TO DO THIS WITHOUT PROVIDING ANY PROOF OF CAUSE. Can you figure out what happened? I can. Some clown in a corner office decided that we should not have this coupon, and so we were summarily canceled from service permanently. And if you try to speak to a higher level administrator, you are told that "we do not have their contact info". REALLY?? What is this, the mob, where the rank and file have no ability to contact the upper echelons? Airbnb is a no account, take a chance with you lodging, junk service. I will be reporting them to the Better Business Bureau and the state attorney general's office.

We booked a condo in Anaheim two months in advance for our spring break vacation and a week before our trip the host decided to cancel on us leaving us scrambling to find a hotel or anything else to accommodate five of us , when we called airbnb the person who answered all what he have to say is sorry sometimes the host cancel . Back to old fashion way book a suite whith a reliable hotel and don't worry about some jackass host to cancel on you, for me never again .

Booked a stay in Paris, and days later host asked me for a 500Euro deposit. I was suspicious and called airbnb. Come to find out its a scam, and they told me to stop all communication to the host bc host has already been flagged for security issues. Now my concern is the $1300 already charged to my credit card for this booking. I have called every day for the last 5 days, only to receive a run around from all these 'agents' who can't seem to take care of the matter. No one can reassure me that I will get my refund in full, and any type of timeline in which it'll happen. And there seems to be no urgency to the matter. I have spoken to manager after manager. Airbnb must employ complete idiots, or their business structure is totally WHACK and customer service is the least of their concerns. I hate that this was my first experience with Airbnb and will surely be my last.

We had to put in credit card information in order to contact host to see if property available for chosen dates. After putting in card info, site went back to calendar which showed dates UNAVAILABLE. There is no way to contact these people or site. Email address doesn't work, my account name and password returns a "page not found" response, and to call a number given on a notice that my credit card had been charged, tells me to enter my phone number, and then a voice says the number is "not recognized"!! It's the biggest scam going. We actually reached a host, and he said there was nothing he could do about it, and had no number to call for us to reach Airbnb. We just lost $1,300 but are going to call FBI, and have instructed our credit card company we are disputing charge. DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY. HUNDREDS OF SAME NEGATIVE REVIEWS!!!!

the laundry list of bad service starts with the fact that I had to go to gethuman to get Airbnb's phone number. Next it seems that if you are not connected to Facebook, Linked or Gmail it is impossible to get "verified" so you caN use their services. I AM A 65 YEAR OLD BABYBOOMER WITH MONEY TO SPEND. Airbnb isn't what I would describe as helpful. If they aren't helpful on the front end why should I think they will be helpful or cooperative when there is a real problem. So far it has taken over 14 hours for their folks to get back to us so we can book. Our "reservation" timed out. They have a great idea. I can only hope someone enters into the field but can spell service. I am thinking that Hilton sounds better and better.

Attempted to use Airbnb, had money reserved whilst awaiting confirmation on a booking, Host then deliberated on and off over five or six hours as to whether she could/could not take the booking - then decided not as she was not there to "meet and greet" it then took three days to have pre-authorised money returned on a booking that was never confirmed??? Thought I would give it one more go - and this time, contacted the Host first, who took 24 hours to return every question, was just about to book, when they admitted that the Photos on the site did not relate to the place being rented!!! wasted four days - and decided it is totally unprofessional, and realised the no checks are obviously made on the people who are renting their property out and the property that they claim is available. Dangerous really - but the old adage is true - if it sounds too good to be true - it generally is! Caveat Emptor.

First time using AirBNB will be my last. Apartment was not ready at the pre-communicated time of arrival. The house cleaning lady (that spoke very little English) said it would be 2 hours before it would be ready. I questioned the host about parking and she implied that it would be no problem. The first 3 days we had to walk 6-7 blocks to the apartment after parking at night. First night trying to sleep was horrible!! Was woke up at 1-2 am because someone in a nearby apartment was yelling and cussing like they were dying or coming off a drug addiction. This went on for 2 hours or so. Then, that same morning two people were having a heated argument outside of our door. When I call the host to tell her about these problems her only suggestion was that she could move us to another apt. upstairs. I told her that wouldn't help the situation. Then she said that if I would move to the other apt. that she would refund $100 if I left a day earlier than scheduled! I told her that still wouldn't help the situation. She said "sorry, contact AirBNB, that is all I will do". When I called her after that conversation she did not answer her phone and the voice message said to not leave a voice message text only. She would no longer return my calls! NEVER AGAIN will I use AirBNB!!!!

Booked with a host that had positive reviews. The confirmation email told me the host would be out of the country and I had to pick my keys up at a nearby restaurant. Also she said not to use her real name or she'd be in trouble with her landlord. Clearly dodgy. Airbnb have not responded at all after two days. I opened another support ticket to ask what was going on, it was just closed with no response. Obviously I was unlucky with my host, these things happen, but the total lack of response from Airbnb is unacceptable. Steer clear!

We are in the middle of a current battle with AirBnB and the homeowner on getting a full refund for a stay we never used. Long story short we booked a place in Naples (Casa Del Sol if you're looking) that looked great online. But... we had family in the area who drove by and took pictures that showed a completely different story than what we saw online. We immediately cancelled and got 50% back which is per policy - not including AirBnB's fees. When I called to explain to AirBnB, they did refund their fees. However, they are deferring to the homeowner to refund the rest of our $700 and not willing to stand up and make this right even though when you book you pay AirBnB. This isn't Craigslist but that's how they're treating it. Not only is the property misrepresented online, but now it has been rented out for the same period we cancelled for so the homeowner is out nothing yet they - both the homeowner and AirBnB STILL refuse to refund us. So now the homeowner is make 150% on her sham. For what it's worth, we have been nothing but congenial and apologetic for the 'inconvenience' to the homeowner and in return have been accused of stalking and harassment. Classy! So I'm done dealing with her and will only go through AirBnB at this point and refuse to let it go despite them telling me that "the case is closed" as if they have some higher authority. Really just weird... horrible customer service... I wouldn't recommend AirBnB to anyone based on this experience.

First thing I should mention is that the registration process is too lengthy and I just felt so annoyed during registration itself. It asks to provide authorization for lot of other social/professional networks and email accounts. Before the booking is confirmed by the owner, Airbnb reserves the credit from our card. In my case booking was rejected by owner without providing any reason. The credit that they reserved was not refunded until today. Airbnb responded that It can take around one week to reflect it in our account. So I cannot look for other rooms at the moment since there were only limited credit in my debit card. This is the worst experience I ever had regarding online apartment/room booking. They don't have any contact number or any other customer service desk details updated in the web site.

We decided to get Airbnb rentals because it was cheaper than other big bame hotel sites. We found serveral places and request to book. Most were accepted. Few days later, we got emails of voided and cancellation on the rental we booked. The credit card is active and in good standing and I went through the verification system. We phoned them and ask why. They said they'll pas our info to another member of the team and get back to us the next day. Never got a reply and we phone them again, same reply. Then the next day we got an email and it said they'll deactivate our account with no explanation and will not look into the matter the further. Complete waste of time and the most useless customer service ever. What is the point of calling customer rep when they can't do anything and have to pass the issue to another team every time? Promise to call back but never did.

I have been a member of Airbnb since 2012. I have both booked properties through the platform for my trips as well have been an active host myself ever since I started using Airbnb. Basic difference between other platforms and Airbnb is that each individual, either a host or a guest, has a personal profile that is openly available to all member to this platform. I believe is a very important tool in order to be able to have an idea about the character of other party before making any commitments. It is a community rather than anonymous listings. The booking system runs very smoothly. All procedures are clear and well explained. The guests & hosts are verified and there are almost no surprises. You are given the option as a host to interact with only verified ID`s as well. In case of damages they have a just system in which guests and hosts interact with each other at first step trying to resolve the issues with mutual respect and understanding. In case they can`t reach an agreement the option to involve Airbnb team generally creates the right results efficiently. The payment procedure is hassle free. Always on time. The user interface is very user friendly. Listings appear very professionally and the reviews mechanism works perfectly for guest and hosts. I would definitely recommend this platform to everyone looking to rent a property as well looking to rent out their own property.

I didn't think I make booking sucessfully anyway, why should I been charged in the first place. Never again airbnb, stay hotel instead

First of all, the availability dates listed on Airbnb are NEVER up to date. I'm not sure why hosts don't update them. I was looking for an apartment in Miami or Sunny Isles that could sleep 6 adults comfortably for 23 nights. I literally had to contact hundreds of hosts, the majority of whom replied with "booked", "already taken", "not available", etc. Once I found a host that claimed an apartment is available, I booked it immediately and paid $9,010 which was promptly taken out of my bank account. I shared the apartment with my entire party and they were all very excited... 5 hours later, I get a message from the host, claiming that "there has been a mistake" and that particular apartment I had just paid for has already been booked by another person. Are you joking?! The host tries to persuade me to "switch" to a different apartment in another building, that's: - Much smaller - Its description says it only sleeps 4 people - Even if they accept 6 people, the third couple has nowhere to sleep - Has no Jacuzzi - Has no terraces - Has no private entrance - Has no nice views like the one I paid for WOW! We call Airbnb and speak with "Janice." She's somewhat apologetic. But she informs me that I shouldn't cancel my reservation, because since there are only 4 days until I'm supposed to travel, I would get NO refund if I cancel now. Huh?! I am then told that I have to wait for the host to cancel it... which he might or might not agree to. "Janice" is unclear on whether Airbnb lets hosts switch properties on customers. I tell her this is a bait & switch practice and that if they are unable to give me exactly what I paid for, I expect my money back. She then proceeds to tell me that "I'm going to hear from someone in their more experience department"... within a few days. Maybe today, maybe tomorrow... who knows. Oh, please take your time, lady, I have 4 entire days until I travel and I'm out $9,010. Luckily, the host cancelled the reservation on their part. I never heard back from Airbnb. I am travelling in less than 48 hours and I still haven't received my money back. Their website says I should be receiving it in 3-5 business days. Luckily, our travelling party has more money in the bank, credit cards, etc. But Airbnb's business practice is despicable.

It is nearly impossible to contact anyone from airbnb if an issue arrives, most inquiries require up to a 72hr wait period before you can make them. Be very, very careful with refund policies. Unlike a normal hotel or resort, airbnb allows many of the hosts to simply keep your money even if cancelling minutes after the reservation was made. I am going to work with paypal to see if I can recover my money but will never again make a booking through airbnb.

Stayed at two Airbnb flats in the Cape Town area (one in Cape Town and one in Paarl). These places were perfect for us, the prices were reasonable, and the hosts were delightful. I rated 4 stars instead of 5 because I have no idea how Airbnb ensures a positive experience between hosts and customers, and from other reviews I've read here, it appears that they might not be doing much in that direction. Possibly my experience is the exception rather than the rule. I will be interested to see if and how Airbnb addresses these grievances.

Airbnb.com availability dates are never accurate. After multiple attempts to book, including entering my CC information, the dates showing available have always been unavailable. Use another rental site, or get in touch with a Realtor, but don't waste your time with airbnb.

Airbnb claims to allow you to have a $50 discount from a $200 TOTAL trip if you are referred by a friend. I place emphasis on "total" because there is no fine print that informs that when they say "total," it means total cost by the renter, not the total cost including the airbnb service fee. As I booked my trip for $213, expecting to receive my $50 discount, nothing happened. I called the help center, for them to tell me that the total requested by the host was $190, while the airbnb service fee was $23, making my "total total" $213. I may never use this service again, except maybe to use my entitled $50 ******* dollars.

I am a host. I have a great place in a Mayan pueblo on a lake in Guatemala. I have three kind people who work with me. After I got on airbn I was full. I had no other advertising. I read the comments here and as a host I wanted to say the people who use the site have been great. We have had travelers from all over the world and with a few exceptions its been a wonderful experience. (The few exceptions have had to do with people being rude or loud to other people staying here.) My biggest complaint with people has been the check in policy where they have to verify who they are. Many people do not use facebook or have the computer skills to take pictures of themselves. They simply want to use their credit card. They do not take money from the account of the guest until 24 hours after they arrive. They have to contact airbnb in this framework. I have had no problem contacting them. I go on the gethuman and have airbnb call me. They are personal and contact the guest when there is a problem (always with not being accepted) the guest has relayed to me. They got famous because of this customer service. It could be they are having growing pains. As far as the man who says he was in another zip code and farther away from the destintion he wanted to be at..this would be fraud by the owners. It my have described exactly where it is in distance. I do not know. The reviews are not consistent. Its a business and they have t make money. Each site determines their own policy. Mine is strict because we are a small business and prepare for guests. We prepare a house for how many people are coming and buy food for the guests and wait for them. If they are delayed a day by circumstance we offer them a free night when they cant get there on time if available we block that night out. I wonder if people just complain on these sites. Oh i believe they are unhappy people and have had real problems but I have only had people very happy with the business end of it all. As far as the reviews.. they are not edited. I have no idea what people will write. Its not just that Im a host Im inviting and working for people i do not know and Ive had good people sent to me.Solina Luna Azul San Pedro La Laguna Guatemala
