The places were all clean and tidy and very much like their listings. All the hosts we meet were very friendly and helpful and all the places were in the right locations as we had researched. After looking at a lot of the reviews on here, it seems the scams and poor service are with the American places, so maybe don't use them in the States or make sure you do your research and communicate with the hosts for a period of time before booking. Given the number of poor reviews against the total number of bookings that there must be, I believe airbnb is a really good option. Do your homework!!!!!!!!

We booked a long weekend away using AIrBnB. We received the email confirming the reservation and the money was deducted from my credit card. I emailed our hosts to let them know how much we were looking forward to a weekend at their beach sturdio. However, the reply from our hosts stated that AirBnB booking had not showed up in their booking diary. The studio had already been booked prior to our booking (the AirBnB calander showed the property was available). AIrBnb are saying that they bear no responsibilty. The email I received from them was clearly a stock email that did not address our particular experience or the specifics of my complaint. We are now stuck without accomodation and with no alternate accomodation availabe in the same location. Very, very unhappy!

Airbnb has been called a revolution in accommodation and I'm sure it works really well for many - but everyone should be aware it's like playing a high risk game of chance with your holiday. Many of the accommodation providers are not serious and can pull out at the last minute (it's obvious if you think about it). We booked a family trip to Washington DC (a big investment) 3 months before travel but the host pulled out 10 days before we were about to fly. The reason - her brother had decide to come to stay in the house! You have no recourse and are left stranded. Despite the company saying they will assist - you are left with the rump end or hugely expensive options. We ended up forking out £500 more for accommodation for 4 nights in a place much further from the centre. This is much more common that Airbnb will admit. I came across many providers who had notes on their feedback that they had pulled out. One pulled out 2 days before the people were due to arrive - urgh! Use Airbnb if you like risk and are happy to have your plans dissolve a few days before your holiday - otherwise beware.

I was a listed owner on Airbnb's site, with about a dozen renters who had mostly positive reviews, and a few clients who had minor complaints about the home. The corporation terminated my service, unilaterally and without notice or explanation. They refused to respond to phone inquiries; the final customer service representative actually stated "...if I did know the reason behind your service termination, I wouldn't tell you." I inquired multiple times via email in an attempt to understand the cause of the problem and resolve the matter. Each time I received a form letter that stated that the corporation has the right to terminate service at any time and for any reason. No other explanation was made. Finally, I complained to the Better Business Bureau of San Francisco, where the corporation is based. The company finally responded to this complaint, but only to say that it used "publicly available information" and repeated its claim that it has the right to terminate service at any time. When asked for further information, the company refused to respond with specific information and simply stated that it has the right to terminate service... As I said, this company is a bully.

The company is all about collecting their fees. The place I booked was not how it was described. There were barking dogs, it was dirty and the air conditioner was NOT working. I did not stay and left immediately. Both Airbnb and the property owners refused to refund my payment. After much argument, they have agreed to refund half. Airbnb kept their FEE! Totally unacceptable practice. The regulators need to stop this practice of collecting and charging up front with no refund. When you arrive art the property, if it does not meet your expectation...you should not be charged. I will NEVER use Airbnb again. i do not recommend anyone else to use this service either.

For an upcoming trip to San Francisco, I gave Airbnb a shot. AFTER taking my money, they insisted on all manner of "verifications", including uploading a video of myself. When I was unable to do so, my reservation was cancelled, BUT THE COMPANY KEPT MORE THAN $1K OF MY MONEY TIED UP WITH PAYPAL. Repeated calls and emails have been ineffectual to date--I am just out my thousand dollars. UPDATE: Four days now since my reservation was cancelled, and STILL no help from Airbnb. PayPal was both helpful and apologetic; all they need, they said, is a note from Airbnb that the reservation was cancelled. Instead of that, here's what I received yesterday: To Me Oct 1 at 11:51 AM Airbnb Airbnb Customer Experience [name], Oct 01 09:51: Hello James, Thank you for your email, As stated in my previous, it may take up to 10 business days to process the transaction back to your account. For more information, be sure to visit our Help Center: If you have any more questions, just let reply to this email. We're here to help! All the best, [name] THIS is the Airbnb "Customer Experience"--beware! Save yourself a ton of grief--DO NOT DO BUSINESS WITH THIS AWFUL COMAPNY; if you do, there is an excellent chance you will wind up without a room...and without your money!!

Booked accommodation through airbnb. airbnb client took my money, no accommodation provided. Airbnb refused to take responsibility and refused to refund me. EBAY and Amazon would assume responsibility and protect the integrity of their markets. Not Airbnb. Their market has no integrity and is doomed. BEWARE! DO NOT USE AIRBNB!

My wife and I have used Airbnb almost exclusively this year for travel through Europe, Africa and Asia. We stayed in 43 homes and must say we had nothing but fantastic experiences. We can not believe all the negative reviews on this site! And people so quick to complain. If you want to read a summary of our 'Year with Airbnb' we did a blogpost about it at 'teachorbeach.'

I booked what looked like a lovely bright basement apartment in Metro New York area - you have to pay in advance if you book a month, which I did. When I got there, it was not a bright basement apartment: it was a dark dingy basement! The advertised three windows, were all covered with "artwork" in the inside and blocked with plants on the outside. The advertised air-conditioning was a square floor fan. The full kitchen, a oven, fridge and over-sized table stuffed into a back storage room. The bathroom was, as the rest of the place, hardly finished - when you shut the shower curtain you were showering in the dark! I could go on and on... but it was HORRIBLE and should never been allowed to be advertised for rental. I arrived late at night, so had no choice but to stay the first night - crying the whole time. The next day I drove everywhere and booked into a suite hotel (at twice the price - but now I see it was worth it!). I found out that in this area, renting out a basement as a sleeping area is actually illegal!! I contacted Airbnb via their Resolution center as per their procedures and filed a complaint on false advertising and misrepresentation. I felt bad for the elderly lady who was the owner of the place, so I didn't even ask for the full amount back (I told myself I had stayed one night). From that moment on I got the run-around from Airbnb and am still fighting them for my money back! They told me that the owner hasn't been replying to them and hasn't agreed to give me my money - I told them all of the above and more... but they still are "waiting" on the owner. However, my credit card statement has the money being paid to Airbnb NOT the owner! I'm now going through my cc company to get my money back and will be filling a report with the local police regarding the illegal rental. Now it's not even about the money, it's about the scam - I don't want anyone else to be duped like I was.

When airbnb was new to the market, I eagerly signed on and made took full advantage of the site. I am a very frequent traveler.... domestic and overseas... and much prefer staying in an apartment to a hotel. I would say I have used airbnb more than 20 times, for stays from one night to one month. But recently something seems to have gone very wrong. "Hosts" are hitting me up for huge fees, sometimes called "cleaning" or "service" or whatever, always payable in cash and generally upon my arrival. More often than not requests for reservations simply go unanswered, ignored, while airbnb freezes money in my credit card accounts. My experiences at properties have also gone downhill with hosts failing to disclose very important issues, such as noise, decrepit buildings, and so on. As I write this I am still waiting to hear back from reservation requests I have made. Looks like I am back to hotel stays from hereon. Sorry, airbnb, it was nice while it lasted!

I rented a house for the weekend for 6 people on airbnb.com. The house had electricity leakage and we were the first guests. We had at least 10 shocks and were easily convinced that the house was not safe. (Imagine taking a shower) . I called owner. Owner didnt pick up. I called airbnb for a stay. We finally got a hotel arranged same day 3am!!! The arrangement was only for 1 night so we had to check out at 12pm. Right now we have no place to stay with no arrangemens for our second night. For a group of 6 running around with suitcases this is incredibly inconvenient. I had a similar situation wih booking.com and they had rebooked and settled perfectly within just a few hours. The customer service takes 30 minutes to pivk up the phone and can get disconnected any time. I spent 3 hours on the phone. (Again during a vacation). Your vacation is not guaranteed here. Go to booking.com

In short, I rented a house through Airbnb and it was broken in by a theft and he took away some of my belongings. Called both 911 and the host. Contacted Airbnb and was told "not insured for this incident". Although the host refund me the rental fee, I realize my personal safety and belongs is not protected by anything at all! Please take this lesson.

Absolutely terrible. Of the 4 times I have used AirBnB, twice there have been cancellations by the host less than 24 hours before the trip started. This leaves you with no-where to stay, and no cover from AirBnB. So you get to book an expensive hotel like you should have done beforehand, probably miles and miles from where you want to be. They might offer you a derisory £50 voucher - which you can spend only with them! - but certainly no help to fix the problem created. Avoid, avoid, avoid. AirBnB is a dirty little scam. The only winners are the founders.

I own an apartment and just recently found out that my apartment was rented out through Air bnb, at least 16 times. All positive reviews talking about the nice "owner". But guess what, this very nice gentleman is not the "owner" at all, because I am. This gentleman was renting this apartement on a monthly base and it states clearly in his contract that it is not allowed to subrent. But Air bnb does not seem tot see any necessity to check who the person is that is putting up an apartment for a rent. And the worst off all is I can't even get in touch with Air bnb, since I do not have an account, which I probably never will have. I just want the money that he and Air bnb earned on my apartment without me knowing.

So we went to London for two days and rented an Airbnb in Shoreditch and it was awesome! I had been in touch with the host since the booking in March and we went in August 2014 and No issue at all. We left London and flew to Paris where we had rented a flat about 5 minutes from the Eiffel Tower. This part was not so great because the owner had his friend meet us there with the key and the friend was an hour late so we were waiting around Paris with our luggage and people looking at us like we were serial killers. Come to find out once the friend arrived, we found out the the key was supposedly left under the door in an envelope..... There was no key to be found. So after all of us being on or knees looking under the door and trying to acquire a hanger so we could see if the envelope was further under, there simply was no key, the owner was in Morocco and wasn't accommodating or willing to get a locksmith or anything. He was talking to his friend on the phone and told him to tell us to just call airbnb and get a refund. Not having any concern for the fact that we were completely without a place to stay, smh. So we got in touch with Airbnb and one of their customer service reps (Nikki) was the epitome of what customer service should be. Not only did she express great concern for our situation but she also arranged us a two night stay in a hotel equivalent to the price we paid for the rental... but It gets better. She kept In touch throughout and when I let her know that with our new location, we were extremely out of the way from everything and the taxis's would be a fortune, she gave us a $120.00 credit towards dinner and $50 credit towards or transportation, and because we had such a crazy experience and I was in Paris on my birthday she was very understanding at how frustrated I was and gave me a rental coupon worth $225.00 towards another place as long as we used the coupon within a year from the date she issued it!!! The refund process was easy and I just had to scan our receipts and send them to her and she would give us a payout for the taxi and dinner we put on our credit card. She made what could have been a nightmare into a pleasant smooth customer service interaction the way it should be. I'll totally be using Airbnb again of course and I'll also know to make sure these people I rent from are verified and have a lot of reviews and do my homework before any bookings. ~P.S. The comments about them contacting you whenever they want is funny because the complainer said that Airbnb doesn't treat them like responsible adults. Please note that as adults, you can adjust those notification settings in your dashboard of your airbnb account. Do yourself a favor when you sign up for airbnb and go through the entire website and READ!!! Most of these complaints I keep reading are silly and could've been avoided had responsible adults known what they were doing. And no I do not work for Airbnb at all lol!
There is no incentive for people who book to honour cancellations. I had 4 bookings and all four cancelled wasting my time. cancelled my account after less than a week.

For the 2 reservations I have made through Airbnb I have been harassed by Airbnb with multiple texts and emails of reminders for the upcoming stays. These texts have come in the middle of the night. This creates anxiety when you are woken from sleep to hear your phone going off. Airbnb has no consideration for the booking clients. They think they can contact you at all hours of the day and night. They assume that none of us are responsible adults. ONE reminder via email during waking hours is sufficient. Airbnb needs to learn lessons from their hosts who are great. I called Airbnb to register this complaint and was on hold for 40 minutes before I hung up. Another example of their conceited way of doing business. There is no email to contact them to complain.

After some good airbnb experiences in New England/Montreal, and Washington D.C., my family used airbnb for two of the places we stayed during our vacation in Belize last month. Our experience went from bad to worse. At least for the first (bad) experience the host gave us a partial refund, but then trashed us on a review - we had the chance to reply so we felt like it worked out. The second place we stayed was completely misrepresented and we got absolutely no customer assistance from airbnb. We have concluded that airbnb is a scam that just takes your money if you have a bad experience and miss the 14 day review period through no fault of your own, then you can forget any recourse. I would never recommend or use airbnb abroad again.

Airbnb won't let owner speek with potential client. System is hard to adjust price for deposits, taxes, cleaning. Can't get 50% now and 50% before occupancy to work. Spent 4 days trying to book a place in Montana and gave up because of lack of clarity. Watch out, Airbnb are quick to authorize credit card and charge the fee but slow to let owner and client work out details.

After filing a complaint about a fraudulent host i spent a week and a half calling every day only to be given the same story. No one called me back, they refused to give me any contact details of the head office for where my 'ticket' was being dealt with and they even refused to give me their names when i spoke to customer services. The best i got from them was a repeat email, almost word for word, sent 3 times, telling me they were not going to do anything to rectify the issue, despite our financial loss of 1000 euros. they are a billion pound company, with insurance for these exact scenarios, yet they go out of their way to ensure they don't have to pay out, by wearing you down until you give up. We book through them and pay a fee to protect our money and improve the experience of the holiday - yet my First experience has been a major disappointment. I will not use this company again, and advise anyone considering it to think twice.

Was a huge fan originally but 5 of the past 6 deals have had problems. Have had holidays disrupted, spoiled and wasted hours of frustration - and airbnb just doesn't care. They NEVER refund their fees so you could be out $165.00 like I was when you arrive at a place and it is disgusting. Plus everything has to be up front. Still waiting on another $145.00 that was supposed to be refunded MY RECOMMENDATION - STAY AWAY. TOTALLY UNPROFESSIONAL AND IF IT WASN'T A BILLION DOLLAR COMPANY I WOULD CALL IT A SCAM.

To start, I tried to send airbnb some suggestions on some of the problems, annoyances, and blatant non-working functions when you click on them. When I went to fill out the check box that asked 'How am I feeling right now', the check box deleted all of my text. How ironic is this, the suggestion part of the website deletes your suggestions to fix bugs on the websites. Anyways, here is what is really WRONG with Airbnb. When I want to host a person who has no reviews, I ask them to tell me about themselves. Sure enough all of the links to LinkedIn, Profile Websites, Activities they are doing in the city are blocked ("Website Hidden"), ("Email Address Hidden"). How am I supposed to verify this user? I get that they don't want people to collude offline to bypass the fee's. But what Host would want to do that anyways, part of the reason we use Airbnb is for the $1,000,000 insurance policy! Secondly, what really makes me angry, is that Airbnb expects us to trust Host & Travelers for the website to work. But ironically enough, the website has ZERO trust for it's own users, blocking websites, emails, etc. It's awful really, how long do they expect users to live with this disrespectful double standard. And it's getting even worse. Now you can't even get the Host/Travelers real email address. They force you to use an airbnb proxy email. You've got to be kidding me Airbnb. Not to mention the numerous bugs on the website. It's getting really annoying to use this service. The problem with reviews. Etc. I can't wait for the next start-up to move my business elsewhere.

I recently used airbnb for the first time to rent a house in Seattle for me and my family. Pics looked great and it had nothing but 4 star ratings. But when we arrived, it was a different story: the place was practically falling apart, there were gross smells, stained carpets, no real security, black mold in the shower, and traffic noise all night long. While lying awake in this dump/firetrap with my children in the next room, I had a realization. Maybe boring, grown-up things like taxes, insurance, laws, regulations, codes, etc. exist for a reason. Like to protect consumers. I'll never use airbnb again.
Even if the photos being uploaded have enough quality and resolution they're being resized and are shrinked by server having unacceptably low resolution in the end.

I am using air-bnb three years now as a host and a guest. I have needed a few times assistance and every single time I had fast and effective responses by air-bnb stuff. I really cannot understand all these bad reviews here. I would really recommend you to try it and see for yourself! :)

I've used airbnb for recent trip. Problems include: now from this experience of 4 places: state of cleanliness in some cases very dirty and smelling, fouled linen, bad food in fridges, blocked drains, etc. No way of leaving any detrimental postings to advise possible future clients not to use. Seems airbnb only cuts & pastes any good comments clients inform. Easy for Hosts to say nice things about clients. Will not use again for sure. There is no regulation of quality of property or state of cleanliness. Easy for Hosts to be good at corresponding but providing a decent clean environment is another question.,

I've had great experiences with airbnb in Europe, Turkey, and the US over the past four years, but after our experience with it last summer, I am never, ever, ever getting back together with airbnb! In fact, I'm hoping no one I ever recommended it to remembers that I did. Last summer we ran into numerous problems with it. First, I was no longer able to make reservations on my account. We missed out on several places we really wanted because of this. Online support consisted of canned emails which did nothing to address the problem. I think there is only one poor tech support person working there, and from what I can tell she hasn't had any training. Finally my husband created an account and was able to get us places to stay. Secondly, and worst of all, in London our host was not there to meet us. I called airbnb (btw, finding an actual airbnb phone number is extremely difficult). I never received a reply or even an acknowledgment from airbnb. So much for having our backs! (The host and I eventually connected, no thanks to airbnb.) Finally, the personal touch we used to find is mostly gone. Many of the rentals are now large, anonymous apartment complexes instead of people's homes or apartments. We're not using it again. It was nice while it lasted. But now I have a very bad taste in my mouth, and am a little afraid if using any online booking agency.

even thought they had verified my identity in the past as well as on the phone when i called them, the additional security check on the site was not letting me post a listing bc my phone was not working and the technical team was not able to do anything about it! i find it to be very disappointing and surprising that their tech support is so bad and incapable of solving technical issues. their automated reply sent me a message to rate their service regarding this issue even though the problem is still not solved. i'd rate it 0.

When I was unable to find a record of a reservation I had booked it was only with great difficulty that I found any way to write for assistance. Finally was able to message airbnb community member, whatever that is. I got a message back that my issue had been referred to the airbnb staff. I was never contacted. When an automated email came to ask if my problem had been resolved, no response. 2 more automated surveys about my experience came and I pleaded for help in each of them. Weeks later now, never any response. Fortunately I was able to figure out I had 2 accounts and to log in to the correct one to change the reservations. I am hesitant about ever dealing again with such a business.

I have used this website several times (as a guest), and highly recommend for travelers. I have only booked rooms that had a lot of reviews- which I guess doesn't help those just starting out. I can understand though that being a host comes with a lot more risks, I guess reviews, deposits and insurance would help there.

I was looking to rent a room for 2 months. There was a listing for a 1 bed, 1 bath. I booked it only to find out later that it's a 2 bed 2 bath unit. I spoke with the host and he agreed to cancel the reservation and issue a refund. The problem is Airbnb. I've called on several occasions to check on the status of my refund request. First of all, even if the reservation is cancelled, the fee Airbnb charges is not refunded, even if it was due to a misleading advertisement. Second, they have no clue when I will be issued a refund. The operators themselves are nice. But they are clueless. After being on a phone call with an operator, she said there's nothing else she can do. And she still has no idea when my "ticket" will be worked on. This was my first experience with Airbnb. STAY AWAY!
The worst site I've ever used. They auto post listings you will never be able to stay at and then never refund your money, the worst I'v ever ever used.

AirBnB sucks! I loved it at the start but I had a very bad experience now so I feel the urge to warn all of you who are thrilled about AirBnB like I was. I am still waiting for 700 EUR for a cancelled booking since over a month. AirBnB has very hidden customer service and no contact email or anything. (only for emergenies). I used the help center to contact them 3times, no response. Also, even if you cancel in advance (like I did, 1 month) you have to pay 10% fee to AirBnB, which in my case adds up to 80 EUR. For almost no service that AirBnB provided to me. It pretends to be a social site, sounds all nice and lovely, and I really liked the philosophy behind it. But the reality is different.

Rented a "luxury" condo in Boston that was described as "modern with all necessary amenities for your stay" including TV and Wifi. As this was a business trip, I planned on spending a great deal of time in the condo working on the computer. When I booked the condo, I made it clear to the host that I would be there on business, and that I'd be spending the bulk of my time at the condo working on the computer. Come to find out that, while there is a TV, there are only 4 channels available. As for the wifi, that involves trying to connect to the business center wifi that's on a different floor, and kicks you off every 3 minutes. Totally impossible to get any work done on the computer from the condo. When I asked the host about the wifi, she wrote back that they just use the business center wifi, and basically tough s*it. Definitely not as advertised, and if I'd known that there was no internet I would have booked somewhere else. Airbnb was completely unhelpful. Because there was the slight chance of connecting to the business center wifi, they said that this qualified as wifi. Technically, I guess they do have a TV, but what good is a TV with no channels? Fair enough, having spent over $10k with Airbnb in the past 2 years, this will be the last time I book with Airbnb. If you're going to use Airbnb, just make sure that you clarify exactly what the amenities are prior to booking. If's something goes wrong, or isn't as described, you're out of luck.

My husband and I have been living in Europe for the last 5 years. We love to arrange our travels independently from big travel agencies. We have used Airbnb numerous times in Europe (where we have forged live long friends) as well as in North America. Our experience is Airbnb represents a wonderful alternative to the normal travel vector. In Europe it follows suite to your Airbnb Belonging Mission Statement-"That’s because the rewards you get from Airbnb aren’t just financial—they’re personal—for hosts and guests alike." However, what we find in the U.S that this follows more under the U.S capitalistic market style. Individuals are now purchasing properties solely to rent out on Airbnb and the personal touch is utterly missing....actually completely missing. Yes, maybe the company will benefit from more and more rentals on the site. Though in the long run it will dissuade passionate loyal AirBnB customers from the services, which are the ones who have promoted Airbnb via word of mouth. Every experience we've had in Canada, U.S, & Puerto Rico has lacked any human contact what so ever. We are lucky if we get to talk to the host via a telephone. Which always ended up being a long distance call from half way across North America or via an email to a code for a key drop box to gain access to the property. The second issue on this side of the pond is the degree of capitalism and cost savings the host is going through, which in turn short sides the customer (Lukewarm water for example or stating you have air conditioning although its a plug in A/C (which really just heats the house), or only operates in one room in the house or doesn't exist). I apologies for the diatribe. Thirdly, Airbnb has official Bed and Breakfasts registered on the website in the Puerto Rico. Yet, they are only camouflaged B&B, which have been operating for decades and are marketed to customers as a genuine intimate Airbnb experience. If we wanted to stay at a Bed and Breakfast (and/or Hotel) we would use Hotels.com or other established websites. Yet what differentiates Airbnb seems to been lost at the present moment. In Europe we were one of Airbnb biggest fans telling hundreds of U.S Military colleagues and friends how great the services is although I'm not comfortable at the moment staking my reputation on the services provided in North America. Tomorrow will make the second Airbnb location, we are departing days early from to go to a hotel. I hope to see Airbnb back on top in the future.

I have been working with airbnb for 3 yrs now, especially this year I have exprerinced very interesting cases where the guest complained with funny things or unacceptable money back claims. Airbnb customer service had been very responsive to guests and accepted their money claims even not asking me for an explanation. How on earth , a woman claims of 7,5 pounds for using external drying facility every single day that she stayed and airbnb finds this ok ???? how on earth she can wash clothes every day for 25 days, come on airbnb , just common sense please. I sent number of emails and phone calls and I was told someone would come back to me etc.. but 4 days no reply at all. They completely lost the track . DO NOT LIST WITH AIRBNB , THERE ARE NOW INCREADIBLY MUCH BETTER RENTAL WEBSITES WITH BETTER/FASTER CUSTOMER SERVICE.
No guarantee. Host can cancel your booking at the very last minute leaving you stranded. If you want your holidays to be ruin.. Be my guest.. Try airbnb

airbnb - what a bloody shambles! Could not find a hotel or B&B for love nor money, hugely busy weekend in a very small country village in Dorset, UK. So resorted to airbnb; found one property left on 4th Sept in Lymington, reserved it, (£55 bed no breakfast plus £60 cleaning fee - for one night, but needs must when the devil drives) then host said no then airbnb said no gettee sleepee no payyee monee! Airbnb confimed by email on 5th that host has not responded within 24hrs and host texted to say he could not do the night of 6th. All good so eventually after 6 hours on the phone I found a hotel cancellation and got that. Then host at 4 A.M this morning 6th for reservation for tonight 6th texted to say ok he could do it and tried to take the money. There is no direct contact with airbnb and every avenue of 'Help' refers back to a community member not airbnb themselves who contractually are the agent. Have had to resort to reporting issue to credit card company and notify both host and airbnb that any attempted transaction will be fraudulent. I'm sure other people have had good experience with airbnb but I will never touch them with a bargepole again. I'd rather sleep in my car!

I booked accommodation through Airbnb. Turns out that even though the listing was showing as available and I was able to take steps to secure it, the owner was selling (although, Airbnb tells me that even though it looks available, and I am able to click the dates and proceed with the booking, I should message the owner and check if it really is available, in case it is pretending). My money was then taken and listed as a pending transaction. After speaking with my bank, they advised Airbnb need to fax a request to remove pending status from the payment. After calling 4 different operators at Airbnb (and being hung up on by one), I was told no managers were available and that the payment was with 'the payments team', who I wasn't able to contact, in fact, the operators themselves couldn't contact them. After jumping up and down like a lunatic, I finally received a call back from the manager, who told me there was nothing to be done. I received an email from the elusive 'payments team' telling me that a fax had been sent to my bank to action the request and that they needed my consent to send my card and transaction details (although, being my bank you would assume that they had them already?). Contacted the bank again to be told that the fax had incomplete details and the request couldn't be actioned. I have since emailed 'the payments team' back, as you cannot contact them by phone apparently. The saga continues.... Just don't. Never. Never ever. Never ever ever ever. They are THE WORST!!!! Update: Have had to lodge complaint with our Consumer Affairs office. Have tried to call back but apparently the 24/7 helpline is closed. They must recognise my number. Stay tuned. Update: Made a complaint on their Facebook page and sympathised with other users experiencing the same issue without aggressive or derogatory language. All comments were removed and I was blocked from the page.

I've rented places with airbnb 3 or 4 times, and up to now it's been fine - as long as you go in with your eyes open (check reviews, double-check all property details, check anything you're not sure of directly with hosts, and always remember you're dealing not with a business but with a person you've never met). But my experience today has changed my views. A host cancelled a booking I made three weeks ago - for a booking in less than a month - simply because he got a better offer. This was a host with dozens of good reviews. From what I can see, airbnb is weighted strongly in favour of hosts, who can cancel without major consequences. The moral: be aware that until airbnb changes its procedures, your host can cancel a booking at any time and leave you with nowhere to stay.

The website was well designed that enable users' easy navigation. But I realized the service fees they are charging are outrageous! Some times I will have to pay the amount equals to one night accommodation! I believe this is too much for travelers who wants to find good and reasonable priced accommodations overseas. Added up all the fees I'd rather staying in a hotel which is actually cheaper than AirBnb charged!

Trying to sign up as a property owner to Airbnb was one of the most appalling customer service experiences of my life. It took 3 entire days for each email to be answered. 3 emails, 9 days. And after 10 days I was still having to prove who I was. Someone is going to easily come up with a better mousetrap. I gave up and signed up with HomeAway. Way better service and people who can actually help you get it done. Took 36 hours for the whole process.

I tried to book a property in Positano, Italy for 5 days in September. I signed up with my credit card, and booked a place after searching for hours. I liked the site and enjoyed looking at the properties to find the right one for us. 24hours after booking, when I thought it was all squared away,I got a rejected, no reason, nothing. I tried to email the host, no answer. I tried to contact the site - oh, my god, nothing on the site for customer contact let alone customer service. So I booked another place, again, 24 hours later, just rejected. Nothing from the host to say why. Three days now and tried to book three different places. All rejected. Emailed the hosts all seemed good, then just nothing. Don't waste your time and energy on this site. The costs of the properties change from page to page, in the search then in the property page - a bug in the site. So that sucks too. Awful experience. Stressful. And the fees to the site are very high - and for what? Poor service, buggy site. No communication. Are they kidding? Then I found Summer in Italy - and had a great experience. So don't waste your time on this site.

I have de listed MY property due to the poor customer service and the long waits to get paid.We have waited almost a month and still no payment.The customer service keeps changing the date of payment to me.They do not respond to emails,they have been paid by the guest 3 months in advance but still jerk you around on paying the host.DO NOT LIST YOUR PROPERTY with AIR B&B

FULL DISCLOSURE: I'm a "host". I would NEVER stay in a property offered by AirBnB (if it ain't the Hyatt, I'm not stayin'). YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR. I'll be honest. I've made a TON of money using AirBnB. They have an uncanny ability to fill the smallest gaps between otherwise lengthy rentals. But their customer service is non-existent. Automated response to email is one thing but when there's a PROBLEM with a rental a SUPERCOMPUTER can't deal with it. Sometimes they forget to pay. Sometimes, they just don't give a hoot after the reservation is done. One thing I have noticed is that there is an unfortunate commonality among the "guests": a great majority of them expect a "babysitter" approach to the rental and when they aren't coddled like they think they should be, a negative review ensues. I've been doing short term rentals for longer than the founders of AirBnB have been on this planet. It's the flavor of the day, and it too will run its course. Use it for what it does well and wait for the next greatest thing which no doubt is in the mind of some enterprising genius--I'll be first in line for that! Really hate their review rules. Really, really hate their "trust and verification" process. Really, really, REALLY hate their "touchy feely reach out" automated emails always signed "with love" (very creepy).

My first foray into Airbnb and never again. My money has been put on hold on my credit card without me confirming a booking. I have no receipt of this and have been provided with no transaction details at all. The first I know of it is when I can't buy something on my card as $1700+ is on hold. After searching the site I finally found a phone number and was told it would probably be up to a week before the reversal happens. Is this legal? Can they actually hold your money without telling you or giving a receipt? I think not. Never, never again.
Lady is a druggie her house is full of mold mold report done 6/13/14 be warned

We booked an apartment for a family reunion with my sister . Money taken instantly from our account . Owner of apartment sublets firstly which is a violation of her apartment lease agreement One week after our vacation we were notified that we had wild drinking parties and I received slanderous texts about "y'all can't hold your liquor " and that we had broken drinking glasses and a shower curtain Rod . Also accused of scratching in closets which leads me to believe that there may have been hidden cameras or the owner came back while we were out and went through the apartment which violates our privacy rights Today I received a formal complaint demanding money to settle this account or she will seek legal counsel My bad for wanting to try something unique ! Will never use this site again and only hotel bookings from now on Most dissatisfied and unpleasant vacation experience !

My host confirmed my booking request without reading that there are two travelers. She then messaged and asked me to cancel the booking since her place only allows 1 person. So I did. Guess what? Airbnb promptly charged me $24 "service fee". I tried to call them and explain that this is the host's mistake but the numbers they provided do not work--it keeps hanging up on me. It is the worst experience trying to book a place. I have no idea if I will get my money back. I would stay away, or be very very careful before trying to book a place.

Airbnb and its community is a remarkable one. I never had any problems reaching them and getting their full support when questions/concerns/problems arised. They were always on time addressing my worries and even double checking it if I have had any help with it. When super typhoon Haiyan devastated my island, they were the first one who reached out to me first to check if I and my family were ok. I was worried sick about my guests who were booked to stay in my house shortly after the typhoon and being that the internet connection was really bad, I lost sleep because of that. But I didn't even have to worry since they took care of every one of them. Even giving me the full payment of some bookings which enabled me to help some families who lost their homes. Some of my Airbnb guests and would be guests who cancelled reached out and gave me their wellwishes and support. So yes, Airbnb have a huge heart that extends to its' amazing community. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

I have spent 4 days looking for a two night stay in Vienna apartment, 6 months before the trip.i had tried to reserve in different apartments one by one(about 20 apartments in total),every time the check-in and check-out dates in calendar were available,each reservation my credit cards information was required . the owners are allowed 24 hours to respond. Some of host didn't response ever, some of them declined the request and I had to deal with rather inexperienced and insecure hosts who could not manage a timetable. No results after 4 days of my wasted time.

Booked an apartment with Airbnb for the Seychelles approx 2 months ago, full payment is taken a the point of booking. Today, less than 2 weeks before our holiday, Airbnb demand that I give them a copy of my passport or driving license in order to link my account with facebook and share my phone number, email address and other personal information so that "members" can view me as "trustworthy". Their privacy policy states that only a small number of employees will have access to my personal and sensitive information but in the next sentence they state that 3rd parties will use the information provided by my verified ID - so which is it. I am not happy to share such personal and sensitive information but apparently having my full payment is not enough. A final kick in the teeth is that I cannot access the cancellation policy without having verified my account! I am sure this breaches numerous consumer rights and data protection policies. They have threatened that if I do not provide my Passport or driving license they will cancel our accommodation, leaving us with less than 2 weeks to source other accommodation. Oh and if you want to get in touch with somebody...good luck, they would prefer your communication is sent to other members for a response!

I used Airbnb to rent an apartment in Budapest. The apartment was great and we had no problems with the actual rental. But somebody hacked my account after I got back. Used my name and telephone number to scam other travelers. Tons of problems. Airbnb was worst than horrible at helping to resolve this problem. You wait an hour to reach a customer service person, and I'm not exaggerating. And while you wait, they play recordings of their staff performing really awful music, and I'm not kidding. Meanwhile, on my computer screen, I'm looking at my Airbnb account page with someone else's photo and descriptions of a non-existent property in Greece, and dozens of hopeful inquiries from hapless travelers, and my phone number. I have no way to change anything because the thieves have locked me out of my own account. So just don't deal with Airbnb, friends. Just don't. There are other ways to rent apartments in Budapest.

It has been 16 days since I cancelled the accommodation that I booked on Airbnb after getting it for the first day and discovered that hygiene was absent from the equation ! I got some of the money back, nevertheless I have been charged 64 €. The host told me that she received only 32 € and she will pay me back. I contacted Airbnb to let them know that I haven't used the flat that I booked so I don't want to pay any fees for Airbnb, besides I booked another flat the same day and I paid them. 13 Days later, and after I sent 3 messages, I am still waiting to hear from them. Their customer's service is really bad or slow. They are charging us a lot for the booking but when we want to talk to them. They don't answer back.

My host told me that the place I booked in Bratislava, had electrical problems and would not be available and offered other places, some at higher costs. When I said I did not want to stay in those locations, he offered to refund my money. Once the AIRBNB office was involved, I was told that If I did not accept a substitute property, I would not receive a full refund. I protested that the property I choose was not available. When asked in another email, if this is the policy of AIRBNB, that Hosts can substitute properties after booking, I finally was told that I did not have to accept a substitute property and I would receive a full refund. Most of my experience with AIRBNB this past year have been as expected, I hope that this is a rare event. I applaud AIRBNB for finally agreeing with me and refunding my money.

August 2014, arrived in Portland, OR for four night stay in prepaid 2 bed apartment. Owner was away but had arranged for someone else to let us into his apartment. It had been described as being "professionally cleaned". It was filthy, the sheets were soiled and there were no clean towels, just some heavily soiled ones in the laundry basket. YUK. We had to scramble to find alternative accommodation, which ended up being three times the amount we had paid to Airbnb. We were promptly refunded the amount we had paid for the apartment, but were still heavily out of pocket. Have never had problems with VRBO or Homeaway, but would never use Airbnb again. I was unable to leave a review on their site as we did not actually stay in the apartment, so subsequent tenants could experience the same problems we did.

I used Airbnb for the first time last year, and I could not have been happier with the experience. I feel my information is safe and secure, I've loved all of the hosts I've been able to meet, and now book all of my stays on Airbnb instead of hotels. I think the system they have is great - it's all about peer reviews, and they have customer support there ready to help you in the case of any emergency. I recommend Airbnb to all of my friends, and know every one of them that has used the service has only positive things to say about it.

I discovered Airbnb last year when I embarked upon a year of living in Berlin and traveling around Europe. My first experience was in Prague and I've never looked back. Searching through the diverse rental options and getting to know my hosts have become some of my favorite parts of traveling! The platform is super easy to use, and my hosts have always been reliable, hospitable, and engaging. The prices aren't cheaper than traditional hotels or hostels 100% of the time, but the times I've paid comparable or slightly higher prices have been totally worth it for the unique experiences those homes and hosts offered (i.e. I now have priceless memories/stories about staying in a multilevel family compound in Cinque Terre where my host gave us endless supplies of Nutella and drove us wherever we wanted to go in her lime green Fiat). Highly recommend - especially after the site's beautiful redesign!

Let's be honest, airbnb isn't for everyone. If you don't want to be driven around in a car with a stranger who may or may not know their way around the city, don't use ridesharing apps. If you don't want to sleep in someone else's house that may or may not be EXACTLY as pictured, don't use airbnb. If you are flexible, smart, understanding, and adventurous staying in an airbnb.com rental is the BEST way to see an new city. If you have OCD, need a concierge desk, or if you don't like immersion travel experiences, it is NOT the accommodation site for you. That being said, airbnb is the future. It's sustainable, supports local economies, and brings us together as human beings (not just guest #4663 in room 1033 at location US34). I love you airbnb!

Airbnb stole 3000€ from us in France. We rented an apartment through their website and when we arrived we found the apartment totally different than what was listed on their website. Plus it was so dirty, and doesn’t provide minimum living circumstances for human beings. As a result we left the apartment directly, but nothing was refunded until this moment. Airbnb are scammers and thieves. They stand by the scamming property listers since these are the one's who are making them good business. I actually wasn't willing to give them a 1 star rating because they don't deserve that star, but this is the minimum possible.

Paid in full for a 4 night stay. No problems booking and the owner of the accommodation is lovely. On the website it says identification is verified and it all went through smoothly. This was at the end of July. Then 2 days before we drive down to our holiday, AirBNB emails me demanding that I verify my identity by uploading a piece of Government-issued id to their website (passport or driving license). My favourite bit was where they threatened to cancel my reservation if I didn't comply within 48 hours. I replied explaining that I didn't want to hand over such personal information and also got in touch on the Facebook. Their response was basically, "Tough". Apparently my full payment of £240 (which had gone through), my email account and my Facebook account (both of which I was using to contact them with) were not enough evidence that I am, in fact, 'real'. So 2 days before my hol, they've cancelled my holiday and are processing my refund - who knows how long that will take, even though I need it NOW to book accommodation somewhere else. Not happy is an understatement. Avoid.

I've had no issues with AIRBNB either as a traveler or a host. The problems have been with the actual hosts of properties I've booked. They have been the misrepresentative ones and I now carefully read all reviews and identification process on the people I will be interacting with. As a host, I screen the requests the same way. Read the reviews and decline ANYTHING fishy. People will try to go around the system to get to your home. AIRBNB is a tool and with skill of your own it can work well for your purposes.

We had experienced some communication issues with the host prior to our scheduled stay that made us wary of quality of service/experience we would receive if we went ahead and stayed with the booking. All of the communication and transactions that took place were explicit on the messaging board that is provided on the Airbnb platform. This was intentional as I came to realize that this messaging board provides a form of accountability, a "document" trail, if you will, that shows record of communication. I was proactive about the problem (meaning that the issues occurred prior to our stay and within cancellation stipulations) and contacted Airbnb to inform them of the issues we were experiencing with our host. The rep with whom I spoke listened to my concerns; she responded with an email that summarized our conversation. Long story short, we felt that our peace of mind was more important than "saving" money and went ahead and cancelled the reservation - willing to bite the bullet (in the loss of money due to Airbnb fees), and had committed to no longer use Airbnb because of the experience with the host and uncertainties we were faced with. I had informed Airbnb of our decision. Their response to bring resolve to the issue went above and beyond our expectations and restored our trust in the establishment. I really do need to commend the rep who took care of the issue. She was on the case; and was timely. Her emails and willingness to help made me feel that my concerns were heard.

SEASONED HOST AND GUEST I am a seasoned host and guest of Airbnb. I have used them for years traveling the World. It is one of the most exciting adventures anyone could take into the lives of others. The warmth and experience received from staying at someone's home beats staying at a cold and unemotional hotel. The NEGATIVE reviews are probably from people who do not always use Airbnb and they are unfamilar with its service. Granted, if you do NOT know what you are doing, you can run into some unprofessional and shady people. For example, you should always look for hosts or guests that have prior reviews and VERIFIED photos of their apartments. I have noticed some host will not take photos that display an accurate view of their apartment. Some host will even lie about the amenities. in one incident, I walked into a hosts apartment and the electricity and cable was cut off. The apartment was dirty and cluttered with her personal items to the point I could not walk around without hitting something. But the photo she posted on Airbnb showed an empty apartment. So look out for shady people on Airbnb and use their security features to weed out the bad people. HOWEVER, the experience has been wonderful. Also, you can't blame Airbnb for trying to manage the thousands of calls it gets for customer service. Not many companies can handle such a huge demand. Also, Airbnb added their cleaning service Handybooks, which has been cleaning our apartment after each guest and they make the beds, put on their own sheets and add their towels for the next guests like a hotel service. AIRBNB WILL BE AROUND FOR A VERY LONG TIME AND IT WILL GROW

We are dealing with a hurricane at the moment and I want to be able to let my guest cancel his booking - but airbnb has some sort of lengthy protocol on their web site. Nothing as simple as a refund. I'd even settle for an email address. I've had very nice guests and good bookings but am ready to pull the plug on airbnb because of not being able to contact anyone in the company.

Have booked before via this company but now they have this b….sh…. verification deal which is soooooo annoying. Waiting for confirmation sms that never came and now they have all my personal details….goodness knows what the security is like

dear friend, 1. charges are too high and 2. People are sub letting their accommodations without the owners authority. This company started well but I am afraid things have got out of hand. I do not use them now.

I am surprised to read such poor reviews on Airbnb. I have used them for three cities and have had nothing but praise for the hosts, accommodations and the Airbnb service. I sense that there are some hosts who were not well organized to begin with and/or that guests did not do thorough research when booking accommodations. I spent hours before making a reservation on all three occasions and lots of emails back and forth with the hosts to determine if the accommodations would serve our needs. Also, read every single bit of feedback about the space advertised and the host.

I would like to share my story to any potential host so that they know what to expect. Four years ago i bought this lovely apartment in the center of Athens right under the Acropolis in the Plaka area. For me it was a dream come true. These properties pass from generation to generation and its almost impossible to buy one. I was lucky enough to buy one.Then depression struck Greece and i thought that it would be nice to show people around Athens and the Greek culture and make some money also. So i decided to go for Airbnb since it seemed like a nice idea and a nice platform. At first things were normal and since i am a very hospitable person i got some really great reviews. I realized that i had to go the extra mile and do much more form my guests.But i didnt mind cause i thought i was doing the right thing. Then trouble started coming my way.At first i had these guests who decided to have a party in the terrace of my apartment. Most of my neighbors got upset and after my guests started throwing bottles out of the terrace they called the police.(At this point i would like to to say that in Greece there is no law covering short term rentals and the penalty is 50.000 euro.)I got lucky and the police officers didnt press any charges on me.Shortly after i had another couple that liked to scream while they were having 'personal moments' the police was called once more.Again i got lucky and they didnt press any charges on me. At this point i knew i had to let things calm down a bit. So i contacted my future guests explained them the situation and i asked them if they wanted me to cancel their reservation or to book them a hotel room which i would pay. Some wanted to cancel and some went for the hotel room. So at this point im having disputes with my neighbors i am paying for my guest hotels and i get bad reviews for cancelling reservations. After a while i decided that i couldnt keep on paying hotel rooms so i rented a new nearby apartment renovated it and offered to transfer my guests there. Things seemed to be back to normal for a week and then i have a guest coming in who had a 3 days reservation and asked me for one more day prior to the reserved days. So this is where i make the mistake to accept it and even let her stay for free without any charge. After the first free night the guest started to complain about smell of paint in the apartment and asked to leave.I realized i had made the mistake to tell her about my problems in the past and how i offered my guests hotel rooms and she probably thought she could do the same. I did offered her a hotel room.Then she didnt like the hotel room and complained about that also.We agreed that i would cancel her reservation in order for her to get a full refund and then she would find other accommodation from Airbnb.Meanwhile i let her stay in the apartment while she was looking for other accommodation from Airbnb. Then she had her daughters coming in to stay.Days passed and she kept on saying that airbnb couldnt find her other accommodation. In the end four days passed in total and she stayed there free of charge.I contacted airbnb and they told me what a great guy i am who let her stay in there and that i would get my money.I told them i dont mind about the money for me it was more important for my guest to have a good time.They told me that still they wanted to pay me. After a few days i got this email from airbnb which said that my guest was refusing to pay since there were some amenities missing.Not only that but she provided pictures and a list of missing amenities.Also since i had bad reviews in the past (they meant the canceling penalties) they would not pay me.(i never got to see these pictures or at least answer why there were missing amenities especially since i had a guest who shouldnt be at my apartment and wouldnt allow me to go in) So at this point i have trouble with my neighbors because of airbnb i have spend a fortune for my guests and now i have airbnb insulting me. I got really upset and even though it wasnt in my intention i decided to claim my money.So i send them a mail asking who was responsible for the area (i would like to tell you that no employee in Airbnb has a surname.Its Joe Jim Nikki Sandra etc but no last name.)After the mail i send them another employee (without surname again) sends me a mail saying that because i had cancelled reservations in the past they would suspend my account and unlist my listings.Furthermore they warned me that they could delete my account. That was the last drop for me.I am cancelling all my future reservations and it saddens me to cause so many people inconvenience but i feel that nothing of all these is my fault and that airbnb has a lot of flaws. So from my experience i would say its too good to be true if you are a host and too risky if you are a guest.One last thing is they way they handle the money a host earns.If you see future payouts that isnt your money unless they decide to.They can refuse payments with little or no excuse at all.I really think that its about time someone deals with this company.I cancelled 15.000 usd reservations but i didnt mind because i will be able to sleep well at night again and also im happy that airbnb wont get 3.000 usd as a fee from MY apartment.

No professionnals! Spent two days of my life looking for a one night stay in Copenhagen (the owners are allowed 24 hours rather than seconds to respond) and had to deal with rather inexperienced and insecure hosts who could not manage a timetable. Nothing at the end of it. A non-starter.

Airbnb is a poorly run operation with a customer service team that is lame at best. They do not care about the customer experience as long as they have made their money off the rental. I have rented more than 20 times from them, but now will never again use their services. It is probably good that they are under investigation by the government. They probably need to be regulated or closed down.

I have read through the horrible reviews on here and while I understand some of the issues, I believe using this site really requires practice and scrutiny. As a host, I pay attention to who requests to book. I always require an introduction (who are you, what are your plans, etc, which most guests provide up-front, anyway) and if I don't get a good vibe or if they have negative reviews or no reviews, I tend to suggest they find another place. I am particularly annoyed by people asking for a discount for a 1-2 day stay. I do not add any extra fees (cleaning, deposit or other) and my property is one of the least expensive in the area, so I only offer discounts to longer stays or returning guests. Also, guests may not realize that it is detrimental to a host to cancel a reservation, so airbnb does not take it lightly. If a host cancels, their post goes down to the bottom of the list and it takes a long time to get it back up. That can cause hundreds of dollars in lost revenue to a host. As a guest, I also look very closely at reviews. I would never stay at a place that had no reviews. I have only had wonderful experiences as a guest (as a solo female traveler and with my partner), so I highly recommend reading the posting and the airbnb rules before committing. I also have had trouble with airbnb charging me, but they have always quickly resolved the problem and I have had at least 2 $100 coupons as a result.

When we found out that we weren't going to be able to make it about 3 days before our check in, we let the owner know about the cancellation. Well after many trying contacts for airB&B, because our strict refund policy we get NOTHING BACK even though I had about two days before the week was included. SO MAKE SURE NOT TO BOOK WITH A STRICT REFUND POLICY. MAYBE THAT'S WHY SHE WAS AVAILIBLE...

Beware Airbnb! I made a request to book, then spoke to the host about a different property which we ended up booking through them directly. They voided the original booking. Airbnb sent me an email confirming that they voided the charges, but still put through the charges on my credit card. Now I am stuck with the charges until they contact the credit card company and have no one to speak to at Airbnb to sort this out. I will never trust them again.
i rent a guest house, the renter was using Airbnb without my permission, Airbnb has not removed the advertisement for my property

We wanted to book an apartment in Venice, and found one in a price-level that fitted our budget. But in the end the price was doubled(!!!) with all the extra fees! Looks like this: Apartment payment pr night (2 nights) Airbnb fee cleaning fee (same as one night in the apartment!) check-in fee (never heard of it before) -------------------- FINAL PRICE _____________ So futurewise I trust the booking.com much more for apartment rents - because here you see the price you end up paying while you say yes to book it.
Sneaky and dishonest AIRbnb are. Won't use them again.

Generally good but your reservation can be cancelled in the last minute and you just get money back without any penalty. But if you cancel, you owe big time.. If you book you have to have back up plan.. So wouldn't recommend it

I had a trip planned to go to Israel...but due to the circumstances I needed to cancel ...airbnb gave me full credit back to my card...in addition gave me $100 dollar coupon to use on my next trip...took a little while to rectify the issue...but at the end they were very helpful and considerate of the situation!

Airbnb states in capital letters in its t&c's that it is not responsible for the accuracy of its listings, nor any experiences you may have as a guest. That's the part to look out for: YOU HAVE NO IDEA WHAT YOU'RE GETTING. In our case, it was a filthy illegal sublet with the front door key hidden in a lock tied to a lamp post. We were then advised to sneak in via the side entrance and avoid management, reception and neighbours' questions at all costs. The entire organization operates in some sort of legal grey zone. We'll be staying away - and giving our money to honest, tax-paying legal BnBs in future. Goodbye Airbnb. Good riddance.

Imagine my shock when, days after a cancelled reservation had been refunded in full, including having received confirmation emails from Airbnb of the cancellation and refund, and verifying that the pending transaction had been cancelled and the funds returned to my bank account, I log into my bank to discover the fraudsters had just charged me for the cancelled and refunded reservation!! Days after the refund! This is nothing short of fraud. Ripoff. Stealing money. Blatant illegal practices. HOW IN THE WORLD CAN THEY JUSTIFY THE LEGALITY OF DOING THIS?? Thankfully this is my PayPal account, and Paypal clearly has a policy in place to combat Airbnb's fraudulent charges, and apparently deal with this kind of thing all the time, because they helped me get my money back to begin with. Tomorrow I will be filing another dispute with PayPal and I'm hopeful they can set up a block on my account to prevent Airbnb from ever accessing my money again. I regret the day I ever considered using their godawful 'service'. Buyer beware- just don't. Side note- if this continues to be an issue, I will file a claim in small claims court, which in my city and state goes up to $5,000. I'm thinking if more people filed legal claims they'd think twice about stealing consumer's money.

We were planning a 3 day trip to Colonial Williamsburg with our daughter and our 3 grandchildren. We booked two nights at a local resort through Vacation Depot, who is the host (owner) of the condo at the resort. We received an email of our confirmed reservation four days prior to arrival, and airbnb charged our credit card at that time. The following day, Vacation Depot canceled our reservation. The only notification I received were two emails - one from Vacation Depot and one from airbnb. No one called me. No one emailed my wife or called her at all. I checked my email two days later and that was the first time I was aware of the cancellation. airbnb's email offered a 20% credit toward a replacement location, but none were available for the nights we were scheduled to go. In order to get a refund, we had to go to their website to ask for the refund, then wait several days for the credit card company to credit our account. When I called the customer service number, I was on hold for an hour, and when I finally got to speak with someone, he didn't say "how may I help you?" His first statement was "What's your phone number? What's your email address? I can't verify your account." Once we were able to verify the account, they had no help to offer me other than to request a refund and they would send me a $50 coupon for my trouble. Vacation Depot was even worse. They sent me an email without a phone number to call. In my opinion, airbnb made several errors that contradict the tenets of basic customer service: 1. They made no effort to call me when they learned of the cancellation: All I got was an email. 2. They did not properly screen their host - in this case, Vacation Depot had a condo with plumbing problems, but the condo was listed on airbnb's site as being available. No one at airbnb or Vacation Depot checked to verify that the condo was available. 3. They took our money as soon as the reservation was confirmed, without making sure that the host's property was ready and available. This was four days before we were scheduled to arrive. 4. They left me on hold for an hour when I called customer service. 5. They had no backup plan to move me to another location other than another airbnb host, and that location was not acceptable. They could easily make arrangements with other travel companies to help out their guests when a problem like this happens. 6. When I pointed all of these things out to the customer service rep, he had no explanation other than a fifty dollar coupon and instructions on how to request a refund. "there's nothing else I can do." I will never use this service again, and I hope that no one else will, either.

I've used AirBnB throughout my travels in the USA. Mainly on the west coast. I have had nothing but fantastic experiences through AirBnB and at no time have I experienced anything sour or off putting. I would and will recommend this service to anyone out there!

I stayed at an AirBnB in the Old Northeast section (EXPENSIVE) of St. Petersburg, Florida (early summer 2012). My host did a walk-through of his rental with me before I left, and then he drove me to the airport, where we shook hands and said our good-byes. BUT upon my return home, I received an e-mail message from him asking me to pay for new BOX SPRINGS for two beds (one for a bed I didn't use at all), new CARPETING, and the cleaning of TWO CHAIRS that had food debris in them prior to my stay. Not to mention that the guy was WEIRD (which I attributed to the fact that his wife was sick and then died of ovarian cancer during my six-week stay) and made me feel uncomfortable (I was traveling alone as a single woman). Although I provided a positive review upon the conclusion of my trip, when I look back on it now, I WOULD THINK TWICE AND THEN A THIRD TIME ABOUT USING AIRBNB AGAIN, ESPECIALLY AS A SOLO FEMALE TRAVELER. YOU ARE TYPICALLY SAFER IN A HOTEL, I BELIEVE, PARTICULARLY WHEN THE HOST OF AN AIRBNB IS MALE.
Simply this - DON'T USE THIS COMPANY

Really?!? And even if I trust you now, what happens if your company gets hacked -- or sold?? This is just intrusive and... creepy...

Customer service as a guest was great. I couldn't be happier with airbnb's customer service (and especially the efforts of [Name] at customer service, [Name] at Airbnb trip experience, and whoever else was on the team that handled my case). I've dealt with hotels, airlines, all sorts of institutions where problems sometimes arise, and I've never before seen such a fast and fair resolution.

I am a 5 star host with over 60 5star reviews and I am in total agreement with what others have stated with how airbnb now treats their hosts ... -The customer service was once great is now a joke, the feedback leaves me wondering if they even bother to read my email or do they just cut and paste a standard reply. -Every time there is a currency exchange involved, it's ALWAYS works out in their favor!! Even euros to Canadian!!! WTF?! -The new contract leaves airbnb completely blameless and hands off. Once the guest and host connect, airbnb washes their hands and collects the money. -They are so over-saturation with hosts! Last summer I was booked weeks to months in advance, now I get last minute and days notice because airbnb now tells guests to keep looking without even waiting to hear from me. -There is no regulation on who can hosts and no filters. Landlords are now renting apartments on airbnb - one host I rented from has 27 apartments in her city, all on airbnb!! How si this fair? I feel very let down as a host on airbnb. A once great concept has been swallowed by greed.

So... Here's the thing. I searched for a holiday property on airbnb and found what we thought to be a great property. One week in August by the sea. Although the host had 0 reviews we were not suspicious as they had only been a member for a few months. So far so good.. Messages start to arrive, we have been pre-approved ( what does that mean ? ) confirm the booking quickly before it expires ?? A few more checks on the small print... everything seems fine , confirm the booking, pay the full amount. All happy, family happy , confirm the dates with work and make the other necessary preparations. ( travel arrangements for all the family ) 48 hours go by , I have established direct contact with the host and then…… “ message from host “ Really sorry but I gave the property to a local estate agent and they have just told me that they have a rental for the whole month so.. sorry, but your rental of a week is now cancelled. Nothing that airbnb can do , host cancelled therefore so is your holiday. Standard aibnb .. we can help you look for another property with a 20% increase. Their offers were not comparable to the original property ( why wouldn’t I have chosen them in the first place ? ) so it’s a refund. Can I leave feed back , (to warn other potential renters that this host is totally UNRELIABLE ) … No. you can’t leave negative feedback on AirBnB unless you stay at a property, so there is no other way for us to warn people about this on their site. The only thing that now appears on the hosts page.. ( if you click on reviews ) is The reservation was canceled 28 days before arrival. This is an automated posting Why do airBnB not make it clear that it was the HOST that cancelled and why. I would probably have stayed clear of this property if I had known. To airBnB’s credit, they did refund the whole rental amount very quickly and also compensated us for ancillaries that we would have forfeited ( transport to a place that we no longer could go to because our holiday rental had been cancelled ) because they cannot be used if we don’t have the property. Beware …. You and your family can spend a fortune on tickets and suffer disappointment in your holiday being cancelled. You have been warned !!

I rented 2 places in the past year with great success. While planning a trip to Vancouver BC I requested availablity of a host. The new Airbnb website takes you credit card information on the front end and clearly says that they will not charge if the host refuses the reqeust. There is no other option. The host responded quickly and appologized that she would not be renting the space that month. Imagine my surprise when the next morning I receive an email says that I had been accepted and my credit card charged by Airbnb! I casting about their website is ti very hard to find any customer server support or information although I did find the cancellation button which I selected. I finally did find a complaint page that netted me a response from an off-shore person who quoted the cancellation policy and suggested I should work it out with the host!?? I am done.
